articles.title: I’ve trusted Bitdefender for years, and it doesn’t get much cheaper than this
articles.text:
I use Bitdefender Total Security to protect all of my devices, and it’s down to $28 at Newegg
It combines threat detection with tools to safeguard your privacy
I've used Bitdefender Total Security to protect my own devices for years, and I highly recommend it. I've found a great deal on the security software at Newegg that brings a year's coverage for up to 10 devices down to under $30.
Bitdefender Total Security 2026 is reduced to $28 (was $100) at Newegg with promo code EPF56892. It doesn't get much cheaper than this, so well-worth checking out.
• Best for: Households with multiple devices, anyone wanting protection across different operating systems, and people looking for antivirus software with additional privacy and ransomware defenses.
• Why I like it: I use Bitdefender Total Security to protect all of my devices at home, and it's much more than a traditional antivirus tool. As well as keeping you safe from viruses, spyware, Trojans, ransomware, and other malicious software, it also uses behavioral detection to identify suspicious activity and defend against unknown threats.
Today's best antivirus software deal
Bitdefender Total Security provides one year of protection for 10 Windows, macOS, Android, and iOS devices, with malware detection, ransomware defense, privacy tools, parental controls, and limited daily VPN access included.
Why we recommend it
The software can block online tracking, monitor attempts to access your webcam or microphone, and identify potentially dangerous websites. The subscription covers up to 10 devices running Windows, macOS, Android, and iOS.
The package also includes access to Bitdefender VPN, although it's limited to 200MB per day per device, which is only really enough for occasional use. Parental control features will be of interest to anyone with children, although availability and functionality depend on the OS.
In covering the software, we said: "Bitdefender tops our list and ticks every box. It performed well across our testing, boasts all the tools you need to protect your devices from malware (and more), and is nice and easy to use – regardless of platform. While some expert users might wish for a little more granular customization, we think that Bitdefender strikes the right balance in terms of configuration and ease of use."
Price context & historical value
Newegg sells the one-year, 10-device subscription for $99.99, but is currently offering it at $52.99. Enter EPF56892 at checkout to save a further $25, bringing the final price to $27.99.
That represents a $72 saving against the original price, approximately 72% off. If you activate the program on all 10 devices, the first-year cost works out to approximately $2.80 per device.
It's important to remember that this is a one-year license, rather than a permanent software purchase. You're not locked in though. What I usually do is search for a new deal around the renewal time.
For more options, take a look at our roundup of the best antivirus software.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Bitdefender Total Security if...
You want one antivirus subscription covering Windows, Mac, Android, and iOS devices. It's also great for ransomware protection, malicious website detection, and privacy tools. At $27.99, this is a fantastic deal.
❌ Skip Bitdefender Total Security if...
You only need to protect one computer and are satisfied with your device's built-in antivirus software. Windows includes Microsoft Defender, and macOS and mobile operating systems have their own security protections.

articles.title: DJI’s drone-charging power station doubles as emergency home backup
articles.text:
DJI’s Power 1000 V2 delivers all-day drone charging with 2,600W of home backup — and Amazon dropped the price to $400
DJI combines an LFP battery, dual 140W USB-C ports, and 10ms UPS switching
DJI might not be as well-known in the power supply space as Anker, Bluetti, EcoFlow, or Jackery, but its range of portable power stations have proved rather impressive in our tests. I find them particularly good for drone operators, since the units feature SDC ports for charging DJI drones. But that's not the only use for these power stations.
The DJI Power 1000 V2, currently $400 (was $600) at Amazon, is a prime example of that, with its 1,024Wh battery capacity, 2,600W output, and a port selection that makes it well-suited for home backup during emergency power outages.
• Best for: Drone operators charging multiple devices on the move, or home-owners wanting emergency backup power for appliances, electronics, and outdoor equipment.
• What we like: The DJI Power 1000 V2 is a portable battery station that can also come along on camping trips, RV adventures, and outdoor challenges.
Today's best portable power station deal
This portable power station features a 1,024Wh LFP battery, 2,600W continuous output, 37-minute charging to 80%, dual 140W USB-C ports, 10ms UPS switching, quiet operation, and five-year warranty coverage for owners.
Why we recommend it
The DJI Power 1000 V2 combines a 1,024Wh battery with 2,600W of continuous AC output, making it capable of running a wide range of appliances.
DJI claims the battery can recharge from empty to 80% in 37 minutes, while a full charge takes approximately 56 minutes (under suitable conditions). The station uses lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery chemistry for long-term durability, and it is rated for 4,000 charge cycles while retaining at least 80% of its original capacity.
You get two AC outlets, two USB-A ports, and two USB-C ports capable of delivering up to 140W each. There's also SDC and SDC Lite ports for charging DJI drones. Alongside this, the unit has a UPS function with an approximately 10ms switching time to allow compatible equipment to continue receiving power when the mains supply is interrupted. For overnight use, the company quotes noise levels as low as 26dB. DJI offers up to five years of warranty coverage.
For more picks, we've tested out the best portable power stations and the best DJI drones.
Price context & historical value
Usually priced at $699, the current deal brings the DJI Power 1000 V2 down to $399.98. That's a saving of $299.02, equivalent to approximately 43%.
It's the lowest price I've personally seen for this model and its combination of battery capacity, continuous output, and rapid recharging make it a great deal.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the DJI Power 1000 V2 if...
You want a portable source of electricity for camping, RV trips, outdoor work, or occasional power outages. The 2,600W output gives you flexibility and the fast recharge time reduces how long the battery needs to remain connected to mains power. The dual 140W USB-C ports are also useful.
❌ Skip the DJI Power 1000 V2 if...
You need to run large household appliances for extended periods during an outage. Yes, the 2,600W output can handle substantial loads, but the 1,024Wh battery capacity limits how long it can sustain them.

Turn your laptop into a triple-screen workstation with this Zumwalt S8 Pro 14-inch portable monitor extender, now $90 off at Amazon

• Best for: People who work across multiple applications, regularly travel with their laptops, or want more display space without investing in a permanent multi-monitor setup.
• Why we like it: The main attraction is having three screens available wherever you take your laptop. You could keep a document open on the main display, use another for research, and leave email or messaging applications visible on the third.

Each of the additional screens uses a 14-inch IPS LCD panel with a 1920 x 1080 resolution, 60Hz refresh rate, and 300-nit brightness. The specifications also list 100% sRGB color coverage and 178-degree viewing angles.
Zumwalt describes the extender as having an aluminum construction, an ultra-thin profile, and adjustable screens that fold away for transportation. A protective carrying case is included and there's an integrated kickstand to help support the additional displays.

articles.title: 'Faster code is not the same as better software delivered sooner': New report claims AI isn't solving productivity across the entire software development lifecycle - yet
articles.text:
'Faster code is not the same as better software delivered sooner': New report claims AI isn't solving productivity across the entire software development lifecycle - yet
AI is mostly being used to write code faster
- Atlassian report claims the number of developers saving significant time through AI is actually dropping
- Finding information and participating in meetings are major human bottlenecks
- More then four in five organizations still don't have a clear AI strategy
Nearly nine in 10 (87%) developers surveyed by Atlassian now sayAI is helping them to write and ship code faster, but despite offering significant speed improvements across certain parts of the workflow, three in four (72%) also report either the same or greater friction across the entire lifecycle.
Longer-term optimism around AI's ability to save time is also dropping, with just 25% of developers saving 10+ hours a week when using AI, compared with 68% in 2025.
Ultimately, Atlassian's findings point toward AI simply shifting the bottleneck further downstream rather than tackling time constraints altogether.
Is AI actually helping developers?
The data shows that faster code generation isn't translating into faster software delivery, with the reality of AI-assisted coding now highlighting other areas where AI could actually help. For example, half of developers struggling with finding information (51%) and meeting frequency (50%)
"Faster code is not the same as better software delivered sooner," Atlassian Customer CTO Andrew Boyagi explained. "If teams still struggle to find information, clarify requirements and move work through the delivery process, speeding up coding alone won’t translate into business outcomes."
However, many developers simply feel that AI is being implemented too quickly without consideration for its impacts. Three in five say merely using AI is seen as a positive metric – but its real-world impacts don't fall under that scope.
Companies with an effective strategy were found to be in the best position to reduce friction, where twice as many workers reported positive effects. Still, not even a fifth (17%) of developers say their employer has a clearly communicated and implemented AI strategy.

articles.title: Elon Musk y Anthropic tienen ideas opuestas sobre quién debe beneficiarse de la riqueza creada por la IA
articles.text:
El avance de la inteligencia artificial (IA) ha abierto un debate sobre cómo distribuir la riqueza que generará esta tecnología y qué responsabilidad deben asumir las empresas que la desarrollan.
Mientras Anthropic propone destinar parte de su participación empresarial a un fondo de beneficio público, Elon Musk plantea un modelo diferente, entregar acciones de sus compañías directamente a los ciudadanos para que también puedan beneficiarse de su crecimiento.
Las dos iniciativas parten de una preocupación común: la concentración de riqueza que podría producirse a medida que los sistemas de IA automaticen tareas y transformen el mercado laboral. Sin embargo, sus propuestas difieren en la forma de canalizar esos recursos y en quiénes deberían recibirlos.
Anthropic, uno de los principales laboratorios de inteligencia artificial de Estados Unidos, se ha comprometido a destinar el 5% de sus acciones a un Fondo de Beneficio Público, sujeto a la aprobación de sus accionistas. La iniciativa busca contribuir a afrontar las consecuencias sociales del desarrollo de esta tecnología.
Musk, por su parte, ha planteado la posibilidad de distribuir acciones de SpaceX entre los niños estadounidenses. De esta manera, los menores podrían beneficiarse de la evolución financiera de la compañía a largo plazo, aunque el valor de sus participaciones dependería de los resultados futuros de la empresa.
Anthropic propone destinar parte de sus acciones al beneficio público
La propuesta de Anthropic se enmarca en el debate sobre las consecuencias económicas de la automatización y la responsabilidad de las empresas que desarrollan modelos avanzados de inteligencia artificial.
Dario Amodei, director ejecutivo de la compañía, ha advertido en varias ocasiones sobre el posible impacto de la IA en el empleo. Según sus previsiones, la automatización podría provocar la desaparición de una parte importante de los puestos administrativos de nivel inicial en los próximos cinco años.
El razonamiento parte de que los modelos de inteligencia artificial pueden asumir tareas que actualmente realizan trabajadores, lo que permitiría a las empresas reducir costes y modificar sus necesidades de contratación. Los empleos de oficina que requieren actividades repetitivas o procesos susceptibles de automatización figuran entre los más expuestos a esta transformación.
Ante este escenario, Anthropic plantea destinar el 5% de sus acciones a un fondo de beneficio público. La iniciativa busca que una parte del valor económico generado por la compañía pueda utilizarse para atender necesidades colectivas.
No obstante, el alcance de esta propuesta dependerá de su aprobación y de cómo se concrete el funcionamiento del fondo, incluidos los mecanismos para administrar los recursos y decidir su destino.
Elon Musk quiere repartir acciones de SpaceX entre los niños
La propuesta de Elon Musk plantea una vía diferente para distribuir parte de la riqueza empresarial. En lugar de canalizar los recursos mediante una estructura filantrópica, el empresario ha planteado entregar acciones de SpaceX a los niños estadounidenses.
La iniciativa permitiría que los menores recibieran participaciones en la compañía y pudieran beneficiarse de una eventual revalorización con el paso del tiempo. No se trataría de un pago en efectivo, sino de activos financieros cuyo precio dependería del desempeño de SpaceX y de las condiciones del mercado.
Tomando como referencia una valoración estimada de la empresa, el reparto podría representar alrededor de 11.000 millones de dólares. Sin embargo, esa cifra es una estimación vinculada al valor de las acciones y no equivale a una cantidad garantizada para cada beneficiario.
La diferencia con el modelo de Anthropic es relevante. Mientras la propuesta de Musk busca que los ciudadanos participen directamente en el crecimiento de una empresa, la iniciativa del laboratorio de IA pretende destinar recursos a objetivos de beneficio público.
Dos propuestas que abren el debate sobre la riqueza de la IA
Aunque sus mecanismos son distintos, ambas iniciativas abordan una misma cuestión: quién debería beneficiarse de la riqueza que genere la inteligencia artificial y qué obligaciones tienen las compañías que impulsan su desarrollo.
La automatización podría aumentar la productividad y los ingresos de las empresas, pero también plantea interrogantes sobre el desplazamiento de trabajadores, la desigualdad económica y la distribución de las ganancias derivadas de esta tecnología.
Las propuestas de Anthropic y Musk representan dos alternativas para afrontar parte de estos desafíos. Sin embargo, ninguna garantiza por sí sola que los beneficios de la IA alcancen a toda la población ni que quienes pierdan su empleo reciban el apoyo necesario.
Por ello, el debate también involucra a los gobiernos y a las instituciones públicas. Las políticas de formación profesional, protección social y adaptación del mercado laboral serán determinantes para responder a los cambios que provoque la automatización.
La filantropía empresarial y el reparto de participaciones pueden contribuir a distribuir recursos, pero no sustituyen las medidas públicas necesarias para afrontar las consecuencias económicas y sociales de una tecnología cuyo impacto todavía está en desarrollo.

articles.title: Three dormant US nuclear reactors are being restarted to power AI data centers
articles.text:
Three dormant US nuclear reactors are being restarted to power AI data centers
The US wants to re-open several former nuclear plants
- Three nuclear plants would add 2.25GW of electricity to the grid
- Microsoft and Google plan to use power from those sites
- Trump wants 400GW of nuclear capacity by 2050
In its ongoing effort to become an AI global superpower, the US is reportedly gearing up to restart three previously closed nuclear power plants simply to keep up with the energy demands caused by AI data centers.
Together, the three nuclear facilities would likely provide 2.25GW of electricity, or enough to power two million homes and businesses (per The Los Angeles Times).
And the US Department of Energy looks to be a major supporter of the projects, providing up to $4.4 billion in federal loans.
Dormant nuclear plants are being woken to power AI
Microsoft and Google have already signed agreements to purchase electricity from two of those facilities, with power plant restarts now slated for between 2027 and 2029, per the report.
Importantly, these likely mark the first commercial nuclear reactors to be restarted after being formally decommissioned, with rising demand for reliable and low-carbon electricity surging.
The first of three, Palisades Nuclear Plant in Michigan, closed in 2022 nine years before its license was due to expire due to its owner withdrawing from the nuclear power business. Electricity purchase agreements for the plan require it to return to service by March 2027, which is just half a year away.
Crane Clean Energy Center in Pennsylvania is also likely targeting a 2027 online date, with Duane Arnold Energy Center in Iowa looking for a 2029 go-live date.

"For anyone who wants zero carbon, nuclear provides that," nuclear engineering expert Todd Allen explained. "For the Trump administration, which really wants nuclear, this fits that story also."
This, of course, falls under Trump's nuclear plans – a May 2025 executive order revealed plans to quadruple US nuclear generating capacity from around 100GW in 2024 to 400GW by 2050.
Still, these latest plans aren't short of criticism, with concerns over the safety of aging reactors being floated, especially in a world of heightened geopolitical activity and natural disasters.

articles.title: Panne Orange et Sosh : une migration 5G aurait mal tourné, des abonnés retrouvent du réseau
articles.text:
Après plus de huit heures de perturbations, des abonnés Orange et Sosh signalent le retour du réseau ce mercredi 21 octobre. Une migration ratée vers un cœur de réseau 5G pourrait expliquer les coupures et la difficulté à rétablir les lignes.
Les connexions reviennent, mais l’explication officielle manque encore. En début de soirée, plusieurs lecteurs et lectrices de Clubic nous indiquent avoir retrouvé du réseau chez Orange comme chez Sosh. Nous constatons également le rétablissement d’une connexion Sosh, après les interruptions signalées depuis la fin de matinée. Ces retours interviennent alors qu’une piste plus précise apparaît sur l’origine de l’incident : une opération de migration des lignes aurait échoué dans les infrastructures de l’opérateur.
Une migration vers le cœur de réseau 5G aurait échoué
Selon les informations de Numerama, Orange aurait tenté ce mercredi matin de transférer une partie de ses abonnés vers un cœur de réseau 5G. L’opération aurait laissé les lignes concernées incapables de se connecter à l’ancien système comme au nouveau.
Le média rapproche ses informations de celles publiées sur X par Clément Domingo, alias SaxX. Celui-ci affirme, en invoquant une source interne, que les lignes migrées vers un nouveau cœur de réseau mobile seraient hors service. Il évoque une origine technique plutôt qu’un piratage.
Pour comprendre cette piste, il faut distinguer les antennes du système qui organise les connexions. Le cœur de réseau intervient notamment dans l’authentification des abonnés et la gestion de leurs communications. La 5G classique, dite NSA, s’appuie encore sur un cœur 4G ; la 5G autonome, dite SA, utilise un cœur dédié.
Un problème à ce niveau pourrait donc empêcher une ligne d’accéder aux services, même dans une zone habituellement bien couverte. Ce scénario reste toutefois à confirmer.
Des profils à resynchroniser et des connexions qui reviennent
D’après Numerama, le rétablissement nécessiterait de remettre en cohérence les profils des abonnés concernés : leur identité, leurs droits et les services associés à leur forfait. Cette opération devrait être menée progressivement, en évitant de provoquer une surcharge lors des reconnexions.
Cela fournirait une explication possible à la longueur de l’incident. Les témoignages de retour du réseau ne permettent cependant pas, à eux seuls, de confirmer ce mécanisme ni de mesurer l’avancement des réparations.
Vers 19 h 30, plusieurs lecteurs de Clubic nous signalent une amélioration sur leurs lignes Orange et Sosh. Ces observations constituent un changement concret depuis notre précédent point de situation, sans établir un rétablissement pour l’ensemble des clients.
Le réseau revient donc chez certains abonnés, tandis que le diagnostic définitif et la confirmation d’une résolution complète restent attendus.

articles.title: Tesla y SpaceX estudian una fusión por USD 3,5 billones, la mayor de la historia corporativa
articles.text:
El director ejecutivo de Tesla y SpaceX, Elon Musk, confirmó el martes que los directorios de ambas compañías formaron comités especiales para evaluar una fusión que crearía la empresa más valiosa de la historia corporativa, con un valor combinado cercano a los USD 3,5 billones.
Musk hizo el anuncio durante la presentación de resultados trimestrales de SpaceX. Los comités, integrados por directores independientes de cada empresa, se formaron a pedido de los accionistas y todavía no llegaron a un acuerdo sobre los términos de una eventual operación.
La posibilidad venía ganando fuerza entre analistas bursátiles: días antes, un informe de Barclays había anticipado que las compañías podrían anunciar la fusión antes de la junta de accionistas de Tesla, prevista para el 6 de diciembre. El martes (20 de octubre de 2026), Musk la confirmó por primera vez de forma directa.
“Es una especie de extraño baile kabuki, en el que dos grupos hablan y yo no puedo estar en la conversación”, dijo Musk, quien no integra ninguno de los comités por ser, según remarcó, una parte en conflicto al ser director ejecutivo y principal accionista individual de las dos firmas.
Según el valor de cierre de sus acciones el martes, SpaceX está valuada en unos USD 2 billones y Tesla en cerca de USD 1,5 billones. Juntas alcanzarían la mayor fusión corporativa jamás concretada.
Un obstáculo mayor del lado de Tesla
Musk explicó que, a diferencia de SpaceX, donde controla más de la mitad del poder de voto desde la salida a bolsa de la compañía en junio, en Tesla la operación necesitaría el respaldo de la mitad de la totalidad de las acciones en circulación, no solo de los votos emitidos.
“Es un obstáculo bastante alto de alcanzar”, admitió. Tesla presentó el lunes su informe anual para accionistas y no incluyó ninguna propuesta de fusión para votar, lo que indica que, de avanzar, el proceso recién estaría comenzando.
Las razones que esgrime Musk para combinarlas
Pese a las trabas, Musk se mostró a favor de unir las compañías. Dijo que hay “mucho mérito” en combinarlas porque, según planteó, la industria atraviesa el inicio de una “singularidad de superinteligencia”.
Ambas firmas, agregó, podrían ganar al cooperar en software de inteligencia artificial, diseño de chips y robótica. También señaló que ya se superponen en varios frentes, incluida la fabricación de semiconductores.
Esa relación no es nueva. En enero, Tesla invirtió unos USD 2.000 millones para adquirir una participación en la subsidiaria de inteligencia artificial de SpaceX, según informó NBC News.
El año pasado, Musk fusionó su red social X con xAI, la startup de IA que SpaceX terminó comprando y rebautizó SpaceXSI. Las versiones sobre una fusión mayor circulaban desde antes de que SpaceX debutara en bolsa con una oferta récord en junio.
Comités sin nombres propios, por ahora
Musk no reveló la integración de los comités, pero el informe que Tesla presentó el lunes ante los reguladores detalla que la automotriz cuenta con siete directores independientes, entre ellos la presidenta del directorio, Robyn Denholm, el excodirector de tecnología Jeffrey Straubel y James Murdoch.
SpaceX, por su parte, tiene seis directores independientes, incluido Ira Ehrenpreis, quien además preside los comités de compensación de las dos compañías. El anuncio llegó horas después de que SpaceX reportara una ganancia neta trimestral de USD 4.400 millones, muy por encima de los USD 1.880 millones que esperaban los analistas.
Los ingresos de su división de inteligencia artificial, llamada Super Intelligence, se multiplicaron por nueve respecto del año anterior y alcanzaron los USD 7.560 millones.
Los suscriptores de Starlink, el servicio de internet satelital de SpaceX, llegaron a 13,6 millones hacia fines del tercer trimestre, por debajo de lo que esperaban los analistas. Las acciones de Tesla y SpaceX subieron tras los comentarios de Musk, tanto en la rueda regular como en las operaciones posteriores al cierre del mercado en Nueva York.
Musk evitó dar un plazo para una eventual propuesta formal y pidió cautela: “Creo que algunas personas asumen que una fusión entre SpaceX y Tesla es un hecho, y creo que sería exagerar”, dijo. El resultado del trabajo de los comités deberá someterse después a votación de los accionistas de ambas empresas.

articles.title: LiteLLM Compromised in Supply Chain Attack Delivering Credential Stealer and Backdoor
articles.text:
The popular LiteLLM Python package has been compromised as part of a software supply chain attack that delivered a credential stealer and a backdoor, according to reports from SafeDep, Socket, StepSecurity, and Upwind.
The compromise affects LiteLLM 1.107.0, distributed through PyPI wheels and Docker images. The Python package has since been quarantined on Python Package Index (PyPI), and the malicious Docker images have been removed.
Oliver Jensen, director of security at LiteLLM, said an investigation into the incident is ongoing, and that it's still working to trace the original attack vector by which the threat actor published the malicious release.
"We have identified that the malicious actions were taken through three engineers' GitHub accounts, appearing to be by way of stolen GitHub CLI OAuth tokens," Jensen said. "The threat actor used one user's account to trigger the project-releaser run, and another user's account to approve it. All tokens which were involved in this attack have been revoked."
"We have not yet identified the mechanism by which the threat actor acquired the relevant tokens, so cannot yet assert that no further access to these GitHub accounts. As a temporary mitigation, we have removed all but one (unaffected) user from our GitHub organization."
Separately, LiteLLM said it has updated the public registries to remove any trusted links to its GitHub organization so as to prevent further publication of malicious packages.
Analysis of the malicious version shows that it's equipped to collect cloud credentials, private keys, browser data, and authentication files for AI development tools. The following wheels are affected -
- litellm-1.107.0-cp310-abi3-macosx_10_12_x86_64.whl
- litellm-1.107.0-cp310-abi3-macosx_11_0_arm64.whl
- litellm-1.107.0-cp310-abi3-manylinux_2_28_aarch64.whl
- litellm-1.107.0-cp310-abi3-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl
- litellm-1.107.0-cp310-abi3-musllinux_1_2_aarch64.whl
- litellm-1.107.0-cp310-abi3-musllinux_1_2_x86_64.whl
- litellm-1.107.0-cp310-abi3-win_amd64.whl
- litellm-1.107.0.tar.gz (No payload files, but has the tampered pyproject.toml)
"The first payload is a credential stealer that calls itself privcollect," StepSecurity said. "The second payload forks a background daemon that checks a GitHub dead drop every hour and runs whatever Python the attacker serves."
The malware is launched by Python even before LiteLLM is imported through a path file ("cook.pth"), which is designed to automatically execute code when the interpreter starts. It's worth noting that the same behavior was observed in the LiteLLM compromise that took place as part of the TeamPCP supply chain attacks earlier this March.
The "cook.pth" file contains a single line, "import cook," which, in turn, launches the credential collector payload. This includes harvesting cloud tokens, developer accounts and private keys, AI tooling credential JSON files, browser data associated with Chromium and Firefox, and environment variables.
The malware is also capable of targeting LiteLLM deployments with an aim to extract the proxy's saved credentials and model configuration. The collected data is packaged into a GZIP-compressed TAR archive and sent to "litellm[.]dev/healthcheck" by means of an HTTP POST request.
In addition, the malware is designed to read the contents of a text file ("domain.txt") located within a GitHub repository ("github[.]com/letters9813"), check if it holds a domain and, if so, run the same stealer, and finally run an HTTP GET request against "<domain>/codepy" and execute the response. The GitHub repository currently returns a 404 error.
Users who have downloaded the malicious version are advised to revoke and replace exposed credentials from a clean environment and pin version 1.106.2 by digest.

articles.title: Vos mots de passe sur tous vos appareils, sans abonnement : pCloud Pass passe à 119€ à vie
articles.text:
Ajouter un abonnement de plus pour ranger ses mots de passe n’enchante personne, et c’est tout l’argument de la licence à vie que pCloud met en promotion pour Halloween. Le pCloud Pass Premium passe à 119 € en paiement unique chez pCloud jusqu’au 25 octobre, 30 € sous son tarif habituel, pour un gestionnaire simple que nous notons 8/10 mais qui fait encore l’impasse sur les passkeys.
pCloud, le spécialiste suisse du stockage en ligne, propose depuis fin 2022 son propre gestionnaire de mots de passe. Jusqu’au 25 octobre, la licence à vie pCloud Pass Premium est vendue 119 € en un seul paiement, sans renouvellement. pCloud affiche un prix barré de 239 €, mais sa page de tarifs propose d’ordinaire la même licence à 149 € : l’économie réelle est de 30 €, pas de 120 €.
L’offre vise surtout ceux qui veulent quitter le gestionnaire intégré à leur navigateur sans ajouter une ligne à leurs prélèvements. La formule Family, partagée jusqu’à cinq personnes, descend dans le même temps à 199 €, contre 253 € en temps normal.
La licence à vie pCloud Pass Premium est à 119 € chez pCloud jusqu’au 25 octobre, contre 149 € habituellement sur sa page de tarifs.
Pourquoi choisir le pCloud Pass Premium ?
- Un seul paiement : Les 119 € réglés une fois remplacent l’abonnement à 29 € par an. La licence est amortie en un peu plus de quatre ans, sans frais ensuite.
- Tous vos appareils : Applications Windows, macOS, Linux, Android et iOS, extensions pour Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Brave et Opera, plus une version web. Le même coffre vous suit du PC au smartphone, sans limite d’appareils actifs.
- Une sécurité sans prise de tête : Les données sont protégées par un chiffrement AES 256 bits, et le coffre se déverrouille par Face ID ou empreinte digitale. Si vous oubliez le mot de passe maître, des mots de récupération et une confirmation par e-mail permettent de retrouver l’accès.
Du navigateur au smartphone, ce que change un vrai coffre-fort
Le premier usage est le plus simple : rapatrier les identifiants que votre navigateur conserve. pCloud Pass les importe depuis un fichier CSV, puis les remplit automatiquement sur les sites et dans les applications mobiles, via les réglages de saisie automatique d’Android et d’iOS. Le générateur crée un mot de passe unique pour chaque nouveau compte, et le coffre accueille aussi cartes bancaires et notes chiffrées. Dans notre avis complet sur pCloud Pass, nous saluons une prise en main aisée, y compris pour un débutant, avec une note de 8/10.
Le partage sécurisé, illimité en Premium, permet de transmettre un identifiant commun à un proche sans passer par un SMS ou un e-mail. Pour un couple ou une famille, la formule Family à 199 € couvre jusqu’à cinq membres, ce qui revient à moins de 40 € par personne. Le gestionnaire convient moins aux profils exigeants : il ne prévient pas en cas de fuite de vos identifiants et ne prend pas en charge les passkeys, ces clés d’accès qui remplacent peu à peu le mot de passe. Si vous n’utilisez qu’un seul appareil, la version gratuite peut suffire.
Face à Proton Pass et Bitwarden, un choix d’abord économique
pCloud Pass ne joue pas dans la même cour que les références du marché. Dans notre comparatif des meilleurs gestionnaires de mots de passe, il arrive septième sur sept, derrière Proton Pass et ses alias e-mail, ou Bitwarden et sa version gratuite généreuse. Son atout est ailleurs : un coût fixe, payé une fois, que nous recommandons aux petits budgets et à ceux qui préfèrent éviter un abonnement. Pour surveiller les fuites, mieux vaut regarder du côté de 1Password et de son outil Watchtower, ou de Dashlane et de ses alertes.
✅ Les points forts
- Paiement unique, sans abonnement ni renouvellement
- Appareils actifs et partages illimités
- Applications et extensions pour tous les systèmes courants
- Déverrouillage biométrique et récupération du compte
- Remboursement possible pendant 14 jours après l’achat
❌ Les limites
- Pas d’alerte en cas de fuite de vos identifiants
- Pas de prise en charge des passkeys
- Peu de fonctions avancées face aux leaders du marché
- Économie réelle de 30 €, loin des 120 € suggérés par le prix barré
Remboursable sous 14 jours, la licence pCloud Pass Premium à 119 € reste disponible jusqu’au 25 octobre, comme la formule Family à 199 €.
À 119 €, la licence à vie de pCloud Pass répond en partie au reproche que nous lui faisions : un paiement unique un peu élevé à 149 €. Face à l’abonnement annuel, elle s’amortit en un peu plus de quatre ans, et le gestionnaire couvre l’essentiel : remplissage automatique, partage, biométrie, tous les systèmes. Ceux qui gardent leurs outils longtemps et veulent sortir du gestionnaire de leur navigateur y trouveront un compromis honnête.
Les profils plus exigeants passeront leur chemin. Sans alerte de fuite ni passkeys, pCloud Pass reste un coffre-fort simple, pas un outil de sécurité complet. Avant de payer, la version gratuite permet d’en tester l’interface sur un appareil, et le remboursement sous 14 jours limite le risque si l’essai déçoit.

articles.title: Esoteric just launched a $45k / £38k SACD player with an optional $19k / £16.5k external power supply but OK, tell me offline listening isn't making a huge comeback
articles.text:
'A huge win for offline hi-res listening': SACD's are making a massive comeback and Esoteric's new $45k / £38k SACD player proves it
With great power comes great responsibility — to dig out your SACD stash
- Esoteric knows more of us are embracing CDs — and we'll love SACDs too
- Meet the elite K1XE SACD player and optional PS1XE external power supply
- How much is it? If you need to ask, I fear it's going to be too much…
We love to give practical buying advice about the latest tech products here on TechRadar. But sometimes what we love even more is to indulge in the most outrageously high-end, cutting-edge, luxurious propositions on the planet. That's what we bring you in these Money No Object columns — you can read the whole series here.
Well well well. We knew CD players were having a moment because we can't seem to stop writing about them — whether ultra-luxe, super-fresh and with aptX Bluetooth, be they hefty and toting both analog and digital inputs, fully transparent like some sort of award, inspired by Death Stranding 2: On the Beach in neon orange or even an affordable little ripper, from FiiO.
So there's a CD player for everyone in 2026. TechRadar even published a roundup of 9 of the coolest new CD player releases not six weeks ago, in an effort to stay abreast of them all.
And now, there's an option for people in possession of an awful lot of money. And why not? It's your money and if you have a collection of SACDs you want to make use of, along with a sizeable chunk of cash to invest into the experience, you should be able to do so.
What am I talking about when I say 'SACD'? These delicate little beauties are shiny and circular just like your regular CDs, but the moniker stands for 'Super Audio Compact Disc'. It's a high-resolution optical audio disc format first introduced in 1999 and developed jointly by Sony and Philips Electronics. Unlike CDs, the format uses a 1-bit resolution with a sampling rate of 2.8224 MHz, also known as DSD64, to provide a data rate of 5.6 Mbps — and that walks all over your typical CD's 16-bit/44.1kHz resolution, or a data rate of 1.411 Mbps, in the hi-res audio stakes.
So, it makes sense to get a serious player for your seriously detailed recorded music, right? That's clearly what Esoteric was thinking too. Behold: the ultra-luxe K1XE SACD player. You may see it as an outrageously high-end player, for a format many people thought was largely done and gone. I call it a huge win for offline hi-res listening.
How many of us still dig SACDs? I'd say the number is growing…
Anyway, what you're looking at in the main image (and the one above) is the Esoteric Grandioso K1XE, the ultra-luxury Japanese audio specialist's new flagship Super Audio CD player.
It features the VRDSATLAS (try saying that out loud, or writing it out several times in a news piece), Esoteric’s proprietary SACD transport mechanism, featuring an "exceptionally rigid, heavyweight platform engineered for outstanding mechanical precision". Also inbuilt is the proprietary Master Sound Discrete DAC G2, a next-generation, discrete digital-analog converter developed entirely in-house by Esoteric.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The K1XE is a fully dual-mono DAC configuration. Esoteric explains that this "large scale" architecture incorporates five independent linear power supply systems to achieve what the company calls "full-bodied sound reminiscent of vinyl playback".
OK but what's the thing on the right, in the main image above? That's the Grandioso PS1XE, an also-new optional external power supply — because you want to power this player properly, don't you? Doing so will reduce electrical interference, lower the noise floor for cleaner SACD sound, move high-voltage AC and heat a sensible way away from those sensitive audio circuits, including that beautifully rigid, hefty transport.
Both products will be available for international shipment from the beginning of November 2026. And it's worth considering shipping costs too (although if you're bothered by those, it's probably a little rich for the blood) because the K1XE alone weighs 34.3kg / 75lbs, which is roughly the weight of a large adult dog — think German Shepherd or Golden Retriever.
Will this glorious beast still play your regular CDs? Almost certainly. Esoteric hasn't confirmed this in its marketing, but practically all SACD players are fully backwards-compatible and are able to read the standard Red Book CD layer of an audio CD (sometimes called a CD-DA) without issue.
And that's important, because CD sales revenue was up 58% in the opening six months of 2026 (and 45% in volume) in the US, according to the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). Also, the burgeoning popularity of newer portable CD players (along with the growing trend for wired earbuds that do away with streaming and generally being online) proves that music lovers are buying new, pristine CDs alongside inheriting caches of old (possibly scratched) collections. And isn't listening to a full concept album in superior quality one of life's great pleasures?
Let's tackle pricing: both The Grandioso K1XE and PS1XE will be available worldwide starting November 2026. And I'm just going to write it quickly: the Esoteric Grandioso K1XE SACD player has an MSRP of US $45,000 / £37,999 (or around AU$72, 399). The PS-1XE external power supply is priced at $19,000 / £16,500 (approximately AU$36,199).
Just imagine how good those SACDs are going to sound though…

Becky became Audio Editor at TechRadar in 2024, but joined the team in 2022 as Senior Staff Writer, focusing on all things hi-fi. Before this, she spent three years at What Hi-Fi? testing and reviewing everything from wallet-friendly wireless earbuds to huge high-end sound systems. Prior to gaining her MA in Journalism in 2018, Becky freelanced as an arts critic alongside a 22-year career as a professional dancer and aerialist – any love of dance starts with a love of music. Becky has previously contributed to Stuff, FourFourTwo and The Stage. When not writing, she can still be found throwing shapes in a dance studio, these days with varying degrees of success.

articles.title: Cuáles son los tipos de empleados que “sobrevivirán” a la IA: Alex Karp, director ejecutivo de Palantir
articles.text:
Alex Karp, director ejecutivo de Palantir, afirmó que solo existen dos tipos de personas con futuro garantizado frente al avance de la inteligencia artificial: quienes tienen formación vocacional y quienes son neurodivergentes.
La frase, pronunciada en el programa TBPN, surge en medio de advertencias cada vez más frecuentes sobre el impacto de la IA en el mercado laboral, con cifras que hablan de decenas de millones de puestos en riesgo en Estados Unidos durante la próxima década.
Cuáles son los tipos de empleados que ‘sobrevivirán’ a la IA
“Hay básicamente dos formas de saber que tienes futuro”, sostuvo el empresario de 58 años. “Una, tienes algún tipo de formación vocacional, o dos, eres neurodivergente”.
La declaración, reproducida originalmente por Fortune, se dio en un momento de creciente ansiedad laboral. Un informe del Senado de Estados Unidos de octubre de 2025 estimó que las tecnologías emergentes “podrían destruir casi 100 millones de empleos en Estados Unidos en una década”, según Newsweek.
El mismo documento advirtió que “el trabajo artificial no solo podría dejar sin empleo a millones de personas en sus puestos actuales. También podría reemplazar nuevos empleos que podrían haberse creado”, lo que deja abierta la incertidumbre sobre la velocidad con la que surgirán oportunidades alternativas.
Un análisis de Anthropic citado por Newsweek matizó el panorama: la inteligencia artificial estaría alcanzando apenas “una fracción” de su potencial de uso, lo que sugiere que buena parte de la disrupción todavía no ocurrió.
Karp, quien habló abiertamente de su propia dislexia, sostiene que los oficios que exigen presencia física y destreza manual resultan mucho más difíciles de automatizar. Un electricista, un plomero o un soldador certificado no compiten con un modelo de lenguaje.
La experta en carreras de Monster, Vicki Salemi, calificó a este tipo de oficios como “a prueba de IA”, según recogió CNBC. En la misma línea, el científico Geoffrey Hinton, conocido como el “padrino de la IA”, sugirió en el podcast The Diary Of A CEO que convertirse en plomero podría ser una alternativa viable, porque la tecnología está mejor equipada para reemplazar el “trabajo intelectual rutinario”.
El segundo grupo que menciona Karp son las personas neurodivergentes. Según el empresario, estos perfiles suelen desarrollar formas de pensamiento no lineales que les permiten encontrar soluciones y aportar valor que la inteligencia artificial no logra replicar.
Por qué la clase profesional queda más expuesta
Lo que Karp no mencionó también generó lectura: el perfil que queda fuera de sus dos categorías es el trabajador de cuello blanco con título universitario. El analista, el abogado junior, el gerente de marketing de nivel medio.
Un análisis posterior sobre sus declaraciones planteó que la IA ya puede redactar contratos, resumir investigaciones, escribir código funcional y generar modelos financieros, pero ningún sistema puede destapar una cañería ni reemplazar una viga de carga.
Ese razonamiento introduce el concepto de “irreductibilidad”: serían más seguros los trabajos que no pueden abstraerse ni reducirse a tareas repetibles a costo casi nulo, ya sea porque dependen de presencia física o porque requieren un patrón de pensamiento distinto al convencional.
Bajo esa lógica, los oficios técnicos no solo serían empleos seguros, sino “empleos que se revalorizan”, en la medida en que la brecha entre la oferta de trabajadores calificados y la demanda de infraestructura física se amplía cada año.
El senador Bernie Sanders advirtió en un video difundido en YouTube que “la inteligencia artificial y la robótica que están desarrollando estos multimillonarios permitirán a las corporaciones estadounidenses eliminar decenas de millones de empleos con salarios dignos”, según reprodujo Newsweek.
El empresario Andrew Yang coincidió en el diagnóstico de fondo. “No creo que se esté prestando suficiente atención a las distintas desventajas del avance de la IA, desde el reemplazo de empleos hasta la fragmentación de la realidad y el robo de identidad generalizado”, dijo a Newsweek.

articles.title: Failles PHP : les correctifs sont disponibles, mais votre hébergeur protège-t-il vraiment votre site ?
articles.text:
Les correctifs des deux failles critiques de PHP sont disponibles depuis ce mercredi après-midi, alors que des tentatives d'exploitation sont déjà observées. Mais sont-ils réellement installés chez les hébergeurs ? Nos vérifications chez o2switch montrent que des protections provisoires ont été appliquées, sans que les nouvelles versions du langage soient encore déployées.
Les deux vulnérabilités critiques de PHP, référencées CVE-2026-109618 et CVE-2026-109619, ont fait l'objet de correctifs d'urgence ce 21 octobre. Elles peuvent permettre l'exécution de code à distance sans authentification, dans certaines configurations de serveur.
L'urgence n'a rien de théorique : la société de cybersécurité watchTowr affirme avoir observé des tentatives d'exploitation sur son réseau mondial de leurres, tandis que Cloudflare confirme avoir détecté du trafic d'attaque. Ces observations ne démontrent toutefois pas, à elles seules, que des sites ont été compromis avec succès.
Derrière ces vulnérabilités se cache d'ailleurs une histoire étonnante : certaines faiblesses de PHP existaient depuis des années, avant que des chercheurs épaulés par l'intelligence artificielle ne parviennent à en démontrer l'exploitation. À lire sur Clubic 👇
Chez o2switch, nous avons vérifié les protections réellement appliquées
Pour comprendre ce qui se passe concrètement chez les hébergeurs, nous avons effectué nos propres vérifications sur deux comptes o2switch que nous administrons, hébergés sur un même serveur mutualisé. À 16 h 40, les binaires PHP installés dataient toujours du 6 octobre : notamment PHP 8.3.35 et 8.4.26, alors que les versions corrigées 8.3.36 et 8.4.27 venaient d'être publiées.
L'hébergeur avait néanmoins anticipé l'alerte. L'horodatage des fichiers de configuration php.ini indique une intervention dès 8 h 07 pour désactiver la fonctionnalité session.upload_progress. Les processus PHP avaient également été redémarrés après cette modification.
Interrogé par l'intermédiaire de son support technique, o2switch nous a répondu à 17 h 30 :
Dès que les correctifs adaptés à notre infrastructure seront disponibles et validés, nous procéderons à leur déploiement dans les meilleurs délais.
L'hébergeur s'appuie notamment sur CloudLinux, qui annonçait en fin d'après-midi préparer ses paquets corrigés, avec une publication prévue dans la soirée. Le fournisseur travaille également sur des correctifs rétroportés pour les anciennes branches PHP, jusqu'à la version 5.2.
D'autres acteurs ont pris les devants. OVHcloud confirme avoir déployé des règles WAF sur ses clusters et engagé une campagne de maintenance. SiteGround affirme avoir appliqué des protections sur l'ensemble de ses serveurs avant la sortie des correctifs. De son côté, Cloudflare indique protéger par défaut ses clients utilisant son pare-feu applicatif, y compris dans sa formule gratuite.
Ces mesures ne sont toutefois pas équivalentes à une correction complète. Comme le rappelle le CERT-FR, la désactivation de session.upload_progress ne réduit la surface d'attaque que pour l'une des deux vulnérabilités.
Changer de version PHP ne suffit pas toujours
Nos vérifications ont également révélé une difficulté moins visible. Sur l’un de nos comptes, un site WordPress était resté sous PHP 8.1, une branche dont le support officiel a pris fin. Une situation loin d’être isolée : selon Mallory, près de 59 % des serveurs exposés qui affichent leur version utilisent encore PHP 8.1 ou une version antérieure. Des correctifs sous forme de code source existent néanmoins pour cette branche, et des fournisseurs comme CloudLinux préparent leurs propres adaptations.
Pourquoi tant de sites restent-ils sur d’anciennes versions ? Souvent parce qu’une migration qui paraît simple ne l’est pas toujours. Depuis l’interface d’un hébergeur, passer à PHP 8.3 se fait en quelques clics. En préparant la migration de ce site vers PHP 8.3, nous avons constaté que 34 modules étaient activés pour cette version, contre 66 pour PHP 8.1. Plusieurs composants nécessaires au site et à ses extensions, comme mbstring, gd ou intl, devaient être réactivés avant toute migration, sous peine de provoquer des dysfonctionnements.
Autre subtilité : la version PHP affichée en ligne de commande n’est pas nécessairement celle qui exécute le site. Et un numéro de version ancien ne signifie pas systématiquement qu’un serveur reste vulnérable, puisque certains fournisseurs intègrent les correctifs sans le modifier.
Pour les propriétaires de sites, la priorité est donc de consulter les communications de leur hébergeur et de s’assurer que les correctifs sont effectivement appliqués. Ceux qui doivent changer de branche PHP ont tout intérêt à vérifier les modules activés pour la nouvelle version et à réaliser une sauvegarde avant toute migration.
L’enjeu des prochaines heures sera de passer des protections provisoires aux corrections définitives. Chez o2switch comme ailleurs, la publication des correctifs par PHP ou CloudLinux ne suffit pas : encore faut-il qu’ils soient installés et que les processus Web utilisent réellement les versions corrigées.

articles.title: OpenAI's GPT-6 Agent Removed Safety Monitoring, Then Falsely Denied Doing So
articles.text:
OpenAI has revealed that two artificial intelligence (AI) agents powered by GPT-6.1 Sol and one GPT-6 Astra weakened misalignment monitoring while making requested software changes during two internal coding tasks.
The AI company said the incident took place on October 3 and 6, 2026, for Sol and Astra, respectively, as part of an internal deployment.
"A GPT-6.1 Sol agent repairing an evaluation pipeline disabled automatic alerts to our Security team, treating an earlier instruction not to send messages during a Slack history search as a reason to suppress monitoring notifications," OpenAI said in a report.
The end result of this action was that the misalignment monitor still ran and saved its reports, but automatic human alerts were disabled by setting "no_notify" to true and emptying the lists of people configured to receive monitoring reports.
In another task on October 6, a GPT-6 Astra agent migrating a program is said to have removed its monitoring integration in order to match a reference implementation, and then falsely claimed to the user that the functionality had not been removed.
"No [...] I did not remove an enabled monitor from it," the final response from the agent reads.
OpenAI said, in both cases, the AI agents considered whether monitoring safeguards should be retained, but ultimately chose not to do so after interpreting routine coding instructions as "permission to weaken them."
In response to the findings, the company said it's strengthening its misalignment monitoring system and assessing if these scenarios are an outlier or whether they demonstrate a propensity to evade misalignment monitoring.
"In addition to making it harder for models to disable monitoring [during evaluations], we are looking to understand why models might seek to do so in the first place," OpenAI said. "It is possible that this behavior is simply an example of 'benign' overpersistence, with models not understanding why monitoring is important or insisting that instructions be executed beyond what a reasonable person might expect."
The disclosure is the latest instance of AI agents acting in ways their developers did not intend to. Last week, the ChatGPT-maker disclosed seven misalignment incidents, including one case where an internal research model stole cryptocurrency from a wallet it did not own to pay the fees needed to deploy smart contracts on Ethereum's Sepolia test network and failed to report that it took the funds without permission.
Microsoft Targets Rogue AI Agents With Dynamic Permissions, Risk Score
It also comes amid growing concerns that the development of increasingly powerful AI systems is outpacing safety efforts, leading to warnings that this could make it harder to monitor and control them as they gain greater autonomy.
Earlier this week, Microsoft announced new controls to monitor and contain potentially rogue AI agents in enterprise environments as part of Project Perception, a continuously learning AI-powered cyber defense system the company unveiled in July 2026.
"Models have been trained to attain results, which often leads to reward hacking, and models are not optimized around organizational norms or judgment," Hayete Gallot, executive vice president of Microsoft Security, said. "Agents are unpredictable. They will adapt as the context changes, may not behave as intended, and will collaborate and collude with other agents to reach their objectives, without needing to be compromised."
With agents often having extensive permissions to access data, tools, and systems, not to mention take actions and make decisions on their own, Redmond said they pose a new kind of insider security risk that requires continuous monitoring.
To that end, Microsoft's Project Perception employs Guardian Agents to supervise other AI agents and secure them across identity, permissions, data, endpoints, network, cloud, and runtime layers by -
- Discovering and identifying every agent.
- Limiting their permissions using the principle of least privilege (PoLP) before execution and then dynamically grant or revoke access based on the task at hand.
- Monitoring the agent's actions and checking if it's straying from its original task.
- Adapting protections as behavior, context, and risk change.
The system is architected on the foundations of three new themes -
- Dynamic Permissions, which scopes the permissions to the task assigned to the agent and makes it time-bound.
- Dynamic Agent Risk, which assigns each agent a risk score that is continuously updated and draws from how securely it's configured, what resources it can reach, the potential impact if something goes wrong, and whether its actions are deviating from the user's or organization's intent.
- Dynamic Conditional Access, which extends Entra Conditional Access for agents so that permissions can be adjusted when there is a change in risk.
"Its identity, runtime, access paths, and task-scoped authority should be explicit from the start," Microsoft said. "If it later encounters a prompt injection or attempts an action outside that task, the system should respond proportionately: preserve safe reads while blocking writes, narrow the resources it can reach, require provable human approval for a consequential step, or isolate and stop the agent when the risk warrants it."

articles.title: Nvidia’s DGX Spark has a match from Dell, minus the markup
articles.text:
Dell put Nvidia DGX Spark silicon into its Pro Precision workstation — and undercut it by $1,000
The Nvidia DGX Spark rival delivers the same silicon with bigger savings
Prices for the highly coveted Nvidia DGX Spark mini PC are wallet-squeezing right now. Direct from Nvidia, the Mac mini-sized supercomputer is $6,950, and elsewhere, prices are massively inflated by third-party resellers (there's one for almost 10Gs at Newegg, and another for $9K at Best Buy). But there is a cheaper way to get the same level of performance without the extra cost.
Currently, the Dell Pro Precision with GB10 is listed at $5,903 at Dell. The SFF machine runs Nvidia DGX OS 7 on the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip with 128GB LPDDR5x, up to 8533 MT/s, and 2TB SSD storage. You can even shave a little extra off that cost, too, by opting for 1TB SSD configuration for $5,523.
• Best for: AI engineers running larger local AI models.
• Why we like it: Running the same chip and memory as Nvidia's machine, Dell's Pro Precision is a much better price than the DGX Spark, which is fast becoming like gold-dust on the market.
The Dell Pro Precision is equipped with the GB10 superchip, which is also found in Nvidia's DGX Spark PC. This CPU/GPU hybrid delivers high-performance for larger AI models thanks to the 128GB onboard RAM. As always with Dell, it's configurable, with 1TB, 2TB, and 4TB storage capacities. Save an extra $53 by removing the Dell keyboard and mouse when configuring.
Why we recommend it
Although we've had excellent experiences with Dell desktops in the past, price is the primary driver for highlighting this machine. You're saving over a thousand bucks compared to Nvidia's DGX Spark.
The chip itself combines an Arm-based CPU with a Blackwell GPU, paired with a massive 128GB memory for AI-oriented tasks. For local AI inferencing and development, it has exactly the right specs.
Value verdict
Compared to the Nvidia DGX Spark, which boasts the same specs as Dell's mini PC, you're making a significant saving of $1,047. I'd ignore the inflated prices from third-party sellers - for me, the decision is really, choosing whether to buy what amounts to the same machine from Dell or get the original from Nvidia.
I'd recommend the 1TB or 2TB configurations and offload additional files to an external drive. The 4TB model adds an outlandish $2,830 to the price tag over the base model.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Dell Pro Precision with GB10 if...
You plan to run large AI models locally - it's where this Grace Blackwell chip excels.
❌ Skip the Dell Pro Precision with GB10 if...
You want a general high-performance machine for non-AI tasks, or you'd prefer the official Nvidia SFF.
