articles.title: Attackers Abuse UpdraftCentral Keys to Plant Backdoors on WordPress Sites
articles.text:
Unknown threat actors breached TeamUpdraft's website and potentially gained unauthorized access to customers' connection keys for UpdraftCentral, UpdraftVault, and UpdraftClone, using them to backdoor WordPress sites.
TeamUpdraft is the developer behind UpdraftPlus, a popular WordPress backup plugin with over four million active installations. The vendor also offers UpdraftCentral, a remote management service that's used for managing multiple sites remotely. A client component of UpdraftCentral is shipped within every copy of UpdraftPlus.
"Over the weekend of 17-18 October we identified unauthorized access to the teamupdraft.com website," TeamUpdraft said in a statement. "Our team responded straight away and worked through the night to contain it – we closed the access route, signed out every account and replaced the keys and credentials that could have been affected."
As a result of the incident, threat actors are believed to have accessed its customer database, which holds the following information -
- Names, email addresses, billing addresses and order history
- Account passwords, stored only in hashed (scrambled) form and never in plain text
- Two-factor authentication (2FA) settings
- Connection keys for UpdraftCentral, UpdraftVault and UpdraftClone
TeamUpdraft said the database does not hold any financial information, and that they are handled by Stripe and PayPal. It also emphasized that the UpdraftPlus plugin, along with self-hosted versions of UpdraftCentral and backups sent to customers' own remote storage, are not impacted.
"However, if your site was accessed through UpdraftCentral, please also re-authorise your remote storage and change any storage access keys, as a precaution," it said.
In addition, TeamUpdraft said it deployed a fix to address the underlying issue, signed out every teamupdraft.com account and reset login security across the site, and released UpdraftPlus 1.26.13 (free) and 2.26.13 (Premium) to automatically disconnect every UpdraftCentral connection made before 10 p.m. BST on October 18, 2026, to prevent the old keys from working.
Other steps taken by the developer are listed below -
- Disconnected every site from UpdraftVault and issued new credentials
- Replaced every UpdraftClone client key
- Rotated its keys with payment providers and other connected services
- Implemented additional monitoring in place
- Reported the incident to the U.K. Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) and other relevant authorities
Users who have a teamupdraft.com account are advised to change their password with immediate effect (and elsewhere, if the same password has been reused), reset 2FA settings, and exercise caution when receiving unexpected emails claiming to be from TeamUpdraft.
TeamUpdraft is also recommending that cloud customers of UpdraftCentral follow the steps below as soon as possible, since the connection keys can send commands to the connected sites -
- Log in to the site's own WordPress dashboard, not through UpdraftCentral.
- Update UpdraftPlus to version 1.26.12 (free) or 2.26.12 (Premium) or later.
- Disconnect it from UpdraftCentral: go to Settings > UpdraftPlus > Advanced Tools > UpdraftCentral and delete the connection key.
- Go to Users and check for any administrator accounts you don’t recognise. Remove them.
- Go to Plugins, including the Must-Use tab if you can see it, and check for anything you don’t recognise. Remove it.
- Change the passwords for all administrator accounts on the site.
- If you find anything suspicious, consider restoring the site from a backup taken before 17 October.
- Reconnect the site to UpdraftCentral.
UpdraftVault users are being urged to reconnect their sites to the backup service, and UpdraftClone users who have created a client key are required to copy the new keys from My Account > UpdraftClone > UpdraftClone Key Management and share them with their clients.
The development comes as WordPress security company Patchstack said it observed an attacker holding valid UpdraftCentral dashboard keys issuing commands to install backdoor plugins on connected WordPress sites. The campaign is said to have run continuously through an 18-hour window on October 18 and 19, 2026.
"The attacker sends a signed plugin.upload_plugin command over the plugin's remote procedure call channel, which listens on ordinary POST requests to the site root. WordPress installs and activates the supplied plugin through its standard installer," Patchstack security researcher Dave Jong said.
Slovakia-based penetration testing company Nethemba, which first detected the attack in the wild, has described the rogue plugin as a backdoor that hooks into every request to the site to check if the URL contains the parameter "?_9f5696=" and compares it with a 32-character token.
If a matching token is detected, it creates a user "data-ops43" with the display name "Site Tools," assigns it the Editor role, and grants the account "manage_options" and "install_plugins" permissions, allowing the operator to upload arbitrary PHP plugins and open site settings.
"Enabling registration and setting the default role to administrator is enough for the attacker to create a full administrator," Nethemba said. "On a standard WordPress site, an Editor also has unfiltered_html, so the account can put JavaScript into posts that runs in the browser of every administrator."
"The backdoor has a second layer as well. The account it creates, with a known password, stays in WordPress even after the plugin is removed, and the attacker can log in with it through the normal login form unless two-factor authentication is enabled for that account."
Although an early version of the plugin suffered from a coding error that causes impacted sites to fail with error 500, Nethemba said the threat actor deleted the broken backdoor by sending a "plugin.delete_plugin" command and then uploaded a working version that creates a full administrator account or logs in as an existing administrator.
WordPress site owners are advised to check for the following indicators of compromise -
- Plugin names: Site Health Cache or Site Health 364F, Asset Forge 2, Content Helper, Wp Forge, Query Shelf, Style Bridge 8F5, Media Kit 183, Query Shelf, Post Dock 776, Nav Hub, Speed Desk, Speed Kit 300, Link Latch, Script Shelf, or Feed Case
- Account names: system_team850, web.tech988, cmseditor170, cms.tech644 or web_mgr684, with an email at @example.com and a display name such as System Team, Web Tech, System Staff, System Ops, or Cms Tech
- IP addresses: 43.250.53.42 and 2a09:bac5:4e21:2e3c::49b:9
In all, Patchstack said it observed 99 distinct backdoor plugin names, with each sample carrying the line "Small maintenance toolkit: keeps option storage tidy."
Wordfence, which published its own analysis of the incident, said a WordPress site may be affected if the below criteria are satisfied -
- The site had UpdraftPlus Free or UpdraftPlus Premium installed and active while the affected UpdraftCentral connection key was present.
- The site has, or had during the incident, an active connection key for TeamUpdraft’s cloud-hosted UpdraftCentral service.
"This is the second incident in this channel in five months," Patchstack warned. "In June 2026 the vendor fixed CVE-2026-10795 (CVSS 8.1), where an obsolete unsigned message format let an attacker forge UpdraftCentral commands with no keys at all. That was fixed in 1.26.5 and 2.26.5, but exploitation attempts continue, so sites below those versions face both problems at once."
The development comes days after the website of the Rank Math PRO WordPress plugin was hit by a software supply chain attack, causing users who downloaded version 3.0.123 between October 15 at 8:02 p.m. UTC and October 16 at 7:12 a.m. UTC to receive compromised versions that planted hidden backdoors.
The incident has been assigned the CVE identifier CVE-2026-111862 (CVSS score: 9.8). The issue was fixed in Rank Math PRO version 3.0.124.
"The malware may establish persistent access, communicate with rank1cdn[.]com, recreate hidden backdoors on page visits, and expose WordPress credentials, database credentials, API keys, and other secrets accessible to the web server," Wordefence said.
The findings also coincide with an advisory from PHP, which said it intends to ship a security release that fixes two critical vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, CVSS scores: 9.2), as information about the flaws leaked ahead of their scheduled disclosure. The flaws have been codenamed PHP2Shell.
According to watchTowr CEO Benjamin Harris, the vulnerabilities affect PHP versions 5, 6, 7, and 8, and were originally due for release on October 22 at 11 a.m. ET.
"PHP is everywhere. It quietly powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood," Huntress said. "When a critical bug lands in PHP itself, rather than in one app built on top of it, the number of places you have to go looking to identify vulnerable PHP versions gets very big, very fast."

articles.title: 'We intentionally forgot what it was like in our previous games and started from scratch' — Stranger Than Heaven director says RGG knew from the beginning 'that we wanted to make this experience different' from the Like A Dragon series
articles.text:
Stranger Than Heaven director says RGG 'intentionally' forgot about Yakuza to create 'something new' — 'Every single aspect of it, we started thinking about it from scratch, just to suit the style of Stranger Than Heaven'
"There was no conversation whatsoever about what Yakuza or Like A Dragon was like"
- Stranger Than Heaven director Mikinobu Abe says the game was always going to be different from the Yakuza or Like A Dragon games
- Abe says, "There was no conversation whatsoever about what Yakuza or Like A Dragon was like"
- He adds that RGG Studios "never compared" Stranger Than Heaven to its past titles, so it became "something new"
Stranger Than Heaven director Mikinobu Abe has explained why the upcoming role-playing action game was developed as a completely new experience from RGG Studio's Yakuza franchise.
In an interview with TechRadar Gaming, Abe said approaching Stranger Than Heaven was "a big task" and a "huge challenge for us," but knew "from the very beginning that we wanted to make this experience different from the previous games."
Unlike the Like a Dragon games, which typically take place in one location and timeframe, Stranger Than Heaven shifts to a historical timeline by telling a story across five distinct eras and cities spanning 50 years.
It's an ambitious decision for RGG, but Abe said the team intentionally forgot everything it knew from making the Yakuza series to create something new.
"While we were developing Stranger Than Heaven, there was no conversation whatsoever about what Yakuza or Like A Dragon was like," Abe said. "We intentionally forgot what it was like in our previous games and started from scratch. We were doubting every single pixel of what we had in Yakuza."
This included everything from the game's map, the UI, and how RGG wanted to approach the world; Abe said it even applied to the narrative and cutscenes, and the team "never compared" Stranger Than Heaven to its past titles.
"Every single aspect of it, we started thinking about it from scratch, just to suit the style of Stranger Than Heaven," he added. "We were never trying to make this different because we never compared it with our previous games, so in the end, it became something new."

articles.title: À l'approche de GTA VI, cet écran OLED de 27 pouces perd 150€ sur Amazon
articles.text:
Le LG UltraGear GX7 est un écran qui brille par sa dalle OLED de 27 pouces dotée d’un anti-reflet pour pouvoir jouer à tout moment de la journée. Pour le trouver à prix réduit, direction Amazon où il passe sous les 700 euros.
Dans quelques semaines, GTA VI sortira enfin. Pour en profiter dans les meilleures conditions, il est peut-être temps d’apporter un coup de frais sur votre set-up en changeant d’écran. Dans ce cas, pourquoi ne pas partir sur le LG UltraGear GX7 qui s’offre un Dual Mode pour s’adapter à tous les styles de jeu et une réduction de 18 % sur Amazon.
Sur Amazon, le LG UltraGear GX7 passe de 849,99 euros à 699,99 euros
Pourquoi choisir le LG UltraGear OLED GX7 ?
- Pour le Dual Mode : Les gamers compétitifs apprécieront de jouer en 720 Hz tandis que les fans de jeux contemplatifs pourront se reposer sur une image en QHD avec un taux de rafraîchissement de 540 Hz
- Des PC à la console : À l’arrière, l’écran embarque deux ports HDMI 2.1 et un DisplayPort pour y connecter simultanément une console récente et un PC.
- La qualité de l’OLED : Pour des noirs plus profonds et des contrastes sublimés, cet écran embarque l'OLED et dispose du HDR True Black 500
Un écran à l’usage polyvalent
À l’arrière de cet écran, on retrouve deux ports HDMI 2.1 et un DisplayPort 1.4. Malheureusement, il n’y a pas de port USB-C, mais cela ne vous empêchera pas de connecter une PlayStation 5, une Xbox Series S/X et un PC. Vous l’aurez compris, cet écran ne se destine pas qu’à un usage professionnel, mais il vise les gamers et surtout eux.
Ce LG UltraGear GX7 possède un écran OLED de 27 pouces, mais ce qui va intéresser les gamers, c’est ce Dual Mode. Les joueurs compétitifs pourront jouer en HD avec un taux de rafraîchissement de 720 Hz. Pour une expérience encore plus fluide, l’écran est compatible avec l’AMD FreeSync et le NVIDIA G-Sync pour limiter les déchirures d’écran.
Les joueurs qui préfèrent les jeux solo contemplatifs partiront plutôt sur la seconde partie de ce Dual Mode. L'écran disposera alors d’un taux de rafraîchissement de 540 Hz, mais d’une image en QHD, soit une résolution de 2 560 x 1 440 pixels.
Un prix avantageux pour défier la concurrence
Si la connectique de cet écran est réussie, son design n’est pas parfait pour autant puisque ce LG UltraGear GX7 va prendre de la place sur votre bureau à cause de son pied. S’il n'est pas épais, il est assez volumineux, mais il présente l’avantage d’être plat, vous pourrez poser divers objets dessus pour maximiser l’espace. Pour rester sur le pied, sachez que vous pouvez l’incliner et ajuster sa hauteur
Enfin, son dernier argument reste le prix. À 850 euros, il peine à être visible parmi les nombreux écrans OLED, mais en chutant sous les 700 euros, il devient plus intéressant puisqu’il se retrouve avec, par exemple, des Samsung Odyssey sortis il y a déjà plusieurs années. Ici, il se démarque donc grâce à sa connectique puisque les concurrents sur cette tranche tarifaire se contentent généralement d’un seul port HDMI 2.1.
✅ Les points forts
- Une dalle OLED de 27 pouces avec la présence d’un Dual Mode
- Un DisplayPort et deux ports HDMI 2.1
- Le NVIDIA G-Sync et l’AMD FreeSync
❌ Les limites
- Le pied est assez imposant
- Un seul DisplayPort et pas de port USB-C
Grâce à Amazon, le LG UltraGear GX7 ne vaut plus 849,99 euros, mais 699,99 euros
Le LG UltraGear GX7 est donc un écran parfait pour les gamers, peu importe qu’ils préfèrent les jeux solo ou les jeux compétitifs. Le Dual Mode fera le bonheur de tous. Son principal défaut reste l’absence d’un port USB-C, mais les deux ports HDMI et le DisplayPort suffiront dans la plupart des configurations.

articles.title: El sube y baja de ethereum: cuál es su costo este 21 de octubre
articles.text:
Ethereum es una plataforma digital que adopta la tecnología de cadena de bloques (blockchain) y expande su uso a una gran variedad de aplicaciones, mientras que ether es su criptomoneda nativa. En el mundo de las finanzas digitales es común que la criptomoneda sea llamada como la red, aunque en realidad no son lo mismo.
La plataforma ethereum, creada en el 2015 por el programador Vitalik Buterin, buscaba ser un instrumento para aplicaciones descentralizadas y colaborativas sobre las que se pueden hacer contratos inteligentes (dAPPs)
Al igual que el bitcoin, el valor de ether se disparó en un corto periodo de tiempo. En enero de 2016, ether cotizaba alrededor de un dólar y actualmente tiene un máximo histórico de 4.953,73 dólares.
La cotización de ethereum para este día a las 14:05 horas (UTC) es de 2470.61 dólares, lo que significa que la criptomoneda registró un cambio de 3.5 % en las últimas 24 horas.
Por otro lado, registró un cambio de 0.0 % con respecto a su valor hace una hora. En cuanto a su popularidad, se ubica en la posición #2.
Cotización de la criptomoneda Ethereum
La nueva era de Ether
Tras varios meses de retraso y con el temor de que ya nunca pasaría, finalmente el 15 de septiembre de 2022 Ethereum llevó a cabo su tan ansiada fusión o actualización al nuevo nivel 2.0 con la promesa de mejorar la experiencia de los usuarios de esta criptomoneda.
“The Merge”, inglés para “La Fusión”, es una transformación en la forma en que Ethereum procesa las transacciones y en cómo se crean nuevos tokens de Ether.
Esta fusión se trata de la combinación de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum con una nueva cadena de bloques separada conocido como proof-of-stake, el cual reduce el consumo de energía de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum en un 99,9 %, según sus propios desarrolladores, lo que la vuelve más “amigable” con el ambiente al tiempo que las transacciones serían más baratas.
Sus defensores creen que la fusión hará que Ethereum resulte favorecido con respecto al máximo rival, Bitcoin, pues podría aumentar su uso.
En el proceso Proof Stake los propietarios de Ether bloquearán cantidades establecidas de sus criptomonedas para verificar nuevos registros en la cadena de bloques, ganando nuevas monedas además de su criptografía “participada”.

articles.title: Technics ressuscite sa platine MK2 légendaire : découvrez la SL-1210MKX et son pitch révolutionnaire
articles.text:
Technics ressuscite sa platine MK2 légendaire : découvrez la SL-1210MKX et son pitch révolutionnaire
Technics fait évoluer sa légendaire platine DJ avec la SL-1210MKX, un modèle qui mise sur un meilleur amortissement des vibrations, un châssis renforcé et une plage de pitch inédite, allant de ±4 à ±50 %. De quoi offrir aux DJ encore plus de précision et de liberté créative.
Technics vient de dévoiler une nouvelle platine vinyle baptisée SL-1210MKX, dont le "X" signifie "Extreme" ou "Expert", qui se distingue par son orientation pro. En effet, si la marque est historiquement spécialisée dans les platines DJ, avec la SL-1200MK2 comme fidèle représentante depuis le début des années 1970, elle est revenue sur le marché au milieu des années 2010 avec la volonté de s’adresser aux audiophiles exigeants.
Ainsi, même si les SL-1200G et SL-1200GR pouvaient très bien être utilisées à des fins professionnelles, elles embarquaient une mécanique bien plus avancée que celle de la SL-1200MK2 originale. Résultat : elles affichaient des tarifs respectifs de 3500 € et 1499 € à leur lancement, trop élevés pour le commun des mortels et loin des 650 € demandés pour une SL-1200MK2 avant son arrêt de commercialisation.
Technics SL-1210MKX
Technics a ensuite allégé sa formule avec la SL-1200MK7, un modèle orienté DJ lancé à 899 €. La SL-1500C a ensuite pris le contrepied avec une approche purement domestique, sans réglage de pitch, pour un tarif de 999 €. Présentée comme une version évoluée de la SL-1200MK7, la SL-1210MKX devient donc le deuxième modèle à vocation DJ lancé par Technics depuis son retour sur le marché en 2014. Un fait qui mérite d’être souligné pour une marque possédant un tel héritage dans ce domaine.
Pieds antivibrations revus et châssis plus lourd que celui de la MK7
Pour justifier cette montée en gamme, Technics annonce avoir doté la SL-1210MKX d’un "châssis nettement plus lourd" que celui de la SL-1200MK7, sans toutefois en préciser le poids, ainsi que de nouveaux pieds antivibrations.
Ces évolutions doivent non seulement permettre à la platine de mieux encaisser les scratchs intensifs, mais aussi de mieux absorber les vibrations mécaniques provoquées par les basses, susceptibles d’être captées par la cellule phono. Ce phénomène peut notamment se produire en club ou lorsque la platine est placée sur le même support que les enceintes. La SL-1210MKX devrait ainsi mieux s’adapter aux environnements les plus contraignants.
Un réglage du pitch inédit chez Technics, désormais de ±4 % à ±50 %
Alors que la MK7, tout comme ses sœurs hi-fi SL-1200G et SL-1200GR, bénéficie déjà d’un amortissement adapté à ces conditions, la SL-1210MKX se distingue surtout par sa gestion inédite du pitch. Pour la première fois sur une SL-1200, Technics introduit un réglage à ±4 %, une plage plus étroite qui permet de gagner en précision lors des transitions entre deux morceaux aux BPM très proches. Jusqu’à présent, les modèles précédents se limitaient à des plages de ±8 % et ±16 %.
La SL-1210MKX introduit également un réglage à ±50 %, offrant une amplitude de variation du tempo encore supérieure et favorisant l’expérimentation sonore et les techniques de mixage les plus poussées. Ces quatre plages de réglage du pitch (±4 %, ±8 %, ±16 % et ±50 %) sont accessibles via un sélecteur placé au-dessus du fader traditionnel, en remplacement du bouton "x2".
Par ailleurs, Technics annonce avoir amélioré le commutateur de réinitialisation du pitch afin de le rendre "plus silencieux", vraisemblablement dans l’esprit de celui des SL-1200 d’antan. Pour l’heure, la marque ne s’est pas étendue sur la conception interne de la platine, évoquant simplement un moteur à entraînement direct sans noyau (coreless) et de "nombreuses améliorations subtiles".
Un design familier et des possibilités de réglage complètes
Côté design, la SL-1210MKX reste tout à fait fidèle à ses aînées. À l’instar de la MK7, elle permet de régler la vitesse de freinage et d’activer la lecture inversée, ainsi que de lire les disques 78 tours, en complément des classiques 33 et 45 tours.
Comme toutes les platines Technics, à l’exception des modèles de la série SL-1500, la SL-1210MKX est livrée sans cellule phono prémontée. L’utilisateur peut donc opter pour une cellule DJ de type Ortofon Concorde ou lui associer une cellule hi-fi plus avancée. Bien sûr, la platine dispose de tous les réglages nécessaires à un ajustement précis de cette dernière, de la force d’appui au VTA (angle de suivi vertical), en passant par l’antiskating.
La SL-1210MKX sera lancée en janvier 2027, probablement à l’occasion du CES de Las Vegas, au prix de 1499 €. À ce tarif, ce modèle permet non seulement à Technics de se rapprocher des professionnels, mais aussi de proposer une alternative plus abordable à ses modèles hi-fi.
Au fil des ans, les améliorations apportées aux modèles les plus avancés de la gamme ont en effet largement contribué à faire grimper les prix, si bien que les SL-1200GR2 et SL-1200GE sont aujourd’hui proposées à partir de 1950 € et 4490 €, respectivement.

articles.title: U.S. Orders DeepSeek Removed From Federal Civilian Systems, Bans New Purchases
articles.text:
U.S. federal civilian agencies must remove DeepSeek products from their information technology systems, along with any third-party products or services "developed using DeepSeek implementations," under a Department of Homeland Security order.
They may also no longer buy information technology products or services from the Chinese AI developer or its affiliates
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin issued the order, dated July 24, 2026, under the Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act of 2018, and the department published it in the Federal Register on October 20. The notice does not define "DeepSeek implementations."
The order names Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co., Ltd., the developer of the R1 and V3 models, and covers its affiliates as defined in federal acquisition rules. The company's privacy policy says it collects, processes and stores users' personal data in the People's Republic of China.
Under the 2018 law, the Federal Acquisition Security Council recommends exclusion and removal orders, and three officials may issue them: the Secretary of Homeland Security for civilian agencies, the Secretary of Defense for the Defense Department and national security systems, and the Director of National Intelligence for the intelligence community.
The DeepSeek order therefore covers only what civilian agencies buy and run. It does not restrict companies or the public.
The 2018 law was first used in 2025, when the Director of National Intelligence excluded Acronis, a Swiss cybersecurity and data protection company, from intelligence community procurement and ordered its products removed from intelligence community systems.
Executive agencies "shall comply with exclusion and removal orders," the law says. An agency can ask the official who issued an order for an exception, and under the council's regulations the request must be in writing and give a compelling justification.
DHS directs questions about the order to CISA's FASCSA Order Implementation Team at fascsa.orders@cisa.dhs.gov.
The order also reaches government contractors. A federal contract that carries FAR clause 52.204-30 bars the contractor from providing or using, in performing the contract, any product or service covered by an applicable FASCSA order, unless the issuing official has granted a waiver.
The clause also requires the contractor to:
- Search SAM.gov for the phrase "FASCSA order" at least once every three months
- Make a reasonable inquiry into its supply chain when a new order could affect it
- Report any covered product or service it has provided or used to the contracting officer within 3 business days of identifying it
- Send further information on mitigation within 10 business days of that report
- Include the clause in its subcontracts
An order issued after a solicitation applies to an existing contract only once the contracting officer adds it by amendment or modification.
The Federal Register notice gives no reasons for the order. The signed order is attached to the notice as four scanned pages and is posted on regulations.gov under docket DHS-2026-0628.
The order is dated July 24. DHS filed it for public inspection at the Federal Register on October 19, 87 days later, and it was published the next day.
The council's regulations leave public release of an order to the issuing official, who "May provide a copy of the order to other persons, including through public disclosure." They set no deadline for it.
The law requires the issuing official to notify the company named in an order and the appropriate congressional committees, and to review the order at least once a year.
Before the order, U.S. restrictions on DeepSeek were device bans adopted one body at a time. By February 2025, Congress, NASA, the Navy, the Pentagon and Texas had barred DeepSeek from government devices. Bills to bar DeepSeek on government devices were introduced in the House and Senate that month and had not advanced past committee as of October 21.
China's foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said at a briefing on October 20 that "China consistently opposes the overstretching of the concept of national security" and that Beijing will "resolutely safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies," the Associated Press reported. DeepSeek did not immediately respond to the AP's request for comment.

articles.title: I tested Antigravity’s new wearable ‘Follow Me’ bundle — and the ring and watch completely change how you fly its original 360-degree drone
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Antigravity A1 is a fantastic drone overall, albeit on the pricey side. It offers an immersive flight experience, and this expansion of its functionality with the Follow Me Bundle is most welcome. The subject-tracking modes and one-tap cinematic shots are fantastic, but they do arguably deliver similar tracking capabilities to the much less expensive DJI Neo 2. The ace up Antigravity’s sleeve, however, is the fact that the A1 captures 360-degree video.
Reasons to buy
- + Expands the use of the Antigravity A1
- + Ring controller allows for adjustments
- + Reliable follow functionality
Reasons to avoid
- - The bundle is expensive
- - Still no ‘standard’ controller
- - The prop guards make the drone large
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Antigravity A1 Follow Me Bundle: two-minute review
When the Antigravity A1 launched in 2025 it was the world’s first 360-degree drone, and for a brief time the only such drone, until the DJI Avata 360 was released shortly after. These two models remain the only 360-degree drones currently available, with their differing designs offering slightly different propositions for drone pilots, depending on what you’re aiming for.
You can fly both drones with FPV goggles and Motion Controllers, though the Avata 360 can also be flown with a standard drone controller. The Antigravity A1’s design makes it look like a camera drone, but with top and bottom 360-degree cameras, while the standard kit's FPV goggles and Motion Controller let you fly immersively with a 360-degree view of your surroundings; you can look around as you fly, which is quite an experience.
A 360-degree drone lets you reframe photos and videos after you’ve captured them, opening up a wealth of creative potential. They're not for everyone, but they undoubtedly provide both an interesting flying experience and equally interesting editing possibilities. The Antigravity A1 Follow Me Bundle is designed to expand the functionality of the drone, and the creative options available to users, further.
The Antigravity A1 Follow Me Bundle enables hands-free shooting, and obviates the need to use the A1’s FPV goggles and Motion Controller for flight. It also improves subject tracking, and offers automated flight patterns for capturing selfies, similar to the DJI Neo 2.
The Follow Me Bundle includes several accessories, with the Watch Remote allowing you to set the flight mode, and the Ring Remote allowing you use gestures to adjust the position of the A1 when in flight.
The Watch Remote also features built-in GNSS for greater precision when the drone is tracking you during fast-paced activities such as cycling, and allows you to select the subject that will be tracked.
The Follow Me Bundle also opens up one-tap cinematic shots, which are automated flight patterns, alongside advanced subject-tracking modes. The former include Fly Away, Antigravity Line, Ascend, Oval Orbit, Spiral Ascent, Arc Shot and Arc Out, while the tracking modes include Manual Mode, Deep Track, Orbit Follow, Cycling Track and Ski Track.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The one-tap cinematic shots, like any automated flight patterns, may feel a bit 'samey' after a while, but they’re fun to try out. It’s the new subject-tracking modes that are most interesting.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
The subject-tracking modes and one-tap cinematic shots can’t be faulted, and the Antigravity performs incredibly well here. I had it track me while running, skateboarding, and cycling through complex environments, including between and under trees, and the A1 didn’t miss a beat. Not to mention, you get the bonus of being able to reframe footage and add effects in Antigravity Studio.
The Watch Remote enables you to initiate take-off and landing and Return to Home, and make basic adjustments to the drone’s position, alongside setting the flight mode and selecting the subject to be tracked.
The Ring Remote offers a Drag-to-Fly feature, where you press and hold the button on the ring, and can then move your hand and arm to adjust A1’s flight position in relation to you to fine-tune its tracking distance and position.
The Watch Remote is about the same size as a smartwatch, with a 1.72-inch LCD screen. It is, however, about 1.5x the depth/thickness of your average smartwatch. The Ring Remote fits a finger circumference of 1.8-2.8 inches / 46-70mm. Both offer IP67 water resistance and, as we’ve discussed, a unique way to control your Antigravity A1 drone.
The main downside of the kit — cost aside, which we'll get to below — is that the propeller guards increase the weight of the drone. The propeller guards take the A1 from the coveted 249g weight, to 351g, meaning the A1 becomes slightly more restricted when this accessory is used.
Antigravity A1 Follow Me Bundle: key specs
| Camera: | Dual 1/1.28-inch sensors | 
| Video resolution: | Up to 8K | 
| Frame rates: | 8K up to 30fps / 5.2K up to 60fps / 4K & 1080p up to 30fps / 4K & 1080p slow motion at 100fps | 
| Video transmission range: | Up to 6.2 miles / 10km (Tested in FCC environments) | 
| Flight modes: | Manual Mode, Deep Track, Orbit Follow, Cycling Track, Ski Track, Fly Away, Antigravity Line, Ascend, Oval Orbit, Spiral Ascent, Arc Shot, Arc Out | 
| Battery: | 2360mAh, up to 24 minutes flight time / 4345mAh, up to 39 minutes flight time | 
| Charger type: | USB-C / Battery Charging Hub | 
| Weight: | 12.04oz / 351g | 
| Dimensions: | Folded: 5.56 x 3.79 x 3.20 inches / 141.3 x 96.2 x 81.4mm Unfolded (propellers extended): 12.15 x 15.05 x 3.51 inches / 308.6 x 382.3 x 89.2mm | 
Antigravity A1 Follow Me Bundle: Price and availability
The Antigravity A1 Follow Me Bundle is available in two kits: one that includes the Antigravity A1 drone and another that’s just the follow accessories for existing A1 owners. The Follow Me Bundle includes the Watch Remote, Ring Remote, Propeller Guards, Lens Guards, a USB-C cable and a Cross Body Bag. This costs $340 / £309 / AU$539, while the kit with all this and the A1 drone, alongside other drone accessories, costs $799 / £639 / AU$1159. The Propeller Guards can also be purchased separately, and these cost $40 / £32 / AU$70.
This is quite expensive when you consider the fact that the DJI Neo 2 only costs $259 / £209 / AU$409 for the basic kit. Sure, if you’ve already got an Antigravity drone, the new Accessory Bundle, including just the accessories, expands the functionality of what you have, but the DJI Neo 2 is smaller, lighter and can be controlled in several different ways. The main and obvious advantage of the Antigravity A1 Follow Me Bundle is the fact that you can capture 360-degree video, which you can’t do with the DJI Neo 2.
One thing that I would like to see with the Antigravity A1, and this could also be released as a kit and standalone accessory purchase, is a standard drone controller; one that allows you to fly the drone without the need for the FPV goggles and Motion Controller, or even the Watch and Ring Remotes. This would make flying even easier and more convenient – simply opening up yet another way to fly the A1. Anyhow, let’s get back to the Follow Me Bundle.
Antigravity A1 Follow Me Bundle: Also consider
DJI Neo 2
The DJI Neo 2 allows you to capture effortless aerial selfies thanks to its intelligent subject tracking that automatically follows you. Gesture controls let you operate the drone hands-free. The drone is lightweight and compact, and although it’s not a 360-degree drone, it offers fantastic subject tracking and selfie modes in an affordable package with several control options available.
Read our DJI Neo 2 review
DJI Avata 360
The DJI Avata 360 is excellent for capturing 360-degree photos and videos. Its intelligent subject-tracking features, including ActiveTrack 360°, make it easy to follow moving subjects automatically, while Spotlight modes provide additional creative control. These are more basic in some ways than the Antigravity A1 Follow Me Bundle, but it’s the only other 360-degree drone available, and it offers some subject tracking functionality off the shelf.
Read our DJI Avata 360 review
Should I buy the Antigravity A1 Follow Me Bundle?
Buy it if...
You want subject tracking capabilities on a 360-degree drone
The subject tracking capabilities of the Follow Me Bundle are impressive, to say the least. Plus, you can shoot up to 8K 360-degree footage.
You already own an A1
If you already own an Antigravity A1 and would rather expand its functionality rather than buying another drone, the accessory bundle is for you.
Don't buy it if...
You’re on a tight budget
Whether or not you already own an Antigravity A1, the basic DJI Neo 2 kit is less expensive than the Follow Me Bundles and offers similar flight functionality.
You don’t need or want 360-degree tracking
This is a no-brainer, but if you don’t need or want subject tracking and selfie functionality in a 360-degree drone, this is not the kit for you.
How I tested the Antigravity A1 Follow Me Bundle
- All functionality tested
- Tested in complex environments
- Used with different modes of transport
The Antigravity A1 Follow Me Bundle was tested over several weeks, tracking myself skateboarding, cycling and running. I also tested the one-click cinematic shots while standing to show how these look with focus on the subject.
To put the subject tracking through its paces, I chose to walk, skate and cycle under and around trees to see how the drone’s collision avoidance coped, alongside how the GNSS tracking on the Watch Remote performed.
All video footage was reframed as simply as possible, with focus on the subject maintained with a ‘normal’ field of view. I chose not to use any special effects to make the capabilities of the tracking modes apparent.
First reviewed October 2026
James Abbott is a professional photographer and freelance photography journalist. He contributes articles about photography, cameras and drones to a wide range of magazines and websites where he applies a wealth of experience to testing the latest photographic tech. James is also the author of ‘The Digital Darkroom: The Definitive Guide to Photo Editing’.

articles.title: Orange : le réseau mobile (toujours) en panne nationale ce 21 octobre
articles.text:
Orange : le réseau mobile (toujours) en panne nationale ce 21 octobre
De nombreux utilisateurs rapportent qu'une panne du réseau mobile d'Orange, ainsi que de Sosh, est en cours ce mercredi 21 octobre. L'opérateur travaille à corriger le problème.
Depuis environ 11h30 ce matin du mercredi 21 octobre 2026, des utilisateurs, sur X ou encore DownDetector, rapportent que le réseau mobile d'Orange et de sa marque low cost Sosh est en panne. L'opérateur a réagi quelques dizaines de minutes plus tard, tandis que les témoignages proviennent de plusieurs villes de France.
Les abonnés Livebox ne semblent pas concernés, et seuls les clients mobiles ne peuvent plus, visiblement, utiliser leurs données mobiles, envoyer des messages et passer des appels.
Le réseau mobile d'Orange ne répond plus
Sur la plateforme DownDetector, plusieurs milliers de personnes ont indiqué la panne dès les premiers instants, témoignant de l'ampleur du problème.
On relèvera également que le site de suivi des incidents d'Orange est lui-même en difficultés, peut-être à cause d'un trafic plus élevé que d'habitude ou d'un souci plus global.
Vers 12h15, Orange a posté sur X, indiquant "rencontrer actuellement des perturbations sur le réseau mobile" et que "nos équipes sont pleinement mobilisées pour rétablir le réseau dans les meilleurs délais." L'opérateur n'a cependant pas indiqué l'origine de la panne.
Bonjour, vous pouvez rencontrer actuellement des perturbations sur le réseau mobile Orange. 
Nos équipes sont pleinement mobilisées pour rétablir le réseau dans les meilleurs délais. 
Veuillez nous excuser pour la gêne occasionnée.
— Orange France (@Orange_France) October 21, 2026
Ne reste plus qu'aux personnes concernées à prendre leur mal en patience ou à trouver un réseau WiFi, tandis qu'en juin dernier Orange disposait de presque 22 millions de clients mobiles en France.

articles.title: Smartphones pliables : les ventes devraient exploser cette année
articles.text:
2026 devrait être une belle année pour les smartphones pliables. C'est ce que montrent les prédiction sur les ventes d'écrans pliables cette année.
Difficile de ne pas voir une année historique pour le smartphone pliable pour 2026. Car si la technologie existe depuis déjà la fin de la décennie précédente, et a depuis été investie par la plupart des grands noms du secteur des smartphones, elle souffrait d'une absence notable : celle d'Apple. Or, ce trou a été comblé cette année, avec les iPhone Duo qui vont bientôt commencer à tomber dans la poche des acquéreurs. Une année historique qui se traduit par d'autres chiffres.
Les ventes d'écrans de smartphones pliables devraient croître de 44% en 2026
Omdia est formelle. La société spécialisée dans l'analyse des marchés annonce en effet que les ventes d'écrans de smartphones pliables vont rebondir très fortement en 2026, avec une croissance attendue de +44% pour cette année. Un chiffre qui apparaît d'autant plus impressionnant quand il est comparé à celui de l'année dernière, où les ventes avaient reculé de 12%.
Ce sont ainsi 29 millions d'écrans pliables qui vont être commercialisés. Et évidemment, si l'on ne peut imposer l'égalité 1 écran pliable = 1 smartphone pliable, une telle croissance montre clairement une rebond très marqué du produit. Rebond qui ne doit rien au hasard, vu les écrans les plus recherchés.
Un marché porté par le Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 et l'iPhone Duo
La nouvelle forme d'écran pliable plus carré, la forme « wide », va représenter une part notable de ces ventes – 44% à elle seule, alors qu'elle n'est arrivée sur le marché que cette année. Et c'est normal, puisqu'elle est la forme adoptée par les deux smartphones pliables les plus populaires, et de loin, du marché actuellement : le Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 et l'iPhone Duo.
À noter que ce rebond est une bonne nouvelle pour Samsung, qui fournit des écrans pour les deux appareils. Autre information, plus étonnante, Omdia indique que la demande pour les smartphones pliables est faible en ce moment en Chine, même si de plus en plus de Chinois sont intéressés par une acquisition potentielle d'un de ces appareils. De quoi y trouver encore de la marge ?
Source : Omdia

articles.title: WhatsApp se inspira en Instagram: así cambiará la barra inferior cuando deslices en los chats
articles.text:
WhatsApp prepara una barra de navegación inferior dinámica para Android que se contraerá cuando el usuario desplace la lista de chats hacia abajo y recuperará su tamaño al subir. La función, detectada en la beta 2.26.41.6, modifica los accesos de la aplicación y replica un comportamiento conocido de Instagram. El diseño reducirá controles sin ocultarlos.
El ajuste resulta importante porque la barra ocupa una zona permanente de la pantalla y puede restar espacio al buscar contactos o revisar mensajes antiguos. WhatsApp conservará los iconos, pero los reunirá en una píldora flotante durante el desplazamiento descendente. La empresa no anunció fecha de lanzamiento; sigue en desarrollo por ahora.
La barra se reducirá hasta convertirse en una píldora flotante
En su estado inicial, la barra inferior ocupará todo el ancho de la pantalla. Ese formato aparecerá al abrir WhatsApp o entrar en cualquiera de sus pestañas. El rediseño ya eliminó las etiquetas de texto bajo los iconos. Al bajar por la interfaz, la barra disminuirá de forma gradual en altura y conservará iconos visibles.
El cambio busca facilitar la búsqueda de conversaciones
La lista de chats explica el objetivo del cambio. Al bajar por la pantalla, el usuario suele buscar una conversación y no cambiar de pestaña. Una barra menor deja más espacio para nombres, previsualizaciones y fechas. Cuando el desplazamiento vuelve hacia arriba, WhatsApp recuperará el tamaño completo para mostrar nuevamente los accesos.
El comportamiento se aplicará a cualquier pestaña, aunque resulta más útil en las conversaciones. En llamadas o actualizaciones, el mismo gesto reservará más área para el contenido. Los iconos seguirán visibles en el formato compacto, por lo que no será necesario abrir un menú adicional para moverse dentro.
Instagram ya utiliza una navegación que responde al desplazamiento
El comportamiento recuerda a la barra inferior de Instagram, otra aplicación de Meta. En Instagram, la barra inferior se hace más pequeña y se convierte en una barra compacta con bordes redondeados cuando el usuario baja por las publicaciones. WhatsApp prueba ahora una lógica semejante, familiar para quienes utilizan ambos servicios. Meta apuesta por interfaces que reaccionan.
La barra ya pasó por varios cambios en las versiones beta
El diseño dinámico es el cuarto ajuste identificado en esta zona de WhatsApp. Antes, la empresa probó una barra flotante, con esquinas redondeadas y sin nombres bajo cada icono. La beta 2.26.41.7 también ensayó un indicador de pestaña circular en lugar de una píldora. El aspecto definitivo todavía puede cambiar antes del lanzamiento.
Cómo descargar la beta de WhatsApp en Android
Quienes quieran probar estas funciones antes de su lanzamiento general deben registrarse en el programa de testers desde Google Play. El proceso comienza al buscar la ficha oficial de WhatsApp y bajar hasta “Unirse al programa beta”.
También es posible acceder al enlace web oficial de WhatsApp Beta Testers e iniciar sesión con una cuenta de Google. Tras pulsar “Convertirse en tester”, la cuenta quedará vinculada y la tienda permitirá descargar o actualizar la beta.
El acceso depende de que haya vacantes, porque los cupos son limitados y suelen agotarse. Puede ser necesario revisar la tienda hasta que aparezca una plaza. No se exige pago ni suscripción adicional. Sin embargo, la beta puede presentar fallos, cierres inesperados o funciones incompletas. Los participantes aceptan enviar comentarios e informes técnicos de errores a los desarrolladores del servicio.
Las versiones de prueba permiten anticipar cambios, pero no garantizan que todas las herramientas estén disponibles para cada usuario. WhatsApp puede habilitar una función para grupos limitados y modificarla, aplazarla o descartarla antes del lanzamiento público. Por ello, quien use la beta debe considerar que su experiencia puede diferir de la versión estable. La barra dinámica continúa en desarrollo.

articles.title: State Bank of India Confirms Data Leak After 3,897 Customer Records Found on Dark Web
articles.text:
State Bank of India has identified 3,897 customer records containing personal information in a set of about 375,000 records available on the dark web, and it does not yet know where the data came from.
The state-owned bank, India's largest, said in a stock-exchange filing dated October 21 that it "has experienced an incident involving the loss of certain data." The count is preliminary, and the bank has yet to establish whether the data is authentic, how far the exposure goes and what risk it poses to customers.
The exposed information "reportedly included customers' registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, branch and CIF identifiers, lead IDs, and metadata associated with loan/lead records and other related files," in the filing's words. A CIF identifier is the customer information file number, the bank's internal ID for each customer.
The bank has not said whether the 3,897 records belong to 3,897 different people, or what the rest of the set contains. The 3,897 are roughly 1 in 100 of the records it examined.
Account numbers, balances, passwords, one-time passcodes, card details and government identity numbers such as PAN or Aadhaar are not among the categories the filing lists. The risk in the listed categories is impersonation: a caller or message that uses a customer's name, mobile number, date of birth, address, branch, and internal ID to appear to come from the bank.
The alert reached the bank on October 16 via its threat intelligence provider, CERT-In, India's national computer emergency response team, and the Defense Cyber Agency, the armed forces' cyber agency under the Ministry of Defense.
The bank activated its incident response and containment procedures and engaged an independent cybersecurity firm from CERT-In's panel of approved security auditors to assess what the filing calls "the alleged compromise."
The incident has no material impact on the bank's core business operations, financial performance or business continuity, the filing says. That covers the bank's business, not its customers.
The filing names no attacker, forum or dataset. The figure of about 375,000 matches a claim that the monitoring account CyberPulse56 flagged on X on October 16.
The account said a threat actor using the name Siriusim claimed to have leaked customer documents and personal data linked to SBI: 375,000 rows in CSV format and 2,722 PDF documents, said to include personal information, loan applications and supporting documents, account-opening forms and addresses.
The Free Press Journal examined the listing on BreachForums, a cybercrime forum used to trade stolen data, and found 4 sample records posted with the listing. The phone numbers in the samples were valid. The WhatsApp profile picture on one number matched the passport-size photograph on that person's KYC document, which the actor had also posted.
That check covers 4 records and does not show that the whole set is genuine or where it came from. The samples were mostly loan-related and carried KYC fields, and they did not show whether the data belonged to SBI itself, one of its subsidiaries, or a third-party provider that handles banking applications.
Nothing in the bank's filing ties its analysis to the listing, and the bank has not said whether the 2,722 PDF documents were part of what it examined.
Whether any SBI system was breached is an open question. The filing leaves the source of the data to the investigation and gives no date for when the data first appeared.
The filing does not mention whether affected customers have been or will be told. The bank's cyber security page, last updated in June, tells customers to report any cyber incident to report.phishing@sbi.co.in or the national cybercrime helpline, 1930. That is general advice, written before the incident.
Bank of Baroda, another state-owned bank, told the exchanges on July 27 about a cyber-security incident in nearly the same words, including "the alleged compromise," after receiving "a communication from an anonymous source claiming access to certain data." That filing named a preliminary cause, "potential business email compromise." SBI's names none.

articles.title: Ambilight sur n'importe quel téléviseur : j'ai testé la caméra Philips Hue Play Screen Sync sur ma TV
articles.text:
Pour rendre un téléviseur compatible Ambilight, plusieurs solutions existent. J’ai essayé la nouvelle caméra Hue Play Screen Sync couplée au ruban de leds Hue Play Gradient Lightstrip Pro pour juger du résultat et le comparer au véritable Ambilight des TV Philips.
Beaucoup d'utilisateurs sont fans de la technologie d’éclairage Ambilight, mais tout le monde ne souhaite pas nécessairement investir dans un téléviseur Philips, d’autant moins lorsqu'on possède déjà un excellent modèle Samsung, LG, Hisense, Sony ou TCL.
Pour les novices, le principe de cette technologie est simple puisqu’il consiste à diffuser sur le mur arrière des halos lumineux reproduisant les couleurs de l’image affichée à l'écran. L’objectif est de donner l’impression que l'image déborde de son cadre et renforcer ainsi l’immersion dans un film ou un jeu vidéo.
Il existe différentes approches pour rendre n’importe quel écran compatible, comme nous l’avons détaillé dans l’article ci-dessous. La base est néanmoins toujours la même : fixer un ruban de leds colorées au dos de la dalle.
Je viens justement de tester la Hue Play Screen Sync, une caméra chargée de “filmer” l’écran du téléviseur. Associée au ruban Hue Play Gradient Lightstrip, elle promet de créer un effet proche de l’Ambilight. Cette caméra se veut plus abordable que les alternatives de l'écosystème Hue. Elle est en effet lancée au tarif conseillé de 120 €, contre 150 € pour le récent boîtier Hue Sync Box 4K (qui ne possède qu’une seule entrée HDMI) et jusqu'à 350 € pour la Sync Box 8K. Rappelons également l'existence d'une application native, réservée aux TV Samsung et LG, facturée la bagatelle de 130 €.
Avec ce nouveau produit, Philips Hue tente de contrer Govee, qui propose depuis quelque temps une caméra du genre, à un tarif agressif qui plus est.
À la caméra, il faut bien sûr ajouter l'éclairage. Comptez 100 € pour un ruban Hue Play Gradient Lightstrip classique, ou 160 € pour la version Pro, qui offre de meilleurs dégradés de couleurs. La facture globale grimpe donc entre 220 € et 280 €, même s'il est souvent possible de profiter de promotions régulières chez le fabricant. On pourra également y associer d’autres luminaires comme les Hue Play.
Notez également que le pont Hue n’est pas nécessaire pour cette installation. Le système peut fonctionner en Bluetooth, un bon point pour ceux qui ne souhaitent pas s'équiper d’un système Hue complet à la maison.
Mais cette technologie fait-elle le poids face à l’Ambilight original une fois installée ?
La première étape consiste donc à installer le Lightstrip au dos du téléviseur. Avant de se lancer, mieux vaut prévoir un accès suffisamment confortable à l’arrière de l’écran, mais l’installation reste très simple.
Des petits guides en plastique doivent être fixés à l’aide de leur adhésif sur les trois côtés du TV (à droite, en haut et à gauche). Mieux vaut soigner leur positionnement et mesurer leur distance par rapport au bord de l’écran pour un résultat le plus propre possible (en plaçant chaque guide à 7 cm du bord, par exemple), sans oublier de prévoir le passage du câble d’alimentation. Il suffit ensuite de clipser le ruban de leds dans les encoches, puis de brancher le câble, et le tour est joué.
Un mur clair se prête évidemment mieux à l’exercice qu’une surface très colorée, qui modifierait la teinte perçue. Un téléviseur presque collé au mur ne donnera pas non plus le même halo qu’un modèle installé avec un peu plus de recul, mais le résultat demeure très convaincant, même avec une accroche murale.
Une fois le dispositif en place, le ruban se fait totalement oublier derrière le TV. La caméra, elle, sera forcément un peu plus visible.
La petite caméra Hue Play Screen Sync se place au-dessus du téléviseur, sa lentille tournée vers l’écran. Il suffit ensuite de la brancher sur une prise classique à l'aide du bloc d'alimentation USB-C fourni. Après un calibrage automatique via l’app Hue, elle analyse les couleurs affichées à l’écran pour les reproduire fidèlement sur le ruban.
Son principal intérêt est de fonctionner quelle que soit la source. Une série lancée depuis l’app Netflix du téléviseur, une vidéo YouTube ou un jeu sur une console branchée en HDMI : la caméra observe simplement ce qui s’affiche à l’écran. Elle est opérationnelle dans toutes les situations, alors que les boîtiers Hue ne fonctionnent qu’avec une source externe (console ou boîtier multimédia façon Amazon Firestick, Google Streamer ou Apple TV 4K, par exemple).
En contrepartie, il faut accepter la présence de cet appendice au-dessus de l’écran. Sur un téléviseur aux bordures très fines, il ne passe pas complètement inaperçu et l'ensemble s'avère un peu moins “joli” en termes d’intégration dans un salon, même si l'on finit par s'y habituer. Notez également qu’il faudra lancer la synchronisation entre la caméra et les éclairages Hue manuellement à chaque fois que l'on allume le téléviseur. L'opération s'effectue en trois clics sur son smartphone via l’app Hue, mais elle n'est pas automatisée.
Dans les faits, le résultat est plutôt réussi. Les couleurs prolongent visuellement l’image sur le mur et cela donne ce petit côté “wow” au salon. Sur des contenus colorés, l’effet fonctionne très bien et apporte ce petit supplément d’immersion appréciable, surtout en jeu vidéo ou en regardant des films d’animation ou des blockbusters façon Avatar. La latence par rapport à un boîtier Hue Sync Box ou à un véritable téléviseur Philips Ambilight est toutefois plus importante. L’éclairage suit les transitions d’image avec un peu plus de retard, mais c’est logique : la caméra doit observer l’image affichée, puis le système doit traduire ces informations en impulsions lumineuses.
Cela ne rend pas l’ensemble désagréable pour autant, mais le décalage se remarque davantage lors de changements brusques ; quand les couleurs évoluent doucement, l’illusion est plus convaincante.
Il faut aussi savoir que les effets lumineux ne seront pas aussi efficaces qu’avec un boîtier Hue Sync Box ou un TV Philips, qui captent pour leur part l’ensemble des couleurs affichées et leur position exacte à l’écran. Ces derniers afficheront souvent plus de couleurs sur le mur, et ce, bien plus précisément.
L’autre limite concerne les films avec des bandes noires en haut et en bas de l’image. Dans cette configuration, la partie supérieure du ruban de leds fonctionne moins bien, car la caméra voit du noir en haut de l’image et les leds s’éteignent. Elles s’allumeront de temps à autre selon ce qui est affiché, mais elles accompagnent moins efficacement les couleurs du film. C’est dommage, puisque ce format est très courant au cinéma et que l’intérêt du dispositif est justement de prolonger l’image autour du téléviseur.
Pour profiter au mieux de l’installation, les contenus qui remplissent tout l’écran sont donc à privilégier. Les animés et les jeux vidéo s’y prêtent tout particulièrement. Les couleurs occupent alors toute la surface observée par la caméra, et le résultat est plus convaincant.
Heureusement, le Lightstrip peut aussi servir de lumière d’ambiance, pilotée depuis l’app Hue quand le téléviseur n’est pas allumé. On retrouve alors toutes les possibilités de cet écosystème, bien qu’un pont Hue soit nécessaire pour en déverrouiller vraiment toutes les fonctionnalités. On pourra ainsi choisir les couleurs du bandeau de leds, régler l’intensité de la lumière, utiliser les galeries de scénarios Hue, etc. On peut bien sûr l’associer aux autres éclairages Hue de la pièce, et le ruban devient alors un luminaire à part entière.
Peu de choses peuvent être réglées concernant la caméra dans l’application, si ce n’est le mode (Vidéo ou Jeu pour des effets plus rapides), l’intensité (soit la vitesse à laquelle les couleurs seront synchronisées) et la luminosité si on veut diminuer ou augmenter la puissance des leds.
L’application Hue reste l’un des atouts de la marque face à ses concurrents. L’interface est agréable, les scènes permettent de changer rapidement d’ambiance et le contrôle des différents éclairages se montre très efficace et intuitif. Celles et ceux qui possèdent déjà des lampes Hue retrouveront ainsi leurs habitudes sans faillir.
L'association entre la caméra Hue Play Screen Sync et le ruban Hue Play Lightstrip remplit bien son rôle pour qui souhaite “Ambilighter” son TV sans trop se prendre la tête. Les bandes noires des films restent toutefois une limite physique (la caméra filmant du noir), et le système n'égale pas la précision d’un véritable téléviseur Ambilight, de l’app native Hue Sync pour TV LG et Samsung, ou d’un boîtier Hue Sync Box, bien que ce dernier apporte d’autres contraintes comme nous l’avons vu. Néanmoins, sur des jeux vidéo, des animés ou des films en plein écran, le rendu fait son petit effet, d'autant que l'application Hue demeure la plus efficace du marché.

articles.title: The Oppo Find X10 is a pro-level phone masquerading as a standard flagship
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Oppo Find X10 is a great flagship phone, especially when it comes to photography. Solid internal hardware and excellent software optimization also make it a pleasure to use, and its design, while thoroughly indebted to the iPhone, is sturdy and elegant. That said, a high price tag, limited availability, and truly awful bloatware dock points from this otherwise wonderful bit of tech.
Reasons to buy
- + Excellent camera system
- + Solid performance
- + Incredible battery life
- + Beautifully built
Reasons to avoid
- - Bloatware!
- - High price tag
- - Unoriginal design
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Oppo Find X10 review: Two-minute review
I’ve been using a selection of Oppo phones as my daily drivers for the last two years, and in that time, I’ve always gravitated towards the higher end of the lineup. I’ve stood by my habit of choosing the ‘pro’ option where possible for several reasons — such as wanting a high-quality camera system, long battery life, a great screen, and powerful internals — but Oppo’s new baseline flagship throws that all into question.
Put simply, the Oppo Find X10 feels like a ‘pro’ phone. It blazes through multitasking, gaming, and productivity tasks. It lasts for ages thanks to an iPad-sized battery. Its three rear cameras are some of the clearest and sharpest I’ve used on a smartphone. And its mid-sized display feels bigger than it is thanks to razor-thin bezels and a super-sharp resolution.
However, the Oppo Find X10 also comes with a pro-grade price tag. While last year’s Oppo Find X9 launched at £899 / AU$1,799 (it wasn't available in the US), the Find X10 hikes that number up to £1,099 (AU$ TBC) — the same price as the Oppo Find X9 Pro.
Really, then, it makes more sense to see the Find X10 as the successor to the Find X9 Pro. This year’s actual step-up model, the Oppo Find X10 Pro Max, is in a different class altogether, with three 200MP cameras and a ludicrous £1,499 launch price.
Still, as you might expect from such an expensive handset, the Oppo Find X10 punches above its weight class as a standard flagship. Though we’ve seen other Android manufacturers like Samsung and Google release phones with triple-camera systems and fast internal components, Oppo’s latest offering has some seriously impressive specs up its sleeve, and it's a strong contender for future inclusion in TechRadar's best Android phone and best camera phone guides.
As well as the aforementioned battery — a monstrously huge 7,150mAh cell (or an even bigger 8,000mAh cell in APAC regions) — the phone comes locked and loaded with two 200MP camera sensors, one of the cleanest Android wrappers in the game, and a thin and light design that takes more than a little inspiration from Apple.
Indeed, the Find X10 makes it clearer than ever that Oppo has no plans of slowing its roll when it comes to taking, ahem, inspiration from the design and engineering teams over in Cupertino. I'll leave you to decide whether that's a help or a hindrance; the phone itself works marvelously, but it’s hardly the most original product on the market. With that said, if you’re someone who absolutely must use Android, but like the look and feel of the best iPhones, the Find X10 is about as close as you can get while keeping a hold of Google’s mobile OS.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Across the industry, phones aren’t getting any cheaper — the standard iPhone 17 is approaching the launch price of the iPhone 15 Pro, and Android phone makers are jacking prices across the board — and Oppo's latest flagships are no exception.
At £1,099, the Oppo Find X10 is very expensive for a supposed base-model flagship, but, to be real, this is a pro-level flagship in disguise. Thanks to its excellent cameras and solid performance, its standard-sounding name is not a facade that holds for long; a pro by any other name still feels as complete.
Oppo Find X10 Pro review: Price and availability
- Costs £1,099
- Comes in a single configuration with 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage
- Not available in the US; Australia availability TBC
The Oppo Find X10 costs £1,099 — exactly the same as last year’s Find X9 Pro at launch and £200 more than the standard Find X9. That might sound like a mighty price hike at first, but the truth is that the Find X10 is more obviously a follow-up to the Find X9 Pro than the standard Find X9, and makes a case for its price point with some properly pro-grade features.
The Find X10 comes in one configuration: 12GB of RAM with 256GB of storage. That is, annoyingly, less RAM and storage space than last year’s Find X9 Pro, which came with 16GB of RAM and 512GB of storage. But with rising prices across the industry and still-excellent performance (as I'll discuss below), the Find X10 is hardly the worst offender on the market when it comes to changes in value proposition.
If you buy the phone directly from Oppo, you get your choice of the Hasselblad Teleconverter Kit or Oppo Watch X3 at no extra cost. Personally, I’d recommend the teleconverter kit — I didn’t get to test it with the Find X10, but having used last year’s version with the Find X9 Pro, I’d recommend it for any keen mobile photographers.
One thing I do appreciate about Oppo is that everything you need to get started with your phone comes in the box. As well as the phone itself, my Find X10 review unit came with an 80W SuperVOOC charger and a color-matched silicone case. Considering how expensive high-power chargers can be, that’s a decent value-add.
- Value score: 3 / 5
Oppo Find X10 review: Specs
Check out the table below for a quick overview of the Oppo Find X10's specs, or keep scrolling for detailed breakdowns of each feature.
| Dimensions: | 156.51 × 74.29 × 8.35mm | 
| Weight: | 216g | 
| Display: | 6.59-inch AMOLED | 
| Resolution: | 2768 x 1272 pixels | 
| Refresh rate: | 1-120Hz adaptive, boosted to 144Hz in certain games | 
| Chipset: | MediaTek Dimensity 9500 | 
| Rear cameras: | 200MP main + 50MP ultra-wide + 200MP telephoto (2.8x) | 
| Front camera: | 50MP | 
| Storage: | 256GB | 
| RAM: | 12GB | 
| OS (at launch): | Android 17 w/ ColorOS 17 | 
| Battery: | 8,000mAh (APAC) / 7,150mAh (EU) | 
| Charging: | 80W wired, 50W wireless | 
Oppo Find X10 review: Design
- Comes in three colors: Glacier Blue, Glow Coral, and Mist Grey
- The most iPhone-like Oppo phone yet
- Simple but elegant, with beautiful details
There’s no getting around the fact that the Oppo Find X10 looks like an iPhone 17 Pro (or indeed an iPhone 18 Pro). Its aluminum frame, glass rear panel, and raised camera plateau housing a trio of rear cameras make this the most iPhone-like Oppo phone ever released — somehow, it looks even more Apple-esque than last year’s Find X9 Pro, and given the brand’s history with taking inspiration from Cupertino, that’s really saying something.
However, despite its lack of originality, I am a fan of the Find X10’s design. In typical Oppo style, the phone feels both tanky and elegant. I wasn’t concerned about it taking knocks in my pocket or at the bottom of a backpack, but I also found myself stopping to appreciate the refinement and precision in its construction. Funnily enough, that familiar-looking camera plateau is perhaps the best example of Oppo's attention to detail; it rises from a rear panel made of a single piece of glass.
It helps, too, that the Find X10 comes with some protective kit in the box — you get a color-matched silicone case at no extra charge, and the phone comes with a glass screen protector pre-installed. The phone has also been separately rated at IP66, IP68, and IP69, meaning it can take a dip in shallow fresh water without any fuss (that’s a safety net, not an invitation).
My review unit came in the Glacier Blue colorway, which is rather nice, and the phone also comes in the stylishly loud Glow Coral (read: pink) and understated Mist Grey (read: grey) color options for those who want something more or less noticeable.
In the interface department, the Find X10 comes equipped with the standard power button and volume rocker as well as the Snap Key, Oppo’s take on Apple’s Action Button. By default, it’s set to activate Mind Space (more on that in the Software section), but I tend to set it as a camera shortcut or handy flashlight button.
The USB-C port uses a USB 3.2 Gen 1 connector, meaning file transfers zip by at a speedy 10 Gbps, and the main speaker alongside it is one of the best I’ve heard on any phone, with plenty of bass and depth to the sound.
- Design score: 4 / 5
Oppo Find X10 review: Display
- 6.59-inch screen
- 2768 x 1272 resolution
- 800 nits of typical brightness, peaking at 3,600 nits for HDR
I’m a large guy who likes large phones, and as such, I’ve spent the last few years daily driving the biggest phone I could get my oversized mitts on. With that said, I’ve found myself really enjoying the Find X10’s slightly smaller screen. 'Slightly' is the operative word here — at 6.59 diagonal inches, the phone isn’t much smaller than the 6.78-inch screen shared by the Find X10 Pro Max and last year’s Find X9 Pro, but it’s still a noticeable, and I dare say welcome, change.
Perhaps I shouldn’t be so surprised. Oppo has long proved itself as a maker of truly excellent displays, and the Find X10 is no different. With a resolution of 2768 x 1272 and pixel density of 460 pixels per inch, the screen on the Find X10 is even sharper than that of its bigger sibling, the Find X10 Pro Max. Oppo claims 800 nits of typical brightness, rising to 2,000 nits in high brightness mode and 3,600 nits peak for HDR content. In daily use, brightness wasn’t really a concern — the display was always legible and colorful, both indoors and outside, and with such a huge battery under the hood, I was content to let auto-brightness just do its thing.
The display also sports razor-thin bezels that measure a uniform 1.15mm around its entire edge. In practical use, they’re basically unnoticeable, which helps the slightly smaller display feel as immersive as a larger premium flagship. An adaptive 1-120Hz refresh rate keeps things feeling smooth in motion, while certain games can bump that figure up to 144Hz.
As usual, you get a choice of color profiles in the settings app — I like the ‘vivid’ look for its richer, poppier colors, though there are warmer, cooler, or more muted options to match other tastes. As is now typical for high-end phones, the Find X10's display uses an OLED panel to deliver deep blacks and excellent contrast, and I found it perfect for watching videos, playing games, and everyday browsing alike.
- Display score: 5 / 5
Oppo Find X10 review: Cameras
- 200MP main camera
- 200MP 2.8x telephoto camera
- 50MP ultra-wide camera
- 50MP selfie camera
The Find X10 makes its strongest case for a high price tag with its camera system.
With two 200MP sensors powering the main and telephoto cameras, respectively, as well as 50MP ultra-wide and selfie cameras, the Find X10 is a performant and reliable camera phone that excels at taking detailed snaps in a variety of lighting conditions.
I was impressed by just how sharp and colorful photos looked, and Oppo seems to have toned down the AI-flavored image signal processing common to its last generation of phones.
The name of the game here is consistency — no matter which lens you pick for your shot, Oppo’s hardware and software teams have clearly worked together to make the photography experience feel reliable, with similar colors, detail, and sharpness offered across the three cameras. The best synergy comes between the main and 2.8x telephoto cameras, both of which have a 200MP sensor at 1/1.4-inches and 1/1.56 inches, respectively. Both take excellent photos and offer superb detail in low light, and while neither can work miracles in pure darkness, the automatic long-exposure feature can garner impressive results.
The ultra-wide camera is smaller, with a 1/2.75-inch 50MP sensor, but it still performs well in bright situations, and serviceably in darker climes.
As standard, the Find X10 bins photos to 26MP JPEGs, but you also have the option to shoot JPEG-XL or RAW files at native resolution. The huge telephoto resolution means the Find X10 can take losslessly cropped 12MP photos at 12.4x zoom. The optional Hasselblad Teleconverter kit affixes a zoom lens to the telephoto camera, increasing the base zoom to 10x — alas, I didn’t get to test it with my review unit, but it’s worth mentioning that buying the phone from Oppo directly gives you the option of getting the kit or an Oppo Watch X3 at no extra cost.
I do, however, miss the Quick Button (Oppo’s version of the iPhone’s Camera Control) introduced with the Find X8 Pro and carried over to the Find X9 Pro. I appreciate that opinions on smartphone shutter buttons are mixed — I’ve got plenty of friends who never touch them, and TechRadar's Phones Editor, Axel Metz, has debated their value with me on more than one occasion — but I personally used the Quick Button almost every time I took a photo with the Find X9 Pro, and I loved swiping across it to access that high-quality telephoto lens.
That said, the Quick Button’s absence on the Find X10 isn’t a dealbreaker by any means, as the camera app is still one of the smoothest and best-featured I’ve used on any phone. The handset’s smaller frame also makes it easy to grab for quick snaps and videos.
