- Camera score: 5 / 5
Oppo Find X10 review: Software
- Android 17 with ColorOS 17
- Fast and reliable, though thoroughly unoriginal
- Bloatware is infuriating at this price point
ColorOS 17, Oppo’s take on Android 17, remains one of my favorite Android wrappers; it’s fast, fluid, well animated, and aesthetically clean. It’s also a clear and shameless dupe of iOS 27, right down to the Control Center-esque menus and Liquid Glass-like transparency effects. If you’re a die-hard Android user who just happens to like the look and feel of Apple phones, it’s a genuinely fantastic option, but those who want something a little more original should look elsewhere.
Debates around originality aside, I can’t overstate how much I enjoy using ColorOS. Its UI strikes the best balance between fluidity and stability of any mobile OS I’ve used. Oppo continues to use parallel animation processing, which runs each UI animation as its own task independent of other on-screen motion, and makes getting to the apps and content you need to access effortlessly fast.
Finally, ColorOS knows when to stay out of the way and when to suggest useful features like Smart Sidebar, which adds a floating dock for apps and files. It’s an impressive bit of software.
Less impressive is Oppo’s continued insistence on shipping incredibly expensive phones loaded with bloatware. On setup, I found my Find X10 review unit stuffed with apps I don’t and won’t use — TEMU, ChatGPT, BIGO LIVE, and Booking.com, among others. It is fundamentally unacceptable to ship a phone at £1,099 while patronizing users by pre-installing this nonsense, and Oppo needs to cut it out immediately.
The Find X10 also offers a few neat features for AI fans. The Snap Key on the left side of the phone is set by default to trigger Mind Space, which is sort of like a self-organizing junk drawer for your digital bits and bobs. Screenshots, notes, and reminders all end up here, processed and categorized into a searchable database. And as an upper-tier Android, the Find X10 is absolutely riddled with Gemini and first-party Oppo AI features like Circle to Search, image generation tools, and audio transcription.
- Software score: 3 / 5
Oppo Find X10 review: Performance
- MediaTek 9600M chipset
- 12GB of RAM
- Fast and fluid in all scenarios
Looking only at benchmarks, the Oppo Find X10 is a reasonable performer that runs in the middle of the pack for its price range, neither lagging behind nor pulling ahead.
As a daily driver, though, I found the Find X10 to be a perfect performer in all kinds of everyday scenarios. I suspect Oppo has optimized the heck out of this thing, as I just couldn’t get it to slow down, no matter how many apps I left open or how high I cranked the graphics settings on Call of Duty: Mobile.
The Find X10 comes with a MediaTek 9600M chipset and 12GB of RAM, both of which are fine for a phone in this price point. The iPhone 18 Pro and Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, respectively, have the A20 Pro and Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 Elite chipsets, which are a bit faster, and many of the best phones give you 16GB of RAM for smoother multitasking and on-device AI. But as mentioned, I couldn’t get the Find X10 to stutter in my varied usage, so I’m not really concerned.
I did run some benchmarks to see what the Find X10’s internal hardware is capable of. Geekbench 7 returned a single-core score of 2466 and a multi-core score of 7759, while Geekbench AI gave a quantized score of 3119. This is on track with previous- and current-gen flagships from Samsung and Apple, and a fair bit ahead of Google — but at this price point, power users might want a little more oomph.
Still, I was always happy with the Find X10 in daily use. It nails the basics, with clear calls and phenomenal haptics, while delivering enough power for all but the most demanding users.
- Performance score: 4 / 5
Oppo Find X10 review: Battery
- Battery capacity varies by region
- 8,000mAh in Asia-Pacific, 7150mAh in EU
- 80W wired charging
- 50W wireless charging
Oppo has long been a leader in the global phone market when it comes to battery life, and the Find X10 offers a serious upgrade over last year’s models… as long as you live in the Asia-Pacific region.
You see, the Find X10 comes in two regional variants: one for the aforementioned APAC region and one for the EU and the rest of the world. The former gets an 8,000mAh battery, up from the Find X9 Pro’s 7,500mAh cell, while the EU version sees a downgrade to 7,150mAh.
My review unit came with the larger 8,000mAh cell, so I can only speak to how well this version’s battery performs — and as you’d expect from a phone with a larger battery than a base-model iPad, it is truly excellent. I found it almost impossible to kill the Find X10 in a single day. I could easily get a day and a half or two days of use on a single full charge, and with cautious use, I reckon three days would be possible.
Again, I haven’t used the 7,150mAh version of the Find X10, but this is still larger than any battery an Apple, Samsung, or Google phone can offer, so expect great battery life at a minimum.
These fantastic results are due to Oppo’s use of silicon-carbon batteries, a technology the brand has long championed and continues to push forward. Silicon-carbon isn’t without its controversies, and some commentators doubt its long-term durability versus the typical lithium-ion batteries you’ll find in the best iPhones and many of the best Android phones — but for those who want all-day battery life with plenty of power to spare, the benefits are obvious.
When it comes to charging, the Find X10 benefits from Oppo’s proprietary SuperVOOC charging tech, with support for up to 80W wired charging or 50W wireless charging. The bundled wired charger hits that 80W mark, and charging is therefore relatively speedy; the sheer size of the Find X10’s battery means this isn’t the fastest-charging phone on the market, but its heft also means that a charge to 50% goes further than it would with Western competitors. It took me around 1:15h to charge from empty to full.
- Battery score: 5 / 5
Should you buy the Oppo Find X10?
| Oppo Find X10 scorecard |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
|---|---|---|
| Value | The Oppo Find X10 isn't cheap by any means. It's certainly a lot of phone, but the era of Oppo undercutting the competition is over. | 3 / 5 | 
| Design | Undeniably beautiful, but completely indebted to Apple's design language. Sturdy with great color options. | 4 / 5 | 
| Display | The Find X10 is a little smaller than its Pro Max sibling, but still feels immersive thanks to a sharp resolution, vivid colors, and thin bezels. | 5 / 5 | 
| Software | One of the best deployments of Android, inexcusably marred by the presence of bloatware. Once you clear the crap, it's terrific. | 3 / 5 | 
| Camera | A truly superb camera system with subtler post-processing than prior generations. The 200MP main and telephoto cameras are class-leading. | 5 / 5 | 
| Performance | The Find X10 runs with the pack performance-wise. It's what we'd expect to see from a phone of this price. | 4 / 5 | 
| Battery | Truly ludicrous battery life meets phenomenally quick charging. A battery champ by any measure. | 5 / 5 | 
Buy it if
You want a great camera phone
With three powerful cameras and superbly balanced post-processing, the Find X10 is a reliable pick for photos and videos. Lossless crops up to 12.6x and 200MP main and telephoto cameras make this one of the best camera phones I've used.
You want fantastic battery life
Whichever regional variant of the Find X10 you get, its battery is one of the largest in any smartphone. Add in rapid charging from the bundled wired charger and you’re unlikely to ever see it power down.
You want Apple-like looks with Android power
Originality isn’t Oppo’s strong suit, but if you’re a committed Googler who enjoys the simplicity and subtlety of Apple’s aesthetics, ColorOS is a solid alternative that runs smoothly in all kinds of scenarios.
Don't buy it if
You’re on a budget
Though prices have risen across the industry, the Find X10 is still both relatively and absolutely expensive — £1,099 is a lot of money, close to the price of an older phone plus a tablet or an entry-level laptop.
You hate bloatware
Oppo, if you’re reading this, I’m never going to let you off the hook for shoving bloatware nonsense onto a four-figure phone. Yes, these apps can be removed, but if you’re the type of person who likes a clean setup experience, the random apps and recommendations built into the Find X10 could be a serious turnoff.
Also consider
Google Pixel 11
If you want a fast and flexible Android phone that keeps the simple things simple while pushing new software and AI tools, the Google Pixel 11 gets you access to the latest Google features before anyone else while still sporting a triple-camera setup and modern design.
Read our hands-on Google Pixel 11 review
iPhone 18 Pro
The Oppo Find X10 looks and feels like an iPhone, but for some users, only the real thing will do. The iPhone 18 Pro is smaller than the Find X10, with lower-res cameras and a smaller battery, but it does give you access to Apple’s ecosystem and still has its Camera Control shutter button.
Read our full iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max review
OnePlus 15
With the OnePlus 16 stuck in China for now, the latest globally available flagship from Oppo’s sister brand remains the OnePlus 15. No complaints from us, though — the OnePlus 15 still reigns as the best Android phone in our rankings, thanks to its huge battery, excellent cameras, and large, high-resolution display.
Read our full OnePlus 15 review
How I tested the Oppo Find X10
☑️ 100s of smartphones reviewed
☑️ 15 years of product testing
☑️ Over 16,000 products reviewed in total
☑️ Nearly 200,000 hours testing tech
I used the Oppo Find X10 in a variety of everyday and test situations for this review. I used it as a daily driver for calls, texts, and social media, took it on dedicated photo walks, played games, and ran benchmarks to stress-test the CPU and AI abilities. I left as many apps open as I could to see how it held up to multitasking, and monitored battery life over the course of days and nights out.
I then applied my experience reviewing phones and journalistic training to provide an assessment of the phone's capabilities and value offering.
First tested October 2026
Jamie is freelance journalist who has written for TechRadar and MusicRadar as well as various specialist news outlets and music blogs. A lifelong tech-obsessive, Jamie began his writing career as a music blogger before studying journalism at Goldsmiths College, and worked at TechRadar between 2024 and 2026. He thinks the iPhone 5S is the greatest phone of all time, but is currently an Android user.

articles.title: Amazon casse le prix de cette batterie externe qui possède une base de recharge sans fil
articles.text:
L’Anker MagGo se présente avec un port USB-C de 27 W et un support sans fil de 15 W pour venir y brancher deux appareils simultanément. Sur Amazon, elle se décharge de presque 25 euros.
À l’approche d’Halloween, il est possible que vous vous rendiez à une soirée déguisée. Par conséquent, il est probable que votre smartphone tombe à court de charge. Pour éviter que ce problème n’arrive, cette batterie Anker perd 31 % de son prix sur Amazon. Parmi les points forts de l’objet, il y a ce format compact qui permet de glisser l’appareil et votre smartphone dans votre poche.
Sur Amazon, l’Anker MagGo passe de 79,99 euros à 59,09 euros
Pourquoi choisir l’Anker MagGo ?
- Une batterie parfaite pour une soirée : Avec sa capacité de 10 000 mAh, l’Anker MagGo pourra recharger presque deux fois un iPhone 17 et une fois un iPhone 17 Pro Max.
- Un design passe-partout : Compatible avec la charge sans fil, vous pourrez coller la batterie au smartphone et glisser le tout dans votre poche. Vous pourrez poser votre téléphone dessus grâce au petit support incliné.
- Un écran intelligent : L’Anker MagGo dispose d’un petit écran intelligent pour suivre le temps de charge restant ainsi que l’autonomie de la batterie.
Parfaite pour une soirée
L’Anker MagGo reste une batterie d'appoint qui pourra vous servir lors d’un concert ou d’une journée à la plage. Elle se présente avec un port USB-C qui fournit une puissance de charge de 27 W, mais aussi un support sans fil de 15 W pour les appareils compatibles comme les récents Google Pixel. Selon votre choix de charge, vous pourrez recharger entièrement votre smartphone en moins d'une heure.
Ainsi, vous pourrez recharger deux appareils simultanément grâce à cette batterie de 10 000 mAh. Si vous ne branchez que votre iPhone 17 Pro Max, vous pourrez le recharger plus d'une fois et presque deux fois s’il s’agit d'un iPhone 17.
Un écran pour faire la différence
Anker possède aussi dans sa gamme un modèle similaire à cette Anker MagGo, du moins en ce qui concerne les performances puisque la MagGo coûte 20 euros de plus. Cette différence de prix s’explique par la présence de ce petit support pour poser le smartphone à la verticale lorsque vous le rechargez sans fil.
Autre différence, ce petit écran situé sur une des tranches de la batterie. Il indique l’autonomie restante de l’appareil, mais aussi le temps d’utilisation restant.
Cependant, ces ajouts ne sont pas indispensables et si vous chargez une batterie simplement pour recharger votre smartphone, vous pourrez vous arrêter sur le produit disponible autour de 35 euros.
✅ Les points forts
- Un écran intelligent
- Un support pour pouvoir poser le smartphone à la verticale
- L'ActiveShield 2.0 pour réguler la température
❌ Les limites
- Qu’un seul port de charge USB-C
- Une charge contenue à 27 W
L’Anker MagGo passe de 79,99 euros à 59,09 euros sur le site d’Amazon
Avec l’Anker MagGo, la marque élargit sa gamme avec une batterie externe portable qui se dote d’un écran latéral pour fournir différentes informations.
Néanmoins, à force de multiplier les produits similaires, il est difficile de s’y retrouver. Si l’écran et le support sont intéressants, ils ne permettent pas à la batterie d’être un produit indispensable de la marque.

articles.title: PHP lanzó parches de emergencia para dos fallas críticas que amenazan a millones de sitios web
articles.text:
El equipo de seguridad de PHP, el lenguaje de programación que funciona detrás de la mayoría de los sitios de internet, anunció un parche de emergencia para dos fallas críticas que podrían permitir a un atacante tomar el control de un servidor sin necesidad de ninguna contraseña.
El aviso oficial, publicado el martes en el sitio php.net, calificó ambas vulnerabilidades con una puntuación de 9,2 sobre 10 en la escala CVSS, el sistema que la industria usa para medir la gravedad de una falla de seguridad. La actualización estaba prevista para las 14:00 UTC de este miércoles.
PHP es el motor detrás de WordPress, Drupal, Joomla y Magento, además de paneles de control de alojamiento y software que ni siquiera anuncia que lo usa por dentro. Según la consultora W3Techs, el lenguaje sostiene cerca del 70% de los sitios web cuyo programa de servidor se puede identificar.
Las dos fallas permitirían ejecutar código de forma remota: que un atacante logre que el servidor corra las órdenes que él mismo escriba, sin haber iniciado sesión, según coincidieron varios investigadores. PHP no detalló qué parte del lenguaje está afectada ni qué configuración activa el problema, y dijo que esa información llegaría recién con el parche.
El organismo de ciberseguridad de la Unión Europea, CERT-EU, recomendó a las organizaciones que no puedan aplicar la actualización de inmediato que consideren desconectar sus sitios de internet hasta tener el parche instalado. El Centro Nacional de Ciberseguridad del Reino Unido y la agencia equivalente de Australia emitieron alertas similares.
Una filtración apuró el calendario
El anuncio llegó antes de lo previsto porque la información se filtró. La empresa de investigación watchTowr confirmó en la red social X que los detalles de las fallas, pensados para revelarse recién el jueves bajo un acuerdo de divulgación coordinada con otros investigadores, se conocieron un día antes por una publicación anónima.
watchTowr dijo que las vulnerabilidades son reales y que logró reproducir una de ellas en un entorno de prueba, aunque decidió no difundir los detalles técnicos hasta que el parche esté disponible. La empresa de seguridad Huntress, por su parte, afirmó que hasta el martes no había detectado que las fallas estuvieran siendo explotadas en los sistemas de sus clientes.
Esa calma no duró. El director de tecnología de Cloudflare, Dane Knecht, escribió en X que la compañía ya veía “ataques tempranos” contra sus clientes y que había desplegado reglas de protección automática como medida provisoria. “Esto es solo un parche temporal. Actualicen apenas PHP libere la solución”, escribió.
Los sitios más viejos quedarán sin arreglo
El parche solo llegará a las versiones que PHP todavía mantiene activas, de la 8.2 a la 8.5. Las versiones 5, 7 y las primeras ramas de la serie 8 no reciben soporte de seguridad desde hace tiempo: sus usuarios no tendrán solución oficial y deberán migrar a una versión reciente o aislar esos servidores de internet.
La firma de seguridad Mallory calculó, a partir de un relevamiento del buscador Shodan, que unos 884.000 servidores expuestos a internet corren versiones de PHP que no recibirán el parche. Según un informe de la empresa Censys citado por Cybernews, solo el 14% de los sitios públicos de WordPress tiene instalada la última actualización disponible.
Esa combinación, advirtieron varios especialistas consultados por medios especializados, deja una ventana amplia para que los atacantes apunten a servidores desactualizados una vez publicado el parche: comparar el código antes y después de una actualización suele ser, para quien busca explotar una falla, la forma más rápida de entender cómo funciona.
Empresas de alojamiento como GoDaddy y servicios de protección para WordPress como Wordfence publicaron guías para que los administradores de sitios identifiquen qué versión de PHP usan y se preparen para instalar la actualización apenas esté disponible. Ninguna ofreció, por ahora, una solución alternativa que reemplace al parche oficial.
PHP confirmó que junto con el lanzamiento, programado para hoy, dará a conocer qué partes del lenguaje estaban afectadas, qué versiones exactas corrían riesgo y los números de las versiones corregidas, información que hasta el cierre de esta nota seguía sin confirmarse de forma oficial.

articles.title: CISA Orders Federal Agencies to Patch Exploited Plex2Shell, Siemens, and SiteGuard Flaws
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Tuesday added four vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, including four vulnerabilities impacting Plex Media Server that's collectively called Plex2Shell.
The vulnerabilities are listed below -
- CVE-2026-96652 (CVSS score: 5.3) - Plex Media Server Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability
- CVE-2026-96654 (CVSS score: 6.9) - Plex Media Server improper neutralization of encoded URI schemes in a web page Vulnerability
- CVE-2026-96655 (CVSS score: 5.3) - Plex Media Server Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability
- CVE-2026-96656 (CVSS score: 8.6) - Plex Media Server external control of file name or path Vulnerability
According to security researcher Zach Main, who discovered and reported the vulnerabilities, a remote attacker could chain the four vulnerabilities to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution. The issues were addressed in Plex Media Server 1.43.3.10861 released on August 3, 2026.
The addition of the four vulnerabilities to the KEV catalog follows a report from security researcher boredhackerblog, who found that threat actors are weaponizing the flaws to deploy cryptocurrency miners and proxy malware.
CISA has also flagged two other vulnerabilities as actively exploited. One of them is a DLL sideloading vulnerability in Siemens Software Center (CVE-2026-110936, CVSS score: 8.4) that has been abused in ClickFix attacks using a platform called Romulus.
The second security flaw is a command injection bug in EG Secure Solutions SiteGuard Server Edition (CVE-2026-106931, CVSS score: 8.5) that the Japanese company confirmed as being exploited. No additional details related to the exploitation activity are currently available.
CISA is urging Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies to apply fixes for CVE-2026-106931, CVE-2026-96656, and CVE-2026-96654 by October 23, 2026, and the rest by November 3, 2026.

articles.title: Oppo Find X10 et Find X10 Pro Max : triple capteur 200 Mpx, batterie XXL… et des prix qui piquent
articles.text:
Oppo Find X10 et Find X10 Pro Max : triple capteur 200 Mpx, batterie XXL… et des prix qui piquent
Avec ses nouveaux smartphones haut de gamme, Oppo mise sur la photo et l’endurance. Mais, alors que la facture s'alourdit, lequel des deux vaut vraiment le détour ?
Présentés ce 21 octobre sous le soleil de Majorque, les nouveaux Oppo Find X10 et Find X10 Pro Max promettent de belles photos sans passer par la case retouche. Voyons également ce qu’ils ont dans le ventre, car la facture s’avère salée.
Oppo Find X10 Pro Max
Deux formats, une fiche technique solide
L’Oppo Find X10 mesure 156,51 × 74,29 × 8,35 mm pour 210 g ; le Pro Max atteint 161,32 × 76,57 × 8,40 mm et 226 à 228 g. Leur dos en verre épouse le bloc photo et se décline en plusieurs coloris : Glacier Blue, Glow Coral ou Mist Gray pour le premier ; Titanium Grey ou Luna White bicolore pour le second. Tous deux ont une âme de baroudeur, profitant des certifications IP66/68/69 et cinq étoiles SGS contre les chutes.
Leurs écrans Amoled de 6,59 et 6,78 pouces bénéficient d’un taux de rafraîchissement jusqu’à 144 Hz dans certains jeux et atteignent, à en croire la marque chinoise, une luminosité maximale de 3600 cd/m². Une promesse que nous mettrons à l'épreuve de nos sondes dans les prochains jours. Sous le capot, on trouve enfin une puce MediaTek Dimensity 9600M (3 nm) ou 9600 Pro (2 nm), 12 Go de RAM et 256/512 Go de stockage pour le X10, 512 Go pour le Pro Max.
La photo, leur vrai terrain de jeu
L’Oppo Find X10 associe deux capteurs de 200 mégapixels (principal et zoom) à un ultra grand-angle de 50 Mpx. Le Pro Max, une première selon le constructeur, passe à un triple module dorsal de 200 Mpx, dont un ultra grand-angle de 124° et un téléobjectif capable de faire de la macro à 10 cm. Les deux proposent une caméra selfie de 50 Mpx, des clichés assez lourds de 26 Mpx par défaut et, en option, un téléconvertisseur Hasselblad x3,28 pour viser loin.
Le traitement LUMO et le capteur True Color promettent de garder des couleurs et des ombres crédibles mais le résultat n’esquive pas un lissage par IA. En vidéo, le X10 filme en 8K à 30 images par seconde ou 4K à 120 i/s sur ses deux capteurs de 200 Mpx ; le Pro Max le fait avec ses trois modules arrière. Dolby Vision, mode Open Gate, Blackmagic Camera optimisée en novembre, accessoires Tilta sur le Pro Max et partage Instagram optimisé complètent l’arsenal.
Une grosse batterie contre une grosse facture
Les deux modèles embarquent une batterie d’une capacité de 7150 mAh, avec jusqu’à deux jours d’autonomie annoncée, 80 % de capacité après cinq ans, et compatible avec la charge SUPERVOOC à 80 W en filaire ou AIRVOOC 50 W sans-fil. Wifi 7, Bluetooth 6.2, NFC, double SIM, USB 3.2 et haut-parleurs stéréo sont au menu, tout comme une touche raccourci personnalisable type Bouton Action.
ColorOS 17 (Android 17) ajoute AI Mind Pilot pour organiser ses tâches et AI Photo Agent pour retoucher sur demande, selon le déploiement local. Comptez 1299 € (256 Go) ou 1499 € (512 Go) pour le Find X10 et 1799 € (512 Go) pour le Pro Max, soit 500 € de plus que le Find X9 Pro qui profitait de 16 Go de RAM, contre 12 Go désormais, et seulement 100 € d'écart avec le X9 Ultra à sa sortie. Oppo propose néanmoins 100 € de remise et, selon les stocks, un téléconvertisseur, une tablette Pad 5 ou une Watch X3 pour toute précommande. Cela suffira-t-il à convaincre ? Rien n'est moins sûr.

articles.title: The Oppo Find X10 Pro Max has some of the best cameras I've ever tested — but they come at an extremely high price
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Oppo Find X10 Pro Max is easily one of the best phones of 2026. Whether you're looking for top-tier performance, cameras, software features, or endurance, this phone has it all. I absolutely love the Find X10 Pro Max, and its only real downside is its sky-high price tag.
Reasons to buy
- + Zero-compromise triple 200MP camera system
- + Incredible video features
- + Great performance and battery life
- + Slick, feature-packed software
Reasons to avoid
- - It's more expensive than the X9 Pro
- - ... and has less RAM
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Oppo Find X10 Pro Max: Two-minute review
The Oppo Find X9 Pro was my favorite phone of 2025, so of course, I had extremely high hopes for the X10 series. Interestingly, Oppo hasn't released an X10 Pro in 2026 — instead, there's just an Oppo Find X10 and an X10 Pro Max.
The Pro Max isn't larger than last year's Pro, but it is larger than the X10. If I had to hazard a guess as to why the name has changed, I reckon the RAM shortage-induced price hike might have something to do with it.
That aside, the Find X10 Pro Max does not disappoint. The star of the show is the new camera system, which now features three large 200MP sensors on the rear. The new model also gets a chip upgrade, a larger battery (in some regions), and a faster, professionally calibrated display.
After using this phone for about three weeks, I find myself with almost no complaints. It's super fast, the software is superb, battery life is excellent (I have the larger-capacity version), and the cameras are some of the best on the market.
Honestly, the Find X10 Pro Max's cameras are so impressive that there's a case to be made for picking up this device over a compact point-and-shoot or a vlogging camera. The fact that it's also a phone only sweetens the deal. As a content creator who likes to travel light, it's a dream come true.
What sets the X10 Pro Max's cameras apart is that you can use any lens in any situation without compromising quality. They all share the same 200MP resolution, and they're all at least 1/1.56-inch sensors, so they handle low-light conditions well. The same goes for video, where each lens can capture at up to 8K/30fps or 4K/120fps, and each supports open-gate capture, Log recording, and Dolby Vision. Even the selfie camera is impressive, offering a super-wide field-of-view and reliable autofocus.
Cameras aside, everything else about the Find X10 Pro Max is great, too. Its display is bright and speedy, its software is among the best around, and it games like a champ.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The only real sticking point is the price (spoiler: it's very, very expensive), but if you can stomach the cost, the Find X10 Pro Max is an extremely easy recommendation.
Oppo Find X10 Pro Max review: Price and availability
- £1,499 for 12GB + 512GB
- Introductory offers and bundles available
- Not sold in the US; Australia availability TBC
The globally available version of the Oppo Find X10 Pro Max only comes in one configuration: 12GB of RAM with 512GB of storage.
As ever, it won't launch in the US, but everywhere else, it'll cost you a pretty penny; the Find X10 Pro Max starts at an eye-watering £1,499 in the UK.
Of course, we have the component shortage going on, so a feature-packed flagship like this was never going to be cheap, and this is a higher price point than most were expecting. Still, the Find X9 Pro launched at £1,099 in the UK, so if you see the Find X10 Pro Max as its successor (which I do), that's a £400 price hike.
That said, the 512GB iPhone 18 Pro Max also costs £1,499, and the 512GB Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra costs even more. Meanwhile, the Find X10 Pro Max's spec sheet is in a completely different league, so perhaps this isn't such an outlandish sum after all.
If you're in the UK, there are some tempting introductory deals to help soften the blow. For a limited time, Oppo is offering £100 off the Find X10 Pro Max, plus you can grab a free accessory worth £500. Options include the Hasselblad Teleconverter kit, Oppo Watch X3, or Oppo Pad 5. Other regions will likely have similar offers.
- Value score: 3 / 5
Oppo Find X10 Pro Max: Specs
Here’s a look at the Oppo Find X10 Pro Max’s key specs:
| Row 0 - Cell 0 | Oppo Find X10 Pro Max | 
| Dimensions | 161.32 × 76.57 × 8.40mm | 
| Weight | 226g | 
| OS | Color OS 17, based on Android 17 | 
| Display | 6.78-inch OLED, 144Hz | 
| Resolution | 2772 × 1272 pixels | 
| Chipset | MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro | 
| RAM | 12GB | 
| Storage | 512GB | 
| Battery | 7,150mAh (Europe) / 8,000mAh (APAC) | 
| Rear cameras | 200MP (f/1.5) main, 200MP (f/2.2) ultra-wide, 200MP 3x telephoto (f/2.1) | 
| Front camera | 50MP (f/2) | 
Oppo Find X10 Pro Max review: Design
- Aluminum frame and glass back
- Titanium Grey and Lunar White options
- IP69 dust- and water-resistant
When I first saw the design of the Find X10 Pro Max, I wasn't quite convinced, but it has grown on me over time. It shares some DNA with the Find X9 series, but the camera bump has grown larger, and the lenses are now covered by a single dark pane of glass.
The Find X9 Pro was already a little iPhone-inspired, but that's perhaps even more noticeable with the Titanium Grey X10 Pro Max, which has a raised platform spanning most of the upper rear panel — just like the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro.
The Luna White model (which is the one I have) looks a little more unique. It has a two-tone rear panel, while the camera island and the module containing the flash and color sensor are completely separated, with no platform underneath.
It's a little quirky, but it's nothing too outlandish, and I've grown to like it a lot. Crucially, having the cameras shoved up in the corner (rather than being in a central circle like on the Vivo X500 Pro Max) means that this phone works really well with MagSafe accessories. And while we still don't get magnets built into the Find X10 Pro Max itself, almost all of Oppo's official cases come with magnets.
Oppo has ditched the somewhat controversial Camera Control clone, but it kept the Action Button (which Oppo calls the Snap Key). It's not a popular stance, but I actually quite liked the Camera Control, and I'll miss it, but I'm very aware that I'm in the minority there.
The Snap Key is great, too, but Oppo's implementation is on the basic side. It can be assigned to access a number of features, like the flashlight, translation, camera, and Mind Space, but you still can't choose your own app. There are also no options for double- or triple-press actions, as we've seen from some competitors.
Otherwise, the Oppo Find X10 Pro Max has the typical flagship look and feel. You get flat aluminum side rails, and a flat front and rear made from Oppo's own Crystal Guard Glass (co-developed with Corning). It's a sizable phone with a bit of heft to it, but I'm used to that, and I felt immediately at home when picking it up for the first time.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
It's hard to speak much about the durability, as I haven't tortured my device much, but on paper, the Find X10 Pro Max should handle the elements well. It's IP69 rated for dust and water resistance, and it has an SGS Five Star Drop Resistance Certification, too.
The phone comes with a basic opaque white TPU case in the box, a factory-installed screen protector, a charger, and a USB-C Cable — although I expect the charger inclusion might differ from region to region.
- Design score: 4 / 5
Oppo Find X10 Pro Max review: Display
- 6.78-inch 120Hz LTPO OLED
- Can boost to 144Hz in some games
- 3,600 nits, 3,840Hz PWM
The display on the Find X10 Pro Max is nothing short of excellent. It has super-slim symmetrical bezels that measure just 1.15mm on each side. That's the same size as the bezels on the Find X9 Pro, but it's just as impressive to see such thinness the second time around.
What is new on the Find X10 Pro Max is the refresh rate. It can dynamically adjust between 1 and 144Hz as required. Oppo admits that only a few games will take advantage of the full 144Hz, like COD: Mobile, PUBG, and Free Fire, and you won't see such high refresh rates outside of those titles. Still, if you play those, it's a great perk.
As for brightness, it peaks at 3,600 nits, just like last year's model. In my experience, that's more than enough for just about any situation. What I find even more useful is the fact that it can dim down to 1nit for late-night scrolling without melting your eyeballs.
On the topic of eye health, the Oppo Find X10 Pro Max supports 3,840Hz high-frequency PWM dimming to prevent screen flicker at lower brightness levels. Above 70Hz, it'll switch to full DC dimming. If you're sensitive to flicker, you'll really appreciate this feature.
One thing that's pretty unique to the X10 Pro Max is that the screen is professionally calibrated and covers 95% of the BT.2020 wide color space — that's 40% more color coverage than most phone screens, which usually target DCI-P3 instead.
As a result, while the image might not look as vibrant or poppy as some competitors, you can be assured that the colors displayed are accurate. That makes a lot of sense on a content-creation powerhouse such as the Find X10 Pro Max, and I appreciate it.
- Display score: 5 / 5
Xiaomi 17T Pro review: Cameras
- 200MP f/1.5 main (1/1.3-inch)
- 200MP f/2.2 ultra-wide (1/1.56-inch)
- 200MP f/2.1 3x telephoto (1/1.56-inch)
- 50MP f/2 selfie camera (1/2.75-inch)
The Oppo Find X10 Pro Max takes a fresh, zero-compromise approach to the camera system. All three rear cameras have a 200MP resolution, and they all have large sensors, too.
Usually, you have a primary camera that's the best of the bunch, while the telephoto and ultra-wide come with compromises — I wouldn't recommend shooting low-light photos with most ultra-wide cameras, or with that tiny 3x telephoto on the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, for instance.
With the Find X10 Pro Max, you don't need to worry about compromises; just pick the right focal length for the scene and snap away. It reminds me of the Vivo X300 Ultra (which has even larger sensors on all three rear cameras), but even that beast makes a compromise with the ultra-wide's resolution.
The Find X10 Pro Max's selfie camera shares most of its specifications with that of last year's X9 Pro, but it has a wider field of view (similar to the ultra-wide on the back), so it's much better for group photos. Reliable autofocus helps in that regard, too. Of course, if you want a normal selfie, the camera UI lets you crop in to a standard FOV.
The Oppo Find X9 Ultra has been my favorite phone for photography since launch, and the Find X10 Pro Max shares a lot of the same DNA. The pro-focused Master Mode is what truly stole my heart, and thankfully, Oppo is extending that joy elsewhere.
The standard photo mode now uses the same tone mapping as Master Mode, and the sharpening and noise reduction have been dialled back a little, too. It's still a very different look to Master Mode — it's still sharpened much more heavily, and the HDR effect is more pronounced — but it's much more natural than before, and I think it's a change for the better.
The picture styles have been reworked on the Find X10 Pro Max, too. They're available in most modes, and they're all extremely customizable, with their own tone pad (like on the latest iPhones) as well as individual adjustment sliders. Primrose is my favorite, which simulates the look of Portra film stock, but there are plenty of other excellent options, too.
To summarize my experience with photography, the Oppo Find X10 Pro Max is unquestionably among the best camera phones, regardless of lighting conditions. The X9 Ultra is really the only phone that beats it. The Ultra still has the edge with long-range zoom and low-light capture, unless we're talking about the ultra-wide camera, in which case the Pro Max easily comes out on top.
Now, photography is only one part of the puzzle, because Oppo put a lot of effort into this phone's video capabilities, too. Again, consistency is the name of the game here.
All three rear lenses can shoot up to 8K/30fps or 4K/120fps, and they all support open-gate capture at up to 60fps. The same goes for Log recording and Dolby Vision. Just use whatever focal length feels right for the occasion, because they can all do everything.
The Find X10 Pro Max is a seriously capable video-making tool. Solid stabilization and microphone performance add to the appeal, too. If you make YouTube content using your phone, this device should definitely be on your shortlist.
If all that wasn't enough, Oppo also has an external (10x equivalent) teleconverter kit for the Find X10 Pro Max, so you can push the zoom even further, or use it on closer subjects for DSLR-like compression and bokeh. There's also a full-on video rig developed with Tilta, if you want to fully transform this phone into a video workhorse.
- Cameras score: 5 / 5

Oppo Find X10 Pro Max review: Performance
- MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro chipset
- 12GB RAM
- 512GB storage
The Oppo Find X10 Pro Max is powered by MediaTek's latest flagship chip, the Dimensity 9600 Pro. In most situations, it beats the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 on performance and efficiency, and it trades blows with the new 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, too.
For the globally released version, the Find X10 Pro Max only comes in one configuration: 12GB of RAM and 512GB of storage. That's less RAM than last year, and of course, we have the data centre-driven shortage to thank for that. Still, these capacities are more than sufficient for my needs — the Find X10 Pro Max never skipped a beat, even under heavy multitasking pressure.
It won't be surprising to hear that the Find X10 Pro Max feels incredibly quick, no matter what you ask of it. You have to boot up a seriously demanding game to get the phone to break a sweat.
For this purpose, I put a few hours into Neverness to Everness, which has a detailed urban open-world map that makes some phones chug. The Find X10 Pro Max, though, can run it at 60fps on the highest graphics preset without issue.
The phone's frame does get fairly hot after a while, but the performance seems steady enough. In reality, that just means the cooling system is doing its job, drawing heat away from the chip. If you use a case or a gaming grip, it won't bother you in the slightest.
Gamers will have a great time with the Find X10 Pro Max, and other phones are unlikely to come close to the performance limits of this hardware. It's great.
- Performance score: 4 / 5
Oppo Find X10 Pro Max review: Software
- ColorOS 17, based on Android 17
- Fresh design and new animations
- New Mind Space and AI features
The Oppo Find X10 Pro Max runs ColorOS 17, Oppo's take on Android 17. I have become a big fan of this operating system over the past couple of years, and it's a big part of the reason that I daily-drive an Oppo phone.
The latest version doesn't stray too far from the winning formula, but it has been spruced up a bit. The animations have been refined with some extra elasticity that makes interactions feel even more natural. Plus, there are subtle new glowing touches that appear over the Liquid Glass-esque quick settings and notification shades. It's not a dramatic change, but it's an extra bit of polish that you'll notice.
There's a lot of Apple influence in the styling, but I'm fine with that. Apple has always been strong in the design department, and while Oppo's approach isn't too novel, it does look great. Plus, if there's anything you don't like in ColorOS, it's all very easy to customize.
Oppo has been putting a lot of effort into making its software feel smooth, and the OS now apparently uses up to 25% less RAM than previous versions. Apps should open slightly faster, and Oppo says its software should maintain this smooth operation even when your storage fills up — but I haven't come close to doing that just yet.
Of course, there are loads of AI tools built into the Find X10 Pro Max. There's plenty that we've already seen, like Mind Space, which organizes your screenshots into searchable collections with AI summaries, and there are some new additions, too.
For instance, there's a new tool called AI Photo Agent, which lets you edit your pictures using natural language prompts. Plus, it can give suggestions for edits that might look good, or attempt to recreate the style of another image.
As with anything involving AI, the results can be a bit of a mixed bag, but on occasion, AI Photo Agent works really well. You can do anything you can dream up, from subtle color adjustments to background replacement, subject removal, subject addition — you name it, AI Photo Agent can do it.
There's also something called AI Mind Pilot, which is designed for AI super freaks. It pulls models from Gemini, Perplexity, and OpenAI all into one app, so you can ask the same question to a chorus of chatbots, or switch between them as you see fit.
Mind Pilot was already available on the X9 Ultra, but this version now has more agentic capabilities. The AI can find files and photos from around your phone, move them, rename them, or even create something with them, like a presentation or a collage.
- Software score: 4 / 5
Oppo Find X10 Pro Max review: Battery
- 7,150mAh battery (EU) / 8,000mAh (APAC)
- 80W wired charging
- 50W wireless charging
The battery situation with the Find X10 Pro Max is a little complicated. If you live in Asia, Australia, or the Middle East, you'll get a mammoth 8,000mAh battery pack. Meanwhile, in Europe, shipping regulations mean that you'll only get a 7,150mAh-capacity cell.
There's nothing unusual about that, except for the fact that I have the 8,000mAh version of the Find X10 Pro Max, despite living in the UK. This means that any of my observations about battery life only apply to the APAC version of the phone. Relevant to some of you, less relevant to others.
Unsurprisingly, with an 8,000mAh pack inside, the Find X10 Pro Max's battery life has been excellent. I'm consistently getting at least a day and a half of use per charge, despite lots of camera use and gaming. Two days on a charge is easily achievable, too.
Charging is also pretty quick. You'll get up to 80W speeds with the official adapter or 55W with third-party USB-PD chargers. It'll still take well over an hour to charge from completely flat to full, but that's understandable with such a large capacity.
- Battery score: 4 / 5
Should you buy the Oppo Find X10 Pro Max?
| Oppo Find X10 Pro Max scorecard |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
|---|---|---|
| Value | The Find X10 Pro Max is expensive, especially compared to its predecessor. It's now roughly the same price as the iPhone 18 Pro Max and S26 Ultra. It's not a bargain, but it's not a rip-off, either. | 3 / 5 | 
| Design | The Oppo Find X10 Pro Max manages to look unique without being outlandish. Meanwhile, IP69 protection and quality materials mean it should last long-term. | 4 / 5 | 
| Display | Super-slim bezels, a speedy refresh rate, and a bright output make this screen a delight to live with. | 5 / 5 | 
| Cameras | No other camera system is as balanced as this. Large 200MP sensors on every camera make for unmatched versatility. | 5 / 5 | 
| Performance | This phone games like the best of them. The slight RAM downgrade is a shame, though. | 4 / 5 | 
| Software | ColorOS is smooth, good-looking, and feature-packed. Software support terms don't match the best in the biz, though. | 4 / 5 | 
| Battery | My battery life has been exceptional; however, I have the larger 8,000mAh version. It's a shame that the EU gets a downgrade. | 4 / 5 | 
Buy it if...
You want a no-compromise camera beast
The Oppo Find X10 Pro Max has one of the best camera systems of any smartphone. The triple 200MP rear setup with large sensors all around means that you can use any lens on any occasion. If that's not enough, the selfie camera is excellent, and the video features are among the best around.
You want an exceptional all-rounder
The Find X10 Pro Max isn't just about the cameras; the gaming performance is great, the software is brilliant, and the battery life is top-tier, too. No matter what you want from your phone, you'll likely find it here.
Don't buy it if...
You already have the Oppo Find X9 Ultra
The Find X9 Ultra beats the X10 Pro Max in both long-range zoom and low-light photography with its larger main and 3x telephoto sensors. That said, the X10 Pro Max has a far better ultra-wide camera and some additional video features. Many will feel that it's a sideways move, rather than an upgrade.
You want something compact and lightweight
There's no getting around the fact that this is a fairly large, chunky, and weighty phone. If you're looking for something that you'll barely feel in your pocket, you should look elsewhere.
Oppo Find X10 Pro Max review: Also consider
The Oppo Find X10 Pro Max is one of the best camera-focused flagship phones, but it's important to consider the competition, too. Here are a couple of competitors that are worth looking at:
Vivo X500 Pro Max
While it hasn't been released globally just yet, we've tried the Chinese version of the Vivo X500 Pro Max, and it's definitely the closest competitor to the X10 Pro Max. The two trade blows in almost every respect, and both have external teleconverters to expand their capabilities. I feel like the X10 Pro Max is more well-rounded, but the Vivo has some incredible video features that could sway you.
Read our hands-on Vivo X500 Pro Max review
Oppo Find X9 Ultra
Oppo's own X9 Ultra is one of the few phones that can truly beat the cameras of the X10 Pro Max. The main reason is the dedicated 10x telephoto camera, but larger sensors on the main and 3x help in low light, too. On the other hand, the X10 Pro Max's ultra-wide is far superior.
Read our full Oppo Find X9 Ultra review
| Header Cell - Column 0 | Oppo Find X10 Pro Max | Vivo X500 Pro Max | Oppo Find X9 Ultra | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Price: | £1,499 | TBC | £1,449 | 
| Display: | 6.78-inch OLED | 6.85-inch OLED | 6.82-inch OLED | 
| Cameras: | 200MP main; 200MP ultrawide; 200MP telephoto | 50MP main; 50MP ultra-wide; 200MP telephoto | 200MP main; 50MP ultra-wide; 200MP 3x telephoto; 50MP 10x telephoto | 
| Processor: | MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro | MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro | Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 | 
| Battery: | 8,000mAh / 7,150mAh (EU) | 8,000mAh (CN) / 6,800mAh (EU) | 7,050mAh | 
How I tested the Oppo Find X10 Pro Max
- Review test period: Three weeks
- Testing included: Everyday use, including web browsing, social media, photography, video calling, gaming, streaming video, music playback
- Tools used: Geekbench 7, 3DMark, native Android stats
☑️ 100s of smartphones reviewed
☑️ 15 years of product testing
☑️ Over 16,000 products reviewed in total
☑️ Nearly 200,000 hours testing tech
I put my SIM card into the Oppo Find X10 Pro Max and used it as my main phone for over three weeks. I used it exactly as I would use any other phone, taking lots of photos, gaming, messaging, working, streaming video, and navigating with Google Maps and Waze.
I also compared the experience of playing graphically challenging games like Neverness to Everness to my experience on other Android flagships like the Galaxy S26 Ultra and Xiaomi 17 Ultra. I ran lots of benchmarks on the handset, including 3DMark and Geekbench, to confirm my performance findings.
I assessed the phone's battery performance based on my real-world usage, and charging times were measured using the official Oppo wall adapter along with the included charging cable.
First tested October 2026
Luke is a freelance journalist with over a decade of experience in the consumer electronics industry. Previously Features Editor at Pocket-lint, Luke can now be found contributing reviews and features on the latest smartphones and camera tech to the likes of TechRadar, Trusted Reviews, Tech Advisor, Pocket Tactics, Digital Camera World, and more. He also runs a YouTube channel called Neon Airship in his spare time, which features deep dives into the latest and greatest smartphone imaging tech.

articles.title: La France commande 4 nouveaux SAMP/T NG, seul bouclier européen contre les menaces hypersoniques
articles.text:
La Direction générale de l'armement indique mercredi avoir commandé quatre sections supplémentaires du système de défense sol-air SAMP/T NG pour l’armée de l’Air et de l’Espace, un bouclier XXL.
On vient d'apprendre, ce mercredi 21 octobre 2026, que la Direction générale de l'armement (DGA) a remis une pièce dans la machine de la défense antiaérienne du pays et de l'Europe. Quatre sections supplémentaires de SAMP/T NG, le système de défense sol-air de nouvelle génération, viennent en effet d'être commandées pour l'armée de l'Air et de l'Espace. Le compteur grimpe ainsi à douze, dont dix exemplaires qui doivent être livrées avant la fin de l'année 2030. Un premier système a déjà été livré au début de l'année.
La France veut stopper les missiles hypersoniques et commande quatre SAMP/T NG de plus pour y parvenir
Pour comprendre le SAMP/T NG, il faut d’abord présenter son aîné, le SAMP/T, pour « Système sol-air moyenne et longue portée/terrestre ». On parle ici d'un bouclier franco-italien installé au sol, chargé d’abattre à distance ce qui menace le ciel. Il est surnommé « Mamba » et est déjà en service dans l’armée de l’Air et de l’Espace, contre les avions, mais aussi les drones et les missiles, y compris balistiques, capables de retomber sur leur cible après une longue trajectoire en cloche.
Seulement voilà, il ne vous a pas échappé que les menaces se sont multipliées ces dernières années, qu'elles ont changé de visage. Elles vont plus vite, changent plus facilement de direction et se font plus discrètes pour échapper aux radars. D’où le lancement en 2021 de cette version dite NG, pour « nouvelle génération ».
Le Mamba change de peau, mais aussi de cerveau. Le SAMP/T NG reçoit une conduite de tir de nouvelle génération, c’est-à-dire l’ensemble qui repère la menace, la suit et déclenche le tir. Ses yeux s’appellent GF300, le radar dernier cri de Thales, conçu pour tirer le meilleur du futur missile intercepteur Aster B1NT. Imaginez qu'une fois ce duo réuni, le SAMP/T NG deviendra le seul système sol-air européen capable d’arrêter des menaces balistiques et hypersoniques, les fameux engins qui filent au-delà de Mach 5, soit plus de cinq fois la vitesse du son.
Une défense sol-air européenne qui s'exporte déjà
En coulisses, la France ne passe pas commande en direct. Elle s'appuie sur l'OCCAr, l'Organisation conjointe de coopération en matière d'armement, un organisme européen qui pilote les programmes d'armement menés à plusieurs pays, comme ici avec l'Italie. Le contrat revient ensuite à Eurosam, une structure commune à deux géants de la défense, MBDA et Thales, chargée de fabriquer le système.
Le SAMP/T NG ne veillera pas seulement sur le ciel français. Le système, né de la coopération entre Paris et Rome, a déjà fait l'objet de commandes à l'étranger. Le Danemark et l'Ukraine l'ont retenu pour leur défense, et d'autres pays ont manifesté leur intérêt. Pour la France, il s'agit d'une réussite commerciale, mais au-delà de ça, enforcer ce bouclier antiaérien, c'est aussi garantir sa souveraineté, autrement dit être capable de protéger son espace aérien par ses propres moyens.

articles.title: Anthropic prevé invertir 750.000 millones de dólares en IA antes de una posible salida récord a bolsa
articles.text:
Anthropic prevé destinar cerca de 750.000 millones de dólares a capacidad computacional para inteligencia artificial durante los próximos años, una apuesta que coincide con los preparativos de una posible salida a bolsa que podría recaudar hasta 100.000 millones de dólares.
Las cifras, incluidas en documentación presentada ante la Comisión de Bolsa y Valores de Estados Unidos, colocan a la creadora de Claude en el centro de la discusión sobre el gasto tecnológico y la rentabilidad futura de la IA.
El plan refleja la escala financiera que requieren los modelos de lenguaje avanzados. Entrenar, operar y ampliar estas herramientas exige procesadores especializados, centros de datos, energía y servicios en la nube. Al mismo tiempo, los compromisos asumidos por Anthropic reavivan las dudas del mercado sobre una posible burbuja de la inteligencia artificial, ante la distancia entre las inversiones previstas y los beneficios que estas compañías pueden generar a corto plazo.
Los contratos con Amazon, Google y Microsoft superan los 250.000 millones
De los 750.000 millones de dólares estimados, Anthropic prevé gastar 450.000 millones en infraestructura de los llamados hiperescaladores durante un periodo de entre siete y diez años. La empresa contempla contratos por unos 111.000 millones de dólares con Google Cloud, 110.000 millones con Amazon Web Services y 31.000 millones con Microsoft.
Gran parte de esos acuerdos no puede cancelarse. Este tipo de compromisos refuerza la relación entre las compañías que desarrollan modelos de inteligencia artificial y los proveedores que aportan capacidad de cómputo. Amazon, Alphabet y Microsoft invierten en plataformas de IA, mientras esas firmas contratan sus nubes, chips y centros de datos para sostener el crecimiento de sus servicios.
La documentación también revela que el 47% de los ingresos de Anthropic procede de Alphabet y Amazon. La dependencia de esos grupos figura entre los factores de riesgo de la empresa, ya que algunos de sus clientes principales no están sujetos a contratos de largo plazo y podrían reducir o interrumpir sus gastos.
Las pérdidas contrastan con el aumento de los ingresos
Las cuentas de Anthropic muestran la tensión entre expansión y rentabilidad. Durante el primer semestre de 2026, la compañía registró una pérdida neta de 80.700 millones de dólares, frente a un déficit de 13.000 millones durante el mismo periodo del año anterior.
En sentido contrario, los ingresos del tercer trimestre alcanzaron 16.800 millones de dólares, un aumento del 46% frente al segundo trimestre de 2026, según datos citados por Bloomberg. La compañía habría entrado en ganancias ajustadas en el último trimestre, aunque estas permanecen lejos del volumen de capital que requiere su infraestructura.
Jun Bei Liu, cofundadora y gestora principal de carteras de Ten Cap Investment Management, resumió la preocupación de parte del mercado: los inversores deben valorar cuánto pagar hoy por beneficios futuros que dependen de gastos enormes. La analista mantiene una visión favorable sobre la adopción de la IA, pero espera retornos cada vez más desiguales entre las empresas del sector.
La salida a bolsa resulta clave para Anthropic. La empresa buscaría captar 100.000 millones de dólares, una cifra superior a los 75.000 millones atribuidos a SpaceX, y alcanzar una valoración de entre 1,8 y 2 billones de dólares. Si se cumplen esas previsiones, sería la mayor oferta pública de venta de la historia.
La documentación formal para comercializar la operación ante la SEC podría presentarse durante la semana del 9 de noviembre. Ese calendario permitiría que la empresa comenzara a cotizar antes del 26 de noviembre, fecha que coincide con el Día de Acción de Gracias en Estados Unidos.
El gasto en IA alimenta la discusión sobre una burbuja
La llamada burbuja de la IA alude al temor de que las valoraciones y las inversiones superen la capacidad real de las compañías para sostener ingresos y beneficios. El foco está en el desfase entre el dinero destinado a chips, energía y centros de datos, y los retornos comerciales que aún deben consolidarse.
Algunos analistas comparan el escenario con las empresas .com de finales de los años 90. Un eventual ajuste no eliminaría la utilidad de la inteligencia artificial, pero podría reducir la especulación y dejar en mejor posición a las firmas capaces de demostrar un negocio sostenible.

articles.title: Hackers Hid Vasilek Backdoor in VMware Tools During 2-Year Russian Healthcare Intrusion
articles.text:
A Belarus-aligned hacktivist group spent nearly two years within the network of a Russian healthcare organization.
According to a report published by Russian cybersecurity firm Solar, the activity has been attributed to a threat cluster dubbed Partisan Zmiy, which is also known as the Cyber Partisans.
Known to be active since at least 2020, the group has a track record of striking industrial enterprises and government agencies in Russia and Belarus with a backdoor called Vasilek that uses Telegram for command-and-control (C2) and data exfiltration.
Some of the attacks have also leveraged phishing lures to deliver an installer that simultaneously deploys the legitimate FortiClient VPN program on the system as well as an open-source program known as DNSCat2 that allows attackers to gain control of the infected host.
A notable aspect of the threat actor is their ability to stage destructive attacks with a wiper referred to as Pryanik, alongside taking steps to systematically clear Windows event logs using a utility dubbed Evlx.
The Rostelecom subsidiary said it discovered the intrusion in December 2025, although evidence suggests that the earliest signs of compromise date back to early 2024. The name of the targeted organization was not identified. The exact initial access vector used to breach the entity is also not known.
Unlike other attacks linked to Cyber Partisans, the threat actors remained on the network for an extended period of time without carrying out any destructive activity, marking something of a shift in modus operandi.
"The attacked organization possessed an extensive infrastructure and two-way trusted relationships with numerous subsidiary medical institutions," Solar said. "We hypothesize that the lack of infrastructure disruption is due precisely to the value of this access for further espionage and trusted relationship attacks."
Observed as part of the intrusion is a loader-scheduler service ("vmauad") that masquerades as a legitimate VMware component to maintain persistence and evade cursory inspection. To accomplish this, the attackers are said to have taken advantage of a trusted-but-unmonitored VMware Tools directory location to plant malicious executables or replace legitimate VMware DLLs with a malicious version ("vmtools.dll") containing the backdoor.
The primary responsibility of the Windows service is to launch the rogue binary "C:\Program Files\VMware\VMware Tools\authd.exe" that, besides launching a GOST tunnel every Saturday from 10 p.m. to 11 p.m., runs an updated version of Vasilek (version 1.5.8) once, eight hours after the service begins.
Once installed, Vasilek is equipped to collect information about an infected computer, execute Windows commands, launch and terminate processes, transfer files, capture screenshots, record keystrokes, and escalate privileges via runas. It can also prevent the machine from going into sleep mode, and update or remove itself.
One new addition is the "move_cursor" command that, as the name implies, allows the backdoor to move the cursor and simulate user input on the victim's screen.
"The group consistently invests in stealth and operational security, rather than new capabilities: hostname binding in two independent components, nightly scheduled payload launches, system proxy inheritance, disguise as legitimately installed but unused software, file rotation across the same paths, time-stomping, outgoing message suppression, and anonymous messages on behalf of the group in operator chats," Solar said.
"The backdoor's feature set has remained largely unchanged over four revisions. Due to Telegram being blocked in Russia by ISPs, communication between the Vasilek backdoor and C2 has become unstable."
The disclosure comes as Solar also disclosed details of a phishing campaign that employs JavaScript attachments mimicking business-themed documents, such as payments and purchase orders, to deliver a previously unreported malware family known as HypeAgent.
The Windows malware is a full-featured trojan designed to take complete control over infected systems, packing the ability to steal files, open a console, change desktop wallpaper, turn on a webcam, log keystrokes, launch hidden VNC and RDP sessions, control the mouse, and even deploy a cryptocurrency miner.
It's also capable of stealing cookies associated with Discord, Steam, GitHub, Instagram, Telegram, Binance, ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor, and tampering with the installed Exodus wallet app to inject JavaScript that can collect the victim's password, PIN, mnemonic phrase, and private key.
Earlier this June, Solar also observed legitimate infrastructure compromised by the ProxyCB proxyware botnet malware making automated requests to Russian websites and online platforms, while identifying possible overlaps between the botnet infrastructure and historical activity linked to TeamSpy, a threat cluster known for abusing TeamViewer to facilitate reconnaissance and data theft.
Last month, the U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) charged Searzhudin Tamirlanovich Aktulaev, a 40-year-old Russian national extradited from Cyprus in May 2025, for exploiting an online messaging service of a well-known freelance employment platform to send malware-laced Excel attachments to about 80,000 of its users in 2016 and 2017 using 255 fake accounts.
The attacks led to the deployment of two types of malware, a variant of the TVRAT (aka Sheldor, SpyAgent, TeamBot, TeamSpy, and TVSPY) and DarkVNC, to harvest and send data from a victim computer to a remote server under the attacker's control. Thousands of computers are assessed to have been infected as a result of this scheme.

articles.title: Voiture électrique à 150 € par mois, entretien compris : voici comment des députés veulent améliorer le leasing social
articles.text:
Voiture électrique à 150 € par mois, entretien compris : voici comment des députés veulent améliorer le leasing social
Une proposition de loi déposée par des députés à l’Assemblée nationale vise à créer un parc public d’un million de voitures électriques à 150 € par mois d’ici 2035.
Déposée le 20 octobre 2026 à l’Assemblée nationale par les élus du groupe Écologiste et Social (Les Écologistes, Génération.s et L’Après), une nouvelle proposition de loi entend revoir de fond en comble l’accès à la voiture électrique. Pour pallier les limites du leasing social actuel et son fonctionnement par campagnes ponctuelles très vite épuisées, les parlementaires proposent d’instituer un véritable service public visant un million de véhicules en circulation d’ici 2035. En plus d’un tarif abordable, la mensualité inclurait tout l’entretien courant afin d’éviter cette charge financière aux ménages les plus modestes.
Un parc électrique financé par la Caisse des dépôts dès 2028, qu’est-ce que ça changerait ?
Concrètement, cette flotte d’un million de voitures électriques serait constituée progressivement entre le 1er janvier 2028 et le 31 décembre 2035. Contrairement au leasing social actuel, ces véhicules seraient achetés et détenus par la Caisse des dépôts et consignations, avant d’être confiés à des opérateurs publics ou privés. De ce fait, les bénéficiaires ne seraient plus soumis aux critères de solvabilité parfois bloquants des loueurs privés, ni contraints de rendre ou racheter au prix fort leur voiture au bout de trois ans. Le véhicule appartiendrait ainsi à un parc public pérenne, sur le modèle des logements HLM, permettant une location durable tant que le foyer en a besoin.
Ces voitures, exclusivement électriques, éco-scorées et d’une masse inférieure à 1 800 kg, pourraient rester dans le parc durant 12 ans en étant louées successivement à plusieurs foyers. Le loyer mensuel moyen serait quant à lui fixé à 150 € hors assurance, mais inclurait l’assistance, l’entretien courant, les réparations liées à l’usure normale ainsi que le remplacement des pneumatiques.
Côté éligibilité, le service ciblerait les cinq premiers déciles de revenus (jusqu’à 16 880 € de revenu fiscal de référence par part en 2026), avec au moins 50 % des contrats réservés aux 30 % des foyers les plus modestes (trois premiers déciles). Ceux-ci bénéficieraient en outre d’une enveloppe de 400 € pour “faciliter les démarches administratives, la prise en main du véhicule et l’installation d’une solution de recharge” à domicile.
En prime, l’attribution ne dépendrait plus uniquement des trajets professionnels, mais prendrait aussi en compte l’accès aux soins, la formation, la recherche d’emploi ou l’absence de transports collectifs.
Pour boucler le budget, la Caisse des dépôts négocierait des commandes groupées visant un prix d’achat maximal de 15 000 € par véhicule après remise. Le montage financier s’appuierait sur une enveloppe grimpant jusqu’à 8,5 milliards d’euros et une subvention annuelle de l’État de 350 millions d’euros, remboursés progressivement par les loyers et la revente finale des voitures.

articles.title: Fusion SpaceX-Tesla : "une bonne idée" pour Elon Musk, qui s'y prépare
articles.text:
L'empire d'Elon Musk va-t-il être rassemblé dans une seule super-entreprise à l'avenir ? Ça pourrait bien être le cas, vu les organisations qui se forment, et l'avis positif émis par le milliardaire.
Elon Musk n'est pas du genre à éparpiller ses sociétés. Au contraire, il est plutôt du genre à les faire fusionner. On se souvient ainsi que Twitter, devenu X, avait fini par intégrer le giron de sa société d'intelligence artificielle, xAI, qui, à son tour, a fini par être absorbée par le géant de l'aéronautique SpaceX. Et l'on pourrait bien dans pas si longtemps être témoin de la dernière étape de cette consolidation, avec une fusion exceptionnelle entre les deux mastodontes SpaceX et Tesla !
La fusion entre Tesla et SpaceX est en marche
Cela fait quelques temps déjà que le marché évoque une fusion à terme des deux géants chapeautéz par Elon Musk, à savoir SpaceX et Tesla. Et cette opération commence à prendre forme, puisqu'Elon Musk a avoué pour la première fois que des comités spéciaux ont été formés dans chacune de ces deux sociétés pour évaluer cette potentielle opération.
D'après l'homme le plus riche du monde, ces comités se sont mis en place à la demande des actionnaires, qui devront à la fin donner leur accord. En tout cas, pour ce qui est du patron des deux firmes, son opinion est déjà faite, et elle est très claire. « Je pense que ce serait une bonne idée, mais c'est vraiment aux comités spéciaux des deux entreprises d'en décider » a-t-il ainsi exprimé, dans des propos rapportés par Reuters. Toujours d'après la même source, les discussions ont débuté il y a quelques semaines, et pourraient s'achever par l'achat de Tesla par SpaceX.
Elon Musk voit des synergies possibles entre les activités des deux entreprises
Le discours est par ailleurs bien rôdé, Elon Musk affirmant ne voir que des avantages, et de nombreuses synergies à venir, avec une fusion de SpaceX et de Tesla. « Je pense effectivement qu'il y a beaucoup d'avantages à fusionner ces entreprises, car nous sommes pratiquement entrés dans l'ère de la singularité de la superintelligence, et il y a beaucoup à gagner à coopérer dans les domaines du développement de logiciels de superintelligence, de la conception de puces, du Terafab bien sûr, de la robotique, du lancement de masse en orbite avec la constellation Starmind, et de la connectivité » a-t-il ainsi précisé.
Et s'il se dit être dans « une situation de conflit d'intérêt », et dont, être incapable de prendre part aux discussions, il aurait aussi tout à gagner au niveau du contrôle dans cette fusion. Pour rappel, Elon Musk détient environ un cinquième du capital de Tesla, et un peu moins de la moitié de celui de SpaceX. Si une fusion advenait, pour les analystes, il obtiendrait clairement le contrôle de la nouvelle entité.
Source : Reuters

He died in Belfast in 2010, aged 61. The 2026 Northern Ireland Open trophy bears his name. His life story is recounted in the unauthorized biography, "The Hurricane: The Turbulent Life and Times of Alex Higgins" by Bill Borrows.

articles.title: Carros más inteligentes: ahora recordarán correos, mapas y más gracias a la IA de Gemini
articles.text:
Google comenzó a desplegar una de las actualizaciones más ambiciosas para Gemini dentro de los vehículos: la Inteligencia Personalizada, también llamada Personal Intelligence. La función llega a Android Auto y permite que el asistente consulte correos, fotos, citas y rutas guardadas para responder sin que el conductor dé ningún dato adicional.
Hasta ahora, Gemini respondía en el vehículo de la misma manera para todos los usuarios. Con esta actualización, el asistente accede a la misma información personal que ya usa en el teléfono, lo que multiplica el contexto disponible en cada conversación al volante.
Qué es la Inteligencia Personalizada y cómo conecta los datos con el auto
La Inteligencia Personalizada es la función de Gemini que, con autorización del usuario, conecta de forma segura la información de Gmail, Google Calendario, Google Fotos, Google Maps, YouTube y el historial de búsqueda. Si el conductor tiene una cuenta de Google Workspace, el asistente también puede usar esas herramientas para dar contexto adicional.
El sistema combina dos capacidades: recuperar un dato concreto, como una reserva de hotel guardada en el correo, y razonar sobre varias fuentes a la vez para dar una respuesta completa. Esa combinación es la que permite resolver pedidos complejos sin que el usuario tenga que revisar cada aplicación por separado.
Esta función solo se activa cuando el usuario otorga permiso explícito desde la configuración de Gemini, y puede desactivarse en cualquier momento. Mientras permanezca apagada, el asistente sigue funcionando con normalidad para navegación, música o llamadas, aunque sin respuestas adaptadas a cada persona.
Qué se podrá pedirle a Gemini al volante
Los comandos funcionan en lenguaje natural, sin necesidad de especificar datos concretos. Camino al aeropuerto, una pregunta como “¿cuál es mi puerta de embarque y llega a tiempo mi vuelo?” alcanza para que el asistente localice la confirmación en Gmail y revise el estado del viaje en un mismo intercambio.
La función también se integra con la navegación. Decir “llévame a la cita del médico” basta para que Gemini busque el evento en el Calendario, extraiga la dirección y comience a dar indicaciones, sin que el conductor recuerde la calle ni la busque antes de salir.
El asistente incorpora además preferencias personales al sugerir lugares. Ante un pedido como encontrar un restaurante en la ruta, puede priorizar opciones acordes a los gustos habituales del usuario, por ejemplo locales vegetarianos si ese es su patrón de consumo.
Otro escenario es recuperar información visual: pedir que localice “el lavadero de autos de la foto que saqué la semana pasada” y que trace la ruta hacia ese sitio, sin necesidad de revisar el carrete de imágenes ni detener el vehículo para buscar la dirección.
También es posible retomar una conversación anterior. Una frase como “llévame a la cafetería de la que hablamos ayer” permite que el asistente identifique el lugar mencionado en un intercambio previo y arranque la navegación de forma directa.
Cómo acceder a estas funciones de IA en Android Auto
Google diseñó la función con el consentimiento como eje central: ninguna aplicación queda conectada hasta que el usuario decide activarla desde los ajustes de Gemini, y la opción puede revertirse en cualquier momento. En los vehículos con Google built-in, las respuestas personalizadas solo se comparten mientras el teléfono permanece conectado al coche.
Para acceder a la Inteligencia Personalizada en Android Auto es necesario mantener actualizadas tanto la aplicación de Android Auto como la app de Gemini en el teléfono, además de tener activada la personalización desde esa misma aplicación móvil, donde se gestionan los permisos de acceso al correo, al calendario y a las fotos.
El despliegue arrancó esta semana en Android Auto, mientras que los coches con Google built-in recibirán la función en los próximos meses. Según pudo conocer el medio especializado 9to5Google, es probable que la actualización llegue primero a Estados Unidos y después a mercados como España, aunque la compañía no confirmó un cronograma oficial para esa expansión.
Quienes ya tengan habilitada la Inteligencia Personalizada en la aplicación móvil de Gemini la verán activa de forma automática al conectar el teléfono al coche. Quienes no la hayan configurado pueden hacerlo en cualquier momento desde los ajustes del asistente, donde también se revisan qué servicios de Google comparten información con Gemini.

articles.title: Glee : c'est officiel, le reboot de la série culte arrive sur Disney+
articles.text:
Glee : c'est officiel, le reboot de la série culte arrive sur Disney+
La série Glee se prépare à faire son grand retour sur le service de streaming Disney+.
Vous souvenez-vous de Glee, la série musicale de Ryan Murphy, Ian Brennan et Brad Falchuk diffusée entre 2009 et 2015 ? Elle va avoir droit à un reboot ! Disney+ et Hulu viennent en effet de commander une nouvelle version du show.
Retour au Glee club
Cela fait plusieurs mois que Ryan Murphy évoque l'éventualité d'un retour de la série Glee, et voilà maintenant que les choses se concrétisent car Disney+ et Hulu ont décidé d'officialiser le reboot du show.
On ne sait pas encore quel forme il prendra, ni si les acteurs de la série originale seront de la fête, mais Ryan Murphy a annoncé en septembre dernier avoir terminé l'écriture d'un scénario pour ce reboot.
La série originale Glee a eu droit à six saisons entre 2009 et 2015 portées par Lea Michele, Dianna Agron, Chris Colfer, Jane Lynch, Kevin McHale, Matthew Morrison ou encore Darren Criss.
Plus tôt ce mois-ci, Colfer déclarait au micro de Bustle qu'il serait difficile pour lui de revenir dans Glee après le décès de plusieurs des acteurs de la série, dont Cory Monteith et Naya Rivera, mais qu'il sait que les fans lui en voudraient de ne pas participer au reboot.
Pour rappel, Glee suivait les tribulations d'une chorale de lycéens et chaque épisode contenait plusieurs numéros musicaux. La série a remporté six Emmy Awards et était produite par 20th Television, qui produira aussi son reboot.
D'ici à en savoir plus sur cette nouvelle version, vous pouvez voir ou revoir l'intégrale de Glee en streaming sur Disney+.
