articles.title: Un fallo crítico en PHP pone en jaque a medio Internet en todo el mundo
articles.text:
Internet funciona tan bien la mayor parte del tiempo que apenas pensamos en todo lo que ocurre detrás de una página antes de que aparezca en nuestra pantalla. Simplemente entramos, hacemos lo que necesitamos y seguimos adelante. Pero hoy la experiencia puede ser distinta: una web oficial muestra mantenimiento, otra devuelve un error y alguna ha dejado directamente de estar disponible. No estamos viendo una única página que falla por casualidad, sino las consecuencias visibles de un problema que afecta a una tecnología profundamente extendida y que ha llevado a varias organizaciones a tomar una decisión poco habitual: desconectar antes que seguir expuestas.
Ahora sabemos qué hay detrás de esas interrupciones. PHP, uno de los lenguajes más extendidos de la web, ha tenido que publicar correcciones para dos vulnerabilidades críticas, CVE-2026-109618 y CVE-2026-109619. La recomendación de las autoridades de ciberseguridad es directa: actualizar cuanto antes y, si eso no es posible o las mitigaciones temporales no bastan, considerar dejar el sistema fuera de línea. Esa cautela ya se ha traducido en decisiones concretas en Europa, donde administraciones y otros organismos de Países Bajos, Finlandia, Dinamarca y Francia han retirado temporalmente webs y servicios públicos de Internet.
PHP trabaja justo en una parte de Internet que normalmente no vemos: el servidor. Cuando abrimos determinadas webs, este lenguaje puede encargarse de generar contenido dinámico, consultar bases de datos o ejecutar parte de la lógica necesaria antes de que la página llegue a nuestro navegador. Esa posición ayuda a entender la dimensión del problema. Según W3Techs, PHP está presente en el 69,3% de las webs cuyo lenguaje del lado del servidor puede identificarse. WordPress, que depende de PHP y alimenta el 39,6% de todas las webs, es quizá el ejemplo más reconocible, aunque las vulnerabilidades no están en WordPress.
Los atacantes ya están intentando abrirse paso
La parte técnica es compleja, pero la consecuencia es relativamente sencilla de entender. Las dos vulnerabilidades afectan a la forma en que PHP maneja ciertos errores de memoria durante una petición y pueden dejar al servidor en un estado inseguro. Si se dan las condiciones adecuadas, una petición construida por un atacante puede aprovechar ese comportamiento para ejecutar código de forma remota sin haber iniciado sesión previamente. No hablamos, por tanto, de un simple fallo que tumba una página: el riesgo está en que alguien consiga hacer que el propio servidor ejecute instrucciones no autorizadas.
La amenaza, además, ya ha dejado de ser puramente teórica. Cloudflare asegura haber detectado tráfico de ataque dirigido contra clientes expuestos a estas vulnerabilidades y afirma que los atacantes han ido modificando sus cargas para intentar esquivar las defensas desplegadas. Eso confirma que ya existe actividad real intentando explotar estos fallos, pero conviene separar cuidadosamente dos escenarios: que haya intentos contra sistemas vulnerables no significa que las administraciones que han desconectado servicios hayan sido comprometidas. Por ahora, no tenemos pruebas de que esos apagados respondan a intrusiones confirmadas.
Como señalamos arriba, este escenario ha llevado a las autoridades a plantear una medida mucho menos habitual: desconectar los sistemas que no puedan protegerse a tiempo. El NCSC británico contempla expresamente dejar un servicio fuera de línea cuando no sea posible aplicar las correcciones o mitigaciones necesarias, una línea que también ha marcado NSA Cyber. En Europa esa opción ya se ha convertido en decisiones concretas: organismos y servicios de Países Bajos, Finlandia, Dinamarca y Francia han retirado temporalmente webs o plataformas. Durante las comprobaciones, algunas mostraban páginas de mantenimiento, otras devolvían un error 503 y algunas ni siquiera respondían.
En estos momentos, varias páginas de organismos públicos europeos siguen sin funcionar con normalidad. Algunas muestran avisos de mantenimiento, otras devuelven errores 503 y unas pocas ni siquiera aceptan conexiones. Estos son algunos de los casos que hemos podido comprobar directamente.
La dificultad ahora está en la enorme fragmentación del ecosistema. PHP ha publicado versiones corregidas para las ramas 8.2, 8.3, 8.4 y 8.5, pero las instalaciones más antiguas pueden depender de proveedores LTS o de una migración a una versión compatible. A eso se suma que PHP vive en el servidor, por lo que su mantenimiento puede estar en manos del administrador o del proveedor de alojamiento y no del propietario de la web. Esa dependencia ayuda a explicar por qué algunas organizaciones siguen retirando servicios incluso después de que la solución técnica esté disponible.

articles.title: ASUS Ships ZenWiFi BN12, the World's First WiFi 8 Mesh System
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 21st 2026
ASUS Ships ZenWiFi BN12, the World's First WiFi 8 Mesh System
ASUS today announced that the ASUS ZenWiFi BN12, the world's first WiFi 8 mesh router, originally unveiled at Computex, is now shipping. It combines ultra-high reliability with intelligent mesh coordination to deliver stable, efficient, and seamless connectivity throughout the modern smart home. The ZenWiFi BN12 is a tri-band model delivering speeds of up to 19 Gbps, featuring advanced WiFi 8 technologies including new Modulation and Coding Scheme (MCS) rates, Unequal Modulation (UEQM), Non-Primary Channel Access (NPCA), and Multi-Access Point Coordination.
Modern homes rely on an increasing number of connected devices across multiple rooms and floors, making consistent coverage and reliable connectivity more important than peak speed alone. The ZenWiFi BN12 combines WiFi 8 technology with Smart AiMesh, intelligent traffic optimization, and enhanced network visibility to provide stable connections across the home, even in demanding multi-device environments. Ultra-high-reliability WiFi 8 offers improved mid-to-long-range throughput, wider IoT coverage, and more consistent whole-home connectivity.Smart AiMesh enhances mesh coordination and backhaul performance for seamless, reliable connectivity throughout the home. The ZenWiFi BN12 also features Adaptive QoE, which dynamically optimizes network resources based on real-time application and traffic demands. Meanwhile, ASUS WiFi Insight enables full-spectrum interference detection and real-time network visibility. And dual 10G Ethernet ports provide high-speed wired networking for demanding home network setups.
The ZenWiFi BN12 also provides comprehensive network protection with commercial-grade AiProtection, security scanning, Safe Browsing, Triple DNS Guard, advanced parental controls, and comprehensive VPN support. Network-level protection helps safeguard connected devices without requiring separate security software on every device, while advanced parental controls give families greater flexibility to manage online access, content, and internet schedules.
WiFi 8 reliability
Unlike previous WiFi generations that primarily focused on increasing peak speeds, WiFi 8 emphasizes ultra-high reliability. New technologies improve performance consistency as signal conditions change, strengthen connectivity at mid-to-long range, and enhance communication with low-power devices at the edge of the network.
The ZenWiFi BN12 empowers users to experience more consistent connectivity throughout the home, including rooms farther away from mesh nodes and areas traditionally affected by weaker signals. Smart-home and IoT devices can also maintain more reliable connections at the edges of WiFi coverage.
ASUS Smart AiMesh flexibility
Smart AiMesh combines ASUS mesh networking technology with WiFi 8 enhancements. Mesh nodes can intelligently coordinate their connections and optimize backhaul performance; the ZenWiFi BN12 provides coverage of up to 7,000 square feet in the two-pack configuration.
As homes become increasingly connected, a strong signal from a single router is no longer enough. Smart AiMesh creates an intelligent, extendable mesh network that takes advantage of WiFi 8 coordination technologies to improve coverage, reduce interference, and maintain reliable connections between mesh nodes and connected devices.
Users can enjoy seamless connectivity as they move throughout the home, with reliable coverage across multiple rooms and floors. The extendable AiMesh ecosystem also gives users the flexibility to expand their network as their coverage needs grow.
Adaptive Quality of Experience
Adaptive QoE automatically observes network traffic and dynamically adjusts priorities in real time based on the needs of different applications and connected devices. Traditional Quality of Service (QoS) relies on predefined classifications and static priorities. The ZenWiFi BN12 responds dynamically to changing network conditions, helping allocate network resources more efficiently as different devices and applications compete for bandwidth. Households can run multiple activities simultaneously, such as streaming, video calls, gaming, smart-home services, and downloads, while maintaining smooth and consistent performance across connected devices.
WiFi Insight
ASUS WiFi Insight provides full-spectrum analysis of WiFi and non-WiFi interference, along with interactive network visualization, intelligent channel switching, and a 24-hour history log. As home networks grow more complex, diagnosing connection issues used to require guesswork or enterprise-grade tools. Through this feature, the ZenWiFi BN12 brings real-time monitoring and interference analysis to your network, making channel optimization simple—for faster, more reliable WiFi. Users gain a clearer understanding of network conditions and potential sources of interference. Intelligent optimization helps maintain more stable and reliable connectivity throughout the home without requiring users to manually diagnose complex wireless issues.
High-speed wired connectivity
The ZenWiFi BN12 also features two 10G Ethernet ports and three 2.5G Ethernet ports, providing flexible high-speed WAN and LAN connectivity for demanding home networks. As multi-gigabit internet services, NAS devices, PCs, and other high-bandwidth devices become increasingly common, multi-gigabit Ethernet helps wired connections remain fast and responsive.

articles.title: 'I love third-person shooters and guns' – Anomalith producer reveals the origins of the upcoming 'mutating girl' survival game
articles.text:
Anomalith producer reveals that 'liminal spaces, including things like the Backrooms' inspired the upcoming third-person survival shooter
FuRyu's ‘mutating girl’ shooter arrives later this month
Anomalith might be one of the most interesting releases of 2026. A third-person survival shooter set in a twisted, retro vision of Japan, it’s a major departure from publisher FuRyu Corporation’s usual role-playing game (RPG) output.
It looks almost like the company’s take on Resident Evil, with 17-year-old protagonist Reona Minazuki venturing into deadly anomaly zones filled with grotesque creatures at the behest of a shadowy government organization.
Real-time gun combat, managing your small inventory, and keeping track of precious ammunition form a key part of every mission. Each run unfolds in an almost extraction-shooter-like format, and between missions you can use the resources you’ve scavenged to upgrade your gear.
There’s more to Minazuki than meets the eye, though, with the hero able to harness a mysterious set of mutant powers brought on by exposure to these supernatural environments. I spoke to producer Gai Kidokoro over email to learn a little more about how this project took shape and discover some of what’s in store for players.
Expanded arsenal
Anomalith is Kidokoro’s first original project, having joined FuRyu in the company’s anime division, which has helped produce hit titles like Is It Wrong to Try to Pick Up Girls in a Dungeon?, before making the leap to its gaming business to direct some licensed titles. Working on games has “always been an area I was interested in,” he says, adding that his career has been “a little different from that of FuRyu’s other producers.”
It therefore seems only fitting that he is producing quite a unique project, with Anomalith standing apart as FuRyu’s first third-person shooter. Interestingly, Kidokoro says that the genre was chosen because both he and the director “love third-person shooters and guns” and set out to create something based on the things they enjoy.
“Rather than thinking, 'Let’s deliberately challenge ourselves with a completely different genre,' it was really more about wanting to make a game in a genre that we personally love,” he continues.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
This fascination with firearms seems evident in the game’s weapon customization system, which lets players “swap out a fairly detailed range of parts,” including a variety of attachments such as “sights, grips, stocks, and more.” These help you personalize the appearance of each gun, but also provide statistical bonuses to help in the field.
The producer is also keen to highlight the player’s ability to scavenge “pieces of equipment called Artifacts that enhance your character’s stats” and change your overall build.
“These include loot-based, hack-and-slash-style elements,” he teases, “and if you manage to equip an Artifact with extremely high values, some skills have the potential to become incredibly powerful.”
The team is well aware that not everyone is going to be interested in tweaking their guns or experimenting with the nitty-gritty of their character’s stats, which is why the game offers a wealth of cosmetic options for players to outfit themselves with – some already available to try in the recent free Steam demo.
“We realized that there are quite a lot of people who don’t necessarily get the same enjoyment we do from firing their favorite, carefully customized gun,” Kidokoro begins. “We thought, 'Maybe adding character outfits and customization would make it more fun for those players,' and that’s why we ended up including such detailed character customization options. Judging from the response to the demo, I’m really glad we added the outfit customization.”
Uncanny valley
The world design is shaping up to be a treat, with plenty of intricate detail to pore over. In fact, Kidokoro highlights this as one part of the experience that he is most excited about. “The development team has put a tremendous amount of effort into designing the Otherworlds,” he explains. “There are many areas where something may initially look like nothing more than an ordinary ceiling, but if you stop and look up, you might find something that gives you a real sense of unease.”
He describes the fundamental concept behind it all as the “anxiety and fear lurking within familiar scenery” and reveals that it was inspired by popular ideas of “liminal spaces, including things like the Backrooms,” referring to the viral meme featuring endless wallpapered corridors that recently inspired a horror film adaptation.
“Within the development team, we often use phrases like ‘give it a liminal-space atmosphere’ when discussing the visual direction.”
This extends to the soundtrack. Aside from the game’s title theme, the music of Anomalith doesn’t feature any vocal tracks. Nevertheless, the producer argues fans “can definitely look forward to the soundtrack” and warns “many of the tracks are quite dark and unsettling.” He jokes: “I recommend listening to them during the daytime.”
Although Anomalith seems very different, long-time FuRyu fans will recognize some common elements shared with the publisher’s past games, such as the focus on a teenage protagonist. Kidokoro thinks the reasons behind this particular motif “would vary” depending on the title, but personally reckons “that it is easier for audiences to emotionally root for younger characters.”
“Watching boys and girls confront unreasonable circumstances and ultimately overcome them can also feel more hopeful and moving than a story centered on adults,” he continues. “Of course, we have been influenced by other games. However, we try to keep those influences as references rather than simply copying them. Our main criterion is always whether a particular element is necessary for players to enjoy the world and experience of Anomalith.”
We will be able to find out whether this formula pays off when Anomalith launches for Nintendo Switch 2, PC, and PlayStation 5 on October 29, 2026.

articles.title: Amazon se convierte en el primer proveedor de nube de la OTAN para información restringida
articles.text:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) se convirtió en el primer proveedor de servicios en la nube aprobado por la totalidad de los países miembros de la Organización del Tratado del Atlántico Norte (OTAN) para el manejo de información clasificada bajo el nivel “NATO RESTRICTED” (NR).
La aprobación permite que la Alianza, sus socios de la industria de defensa y cada uno de sus estados miembros utilicen los servicios de AWS para procesar cargas de trabajo con esa clasificación en cualquier región de la compañía ubicada dentro de un país de la OTAN.
Prolongado proceso de certificación
Para obtener la aprobación, AWS documentó su cumplimiento de la norma D32, la directiva técnica de la OTAN que fija los requisitos de seguridad para el manejo de información restringida en la nube pública. Como parte de ese proceso, el Centro Criptográfico Nacional (CCN) de España evaluó las capacidades de la compañía, antes de que la OTAN diera a conocer la aprobación a todos sus aliados.
David Appel, vicepresidente interino de Sector Público Global de AWS, calificó la certificación como “la culminación de un esfuerzo sostenido de varios años” y aseguró que refleja el compromiso de la empresa “de ayudar a los clientes y socios de los sectores de defensa, del sector público y afiliados a la OTAN a cumplir sus misiones críticas”.
El directivo agregó que “los gobiernos, y los ciudadanos, merecen tener acceso a la misma infraestructura y los mismos servicios que impulsan la innovación en el sector privado”.
La aprobación reduce tiempos y costos de acreditación
El visto bueno otorgado a AWS simplifica el camino que deben recorrer los países miembros y los socios industriales de la Alianza Atlántica para adoptar la nube comercial en proyectos con información restringida. Al contar ya con una base de seguridad común y evaluada previamente, los aliados pueden reducir el tiempo, el esfuerzo y el costo que implica cumplir con las obligaciones de seguridad y cumplimiento normativo que exige la OTAN.
Además, la certificación abre una vía acelerada para que cada país miembro acredite a AWS a través de su propio proceso nacional oficial, sin necesidad de repetir desde cero las evaluaciones técnicas que ya validó la organización a nivel central. Para la acreditación NR, la OTAN delega el proceso en un país miembro o en la Agencia de Comunicaciones e Información de la OTAN (NCIA), en su calidad de anfitrión.
La infraestructura disponible abarca 15 países de la Alianza
Actualmente, AWS opera 15 regiones de infraestructura en países miembros de la OTAN, siete de las cuales se encuentran en Europa continental. Todas esas regiones quedan habilitadas para el desarrollo de sistemas con capacidad para manejar información “NATO RESTRICTED”, de acuerdo con el alcance de la aprobación otorgada.
Dylan Browne, gerente general de la NCIA, destacó que “fortalecer la capacidad de la OTAN para aprovechar de manera segura la tecnología comercial es clave para construir una Alianza más resiliente y ágil”. Browne sostuvo además que la disponibilidad de productos comerciales que cumplen con los requisitos de seguridad de la OTAN amplía las opciones tecnológicas disponibles para la organización y respalda su capacidad de adoptar tecnologías modernas sin resignar seguridad ni resiliencia operativa.
El acceso se canaliza a través de una plataforma específica
La base técnica de este anuncio es AWS Trusted Secure Enclave – Sensitive Edition (TSE-SE), la solución a través de la cual los clientes de seguridad nacional y defensa pueden acceder a las capacidades ahora certificadas. Appel remarcó el compromiso de la compañía de “seguir trabajando para brindar la interoperabilidad que las naciones aliadas necesitan para fortalecer su resiliencia y proteger a sus ciudadanos”.
Los clientes interesados en implementar soluciones bajo este marco pueden coordinar con sus equipos de cuenta de AWS para evaluar cómo la aprobación y el TSE-SE se adaptan a sus casos de uso particulares dentro de los distintos países de la Alianza.

articles.title: Orange et Sosh en panne : le réseau mobile disparaît chez de nombreux abonnés
articles.text:
Décidément, après Revolut hier, c’est au tour d’Orange aujourd’hui. Une panne perturbe les services mobiles de l’opérateur et de Sosh ce mercredi 21 octobre en fin de matinée. Des abonnés rapportent une perte complète de réseau dans de nombreuses régions, avec, à l'heure d'écrire ces lignes, plus de 11 000 signalements sur DownDetector.
Mise à jour du 21/10 à 12 h 30 : Orange a reconnu les perturbations dans un message publié sur X : « Vous pouvez rencontrer actuellement des perturbations sur le réseau mobile Orange. Nos équipes sont pleinement mobilisées pour rétablir le réseau dans les meilleurs délais. »
Vous êtes concerné par cette panne ? N’hésitez pas à nous indiquer dans les commentaires votre ville, votre opérateur et les difficultés rencontrées : appels, SMS ou Internet mobile. Merci pour vos témoignages, qui nous aident à suivre l’évolution de la situation.
Plus de signal, plus de connexion Internet mobile, un téléphone qui affiche « aucun service » : les témoignages se multiplient autour de midi. Les remontées concernent des villes éloignées les unes des autres, de Paris à Toulouse, en passant par Lyon, Strasbourg ou Bordeaux. Elles dessinent un incident qui dépasse largement le cadre d’une antenne locale, même si son périmètre exact reste à préciser.
Des pertes de réseau signalées dans de nombreuses régions
De nombreux commentaires d'utilisateurs publiés en cette fin de matinée décrivent les difficultés à joindre le réseau d'Orange. « Plus de réseau à Clermont-Ferrand », écrit un utilisateur. « Coupure réseau mobile Orange à Paris », rapporte un autre. Des messages évoquent également des interruptions à Lille, Nice, Grenoble, Rouen, Orléans, Poitiers, Limoges, Biarritz ou encore Saint-Brieuc.
Certains abonnés décrivent des conséquences immédiates sur leur activité. À Saint-Genis-Laval, près de Lyon, une utilisatrice signale une box sans connexion et un téléphone hors réseau : « Impossible de travailler, très pénible ». À Strasbourg, un autre commentaire mentionne une perte de réseau sur le téléphone et une box 5G.
Ces témoignages rejoignent les indicateurs de Downdetector et Sosh apparaît également en difficulté.
Une origine et un délai de rétablissement encore inconnus
À l’heure de notre rédaction,Orange n'a pas encore communiqué sur les causes de ces perturbations ou un horaire de retour à la normale.
La météo officielle du réseau mobile ne nous a pas davantage permis d’obtenir un diagnostic : sa consultation nous a uniquement renvoyé la mention « Chargement en cours », avec une page qui tourne dans le vide. 
Les témoignages concernent principalement le réseau mobile. Les mentions de connexions Internet ou de box interrompues doivent être distinguées : une box 5G utilise elle aussi ce réseau. Elles ne suffisent donc pas à confirmer une panne générale de la fibre ou de l’ADSL.
Reste désormais à connaître l’étendue précise de l’incident, les services concernés et le délai nécessaire pour rétablir les communications des abonnés touchés.

articles.title: Après ChatGPT, OpenAI veut révolutionner la création de vos médicaments
articles.text:
Le créateur de ChatGPT vient de s’offrir un spécialiste des logiciels destinés à l’industrie pharmaceutique. Une acquisition qui doit lui permettre de s’imposer dans le développement des médicaments, alors même que l’entreprise continue d’engloutir des milliards de dollars pour financer sa croissance.
Développer un médicament prend des années, et le moindre contretemps peut bouleverser tout un programme de recherche. C’est précisément sur ce terrain qu’OpenAI compte désormais avancer. Le 20 octobre, l’entreprise a annoncé le rachat d’Orchestra Bio, une société spécialisée dans les agents d’intelligence artificielle capables de coordonner les différentes étapes du développement pharmaceutique.
L'opération marque une nouvelle étape dans la diversification du groupe qui ne veut manifestement plus se contenter de fournir des modèles d’IA aux entreprises.
Des agents IA pour accélérer le travail des laboratoires
Un problème de fabrication, des résultats qui tardent ou un essai clinique repoussé peuvent rapidement entraîner des mois de retard. Orchestra Bio a justement développé des outils capables d’anticiper les conséquences de ces imprévus, de réorganiser les tâches et de proposer différents scénarios aux équipes scientifiques.
Les décisions restent entre les mains des chercheurs, mais une partie du travail de coordination peut être confiée à l'IA.
Les équipes d’Orchestra vont rejoindre Rosalind, l’offre d’OpenAI destinée aux sciences du vivant. Celle-ci repose notamment sur GPT-Rosalind, un modèle spécialisé en biologie et en chimie, ainsi que sur Workbench, un environnement permettant d’exploiter les données scientifiques et de préparer des expériences.
En associant ces outils aux agents d’Orchestra, OpenAI espère accompagner les laboratoires bien au-delà de la simple analyse de résultats. L’objectif est aussi commercial, puisque ce type de logiciel peut devenir indispensable au fonctionnement quotidien des équipes de recherche.
Mais avec quel argent OpenAI finance-t-il ses acquisitions ?
Le montant du rachat n’a pas été communiqué, pas plus que ses modalités de paiement. Impossible donc de savoir si OpenAI a utilisé sa trésorerie, ses actions ou une combinaison des deux.
L'absence de bénéfices ne l’empêche toutefois pas de poursuivre ses emplettes. Fin mars, l’entreprise a annoncé 122 milliards de dollars de capitaux engagés avec le soutien de poids lourds comme Amazon, NVIDIA et SoftBank.
De quoi financer une expansion particulièrement coûteuse, même si les investisseurs prennent un pari considérable sur l’avenir. Selon des projections révélées par le Financial Times et relayées par Reuters, OpenAI prévoyait encore de consommer 278 milliards de dollars de trésorerie entre 2026 et 2030.
Le groupe compte donc sur sa croissance future pour justifier des investissements qui dépassent aujourd’hui largement ses bénéfices, toujours inexistants.
Quand l’industrie pharmaceutique et l’IA s'attirent mutuellement
Le rapprochement entre intelligence artificielle et recherche médicale ne date évidemment pas de cette acquisition. En 2023, BioNTech avait racheté InstaDeep pour renforcer ses capacités en IA, tandis qu’AstraZeneca a plus récemment mis la main sur Modella AI afin d’accélérer ses travaux en cancérologie.
Le mouvement fonctionne désormais dans les deux sens. Les laboratoires s’offrent des spécialistes de l’IA pour améliorer leurs recherches, tandis que les entreprises technologiques cherchent à pénétrer un secteur où les besoins en calcul, en analyse et en automatisation sont considérables.
Anthropic avance également sur ce terrain avec son laboratoire de biologie, présenté en septembre, où des hypothèses élaborées avec Claude peuvent être confrontées à des expériences réelles.
- Chat dans différentes langues, dont le français
- Générer, traduire et obtenir un résumé de texte
- Générer, optimiser et corriger du code

articles.title: Novedades de Pokémon GO para noviembre 2026: detalles del nuevo Pase de GO y eventos
articles.text:
Pokémon GO habilitará en noviembre de 2026 un nuevo Pase de GO mensual, un sistema de progreso con recompensas gratuitas y opciones de pago.
Entre los premios destacados habrá un encuentro con Groudon, Pokémonedas, Polvo Estrella, Caramelo raro XL y objetos para el juego.
El Pase de GO de noviembre estará disponible desde el martes 3 de noviembre hasta el martes 1 de diciembre, según la hora local de cada jugador.
Los Entrenadores recibirán el pase gratuito de forma automática y podrán sumar Puntos de GO para avanzar de rango y desbloquear recompensas.
También habrá dos opciones de pago. El Pase de GO Deluxe costará USD 7,99 e incluirá recompensas mejoradas y un avance más rápido. Por USD 9,99, estará disponible una versión que otorgará los Puntos de GO necesarios para llegar automáticamente al rango 11.
Las recompensas obtenidas deberán reclamarse antes del jueves 3 de diciembre, cuando caducarán.
Qué novedades trae Pokémon GO en noviembre de 2026
Durante el sábado 28 y el domingo 29 de noviembre no habrá un límite diario para conseguir Puntos de GO. Esta bonificación permitirá avanzar sin restricciones en el pase durante esos dos días.
El pase gratuito ofrecerá un encuentro con Groudon, 400 Pokémonedas, un Huevo Suerte, Caramelo raro XL y Polvo Estrella, entre otras recompensas.
Quienes compren el Pase de GO Deluxe podrán obtener 1.000 Pokémonedas adicionales, para un total de 1.400, una Superincubadora y encuentros extra con más Pokémon. Groudon podrá aparecer en su versión brillante.
Los jugadores que avancen en el pase desbloquearán bonificaciones según su rango.
Desde el rango uno recibirán un Caramelo adicional por intercambiar Pokémon; quienes tengan nivel 31 o superior obtendrán además un Caramelo XL garantizado.
A partir del rango 25, podrán abrir hasta 40 regalos al día, recibir hasta 125 al girar fotodiscos de Poképaradas y Gimnasios y guardar 10 regalos adicionales en la Bolsa.
Desde el rango 50, el Incienso de aventura diaria tendrá el doble de duración. A partir del rango 75, los jugadores recibirán más Polvo Estrella y EXP —los puntos de experiencia necesarios para subir de nivel— al eclosionar Huevos.
El Pase de GO Deluxe mejorará algunas de las bonificaciones del rango 25: permitirá abrir hasta 50 regalos al día, recibir hasta 150 regalos al girar fotodiscos de Poképaradas y Gimnasios, y guardar hasta 20 regalos adicionales en la Bolsa.
El Pase de GO Deluxe también podrá comprarse en la Tienda web de Pokémon GO. Quienes lo adquieran allí recibirán 10 Ultrabolas, cinco Revivir Máximo, un Pase de Combate Premium y cinco Pociones Máximas. La versión con 10 rangos añadirá un segundo Pase de Combate Premium.
Además, la Caja Ultraespecial del Pase de GO Deluxe de noviembre incluirá 20 Ultrabolas, 10 Revivir Máximo, cinco Pases de Combate Premium y 10 Pociones Máximas. Todas las opciones de compra estarán disponibles una sola vez y su disponibilidad podrá variar según la región.
Cómo empezar a jugar Pokémon GO
Para empezar, descarga Pokémon GO en tu celular y crea una cuenta. El juego utiliza la ubicación del dispositivo para mostrar un mapa basado en el entorno real. Al caminar, aparecerán Pokémon que puedes capturar al tocarlos en la pantalla y lanzar una Poké Ball con un movimiento del dedo.
Las Poképaradas son lugares del mapa donde consigues objetos, como Poké Balls y pociones.
Para obtenerlos, debes acercarte y girar el fotodisco, la imagen circular que aparece en cada punto. Puedes activar las notificaciones para conocer eventos cercanos.
Los Gimnasios te permiten combatir con otros jugadores y participar en incursiones, desafíos grupales contra un Pokémon. Al principio, lo más útil es capturar criaturas distintas, reunir objetos y completar tareas. No necesitas gastar dinero para avanzar.
Antes de salir, revisa la batería del teléfono, usa conexión móvil o Wi-Fi y presta atención al entorno.

articles.title: Deepinder Goyal to foray into AI with privacy-focused engine Dark.ai
articles.text:
Deepinder Goyal to foray into AI with privacy-focused engine Dark.ai
Deepinder Goyal has announced a new AI model called Dark.ai, which aims to protect individual privacy while delivering truthful answers.
Eternal founder Deepinder Goyal has announced his intention to get directly into the world of artificial intelligence (AI) with the promise of a platform that will maintain the privacy of an individual while also providing the answers. The new engine is called Dark.ai.
“I wanted an AI which I could talk to without being judged, without any fear, and without leaving a trace. We have been internally using Dark for a few months now, and I find myself revealing more, asking things I would not ask anywhere else, and going deeper into my research. Because I no longer have to look over my shoulder,” Goyal said in his letter to the shareholders following the company’s second quarter results.
According to Goyal, Dark uses fine-tuned frontier open-weight models, running inside its own infrastructure with end-to-end encryption. “We cannot read your conversations, even if we are forced to. Context carries across sessions through an encrypted memory management layer you control,” he remarked.
This need arose as Goyal felt that the current AI models always have the information of individuals and could pre-empt a lot of things.
Dark is being built for founders, researchers, scientists, enterprises and governments as this group wants to keep their thoughts private as privacy is essential for competitiveness. “On top of privacy, we have fine-tuned our models to give you the absolute best quality of answers we have seen from any LLM (benchmarks will be revealed soon). Our models are trained to not please you, and tell you what they think is the truth,” Goyal remarked.

articles.title: 7 Books with twisted endings for psychological thriller Fans
articles.text:
7 Books with twisted endings for psychological thriller Fans
Discover seven psychological thriller books with shocking twists, unreliable narrators and unexpected endings that will keep you guessing.
Psychological thrillers are at their best when they make readers question everything they think they know.
A seemingly trustworthy character may be hiding a disturbing secret, an ordinary relationship may conceal years of manipulation, and a small detail introduced early in the story may completely change the meaning of everything that follows.
For fans of mind games, unreliable narrators and shocking revelations, a predictable ending can be disappointing. The real thrill comes from reaching the final pages and discovering that the story was never quite what it seemed.
If you enjoy books that keep you guessing until the very end, these seven psychological thrillers deserve a place on your reading list. Each offers a gripping mystery, unexpected turns or revelations that can change how you interpret the entire story.
7 Books with twisted endings for psychological thriller fans
1. The Silent Patient by Alex Michaelides
Alicia Berenson is a celebrated painter whose seemingly perfect life changes when her husband is murdered. After the killing, she stops speaking entirely. Years later, psychotherapist Theo Faber becomes determined to uncover what happened and understand her silence.
As Theo investigates Alicia's past, the distinction between truth, memory and obsession becomes increasingly difficult to navigate. The novel's final revelation encourages readers to reconsider the clues scattered throughout the story.
Why read it: Choose this if you love psychological suspense in which the narrator's perspective may be hiding more than it reveals. The ending is especially satisfying for readers who enjoy revisiting earlier chapters with a fresh understanding.
2. Gone Girl by Gillian Flynn
Nick Dunne becomes the prime suspect when his wife, Amy, disappears on their wedding anniversary. The evidence seems troubling, but the couple's marriage is more complicated than it initially appears.
Told through shifting perspectives, the novel gradually exposes the difference between public appearances and private realities. Gillian Flynn explores deception, control and the stories people construct to influence how others perceive them.
Why read it: This is an excellent choice for readers who enjoy morally complicated characters and stories that challenge their assumptions. Its revelations transform the mystery into a disturbing examination of marriage and manipulation.
3. Verity by Colleen Hoover
Lowen Ashleigh, a struggling writer, accepts a job completing a successful author's book series. While working at the author's home, she discovers an unpublished manuscript containing deeply disturbing accounts of the family's past.
As Lowen reads further, she begins questioning what she knows about Verity Crawford and the events surrounding her family. The story builds tension through competing versions of reality, leaving readers uncertain about whom they should believe.
Why read it: Read this if you enjoy disturbing secrets, morally ambiguous characters and endings that leave room for debate. The uncertainty surrounding the manuscript is a major part of the novel's appeal.
4. The Housemaid by Freida McFadden
Millie takes a job as a housemaid for a wealthy family, hoping for a fresh start. However, the seemingly comfortable household soon reveals unsettling dynamics, and her new position becomes more complicated than she expected.
As the story unfolds, the characters' motives become harder to read. What initially appears to be a straightforward domestic mystery develops into a tense story about power, secrets and survival.
Why read it: Its fast pace, short chapters and escalating revelations make it a strong pick for readers who want an addictive thriller they can finish over a weekend.
5. Rock Paper Scissors by Alice Feeney
Adam and Amelia travel to a remote location in Scotland in the hope of repairing their troubled marriage. Instead of bringing them closer, the trip creates an atmosphere of suspicion as long-buried secrets begin to surface.
Alternating perspectives and revelations about the couple's relationship gradually complicate the story. The isolated setting adds to the tension, while the narrative encourages readers to question how well spouses can truly know one another.
Why read it: This is a good choice if you enjoy relationship drama mixed with psychological suspense. It rewards readers who pay attention to small details and question what the characters choose to reveal.
6. The Wife Between Us by Greer Hendricks and Sarah Pekkanen
A complicated relationship involving a former wife, a new fiancée and a seemingly charming man sets the stage for this psychological thriller. At first, the situation appears to follow a familiar pattern of jealousy and romantic rivalry.
However, the narrative gradually challenges the assumptions readers make about the characters and their relationships. What appears straightforward becomes a more intricate story of deception, identity and control.
Why read it: Pick this up if you want a thriller that deliberately plays with your expectations. The changing picture of the characters is central to its suspense.
7. Behind Her Eyes by Sarah Pinborough
Louise becomes entangled in the lives of her new boss, David, and his wife, Adele, after a chance encounter leads to an unexpected connection. As she grows closer to both of them, she discovers that their marriage hides troubling secrets.
The story builds through suspicion, complicated loyalties and unanswered questions. Its final developments take the narrative in an unexpected direction, making it particularly suitable for readers who enjoy endings that challenge their understanding of the entire plot.
Why read it: Choose this for a particularly unconventional conclusion. If you enjoy psychological thrillers that push beyond familiar domestic mysteries, this one is worth considering.
Final thoughts
The best psychological thrillers do more than surprise readers with a final revelation. They build believable characters, plant subtle clues and create enough uncertainty to make every discovery feel significant.
Whether you prefer the calculated deception of Gone Girl, the unsettling atmosphere of Verity or the intricate mystery of The Silent Patient, these seven novels offer different approaches to suspense and misdirection.
If you are new to the genre, start with The Silent Patient. If you have already read the popular titles, try Rock Paper Scissors or The Wife Between Us for more relationship-driven mysteries.

articles.title: “Grâce à l’IA, cela ne nous a pris que quelques heures” : comment Saint-Gobain veut rendre le ciment plus écologique
articles.text:
“Grâce à l’IA, cela ne nous a pris que quelques heures” : comment Saint-Gobain veut rendre le ciment plus écologique
Le groupe français Saint-Gobain s'ouvre à son utilisation de Microsoft Discovery. Grâce à l'agent IA dédié à la R&D, de nouvelles molécules ont été identifiées pour rendre le ciment plus écologique.
Si l'IA et ses data centers sont un fléau écologique avéré, son utilisation judicieuse peut cependant aider à compenser et à faire progresser la cause écologique dans certains domaines. C'est aujourd'hui l'argument avancé par le Français Saint-Gobain, dont les recherches ont été sérieusement aidées par l'agent IA dédié à la R&D de Microsoft, Microsoft Discovery.
Saint-Gobain veut rendre le ciment plus performant et écologique
D'après Saint-Gobain, la production de ciment est très énergivore et représente environ 7 % des émissions annuelles mondiales de CO₂. La firme a donc deux objectifs : réduire ces émissions de carbone en explorant de nouvelles pistes, mais aussi améliorer la performance de ce matériau central dans la construction.
Pour cela, Saint-Gobain a décidé de passer par l'IA de Microsoft, ouverte depuis mars dernier à la firme, pour accélérer les choses. Mojdeh Rastgoo-Lemaitre, responsable du programme d’accélération numérique de Saint-Gobain, déclare que pour commencer : "Nous avons rassemblé 62 000 brevets et 44 000 publications scientifiques."
Elle ajoute :
	
Il aurait fallu un an à nos chercheurs pour créer la base de connaissances. Grâce à l’IA, cela ne nous a pris que quelques heures.
Une fois cela fait, Microsoft Discovery a affiné les choses et, en six semaines, de nouvelles pistes ont permis d'identifier de nouveaux éléments susceptibles d’entrer dans la composition d’additifs pour ciment. Le but est notamment de réduire la présence du clinker, un constituant du ciment qui fait office de liant, responsable de fortes émissions de CO₂.
	
C’est un moment charnière. J’espère que nous entrons dans une nouvelle ère de découvertes extraordinaires. Je pense que nous devons essayer d’en tirer le meilleur parti.
Pour le moment, des molécules qui n’auraient autrement pas été envisagées, car situées en dehors du secteur de la construction, sont testées par les chercheurs. Si leur potentiel est avéré, la prochaine étape sera de tester l'additif généré dans des conditions physiques réelles.
Si l'intérêt de l'IA pour agréger rapidement de nombreuses données est avéré, Saint-Gobain garde cependant les pieds sur terre. "Il est important de ne pas parler de l’IA comme d’une fin en soi", explique Annica Hagen, directrice de l'IA de Saint-Gobain, "c’est un levier pour nous permettre d’aller là où nous voulons aller." Il y a quelques jours, une chercheuse en IA alertait sur le fait que déléguer à l'IA nous fait perdre en compétence et nous rend dépendant.

articles.text:
Wednesday, October 21st 2026
Chieftec Launches Two New Compact CPU Coolers
Chieftec has launched two compact CPU coolers, the CAC-S90PWM-T120 tower cooler and the CAC-S92PWM-LP45 low-profile model. Both were first previewed at Computex 2026, as we reported earlier. They follow the recent release of the taller CAC-S120PWM-T150 tower cooler, which stands 148 mm tall and features an all-black matte finish. The CAC-S90PWM-T120 measures 80 x 92 x 117 mm and uses four 6 mm heat pipes with an aluminium fin stack. Do not let yourself be fooled by the T120 suffix into thinking it uses a 120 mm fan. articles.title: GM is giving OnStar an AI makeover | TechCrunch
articles.text:
General Motors is adding a personal AI assistant to OnStar as part of a broader makeover of the subscription-based connected car service that the U.S. automaker launched 30 years ago.
The OnStar AI Assistant will debut in the 2027 Cadillac Lyriq EV in the coming months, with more GM vehicles to follow, the company said Wednesday at its GM Forward event in New York, where it made a series of other technology announcements. The company said it will launch a new OnStar mobile app in 2027 that will complement and sync up with its in-car software.
The new OnStar mobile app will replace the current OnStar Guardian app that launched in 2020 as well as vehicle brand apps for Buick, Cadillac, Chevrolet, and GMC.
This tech-centric reboot is unlike other attempts to modernize OnStar and it notably puts agentic AI at the center. The company has updated the safety and roadside assistance service numerous times in its history, especially in the past five years as it tried to stay apace of emerging and tech-forward competitors like Tesla.
In 2021, the company expanded its OnStar Guardian app, which offered crash detection, emergency assistance and location sharing, to anyone with a compatible phone, even if they didn’t own a GM vehicle. A year later, GM started using Google Cloud’s conversational AI Dialogflow to recognize specific spoken requests and expanded in 2023 to give drivers responses to common queries like routing and navigation assistance — all part of GM’s plan to build a $25 billion subscription business by 2030.
GM continued to focus on generative AI, but relied on Google to provide the experience. The company said last year that Google Gemini would roll out in vehicles in 2026.
The OnStar AI Assistant is an in-house effort and one aimed at giving the driver and passengers an interactive and custom experience — and become even more embedded in their daily lives.
“OnStar is now transitioning to be a connected intelligence platform, not just the call center that it’s historically been known as, but a mechanism for interpreting, understanding, and providing predictive, proactive support to its owners,” GM’s chief product officer Sterling Anderson told TechCrunch in an interview ahead of the GM Forward event.
For instance, cameras on the vehicle will be connected to the software to offer live views as well as crash and safety recordings. Users can set up the connected cameras to turn on automatically if the vehicle senses an impending event — for instance an aggressive horn honk — then capture the event and upload it to the OnStar app. Users will be able to use voice to control certain functions on the vehicle, including climate, and ask questions about any specific vehicle feature.
The launch coincides with efforts throughout the auto industry to stay apace of Chinese automakers with technology that is central to the vehicle — and no longer a slapped on gimmick or feature. But that has required GM to change its approach to software development, adopt AI tools, and even design a new electrical and centralized compute vehicle architecture.
The announcement also comes after GM has been criticized and even fined for sharing data with third parties. The company said customers will have the ability to decide what data is shared, and that the recordings have time limits and are encrypted. GM said it and OnStar cannot access Connected Camera recordings.

articles.title: ‘It's our mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more’: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlines what businesses need to conquer the AI frontier ecosystem
articles.text:
‘It's our mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more’: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlines what businesses need to conquer the AI frontier ecosystem
Don’t be overwhelmed by AI, Satya Nadella says
- Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella extols virtues of "frontier ecosystem" for AI
- AI can do great things for human workers, but there still needs to be some control
- Microsoft reveals new research showing a divide between bosses and employees over the future of AI in the workplace
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has urged businesses to embrace AI even further to push on and succeed, but urged caution around giving such systems too much control in everyday work tasks.
"When I think about what keeps us grounded every day at Microsoft, it's our mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more,” Nadella told the company’s Frontier Tour London event.
Looking at what he called the "frontier ecosystem", Nadella identified three key pillars which need to be tackled - including recapturing individual empowerment, as although AI is taking charge of the dullest parts of our jobs, there is still need for a human to have control.
Frontier AI
Nadella also highlighted "the reverse information paradox" - with a digital learning system which is constantly improving itself, the challenge is for organisations to "capture that knowledge and keep it locally to yourself...in other words, you have to own the knowledge that gets created, both with the human capital that you have, as well as the token capital that you generate"
The final challenge concerns trust, as Nadella noted, “our scaling laws are producing even more powerful models that are less and less trustworthy…you need to treat these models as new forms of insiders, and create a zero-trust architecture around it.”
The speech came as Microsoft unveiled new research revealing something of a divide between bosses and employees over the future of AI in the workplace.
It found the vast majority (84%) of business leaders believe the UK can become a world-leading AI economy within five years, compared with just 41% of employees.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
But it also noted that workers are becoming increasingly concerned about the impact on jobs and opportunities for young people, with over half (57%) of employees using AI at work afraid it will reduce opportunities for young people, while 35% fear for their own job security.
For bosses, the future was a bit brighter, with 90% of leaders claiming they had a clear AI strategy in their business, while 84% of those in organisations already adopting AI say they’ve already experienced moderate or significant changes to how their work gets done.
“Bending the curve changes what the UK can achieve, increasing productivity, business growth, better public services, and the measure of that progress is the difference that people feel in their everyday lives,” noted Darren Hardman, Microsoft UK CEO.
“We will not bend the curve unless people see a place for themselves in what comes next…the question is no longer whether you have a strategy, it’s whether AI is actually changing how work gets done.”
“For organizations here, the challenge is to turn AI's potential into improvements that people can feel in the work they do, the services they use, and the opportunities that are open to them...our role at Microsoft to bring intelligence and trust together in AI that puts your organization's knowledge to work helping people achieve more while providing the safeguards and visibility to stay in control.”

articles.title: India’s OSAT Buildout Puts Semiconductor Testing in Focus - EE Times
articles.text:
With five semiconductor plants in India now in commercial production, the harder question is no longer if the country can package chips, but whether it can test them fast enough, across enough device types, to hit production targets.
The testing challenge arrives as global semiconductor test equipment sales are forecasted to grow 31% to $15.3 billion in 2026, following 55.3% growth in 2025, according to SEMI’s July 2026 forecast. The industry body expects sales to reach $20.8 billion by 2028, driven partly by increasing device complexity and more demanding performance and reliability requirements.
Against that backdrop, Indian outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) companies must accommodate different device types, meet production targets, and maintain test coverage as they scale. Some must modernize legacy testing platforms, while others need to develop test architectures from scratch for new chips.
Testing times
When an Indian chip facility announces it can produce 15 million chips a year, that number says little about how many testers it needs. A chip tested in under a minute and one that takes five to 10 minutes can demand very different amounts of equipment for the same output.
In September 2025, Emerson announced a partnership with Kaynes Semicon to deploy its NI Semiconductor Test System (STS) as the primary test platform across Kaynes’ OSAT facility in Sanand, Gujarat. EE Times spoke with Karthik Balasekar, chief business manager for semiconductor and electronics, and Ved Mahanta, principal account manager, both at NI India, part of Emerson.
“Customers typically conduct tester qualification before making a final purchasing decision,” Mahanta said. “The process generally takes six months to one year. In the case of Kaynes, we can publicly state that the company has decided to proceed with NI testers. We are in the process of delivering the testers in the coming months.”
Mahanta added that discussions with other OSAT facilities were ongoing, with many still qualifying test equipment. NI could not identify some of these companies because their engagements were not publicly disclosed.
Balasekar said the number of testers also depends on the time required to test each device and the production target. “Facilities handling millions of devices may need fewer testers if each test takes less than a minute,” he explained. “Testing complex chips that require five or 10 minutes per device could demand more equipment to meet the same production target.”
Mahanta said, “An OSAT might announce an annual capacity of 14 million or 15 million chips, for example. Such figures generally represent the combined output capacity of its production lines, whether the facility operates 10 lines, 50 lines, or another number.”
Mahanta said NI Emerson has not publicly announced a specific number of test systems for Kaynes. He compared OSAT capacity announcements with those of automotive plants, which state how many vehicles they can produce annually. “Actual production depends on customer demand,” he said.
For relatively simple chips, pin count and the types of tests required are key factors. A chip with fewer pins and simpler testing requirements takes less time to test, allowing the same number of testers to process more devices.
In production environments, the priority is to test as many chips as possible in the shortest time while ensuring that devices meet their required specifications.
Mahanta said TestStand, NI’s test automation platform, automates test sequences to speed up decisions on whether a batch of chips is suitable for delivery.
Balasekar indicated that Kaynes’s selection reflects the need for test platforms that can accommodate different semiconductor device types. “Our STS is a platform that supports both mixed-signal and RF applications,” he said. “For example, if Kaynes tests mixed-signal products today and moves to RF products later, it can reuse the same STS tester for different devices under test.”
Flexibility is only part of the picture. The test architecture that an OSAT needs also depends on whether it is handling an established chip or a new design. “Typically, customers want to test two types of devices: legacy devices and new products, commonly referred to as new product development,” Mahanta said.
For legacy products, manufacturers may rely on older test platforms that can no longer deliver the required throughput. “OSATs need to move these products to newer systems without compromising test coverage,” Mahanta said, adding that customers often do much of the preparatory work and specify what the OSAT needs to test.
New designs present a different challenge, particularly when the customer is a semiconductor startup. “Some Indian startups developing their own chips have never performed final testing and depend on the OSAT to guide them,” Mahanta said. “The OSAT must help determine how to test each device reliably and quickly enough to meet production and time-to-market requirements.”
Although new devices do not carry the technical debt associated with legacy test platforms, they may require the OSAT to develop a test architecture from scratch. “This includes determining the test requirements, selecting an appropriate system, and ensuring that it meets test coverage and throughput targets,” Mahanta said. “Such a system could come from NI Emerson or another test equipment supplier.”
Both challenges—migrating established products to newer test platforms and developing test architectures for new devices—become more difficult to address with increasing design complexity, Balasekar said.
As semiconductor devices gain functionality, OSATs will need test systems that can accommodate evolving requirements without compromising existing test coverage. Mahanta said modular PXI (PCI eXtensions for Instrumentation) systems can allow customers to add modules for new tests without changing existing test parameters. “Customers can expand their testing capabilities as their requirements evolve,” he said.
AI enters test development
For new devices, NI applies AI to parts of test development, including the initial design of test architectures.
Mahanta said an engineer could upload a chip’s datasheet to NI’s Nigel AI test development tool, which examines selected parameters and suggest a potential test architecture. “The engineer could then use the suggested framework as a starting point rather than developing the entire architecture from scratch,” he explained.
“This approach targets part of the work involved in test development, rather than replacing the validation engineer,” Mahanta said. “AI could take on some repetitive tasks, leaving engineers to focus on more complex problem-solving.”
Under India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 (ISM 2.0), the government will focus on building an ecosystem across six areas, including advanced packaging and testing units and talent, Ashwini Vaishnaw, India’s minister for electronics and information technology, said at SEMICON India 2026. For OSATs, that makes test system flexibility, device qualification, and the ability to accommodate different device requirements relevant to the industry’s next phase of growth.
Mahanta said NI has invested in local engineering capabilities so its engineers can support OSAT customers on site, reducing the need to bring specialists from Taiwan and Singapore. He also cited Tessolve, an NI partner serving customers globally, as an example of an Indian company participating in the testing ecosystem.
“There are integrated device manufacturers that base 40% to 50% of their product lines in India,” he said. “Building engineering expertise will be essential for Indian companies seeking to serve global semiconductor manufacturers.”
Balasekar said growth in OSATs and electronics manufacturing could outpace the availability of skilled workers. India’s exports of electronic devices and its expanding mobile phone manufacturing base add to the demand for talent. He pointed to the workforce development component of ISM 2.0 as one way to address the gap. “I think that will help India grow faster and keep pace with the market’s expansion,” he said.

articles.title: Crypto Derivatives Exchanges With the Lowest Trading Fees for 2026 - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Trading fees represent the single largest ongoing friction for active crypto derivatives traders. Because perpetual futures positions involve leverage, fee percentages apply to the full notional trade value rather than your initial margin balance.
On a 100,000 USDT position opened with 1,000 USDT of margin, a 0.0600% taker fee costs 60 USDT, equivalent to 6% of your initial capital on entry alone.
However, headline rates tell only half the story. The true cost of trading depends on how much capital an exchange requires before unlocking its first discounted fee tier, whether you trade as a maker or taker, and how funding rate cycles affect overnight positions. This guide analyzes the lowest fee crypto derivatives exchanges for 2026, comparing base schedules, accessible VIP thresholds, and total execution costs.
Lowest Fee Crypto Derivatives Exchanges Compared
The table below compares standard entry-level rates, the first discounted VIP tier, qualifying capital thresholds, and contract counts across the lowest fee derivatives platforms.
| Rank | Platform | Best For | Standard Maker / Taker | VIP 1 Maker / Taker | VIP 1 Qualifying Threshold | Max Leverage | 
| 1 | MEXC | Zero headline maker rates | 0.0000% / 0.0200% (web) | Volume-based scaling | High monthly trading volume | 500x | 
| 2 | BloFin | Most accessible VIP fee ladder | 0.0200% / 0.0600% | 0.0060% / 0.0500% | 50,000 USDT account equity | 150x | 
| 3 | Binance | Low base taker fees with depth | 0.0200% / 0.0500% | 0.0180% / 0.0500% | 5M USD volume plus 5 BNB held | 125x | 
| 4 | OKX | Balanced volume discounts | 0.0200% / 0.0500% | 0.0160% / 0.0450% | 100,000 USDT assets or 5M USD vol | 100x | 
| 5 | Bybit | Deep taker cuts at size | 0.0200% / 0.0550% | 0.0180% / 0.0400% | 100,000 USDT assets or 10M USD vol | 100x | 
| 6 | Kraken Pro | Volume scaling with compliance | 0.0200% / 0.0500% | Scales with volume | Volume based | 100x | 
| 7 | Bitget | Low asset barrier to tier 1 | 0.0200% / 0.0600% | 0.0160% / 0.0600% | 30,000 USDT platform assets | 125x | 
1. MEXC: Zero Maker Fees and Low Headline Web Pricing
MEXC promotes the lowest entry-level fee schedule in the crypto derivatives market. On eligible manual web and app trades, the platform charges 0.0000% for maker orders and a flat 0.0200% for taker fills. For retail traders placing passive limit orders on major pairs, this eliminates transaction costs entirely on execution while deploying isolated or cross-margin capital.
However, active traders must evaluate several hidden cost factors before committing capital. Automated API execution follows a separate, significantly higher pricing schedule of 0.0600% maker and 0.0800% taker, making algorithmic strategies far more expensive than web trading. Contract fee mechanics and risk tiers are detailed on MEXC Learn. Thinner order book depth on secondary altcoins can also produce slippage that quickly offsets headline savings.
- Key Strengths: Zero maker fees on manual web orders, low 0.0200% base taker rate, massive catalog of 1,000+ perpetual pairs, and up to 500x leverage on BTC/ETH.
- Limitations: API trading carries a steep 0.0600% / 0.0800% schedule, order book depth is thin on long-tail pairs, and the exchange holds an unlicensed warning from Hong Kong regulators.
2. BloFin: Most Accessible VIP Ladder and Lowest Tier 1 Maker Rates
BloFin provides the most accessible route to institutional fee discounts in crypto derivatives. Where legacy venues demand 5 million to 10 million USD in monthly turnover to leave base pricing, BloFin unlocks VIP 1 at an equity threshold of just 50,000 USDT. At this tier, maker fees drop to 0.0060% and taker rates to 0.0500%, undercutting VIP 1 maker rates on Binance and Bybit (0.0180%) on BTCUSDT.
A lower fee only helps if the stop includes it. Auto Breakeven adds the trading fee and the funding to the entry, then moves the stop there after a price you set is hit. A second order can keep its own stop under Multi-Position. On the other exchanges that second order is folded into the first and the average price changes. The practice balance is 5,000 USDT. The perpetual count is 508 contracts across USDT-M, USDC-M, and Coin-M.
- Key Strengths: VIP 1 fee discounts unlocked at just 50,000 USDT equity, industry-leading 0.0060% VIP 1 maker rate, Auto Breakeven fee-inclusive protection, Multi-Position order segregation, and 150x leverage on BTC/ETH.
- Limitations: Top-of-book depth on secondary altcoins is lighter than Binance, making it best suited to retail and mid-size active traders rather than institutional block orders.
3. Binance: Low Base Taker Fees and Deep Slippage Protection
Binance features a competitive entry-level rate of 0.0200% maker and 0.0500% taker across its USD-M futures markets. For accounts that execute large market orders, the exchange’s massive order book depth provides superior price protection. Binance has the deepest BTC and ETH books in this set, which is what keeps a large taker order from walking the price.
The trade-off is the height of the VIP ladder for active derivatives accounts. Progressing from base pricing to VIP 1 requires achieving at least 5 million USD in 30-day derivatives volume and holding a daily balance of 5 BNB. Without the BNB fee deduction, standard USDT taker fees remain at 0.0500% at VIP 1. Detailed tier formulas, taker discounts, and collateral options are explained on Binance Academy.
- Key Strengths: Deepest order books in the industry with minimal fill slippage, competitive 0.0500% base taker pricing, 800+ perpetual markets, and multi-asset collateral support.
- Limitations: VIP 1 needs 5 million USD in 30-day volume plus 5 BNB. Binance completed a full exit from the European Union on 1 July 2026. US access is through Binance.US. It has exited Canada.
4. OKX: Balanced Volume Discounts and Portfolio Margin Efficiency
OKX pairs an entry-level fee structure of 0.0200% maker and 0.0500% taker with one of the most flexible VIP pathways among major derivatives venues. Traders can qualify for VIP 1 through two separate routes: maintaining 100,000 USDT in account assets or generating 5 million USD in 30-day derivatives volume. Qualifying drops maker fees to 0.0160% and taker fees to 0.0450%.
The platform further reduces execution costs through its unified portfolio margin architecture. By pooling collateral across spot, perpetuals, and options, OKX dynamically offsets margin requirements on hedged positions. Margin calculation models, risk formulas, and API rate tiers are documented on OKX Learn. This capital efficiency reduces the amount of idle collateral required to maintain active derivatives positions across multiple contracts.
- Key Strengths: Two separate qualifying paths for VIP 1, competitive 0.0450% taker rate at tier 1, capital-efficient unified portfolio margin, and low-latency API tools.
- Limitations: The density of settings within the unified account interface creates a steep learning curve for newer traders, and derivatives services are excluded in the United States.
5. Bybit: Deep Taker Cuts for High-Volume Derivatives Accounts
Bybit charges an entry-level fee of 0.0200% maker and 0.0550% taker on its perpetual contracts. While its standard taker fee sits slightly above Binance, Bybit offers one of the steepest fee reductions once an account reaches VIP status. VIP 1 reduces taker fees to 0.0400% and maker fees to 0.0180%, delivering excellent value for high-turnover traders across 860+ perpetual markets.
To reach VIP 1, accounts must hold 100,000 USDT in platform assets or generate 10 million USDT in 30-day derivatives turnover. The platform backs its fee schedule with a fast matching engine that handles 100,000 transactions per second per contract, keeping slippage low during fast market swings. Tier benefits, liquidation formulas, and trading bot integration are detailed on Bybit Learn.
- Key Strengths: Sharp reduction to 0.0400% taker fees at VIP 1, broad selection of 860+ perpetual contracts, highly responsive order terminal, and native bracket orders.
- Limitations: Base taker fee is higher than Binance, reaching VIP 1 requires 100,000 USDT in assets or 10 million USD in volume, and access is prohibited in the US and Canada.
6. Kraken Pro: Volume-Based Fee Discounts With Regulated Custody
Kraken Pro delivers a volume-based fee model backed by an exceptional security record dating back to 2011 without suffering a catastrophic exchange breach. Base derivatives pricing starts at 0.0200% maker and 0.0500% taker across more than 300 perpetual markets under isolated and cross-margin modes, with 100x leverage on BTC and ETH. Further fee reductions scale progressively across established volume tiers.
Because Kraken operates under regulatory oversight in the United States, United Kingdom, and European Union, traders avoid the compliance risks associated with unregulated offshore platforms. United States clients can trade CME-cleared micro contracts through Kraken Derivatives US with predictable settlement costs. Account structures, fee schedules, leverage brackets, and margin rules are published on Kraken Learn. Altcoin leverage remains at 20x to 50x.
- Key Strengths: Volume-based fee cuts, a security record back to 2011 with no catastrophic hack, regulated status in the US, UK and EU, and 100x leverage.
- Limitations: Smaller perpetual contract menu than offshore venues (300+ pairs), conservative leverage limits on altcoins, and jurisdictional variations in product access.
7. Bitget: Low Asset Barrier to Tier 1 With Broad Copy Trading
Bitget provides standard derivatives pricing of 0.0200% maker and 0.0600% taker across its USDT-M and Coin-M contracts, supporting up to 125x leverage on major pairs. The exchange offers the lowest nominal asset-based VIP threshold among major centralized platforms, granting VIP 1 status to users maintaining 30,000 USDT in platform balance across more than 700 active perpetual markets under isolated and cross margin.
At VIP 1, maker fees drop to 0.0160%, although the perpetual taker fee remains near 0.0600% until higher volume tiers are reached. Traders frequently combine this fee tier with Bitget’s One-Click Copy Trade system, which allows users to study historical trader drawdowns, 30-day returns, and win rates before allocating capital. Fee schedules, margin tiers, and strategy guides are available on Bitget Academy.
- Key Strengths: Low 30,000 USDT asset requirement for VIP 1, massive social and copy-trading network, 125x leverage on major contracts, and monthly proof-of-reserves reporting.
- Limitations: Base taker fees remain at 0.0600% through initial tiers, and liquidity on small-cap altcoins can thin out during sharp market pullbacks.
The Total Cost of Trading: Beyond Headline Maker and Taker Fees
Evaluating derivatives costs solely on entry-level maker/taker tables often leads to poor decisions. Four interconnected elements determine what an account actually pays to trade:
1. The Accessibility Gap in VIP Schedules
Many traders look at a fee table and assume they will pay the discounted rate. Binance’s VIP 1 needs 5 million USD in 30-day volume plus 5 BNB held, and the standard USDT taker stays 0.0500% at that tier unless the BNB discount applies. BloFin opens VIP 1 at 50,000 USDT in equity, where the maker rate is 0.0060% and the taker is 0.0500%.
2. Bid-Ask Spreads and Fill Slippage
A low taker fee provides no advantage if an illiquid order book forces you to cross a wide spread. On BTC and ETH, Binance has the deepest book in this set. On smaller altcoins the spread can cost more than the fee. Check the book on the contract you actually trade.
3. Funding Rate Cycles and Holding Costs
Perpetual contracts do not expire. To keep perpetual contract prices aligned with spot indexes, exchanges use periodic funding rates, settled every 8 hours on most centralized platforms. If funding prints at +0.04% per 8-hour cycle, a long position with 20x leverage pays 0.12% per day simply to stay open. Over a two-week swing trade, funding deductions can easily outpace initial maker/taker expenses.
4. Fee-Inclusive Automation Tools
When managing high-leverage trades, calculating exact breakeven points manually can lead to execution errors. If a trader enters at $80,000 and moves their stop to $80,000, a stop trigger still loses money due to round-trip taker fees and accrued funding. Automated tools like BloFin’s Auto Breakeven dynamically compute fees and funding into the stop placement, locking in true capital protection without guesswork.
How to Choose the Lowest Cost Exchange for Your Strategy
- For Active Limit Order Traders: BloFin offers the lowest cost structure, delivering a 0.0060% maker rate at an accessible 50,000 USDT equity threshold.
- For Passive Manual Scalpers: MEXC provides 0.0000% maker fees on web orders, provided you execute through the browser interface rather than an API.
- For Seven-Figure Market Orders: Binance ensures that massive taker orders execute with minimum price slippage due to its unmatched order book depth.
- For Hedged Multi-Asset Strategies: OKX reduces carrying costs through unified portfolio margin, offsetting collateral requirements across correlated positions.
- For High-Volume Algorithmic Desks: Bybit provides steep taker fee cuts down to 0.0400% once 30-day volume crosses 10 million USDT.
Frequently Asked Questions
Which crypto derivatives exchange has the lowest overall fees?
MEXC offers the lowest headline web rate with 0.0000% maker and 0.0200% taker fees on eligible manual contracts. However, for traders seeking accessible VIP discounts on major centralized order books, BloFin unlocks a 0.0060% maker rate and 0.0500% taker rate at 50,000 USDT equity, outperforming the VIP 1 maker pricing on Binance, Bybit, and OKX.
What is the difference between maker and taker fees on futures contracts?
Maker fees apply when an order adds liquidity to the order book, such as a limit order placed below the current market price for a buy. Taker fees apply when an order removes liquidity immediately, such as a market order or limit order that crosses the spread. Because makers provide liquidity, exchanges charge lower maker fees and sometimes offer rebates.
How does funding rate impact the total cost of a perpetual trade?
Funding rates are periodic cash flows exchanged between long and short traders, settled every 8 hours on most centralized platforms. If the funding rate is positive, long traders pay short traders to keep perpetual prices tied to the spot index. Over multi-day swing positions, positive funding payments can accumulate into a significant cost that exceeds initial transaction fees.
How do VIP fee tiers work on crypto derivatives exchanges?
Exchanges offer progressive fee discounts based on either an account’s 30-day trading volume or total asset balance. On legacy venues like Binance and Bybit, reaching discounted VIP 1 rates typically requires 5 million to 10 million USD in monthly volume. On newer venues like BloFin, accounts can qualify for VIP 1 rates purely by maintaining 50,000 USDT in account balance, bypassing high volume hurdles.
