articles.title: Elon Musk dispara los ingresos de SpaceX a 14.600 millones de dólares: centros de datos e IA, son la clave
articles.text:
Los ingresos de USD 14.600 millones que SpaceX reportó en el tercer trimestre de 2026 estuvieron impulsados por sus centros de datos y negocios de inteligencia artificial, que ya representan el 52% de la facturación de la compañía dirigida por Elon Musk.
La expansión de esta área, rebautizada como Super Inteligencia, explica la transformación de SpaceX: la empresa sumó USD 7.500 millones en ingresos mediante la herramienta de programación Cursor, el bot Grok y, sobre todo, su negocio de nube para inteligencia artificial.
Según TechCrunch, los centros de datos y los agentes de Grok generaron más ganancias de las previstas por los inversores.
La división de IA obtuvo USD 431 millones de beneficio, aunque el resultado fue afectado por USD 1.200 millones en gastos extraordinarios de compensación en acciones vinculados a la compra de Cursor.
Cómo es la iniciativa de Super Inteligencia de SpaceX
La línea de Super Inteligencia combina productos de software y capacidad de cómputo a gran escala.
Su negocio de nube ya cuenta con 1,7 GW de capacidad informática, un volumen que se convirtió en el principal motor de los resultados trimestrales.
El crecimiento de los ingresos también estuvo acompañado por una recuperación de la rentabilidad.
SpaceX registró un beneficio neto de USD 4.400 millones, frente a la pérdida de USD 1.000 millones que había informado en el mismo trimestre del año anterior.
Sin embargo, la expansión exige inversiones elevadas. La empresa destinó USD 19.600 millones a gastos de capital y prevé invertir entre USD 35.000 millones y USD 40.000 millones adicionales en el cuarto trimestre, mientras avanza con un segundo proyecto de centro de datos, Colossus II, y con el desarrollo del cohete Starship.
Cuál es el rol de los centros de datos en SpaceX
Musk sostiene que el principal límite para desplegar sistemas de superinteligencia ya no está solo en los chips, sino en la energía, la refrigeración y la infraestructura necesaria para operar los centros de datos.
Por eso, pasa cuatro días por semana en Memphis, Tennessee, donde se construye Colossus II.
La compañía busca trasladar a esa infraestructura capacidades industriales desarrolladas para sus operaciones espaciales.
Por ejemplo, utiliza técnicas de fundición de metal para fabricar componentes de turbinas y reducir las demoras de entre 12 y 18 meses que enfrentan los fabricantes para conseguir palas y álabes.
La apuesta también se conecta con Starlink, que alcanzó 13,6 millones de clientes. Musk prevé que el crecimiento de los agentes de inteligencia artificial aumente la demanda de conectividad, mientras SpaceX proyecta desplegar una nueva generación de satélites y desarrollar centros de datos orbitales.
Elon Musk presenta la nueva línea Roadster de Tesla
Elon Musk presentó el nuevo Tesla Roadster, un deportivo eléctrico con tecnologías desarrolladas junto con SpaceX y una promesa de producción para 2028.
La exhibición buscó reposicionar al modelo como una demostración de ingeniería extrema, más que como un vehículo de producción masiva.
El Roadster incorpora propulsores derivados de SpaceX, que Tesla utilizó durante la presentación para exhibir maniobras aéreas breves y una aceleración fuera de los parámetros habituales de la industria.
Musk sostuvo que el auto podrá acelerar de 0 a 60 millas por hora en menos de un segundo en algunas configuraciones.
El evento se realizó en una instalación de pruebas de SpaceX en McGregor, Texas. Allí, Tesla mostró un vehículo biplaza capaz de subir una rampa pronunciada, quedar suspendido boca abajo y completar un giro antes de aterrizar con asistencia de chorros de aire.
La compañía no informó el precio ni el volumen previsto de producción.
El proyecto refuerza la alianza tecnológica entre Tesla y SpaceX. Sin embargo, todavía quedan interrogantes sobre la homologación para circular en la vía pública y sobre si las capacidades exhibidas en el escenario podrán trasladarse al producto final.

articles.title: Narnia plus fort que Barbie et Mario : le film Netflix affole les compteurs de YouTube
articles.text:
Narnia plus fort que Barbie et Mario : le film Netflix affole les compteurs de YouTube
La bande-annonce du futur blockbuster Narnia : Le Neveu du magicien de Netflix a cartonné sur YouTube, surpassant le nombre de vues de Barbie et Super Mario Galaxy.
Dévoilée la semaine dernière sur Internet, la bande-annonce du film Narnia : Le Neveu du magicien a confirmé son statut d'événement en enregistrant près de 500 millions de vues YouTube en une semaine. Un score impressionnant, qui place le blockbuster Netflix au-dessus de gros films de cinéma.
Narnia, l'événement streaming de 2027
Selon le site WaveMetrix, la bande-annonce de cette nouvelle adaptation de l'œuvre de C.S. Lewis a enregistré 481,3 millions de vues en sept petits jours sur YouTube. Narnia : Le Neveu du magicien surpasse ainsi le cumul de Barbie (240 millions de vues) sur la même période, offrant au passage un nouveau record à Greta Gerwig, mais aussi des populaires Wonka (237,2 millions) et Super Mario Galaxie, le film (281,6 millions).
Dans un monde où l'attrait des spectateurs est difficile à quantifier, les scores des bandes-annonces sur YouTube restent d'excellents indicateurs. Wonka avait d'ailleurs confirmé cela en générant 634,5 millions de dollars au box-office mondial, quand Super Mario Galaxy et Barbie avait fini leurs carrières respectives à 1,013 et 1,447 milliard de dollars. Un plébiscite qu'espère sans aucun doute Netflix.
Il faut toutefois relativiser, car si la bande-annonce du film Narnia affole les compteurs, cela reste très (très) loin des mastodontes en la matière Spider-Man : Brand New Day détient ainsi le record de la bande-annonce la plus visionnée en 24 heures, avec 718,6 millions de vues, devant celles de Deadpool & Wolverine (365 millions) et Spider-Man : No Way Home (355 millions). Une tout autre catégorie.
Il n'empêche, cet accueil du trailer de Narnia : Le Neveu du magicien reste de très bon augure pour Netflix, qui mise beaucoup sur le film. Le géant du streaming a ainsi investi 280 millions de dollars dans le budget du long-métrage, et lui a réservé une sortie exceptionnelle avec une diffusion sur 1000 écrans IMAX aux États-Unis.
Pour rappel, Narnia : Le Neveu du magicien est écrit et réalisé par Greta Gerwig (Barbie, Ladybird) et compte à son casting les jeunes Beatrice Campbell et David McKenna, accompagnés de Emma Mackey, Daniel Craig, Carey Mulligan, Ciaran Hinds ou encore Meryl Streep.
Le film sortira ainsi en exclusivité au cinéma le 12 férier 2027, avant d'être disponible dans le monde entier (et en France) sur la plateforme de streaming à partir du 2 avril 2027.

articles.title: Los Oppo Find X10 y Find X10 Pro Max llegan para seguir demostrando que China lleva la batuta en fotografía móvil
articles.text:
Aunque los presentaron hace semanas en China, Oppo acaba de confirmar los detalles del lanzamiento europeo de sus nuevos buque insignia para los próximos meses. La noticia aquí es que... no hay sorpresa. Los Oppo Find X10 y Find X10 Pro Max son dos móviles que llegan casi de la mano con los Vivo X500 para cerrar un año espectacular en cuanto a las capacidades fotográficas de los smartphones.
De hecho, ya hemos publicado el análisis del Oppo Find X10 y, aunque evidentemente un móvil de casi 1.400 euros es interesante, el protagonista del desembarco de la marca china es un modelo Pro Max que tiene una única misión: seguir difuminando la línea entre la fotografía en smartphones y las cámaras de fotos "de toda la vida".
En corto. En cuanto a especificaciones, tenemos lo esperado y los dos modelos cumplen con lo que necesita un gama premium actualmente. Comparten una muy buena pantalla, 12 GB de memoria RAM, almacenamiento UFS 4.1 y características como baterías enormes que prometen mucho en el día a día.
En lugar de venir con lo último de Qualcomm, los dos se alían con MediaTek, teniendo el Dimensity 9600 Pro fabricado en una fotolitografía de 2 nanómetros en el caso del Pro Max y por el Dimensity 9600M en 3 nanómetros para el X10 a secas. Aunque sólo cambie una letra, hay un salto entre ambos con más núcleos de alta potencia en el caso del Dimensity 9600 Pro y, además, una GPU más potente.
|  | oppo find x10 pro max | oppo find x10 | 
|---|---|---|
| PANTALLA | Panel AMOLED de 6,78 pulgadas Resolución de 2.772 x 1.272 píxeles Refresco de 144 Hz Brillo pico de 3.600 nits Muestreo de 3.840 Hz | Panel AMOLED de 6,59 pulgadas Resolución de 2.772 x 1.272 píxeles Refresco de 144 Hz Brillo pico de 3.600 nits Muestreo de 3.840 Hz | 
| DIMENSIONES Y PESO | 161,3 x 76,6 x 8,4 mm 233 gramos | 156,5 x 74,3 x 8,4 mm 216 gramos | 
| PROCESADOR | Mediatek Dimensity 9600 Pro | Mediatek Dimensity 9600M | 
| RAM | 12 GB | 12 GB | 
| ALMACENAMIENTO | 512 GB UFS 4.1 | 256 o 512 GB UFS 4.1 | 
| BATERÍA | 7.150 mAh Carga de 80 W Carga inalámbrica de 50 W Carga inversa de 10 W | 7.150 mAh Carga de 80 W Carga inalámbrica de 50 W Carga inversa de 10 W | 
| SISTEMA OPERATIVO | Android 17 + ColorOS 17 | Android 17 + ColorOS 17 | 
| CONECTIVIDAD | Wi-Fi 7 Bluetooth 6.2 NFC GPS Emisor de infrarrojos | Wi-Fi 7 Bluetooth 6.2 NFC GPS Emisor de infrarrojos | 
| OTROS | Certificación IP69 Sensor de huellas ultrasónico | Certificación IP69 Sensor de huellas ultrasónico | 
| PRECIO | 1.799 euros | Desde 1.399 euros | 
Apuesta fotográfica. En características técnicas ya digo que cumplen, pero donde ambos ponen el foco es en la fotografía. En el análisis del Find X10 que ha hecho mi compañero Iván desgrana este punto y pone numerosos ejemplos en los que ver el rendimiento de la cámara.
Además, algo curioso es que aquí no tenemos un modelo "normal" y un "Pro", sino que Oppo ha optado por dar el salto del estándar al Pro Max directamente.Esto implica que el apartado fotográfico de ambos es completamente diferente, como podemos ver en la tabla comparativa.
|  | oppo find x10 pro max | oppo find x10 | 
|---|---|---|
| principal | 200 megapíxeles Sensor de 1/1,3 pulgadas Píxeles de 0,6 micras Apertura f/1,5 Distancia focal de 24 mm OIS | 200 megapíxeles Sensor de 1/1,4 pulgadas Píxeles de 0,56 micras Apertura f/1,6 Distancia focal de 23 mm OIS | 
| telefoto | 200 megapíxeles Sensor de 1/1,56 pulgadas Píxeles de 0,5 micras Apertura f/2,1 Distancia focal de 70 mm, 3x Sistema periscópico OIS | 200 megapíxeles Sensor de 1/1,56 pulgadas Píxeles de 0,5 micras Apertura f/2,6 Distancia focal de 65 mm, 2,8x Sistema periscópico OIS | 
| gran angular | 200 megapíxeles Sensor de 1/1,56 pulgadas Píxeles de 0,5 micras Distancia focal de 13 mm Apertura f/2,2 | 50 megapíxeles Sensor de 1/2,75 pulgadas Píxeles de 0,64 micras Distancia focal de 15 mm Apertura f/2 | 
| frontal | 50 megapíxeles Sensor de 1/2,76 pulgadas Píxeles de 0,64 micras Apertura f/2 Distancia focal de 18 mm | 50 megapíxeles Sensor de 1/2,76 pulgadas Píxeles de 0,64 micras Apertura f/2 Distancia focal de 18 mm | 
Ya no hablamos sólo de megapíxeles, algo de lo que el Find X10 va servido, sino de tres cámaras totalmente distintas tanto en tamaño como en prestaciones. Las del Find X10 Pro Max son las que salen favorecidas con sensores más grandes en el caso tanto de la cámara principal como del gran angular, así como de más distancia focal en el caso del telefoto.
El teleconvertidor como anzuelo. Pero claro, si por algo ha apostado Oppo en sus últimos 'flagships' y que no iba a dejar de lado ahora era por los teleconvertidores. Al igual que Vivo con sus objetivos de la mano de Zeiss, Oppo cuenta con un kit fotográfico junto a Hasselblad que incluye una funda especial a la que acoplar el teleconvertidor al Pro Max.
Esto permite pasar del 3x nativo a un 10x óptico que se puede ampliar tirando de megapíxeles para tener una calidad óptica hasta el 40x. Y digo totalmente en serio que, si tuviera que comprar ahora mismo un móvil, iría a por uno que contara con uno de estos kits porque me parecen una de las mejores ideas que ha tenido la industria estos últimos años.
Cuando vemos algo así, podemos pensar en esos objetivos que encontramos en tiendas como Amazon o Aliexpress que prometen resultados espectaculares, pero que decepcionan cuando los tenemos entre manos. Son objetivos grandes, sin estabilización y que, además, no están hechos para un teléfono en concreto, sino para un abanico de modelos. En el caso de los teleconvertidores de Oppo, Vivo u Honor, son elementos creados para sus propios modelos, por lo que la unión es perfecta y los resultados saltan a la vista.
Completando el tridente. Esto es algo por lo que las marcas chinas están empujando y que las sitúa, en mi opinión, un paso por delante de las estadounidenses o de Samsung. Oppo y Vivo están apostando fuerte por los teleconvertidores (Vivo esta generación con dos modelos de distintas distancias focales) y luego está Xiaomi.
Con el 17 Ultra, Xiaomi montó no sólo un zoom de verdad, sino un sensor de una pulgada en la cámara principal que me dejó alucinado cuando lo analicé. Es cierto que Apple también ha innovado con la apertura variable en el iPhone 18 Pro Max, siendo un recurso creativo muy interesante, pero en cuanto a móviles más completos a nivel fotográfico se refiere, Oppo, Vivo y Xiaomi llevan un par de años demostrando que saben dirigir la orquesta.
La cuestión del precio. Esto, evidentemente, tiene un precio. El del Vivo X500 Pro Max ya lo veremos cuando se presente el lanzamiento europeo dentro de unos días, pero en el caso de Oppo, esa mejora respecto a la generación anterior implica rascarse más el bolsillo.
De los 999 euros del Find X9, pasamos a los 1.399 euros del Find X10. Y de los 1.299 euros del Find X9 Pro que también venía con un muy buen teleconvertidor, pasamos a 1.799 euros. De hecho, el ambicioso y casi conceptual Find X9 Ultra era 100 euros más barato que el nuevo Find X10 Pro Max.
Vale que ambos tienen promociones de lanzamiento y en el caso del Pro Max tienes un kit con el teleconvertidor gratis, pero es un dinero considerable al que, por desgracia, todo apunta que nos tendremos que ir acostumbrando estando la cosa como está con el precio de algunos componentes.

articles.title: Ce génial missile français voit sa cible avant même d’être tiré depuis l’hélicoptère Tigre
articles.text:
La Direction générale de l'armement a mené avec succès, il y a moins d'un mois, un nouveau tir d’essai du missile Akeron LP depuis un hélicoptère Tigre. Conçu par MBDA, il doit remplacer le Hellfire américain à partir de 2028.
Le 25 septembre 2026, sur le site DGA (Direction générale de l'armement) Essais en vol de Cazaux, en Gironde, un hélicoptère Tigre a tiré un missile Akeron LP qui avait déjà repéré sa cible avant de quitter son lanceur. C'est le quatrième tir de développement de ce missile conçu par le Français MBDA, et seulement le deuxième depuis un Tigre. Ce « verrouillage avant tir » n'est qu'une des cartes de l'Akeron LP, un missile très bien conçu, qui transmet ses images en direct à l'équipage, lui permet de corriger le tir ou de changer de cible en cours de vol, et doit l'exposer bien moins qu'avec le Hellfire américain.
Un missile Akeron LP qui ne lâche pas sa cible des yeux
Ce tir effectué avec succès le mois dernier vient couronner une série d'essais menés depuis début 2025 pour éprouver l'Akeron LP brique par brique, du sol jusqu'aux airs. En février 2025, un premier tir depuis le sol avait validé le comportement en vol, le guidage et la propulsion. Le mois suivant, un Tigre lançait pour la première fois l'Akeron LP, surtout pour vérifier que le missile se sépare sans danger de l'appareil. L'essai de Cazaux va plus loin avec le LOBL (Lock-On Before Launch). L'autodirecteur, l'« œil » du missile, accroche la cible en infrarouge alors que l'engin est encore sur son lanceur, puis doit garder cette prise une fois largué, malgré le souffle du rotor et les turbulences.
Cet œil en vaut trois, puisque l'autodirecteur conçu par Safran associe un capteur infrarouge, une caméra TV et un récepteur laser. Thales fournit la liaison de données, un canal radio dans les deux sens qui renvoie à l'opérateur les images captées par le missile pendant tout le vol. Le procédé avait déjà fait ses preuves le 24 mars dernier, lors d'un tir depuis le sol contre une cible mobile en mer, sur l'île du Levant. Selon la mission, l'équipage peut laisser le missile se débrouiller seul (le fameux « tire et oublie ») ou garder la main jusqu'au bout.
Et c'est là que tout change. L'opérateur peut corriger le point d'impact, basculer sur une autre cible, voire annuler la frappe en cours de route. Avec le Hellfire américain à guidage laser, la cible doit au contraire rester « éclairée » par un pointeur jusqu'à l'impact, ce qui contraint souvent l'hélicoptère à rester exposé. L'Akeron LP est aussi pensé pour verrouiller sa cible après le tir, ce qui permettrait à un drone de désigner l'objectif pendant que le Tigre reste caché derrière une colline. Ce scénario n'a pas encore été testé lors des tirs rendus publics.
L'Akeron LP vise le Tigre, puis le Guépard
Le missile français est né du programme MAST-F (Missile air-sol tactique futur), confié à MBDA en 2020 et géré pour la France par l'OCCAR, l'organisation européenne chargée de piloter des programmes d'armement en coopération. L'Akeron LP pèse environ 35 kg et mesure 1,80 m dans son tube. Sa double charge explosive serait capable de percer l'équivalent de plus d'un mètre d'acier de blindage, de quoi inquiéter les chars les mieux protégés, y compris ceux dotés de blindage réactif. Elle vise aussi les bâtiments légers et les petites embarcations, à plus de 8 km depuis un hélicoptère et jusqu'à 20 km depuis un drone. La première commande porterait sur 500 missiles et une centaine de lanceurs.
Ces missiles ne viendront pas seulement renforcer l'arsenal des Tigre français. Ils doivent surtout permettre à l'armée de se passer du Hellfire II, un missile américain soumis à la réglementation ITAR, qui encadre strictement l'usage et la revente des armements made in USA. Ici, les trois piliers du programme, MBDA, Safran et Thales, sont tous européens, et le développement est largement mené en France. Près d'un mois après l'essai d'ailleurs, dans un post LinkedIn publié mardi, Stéphane Reb, le directeur général de MBDA France, a encore salué un succès au service de la « souveraineté » et de l'industrie de défense nationale.
La prochaine étape, c'est celle de la qualification, avec une série d'épreuves qui devra prouver que le missile tient toutes ses promesses. Elle doit démarrer à partir de 2027. Les premières livraisons sont prévues pour 2028, et les Tigre modernisés au standard Mk3 doivent en être équipés à partir de 2029. Ce chantier de modernisation, mené avec l'Espagne, concerne 85 appareils, dont 67 français. Airbus Helicopters planche déjà sur l'intégration du missile au futur H160M Guépard, et l'Akeron LP a même été monté sur des robots terrestres lors d'un projet européen. Sous les cocardes françaises, le Hellfire peut commencer à préparer sa retraite.

articles.title: Microsoft Scales Back Copilot Integration in Windows 11, Removes Eight File Explorer Actions
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 21st 2026
Microsoft Scales Back Copilot Integration in Windows 11, Removes Eight File Explorer Actions
Microsoft is officially cutting back on forced AI adoption that has been troubling Windows 11 users by working to simplify AI use across its operating system. According to a report by Windows Latest, Microsoft is removing Copilot actions related to OneDrive in File Explorer. This means that a simple right-click to open the context menu and then selecting the OneDrive icon will no longer present a long list of tasks that Microsoft's Copilot LLM would perform on the file. These tasks included summarizing, comparing, and asking questions, which provided minimal value on their own. Instead, Copilot features like these can be accessed through "Ask Copilot" or other less intrusive methods. This change is part of a OneDrive update aimed at reducing eight AI actions and keeping them available for those who wish to use them. Image below is a courtesy of Windows Latest, which shows how these actions look like.
MicrosoftAs part of this change, we're retiring the OneDrive Copilot Summarize, Create FAQ, Compare Files, Ask a question, Explain image, Explain images, Compare images, Extract text actions from the File Explorer context menu... Users can still access Copilot features via right-click "Ask Copilot," the File Explorer Home icon, or the OneDrive activity center.
According to Windows Latest, Microsoft is rolling out these simplified actions in stages, with plans to fully implement them by mid-November this year. The wait of a few weeks is worthwhile for those eager to see fewer forced AI integrations, suggesting that other areas may receive similar treatment. Hopefully, this simplification and reduction of AI integration will extend to other parts of Windows 11, but we will have to wait for the mid-November update to find out.

articles.title: 4TB Samsung 990 Pro M.2 SSD falls 27%, hits 20 cents per gigabyte — our favorite high-capacity PCIe Gen 4 drive is the ultimate storage for your game library
articles.text:
4TB Samsung 990 Pro M.2 SSD falls 27%, hits 20 cents per gigabyte — our favorite high-capacity PCIe Gen 4 drive is the ultimate storage for your game library
Still one of the best 4TB SSDs for gaming and productivity.
At one point in time, it was the fastest PCIe Gen 4 drive you could buy. Now, the next generation of PCIe 5.0 drives is available, but the 4TB Samsung 990 Pro still offers extremely fast performance and whopping amounts of capacity in a single-sided M.2 2280 form factor. The main issue at the moment is price. Thanks to the AI boom driving up the prices of memory and storage, SSDs have reached insane highs, so to be able to take advantage of a large 27% discount in these times is nothing to be sniffed at. The 4TB Samsung 990 Pro has fallen from $1,099 to this new price of $799.90, a saving of over $300. This works out as roughly 20 cents per Gigabyte of storage capacity.
● Grab this SSD deal at Amazon
Having reviewed the Samsung 990 Pro 4TB when it was released, we found it to be one of the best 4TB SSDs on the market and among the best SSDs overall. The 990 Pro boasts maximum sequential reads of 7,450 MB/s and sequential writes of 6,900 MB/s, with random reads/writes coming in at 1.6 million and 1.55 million IOPS, respectively, while endurance is rated for 2,400 TBW.
The Samsung 990 Pro 4TB is among the fastest Gen 4 SSDs available thanks to read and write speeds of up to 7450/6900 MB/s, almost maxing out the Gen 4 bandwidth. This M.2 NVMe drive comes in the 2280 form factor and holds enough capacity to store a large selection of your favorite games or files.
Random reads/writes come in at 1.6 million and 1.55 million IOPS, respectively, while endurance is rated for a respectable 2,400 TBW.
Samsung uses 236-layer TLC V-NAND to achieve its 4TB capacity, while also using a single-sided design, making the 990 Pro ideal for use in computers where space is a finite resource. When we tested the Samsung 990 Pro 4TB, we found it scored above the competition on almost every test. On 3DMark's storage test, it had the lowest latency result, a big plus for responsive load times in gaming.
The Samsung 990 Pro is also excellent at sustaining strong write performance. In our IOMeter sustained sequential write tests, the 4TB 990 Pro was able to maintain a speed of 6.2 GB/s for 75 seconds thanks to its generous 10GB of pSLC cache. Once the data spills over into the TLC, it operates at 1.6 GB/s. The Samsung 990 Pro is also a leader in power efficiency, delivering 421.1 MB/s per watt. That number puts it ahead of all competitors but the Addlink A93 4TB and Lexar NM790 4TB.
The Samsung 990 Pro is certainly nowhere near the all-time low prices of years gone by, and I'm not sure at the moment when, if at all, we'll ever see those low prices again on storage, certainly not for some considerable time. If you want 4TB of storage now, then the Samsung 990 Pro is a formidable choice; just try to grab it when there's as much of a discount as possible.

articles.title: Electronic Arts to shut down beloved Canadian studio BioWare
articles.text:
Electronic Arts is shutting down iconic Canadian developer BioWare.
As first reported by Bloomberg, this comes as part of EA’s wider cuts of 400 jobs, including roughly 50 at the beloved Edmonton-based developer. It also follows EA going private in August following an acquisition backed by Saudi Arabia and other investors. As part of that deal, EA took on billions in debt, leading it to come up with a cost-cutting plan fuelled in part by cutting research and development costs.

The studio had been working on an untitled fifth Mass Effect game, which Bloomberg reports was still in “early development” but has since been cancelled. BioWare’s last game was 2024’s Dragon Age: The Veilguard, which received generally positive reviews but did not meet EA’s expectations.
BioWare was founded in 1995 by University of Alberta medical doctors Ray Muzyka, Greg Zeschuk and Augustine Yip. The studio went on to produce numerous beloved and influential RPGs, including the Dungeons & Dragons-based Neverwinter Nights and Baldur’s Gate and Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, as well as original properties like Mass Effect and Dragon Age.
However, the studio has struggled in recent years, with most of its original talent having left to join other studios. 2019’s Anthem, an original sci-fi Destiny-style multiplayer game, had a prolonged and troubled development cycle and ultimately underperformed. BioWare then spent several years working on Dragon Age: The Veilguard, which was a similarly turbulent production. Over the past couple of years, EA had since laid off many BioWare staffers who hadn’t already left, leaving the famed studio a shell of its former self.

articles.title: SpaceX to attempt Starship catch on next flight, with eye on rapid cadence increase
articles.text:
In its current iteration, SpaceX is largely a data company seeking to provide enormous amounts of compute for artificial intelligence. During an earnings call on Tuesday afternoon, company officials spent much of their time discussing ambitious plans to roll out up to 10 GW of compute in 2027—on the ground.
Gone are the days of aspirational talk about sending humans to Mars and settling the red planet. Now it is almost all about artificial intelligence and the data needed to support its expansion. However, the company’s long-term ambitions to provide data services from space, initially with the Starlink Internet constellation and eventually through the “Starmind” data center constellation, still rely on an actual rocket.
That would be the Starship vehicle, and during the earnings call, SpaceX founder Elon Musk and the company’s president and chief operating officer, Gwynne Shotwell, provided new performance targets for the vehicle.
It has been a little more than three weeks since the 14th test flight of the massive rocket, which largely went well despite some issues with the Raptor rocket engine. SpaceX has gleaned enough data from that test, Musk said, to attempt a catch of both the Super Heavy first stage of the rocket and the Starship upper stage on the next flight.
Musk said he believes success is “more likely than not” for these attempts, but he added the company is hardware rich if there are failures. Both catches would happen at the company’s launch site in South Texas, Starbase. SpaceX is currently targeting November for this 15th test flight.
Landing over land
One of the big hurdles is regulatory, as the Starship vehicle must return to the launch site over land, including northern Mexico.
“We have had significant constructive engagement with the FAA, and we expect the license for our Flight 15 to include return to launch site and tower catch for both stages,” Shotwell said.

articles.title: The iPhone Duo is a foldable phone in the most Apple way possible — and that's a very good thing
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Apple iPhone Duo arrives as a fully realized folding smartphone from a company that, perhaps smartly, sat back and watched a category stumble, grow, develop, and solidify into a desirable form factor. As such, it avoids most of its predecessors' missteps while delivering exquisite engineering, a vibrant, virtually crease-free screen, and a compelling design. Even so, when compared to its chief rival, the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8, it isn't a slam dunk, and Samsung's lighter, thinner, and slightly cheaper passport-sized foldable remains compelling. But, for Apple fans who've been eagerly awaiting the Cupertino tech giant's entry into the folding space, there is no other or better choice.
Reasons to buy
- + Excellent design
- + Best folding hinge ever?
- + Flat, matte folding screen that hides the crease
- + Excellent performance
- + Split-screen multitasking
Reasons to avoid
- - Cover screen loses too much space to the dock placement
- - No telephoto camera
- - Needs more third-party app support
- - Missing Face ID
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Apple iPhone Duo: Two-minute review
In the early days of the iPhone, seeing one in the wild, usually in a brave early adopter's hands, was like spotting a unicorn. The excitement was palpable. Over the years, though, as every smartphone has become a glass and metal slab, making it difficult to tell one iPhone release from another, the excitement has diminished. Where I used to keep my 'regular' iPhone review units out of sight, I now casually carry them around in a case, and no one is any the wiser.
That, though, is not the case with the iPhone Duo. In my effort to spend as much time using the new folding iPhone as possible, I carried it everywhere, including to a wedding party for my friend's son. My iPhone Duo test unit was somewhat disguised by being clad in a Taupe Folio with a Kickstand case, but as I held it aloft to photograph the newlyweds, the bride's eyes grew wide.
"Is that...?!"
My eyes darted from her to the phone in my hand, and I considered stuffing it back in my pocket, but I was intrigued by her reaction. I hadn't seen this level of interest and excitement in years.
I nodded wordlessly; the newlyweds started peppering me with questions, and as I folded and unfolded it, and they glimpsed the inner display, the bride's jaw dropped. She asked if I liked it. I mumbled, "Yes, I think so," without offering much more information.
I was determined to use the iPhone Duo's two external 48MP cameras to photograph the event, which meant this scenario repeated itself more than once.
It was obvious that, unlike every other iPhone of the last decade or so, the iPhone Duo could not travel incognito; people were, it seemed, intensely interested in Apple's first truly new iPhone form factor in basically forever.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The interest is warranted.
The iPhone Duo is not simply an iPhone folded in half. I'd argue it's only marginally an iPhone and more of a hybrid, splitting the difference between a sub-sized smartphone and a slightly larger, 8-inch iPad mini.
From the highly polished titanium frame to the curves and pitch-perfect tolerances, the iPhone Duo's design is Apple at its best, and while it doesn't reinvent the genre, the nano-texture finish on the main display cannily solved the chief folding phone complaint: that darn crease. It's not that the crease is completely gone, but in daily use it's virtually invisible. As an added bonus, that matte finish kills reflectivity in bright sunlight, and makes almost everything look better.
Apple includes four cameras, three of which are powerful enough to produce high-quality photos across a range of styles. I saw excellent color accuracy and low-light performance, and the ultra-wide camera feels expansive. The inner-display camera is, it appears, just 4MP, but it does a good job with casual selfies and FaceTime calls.
Apple has almost stuck the landing here, but there is a slight step backwards. I'm fairly certain its decision to move the status bar and dock to the right side of the 5.4-inch outer screen, and therefore shrink the width of most apps, will divide opinion. I like how this makes it easy to tap an app with your right thumb, but the remaining screen real estate makes some app experiences look and feel cramped.
Then there's the lack of Face ID on the cover screen, which means this is the first iPhone in ages that I have to use my finger to unlock.
I'm also less than thrilled that a nearly $2,000 / £1,999 phone starts with just 256GB of storage; although, to be fair to Apple, the $1,899.99 / £1,699 Galaxy Z Fold 8 also starts with the same amount.
Those small nits are like pointing out the missing eyelashes on the Mona Lisa, though. Overall, this is a fantastic entry into the folding phone space, offering the dual capabilities of a glanceable and attractive iPhone that fits in any pocket or hand, and a versatile 7.6-inch tablet.
Not everyone needs two screens in one device, or wants to pay as much as they would for a home appliance for their next smartphone; but for those who feel confined by the boundaries of a typical iPhone and want to do more in less space, the iPhone Duo, which starts out smaller than your average smartphone but unfolds to reveal an almost twice-as-large tablet display, is well worth your consideration.
Apple iPhone Duo review: Price and availability
- From $1,999 in the US
- From £1,999 in the UK
- From $3,499 in Australia
Apple unveiled the iPhone Duo, its first folding phone, as its "one more thing" during the Surprise and Shine event on September 9, 2026.
The list price is $1,999 / £1,999 / AU$3,499 for the 256GB model, which is in line with most of its folding competitors from Samsung, Huawei, Motorola, and Oppo. It's available in storage configurations up to 2TB for $3,199 / £3,199 / AU$5,899.
The iPhone Duo is the most expensive iPhone Apple has ever made, but we should put this in context. Like most foldables, this is a two-in-one device: a pint-sized smartphone with a 5.4-inch 4:3 screen, and a 7.6-inch tablet. Unlike the Galaxy Z Fold 8, which has a similar passport-style shape, and even the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, which is a more conventionally sized and shaped foldable, the iPhone Duo's larger main screen supports digital pen input (this wasn't available for my testing period, but it's expected by November).
You may also be able to soften the price blow a bit with a trade-in; or you might want to look at Apple's leasing program, which will run about $57-to-$83 / £47 to £66.63 / AU$97.19 to over $161 a month for the base model.
In total, the iPhone Duo is probably better value than you think.

Apple iPhone Duo review: Design
- Polished titanium
- Exquisitely engineered hinge and folding operation
- Unfolds flat
- IP68
- Thicker and heavier than nearest competition
- No Face ID
'Satisfying' is the best way to describe the feeling of repeatedly opening and closing the iPhone Duo. It's as if Apple inadvertently created a digital fidget spinner — the more I carried around the iPhone Duo, the more I found myself absentmindedly folding and unfolding the phone.
Apple's exceptional engineering makes it possible to unfold the phone initially, with almost no effort (it almost springs open at the slightest intentional touch), before the internal torque kicks in to allow for the Duo to be opened to almost any angle between zero and 180 degrees (flat).
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
While you can't see the work that went into making this hinge, the effort is evident in every single touch and move. Inside are hundreds of magnets and other components that keep the phone securely closed, but never get in the way of an easy opening. More so than with any folding phone I've tested, the hinge essentially disappears when the iPhone Duo is unfolded flat.
At 5.2mm thick, the fingerprint-attracting polished titanium iPhone Duo is the thinnest iPhone ever. At least that's how Apple markets it, but that's in tablet mode; I do like the sound of a 5.2mm-thick tablet. The 7.6-inch device is thinner than the 8-inch iPad mini (6.3mm). Folded, the iPhone Duo is 11.3mm thick, almost 2mm thicker than the folded Galaxy Z Fold 8. And at 254g, the iPhone Duo outweighs the Galaxy Z Fold 8 by a noticeable 53 grams. It's even slightly heavier than the iPhone 18 Pro Max, which weighs 249g.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
The upshot of all this is that while the 4.64-inch by 3.31-inch folded iPhone Duo fits in even the smallest pocket, you will feel its heft, especially if you pop, say, a Folio with Kickstand case on it.
The iPhone Duo stands out in a way few iPhones have in recent years. Folded, it's closer to square than rectangular in shape, resembling a squat iPhone Pro Max. Plus, the asymmetry — flat and square on one side and curved on the other when folded — means the Duo cuts a unique profile among smartphones.
It does feel good in the hand, though the wider body might take some getting used to. I like the Ceramic Shield 2 front and back, especially the matte-finished back, which makes the Duo almost slip-from-your-hand-proof. The large dual-camera array bump is reminiscent of the iPhone Air, though the similarities end there.
The volume buttons live on the top edge, another departure from the traditional iPhone, and indeed from smartphone design in general — I'm not sure I love that decision. On the right is the long Touch ID-enabled power/sleep/Siri AI button, and below that is the Action button. I often forget that last button exists on my iPhone 18 Pro Max, and I wonder if it was truly necessary here.
I appreciate the inclusion of Touch ID (I registered my index finger and thumb), but the lack of Face ID is frustrating — I had no idea how much I relied on it for quickly unlocking my phone until it wasn't there. Multiple times I've stared at the iPhone Duo's cover screen waiting for something to happen, forgetting that I have to intentionally touch the Touch ID button. A nearly $2,000 device lacking Apple's most powerful biometric security feature is close to unforgivable — I'll probably set up a workaround so that I can unlock the Duo via my Apple Watch.

Along the bottom edge are the USB-C port (the phone ships with a charging cable but no power adapter), the speakers, and the mics.
Unfolded, the iPhone duo feels like a thin, compact tablet — I hesitate to say 'iPad' since the operating system is essentially iOS with some small adjustments for the new form factor.
Remarkably, Apple comes out of the folding gate flourishing an IP68 rating, which means the iPhone Duo is protected against dust and even water. Naturally, I submerged the Duo under a running faucet, and it was none the worse for the experience.
Overall, I like the design and form factor, but it's different from a traditional iPhone, so it does take some getting used to. I struggled, for instance, to figure out the best way to hold the phone for photography. Do I need to turn it into landscape mode, or should I just hold it the way I hold a 'regular' iPhone? I do wonder how many will choose to unfold the phone, and shoot pictures in the same way they might with their iPad.
- Design score: 4.5 / 5
Apple iPhone Duo review: Displays
- Adorable and unusually shaped 5.4-inch cover display
- Industry-leading 7.6-inch foldable internal display
- Crease is canily hidden via a combination of expert engineering and a nano-etched display
- Bright, sharp, fluid screens
Credit to Apple for not skimping on either of its iPhone Duo displays. Both the 5.4-inch outer and the 7.6-inch flexible inner screens are Super Retina XDR-class OLED panels, both with variable refresh rates up to 120Hz, always-on functionality, and up to 3,000 nits of brightness.
Both displays look impressively sharp, and actually offer slightly higher resolutions than the comparable displays on the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8.
The iPhone Duo's 5.4-inch cover display has a 2034 x 1398 resolution (compared to the Galaxy Z Fold 8 cover display's 1972 x 1248), and the 7.6-inch Inner display is 2670 x 1878 (compared to the Z Fold 8's 2448 x 1848 main display).
At first glance, the iPhone duo Cover screen is instantly recognizable as an iPhone, but close scrutiny reveals some interesting adjustments for the relatively short and wide display. First, the pill-shaped Dynamic Island sits in a vertical space along the right side, and when you look at the home screen, the dock is stacked vertically below the time and a status button (a single tap on it expands it to show connectivity and battery, and also drops down the full Control Center).
The Duo takes that right-hand space and rarely gives it up, which means that websites can look cramped in Safari, and some apps like TikTok, and even Apple's native ones, like Sports, can feel a bit squeezed. There are exceptions, like when you use the screen as a viewfinder in the Camera app, or look back at images in the Photo Gallery. In those cases, the imagery fills the entire screen.
I'm less conflicted about the glorious main screen. It's big, it's responsive, and the matte, nano-texture covering almost completely hides the crease by dispersing any light bouncing off it, instead of directing it right back to your eyes. The display looks and feels perfectly flat, plus that matte covering kills all reflections, and makes every image look almost magazine-quality. It could be argued that a tiny bit of visual punch is lost in the texture, but I really enjoyed everything I viewed and did on the screen. It feels wonderful to the touch, and I had fun playing games like PUBG, browsing the web on a big screen, watching Netflix, reviewing and editing my photos, and multi-taking (more on that later).
Unlike the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and 8 Ultra, the iPhone Duo's inner display supports a stylus, specifically the USB-C Apple Pencil. That support is not yet live, but I can't wait to start drawing on the Duo. I did attempt some Procreate Pocket sketches with my finger, and it didn't go well, which is mostly a me problem. However, I had slightly better luck with an analog stylus (see below).
Apple hides the 4MP inner FaceTime camera behind a handful of pixels, but they don't appear to have the exact same mix of matte and pixel density as the rest of the display, and as such are easy to spot. I wonder if Apple should have just gone with a standard, albeit smaller, cutout.
As on the cover display, Apple has positioned the status and dock vertically on the right side of the main display. I wonder why, in Tablet mode, Apple didn't simply copy the iPad and put this bar at the base of the screen. Still, I noticed that the dock disappears when you're in apps like Safari.
There's more to say about app compatibility with this platform, which I'll get into later in the Software section of this review.
I especially like the redesigned Standby feature, which takes advantage of the Duo's multiple displays and foldable nature. You can prop up the phone like a tent and have the Standby display appear in landscape mode. If you flip the phone up so it's standing on your desk like an open book, the Duo knows to switch Standby to the inner display. At one point I popped the Duo onto my old Belkin MagSafe charger, and used it as a nightstand clock. It's so smart and useful.
What we have here are two excellent displays with a wide array of capabilities in one device. It's both a tiny iPhone and a mini tablet, with two screens that should please both the iPhone and iPad crowds. I have my reservations about the cover screen, but as an overall multi-display package, I'm impressed with the Duo.
- Display score: 4.5 / 5
Apple iPhone Duo review: Cameras
- Two strong 48MP cameras
- Excellent 12MP Center Stage camera
- Inner camera is lower-resolution but effective for FaceTime
- No telephoto camera
It's been a long time since I've reviewed an iPhone on which camera considerations come second to design and mechanical engineering, but the excitement revolving around the iPhone Duo is about its folding capability, creaseless inner screen, and unique-among-iPhones form factor.
Even so, there's no indication that Apple has skimped on three of the four cameras. Yes, the inner camera is just a 4MP shooter that's primarily devoted to FaceTime calls, but the rest of the lenses — 48MP f/1.6 Main, 48MP f/2.2 ultra-wide, and 12MP f/2.2 Center Stage — are all excellent.
While I haven't had a lot of time with the iPhone Duo, I have managed to shoot in a variety of conditions and situations, pushing the cameras on speed, image quality, color, and low-light performance.
The two external cameras default to shooting at 24MP, which means each photo has effectively twice as much information per pixel (the process is called binning).
I was particularly impressed by the level of detail in the main-camera shots — just look at the specks of pollen on the marigold flower in the gallery below. That same image shows an exceptional balance of shadows and light; the sunlight bleed on the right does not overwhelm the exposure of the rest of the image.
In a challenging social-club environment, the main wide and ultra-wide cameras acquitted themselves nicely, making exposure adjustments to capture the moment without too much grain. Obviously, there was some motion blur, but I think it added to the emotional weight of the event.
With the iPhone duo, Apple has introduced Smart Take, which I liken to your own personal fashion photographer. The setting lives under the grid menu (drawer) in the Camera app, and once it's on, you can set the phone folded at 90 degrees on a desktop, start posing in front of the camera, and Smart Take will capture the 'best shots.'
When I used it, I noted that while I was trusting the phone to take some decent photos of me, I couldn't see a display to keep track of what it was capturing (Smart Take is not supported on the 4MP inner camera). Still, I started striking poses, assuming that the camera would deem those best. It kind of worked, though I think Smart Take would work best if you're able to put the iPhone Duo up on a tripod or shelf to make sure the camera is closer to eye level.

Similar to what we've seen on other foldable phones, Apple has included a camera mode, Duo Preview, that lets you use the best main or ultra-wide camera while still using the cover display as a viewfinder. It's a useful table-stakes feature that I'm glad Apple included, especially since the inner camera is so underpowered.
Apple says you get 2x effective optical zoom on the main camera, but that's a sensor crop. Yes, the pixels and image information will be real, but I prefer a proper zoom lens. To be fair, the iPhone Duo camera array is quite similar to the 50MP pair on the Galaxy Z Fold 8, which also lacks a telephoto lens.
I also used the cover screen Center Stage camera to shoot some portrait-mode selfies. They were, as you might expect, impressive (not the subject, just the brilliant bokeh).
The iPhone Duo's trio of high-quality cameras meets, in my estimation, the high watermark set by lenses on previous iPhones, including the iPhone 17 Pro (the 18 Pro models come with a variable aperture).

Apple iPhone Duo review: Software
- An iOS tablet hybrid that somehow works
- Dock position will split some
- Split screen for multitasking
- Third-party app support is a work in progress
With the iPhone Duo, iOS officially means multiple things. Where it was once a smartphone platform, it's now a multi-hardware-configuration operating system that can, depending on where it's installed, fork appropriately.
Instead of the iPhone Duo unfolding and converting into an iPad, it remains steadfastly an iPhone with tablet-like capabilities. This has resulted in some odd decisions on Apple's part, like hiding some of the ever-present status-bar information, including battery life, and rotating and moving the dock. Even the iPad doesn't put the dock on the right-hand side.
On the cover screen, the status bar and dock placement cut into screen real-estate for some apps and browser experiences; this is less of an issue on the larger inner screen.
Since this is not pure-play classic iOS, there is some discontinuity in third-party app support. During my testing, Gmail and LinkedIn didn't look great. The former is stretched wide but doesn't fill the full depth of the display; LinkedIn floats in the middle.
For unoptimized apps, I did have the option of using the very iPad-like 2x zoom icon, which stretched the app to fit more of the screen. In some instances, apps appeared to work, but some features were broken. When I played Asphalt Legends on the inner display, tilt-to-steer was broken, though it worked perfectly on the cover display.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Some third-party apps, including Netflix (clips looked pretty good on the Cover display), and first-party apps like Safari and Messages, look great, and effectively use all the 7.6-inch display's real estate. There are even some apps that are already custom-designed to take advantage of the dual-display setup.
One of my favorites is a game called Toastie. On the inner screen, you butter your bread, add cheese and other ingredients, then hit grill, at which point you fold the phone closed, and it gently pulses for each second of cooking. You have to decide when to stop. To see your grilled cheese sandwich, you open the phone — I did this a half dozen times before I had a virtually edible sandwich.
Deck-Man is also a cute concept; this turns your iPhone duo into a classic cassette tape player, complete with the static you hear when the player is on but not playing a tape. When the iPhone is open, you choose a cassette and virtually put it in the player, then you close the phone to access the player controls. I especially liked how "rewinding" the tape reproduced the classic sounds of a physical tape rewinding in an old-school player.
I also played Battle Fleet, which is a Battleship knockoff, and works well when you set up the phone in 90-degree opened desktop mode.
These are all clever apps, though I wouldn't argue that any are the Duo's 'killer app.'
The 7.6-inch inner display is also a good canvas for multitasking. You split the screen by swiping up from the bottom of the display and slowly dragging an app left or right. Inside each pane, you can swipe up to choose a different app. I used this to have Messages and Safari side-by-side, and also for the drawing app Procreate on one side and a reference image from Safari on the left.
Unlike on the Galaxy Z Fold 8, you can't run three apps, though the iPhone Duo will let you add picture-in-picture video on top of two apps you have open.
The iPhone Duo is a good showcase for Apple's growing AI ambitions. Siri AI now knows more about me and my smartphone, so when I ask if there are any emails I should know about, it automatically accesses 'Priority Mail' in the Mail app, and quickly starts reading off the first crucial message. Siri AI is better at maintaining context, so I don't have to restate myself, but it's still not foolproof. I asked Siri where I had been yesterday, and it showed me a picture of myself and listed my age. Siri AI should, though, get better as it continues to index my system.
In general, iOS 27, which is more customizable that ever, has useful widgets and more powerful AI features, and is the perfect platform for Apple's biggest iPhone design leap. It may not have all the design elements right, and the app support is lagging a bit behind, but these are all minor, and I think easily adjustable or fixable, issues.
- Software score: 4.5 / 5
Apple iPhone Duo review: Performance
- Powerful A20 Pro CPU
- 12GB RAM
- Smooth performance across the board
Apple smartly put the same CPU, the 2-nanometer A20 Pro, in the iPhone Duo as it did in the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. As a result, the performance on its first foldable device is equally impressive. In Future Labs benchmark tests, the A20 Pro on an iPhone Duo beat the Galaxy Z Fold 8's Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy in Geekbench 7 single- and multi-core tests, and it also edged out the Qualcomm chip in most of our graphics tests. None of this was by a wide margin, and I'd challenge anyone to notice the difference in real-world scenarios. Still, it's nice to know that the Duo is cooking with gas, just like its Pro counterparts.
In my experience, the iPhone Duo is fast and fluid. Speaking of which, it's fun to start with some third-party apps on the cover screen, and then flip open the iPhone Duo to see the virtually seamless graphics handoff from the smaller display to the larger one. It's both a software and performance feat that nothing stutters or stalls in the handoff process.
The larger inner screen will probably encourage many to try even tougher tasks, like editing 40K 60fps video. I used CyberLink PowerDirector to do so, and while the system and app handled the task fine, the non-optimized app couldn't properly fill the 7.6-inch display.
The back of the phone, near the camera bump, can get a little warm during gaming and other CPU-intensive operations, like recording the aforementioned 4K video, but not uncomfortably so.
Apple's A20 and the 12GB of RAM on board seem well suited to local tasks like photo editing in Cleanup, and both realistic and fanciful image creation in Image Playground.
The iPhone Duo starts with 256GB of storage, which matches the Galaxy Z Fold 8. At this price, though, I think it should start with double that. You can expect strong connectivity across the board from the iPhone Duo. Inside is Apple's C2 modem for better 5G connectivity. Plus, there's support for WiFi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Messages via Satellite.

Apple iPhone Duo review: Battery
- Solid all-day battery life

Apple reportedly squeezed a fairly large, almost 5,000mAh, battery into the iPhone duo, and is promising some pretty impressive battery-life numbers based on fairly specific types of usage. Video playback, which doesn't rely all that much on energy-draining resources, can, Apple claims, go for an eye-watering 44 hours, or 31 hours on the larger inner display.
In more varied use, Apple is claiming a full day of battery life on a charge. In my real-world tests I got around 14 hours, and in our more stringent Future Labs tests, we got 13 hours. That's commendable performance, but not as good as what the same Future Labs tests show for the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8, which managed 14.33 hours.
I still think the iPhone Duo's numbers are good, especially because my experience was easily cruising through a full day of phone activities, without any concern that I needed to plug in.
The phone supports fast charging and, with a 45W charger, I charged to 60% in 30 minutes. The MagSafe back also supports fast wireless charging.

You don't want to see a crease
Apple now holds the crown for best crease concealer, hiding it under nano texture finish that makes it almost impossible to spot the crease unless you really look for it.
Don't buy it if...

The iPhone Duo is not just the most expensive iPhone; it's more expensive than the Galaxy Z Fold 8. Either way, think carefully before buying; not everyone needs two displays in one device.
You want a telephoto camera
The iPhone Duo's main camera promises 2X optical equivalent zoom, but that's a sensor crop, which means there's no dedicated telephoto camera.

articles.title: PHP armageddon: OpenAI, Google's Wiz find ancient holes, panicking the internet | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The U.S. National Security Agency’s sent out an alarming warning on Wednesday that two critical holes had been found in PHP, with patches already issued by the PHP Foundation.
PHP is a server-side programming language so widely used for web applications that it powers roughly 70% of the websites on the internet; by some accounts, that’s more than 33 million sites. It is also used by popular content management systems like WordPress.
The NSA warned that these holes are so severe that if a website can’t be patched immediately, it should be pulled off the web until it can be. The holes allow attackers to infiltrate the server’s file system or a database that may be used by the web app.
Interestingly, these holes have been tucked away in all versions of PHP since version 5, which was released in 2004. Websites not running relatively current versions of PHP will have some updating work to do, as PHP 8.1 and older versions are no longer supported. The recommendation is to update the web server to the current version of PHP, which is 8.5.12.
So how did two such ubiquitous, decades-old flaws that affect nearly every website on the internet suddenly come to light? AI, naturally, particularly via OpenAI and Google’s Wiz.
Security testing company Calif was engaged in OpenAI’s “Patch the Planet” initiative to find flaws in open-source source software. Using GPT‑5.6 Sol, it found one of the flaws, OpenAI disclosed in a blog post. Separately, the Wiz team also used AI, namely its Wiz Atlas security AI agent, Gemini 4 Argon, and GPT-5.6 Sol to find multiple vulnerabilities in PHP.
Both OpenAI and Wiz followed responsible security research practices and worked with PHP on patches before publicly disclosing the flaws. Then they all worked together to flesh out what they found, and test the patches, drawing in a host of others to help.
Wiz thanked Automattic, Akamai, AWS, Cloudflare, Fastly, Imperva, Microsoft, and Vercel. (While WordPress sites use PHP, WordPress has issued a statement saying that the flaw isn’t WordPress specific, and sites running its CMS must patch their servers and work with their web-hosting companies to ensure their sites are protected.)
OpenAI says that these flaws were found by researchers before hackers discovered them. So there were no reports of exploits in the wild. This is also in part because, before AI, these flaws were too hard for hackers to exploit. “With AI this is no longer a barrier. LLMs can help adapt an exploit to different PHP versions, configurations and memory layouts,” Wiz warned in its blog about the flaws.
In other words, this is the kind of security issue that was found and prevented because of AI, but is also a high risk only because of AI.
Now that the issue has been disclosed, hackers are fully in the know. The race is on for the internet to patch tens millions of websites before hackers can attack the unpatched ones. Hence the NSA’s guidance that if you can’t patch your PHP website right away, you’re better off pulling it offline until you can.

articles.title: Elon Musk says ASML and other critical semiconductor equipment suppliers will expedite shipments to Terafab — facility targets volume chip production by Q3-Q4, 2028, in 'highly aspirational' timeline
articles.text:
Elon Musk says ASML and other critical semiconductor equipment suppliers will expedite shipments to Terafab — facility targets volume chip production by Q3-Q4, 2028, in 'highly aspirational' timeline
Musk's AI companies aim to achieve 13 GW of AI compute by the end of 2027, using massive 440,000-GPU Nvidia "Vera Rubin" training cluster
Elon Musk says ASML and other critical semiconductor equipment suppliers have expedited shipments for the ambitious Terafab semiconductor manufacturing facility, supporting his aggressive timeline for the joint megaproject between Tesla and SpaceX. He made the announcement during a live broadcast of SpaceX's Q3 2026 earnings call on X yesterday, October 20. Musk also said the company is targeting volume chip production at the project's primary facility in Gibbons Creek, Texas, by the third or fourth quarter of 2028, emphasizing that the timeline is highly aspirational and carries "big error bars."
"These are very aggressive dates, and we're very appreciative of ASML and all of our other suppliers in accelerating equipment deliveries in order to achieve this outcome," said Musk, CEO of both companies behind Terafab. SpaceX plans to manufacture its first experimental test chip at its research fabrication facility in Austin, Texas, around Q2 2027.
Aside from Terafab, Musk also outlined near-term ambitions for his AI companies during the broadcast, saying he expects them to have 2.5 to 3 gigawatts (GW) of computing capacity active by the end of 2026. He also stated he is highly confident about bringing an incremental 10 GW online in 2027, saying he "would be surprised" if they do not hit a total of 13 GW of AI compute by the end of 2027.
Meanwhile, the next-largest project by planned capacity, the now-restructured 10 GW Project Stargate, was expected to reach full capacity in the 2030s. Meta's 5 GW Hyperion also has a similar timeline. To achieve the 13 GW milestone, Musk revealed that SpaceX and xAI are aggressively procuring upcoming next-generation NVIDIA architecture. He announced plans to get a massive 440,000-GPU Nvidia "Vera Rubin" training cluster online by the end of Q2 2027.
Shifting back to Terafab, Musk also boasted that once fully scaled and operational, the sheer commercial value of Terafab's advanced chip output will place it within the top 20 global country GDPs from a single physical building. For context, the 20th country on the list is Switzerland, with a GDP of around $1.14 trillion. The facility is a planned multi-billion-dollar, vertically integrated chip factory in Texas, with an ambitious goal of manufacturing 1 terawatt (TW) of AI computing power per year. Terafab will fabricate logic, memory, and advanced packaging internal architectures in one place. The project's massive planned output has mandated various collaborations across the semiconductor supply chain. Terafab will utilize traditional extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography systems utilizing Intel's 14A manufacturing node technology.
Intel officially joined the Terafab venture in April 2026 to help co-develop and refactor silicon fabrication technology, providing access to its state-of-the-art 14A manufacturing process. ASML, the world's sole commercial supplier of the $400 million EUV lithography systems required for high-volume, leading-edge chip production, is perhaps the project's most critical partner. Terafab's first EUV tool was reportedly slated for delivery in mid-2027, according to unofficial sources. It remains unclear if this is the expedited timeline Musk referred to in the broadcast.
Other major suppliers include American equipment manufacturers Applied Materials, Lam Research, and KLA Corporation, as well as Japan's Tokyo Electron. These companies will provide front-end processing, metrology, and process control machinery. Tesla and SpaceX are also in talks with about 10 South Korean equipment makers, including Hanmi Semiconductor, known for advanced packaging equipment, and HPSP, a high-pressure hydrogen annealing equipment manufacturer, as well as firms providing specialized piping components and process valves.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Musk's announcement says that several of these suppliers are expediting supply to Terafab, even as capacity remains tight across the semiconductor supply chain. The facility, which aims to mitigate future shortfalls of cutting-edge AI processors from external foundries like TSMC, will supply the chips for Musk's xAI clusters, self-driving vehicles, Optimus humanoid robots, and SpaceX's orbital AI data center, as well as the broader AI industry.
However, many experts have questioned the validity of Musk's 1 TW Terafab ambition. For context, research firm Gartner estimates the total global AI-optimized data center capacity is roughly 44 GW as of late 2026, 4.4% of Terafab's planned output. Although global AI computing capacity has grown by roughly 3.3x to 3.4x per year since 2022, according to EpochAI.

He is a mechanical engineer and senior technical writer with over nine years of experience in documentation and reporting. He is deeply passionate about all things engineering and technology, and is an expert in gadgets, manufacturing, robotics, automotive, and aerospace.

articles.title: Google activó en los autos una versión de Gemini que usa tu Gmail y tus fotos
articles.text:
Google empezó a distribuir una versión de su asistente Gemini en el auto que puede leer el Gmail, el calendario y las fotos del usuario para responder preguntas con información personal, sin que haga falta tocar el teléfono.
La función se llama Personal Intelligence y llega primero a Android Auto, la aplicación que proyecta el teléfono en la pantalla del vehículo. En los próximos meses se sumará a los autos que traen el sistema Google built-in instalado de fábrica.
Con el permiso del usuario, Gemini conecta Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Photos, Google Maps, YouTube y el buscador de Google para combinar datos de varias fuentes y dar una sola respuesta.
Google puso como ejemplo preguntarle a Gemini, camino al aeropuerto, por la puerta de embarque y el estado del vuelo: el asistente busca ambos datos en el correo sin que el conductor tenga que abrir la app de la aerolínea.
Otros ejemplos del comunicado incluyen pedirle un restaurante vegetariano en la ruta según gustos previos, pedirle que lleve al usuario a una cita médica sin decir la dirección, o pedirle que encuentre, a partir de una foto guardada, el lavadero de autos visitado la semana anterior.
Gemini ya estaba en el auto desde el 2025
Google incorporó Gemini a Android Auto en reemplazo de Google Assistant el año pasado. Personal Intelligence ya existía en el teléfono desde enero y se había extendido a las cuentas gratuitas en marzo.
Android Auto es compatible con más de 250 millones de autos en el mundo, según datos que Google difundió en mayo. El sistema Google built-in, en cambio, viene instalado de fábrica en más de cien modelos de dieciséis marcas, entre ellas Ford, GM, Honda, Nissan, Volvo y Polestar.
Apagada por defecto y con límites de acceso
Personal Intelligence viene apagada por defecto. El usuario debe activarla desde la configuración de Gemini y puede elegir qué aplicaciones conectar o desconectarlas en cualquier momento, según detalló Google en su blog oficial.
En los autos con Google built-in, el asistente solo entrega respuestas personalizadas cuando el teléfono del usuario está conectado al vehículo. Sin la función activada, Gemini sigue funcionando para navegación, música y llamadas, pero sin adaptar sus respuestas a cada persona.
TechCrunch señaló que ese nivel de cruce de datos personales, dentro de un vehículo, podría generar incomodidad en algunos usuarios. Google respondió que el control queda siempre del lado de quien maneja, con la posibilidad de apagar la función en cualquier momento.
El despliegue alcanza a cuentas personales de Google de usuarios mayores de 18 años en casi todo el mundo, aunque no está disponible en el Reino Unido, Suiza, Nigeria y los países del Espacio Económico Europeo. Tampoco funciona en cuentas de Workspace para empresas o instituciones educativas.
La actualización llega en un momento en el que varios fabricantes de autos exploran asistentes de inteligencia artificial propios: Apple sumó a Siri funciones que también usan información personal del usuario dentro de CarPlay, su sistema para conectar el iPhone al auto. Google todavía no fijó una fecha exacta para completar el despliegue en los vehículos con Google built-in, más allá de hablar de “los próximos meses”.
Funciones de Gemini en Android Auto
Gemini en Android Auto permite encadenar órdenes, corregir instrucciones y obtener respuestas adaptadas a cada situación sin apartar la vista de la carretera. Su integración con Google Maps habilita búsquedas complejas —“busca una cafetería bien valorada en mi ruta que esté abierta ahora”— y la selección de resultados por voz, mientras que la gestión de mensajes y llamadas entiende correcciones y dictados largos con mayor precisión que su antecesor, Google Assistant.
La productividad al volante se extiende a Gmail, Calendar, Tasks y Keep: el conductor puede pedir la dirección de un hotel desde un correo, consultar eventos del calendario o crear recordatorias sin tocar el teléfono. Para la música, el sistema interpreta pedidos por estado de ánimo o duración del viaje. La función Gemini Live suma conversación continua, con memoria de temas previos, útil para preparar reuniones o entretener a los niños durante el trayecto.

articles.title: Finance influencer V Harish dies by suicide; father alleges cyberbullying
articles.text:
Finance influencer V Harish dies by suicide; father alleges cyberbullying
The family has accused a venture studio CEO of online harassment. The CEO denies the allegation and says he had questioned Harish's financial regulatory credentials.
(Trigger warning: Story mentions suicide)
V Harish, a financial influencer with over a million followers, has died by suicide at a rented villa near Chennai. His father has alleged that Harish was reportedly “targeted” by Jason Samuel, the CEO of venture studio Zemuria Inc. Harish’s Instagram account was disabled by Meta following allegations made by Samuel, after which he began posting videos on a new handle. Samuel has denied the cyberbullying allegations.
Samuel took to X on Tuesday and wrote, “I am deeply saddened, heavily grieving, shocked and frozen at what has happened and I mourn the loss of life.”
“I have not cyber-bullied him. I pointed out his lack of license and authority, misrepresentation of license and fraud on SEBI and AMFI where he has not got SEBI RIA for his work and misrepresented that he had an AMFI license when he got the ARN only recently. i.e., his illegal activity.”
He added, “I literally asked him in the video to come back and do this with a proper SEBI license. I never intended or expected this drastic measure to happen and I mourn the loss.”
His father claimed that the online dispute had caused stress to the 27-year-old, contributing to his death. He has sought a police investigation into the circumstances surrounding his son’s death, but no case has been registered yet.
According to South First, the Tambaram police have added a charge of abetment to suicide under Section 108 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) in connection with V Harish’s death. Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding his death and the allegations of online harassment made by his family.
