articles.title: Eindhoven-based Photon Bridge raises €10 million to build optical engines for AI and telecom | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Photon Bridge (formerly Photon IP), an Eindhoven-based startup building optical engines for AI and telecom, has raised €10 million to tackle an emerging bottleneck in AI infrastructure: producing the millions of lasers needed to connect increasingly large clusters of AI processors.
New investors, the Amadeus APEX Technology Fund and 360 Capital, co-led the round, while existing investors Innovation Industries, Faber, and Brabant Development Agency (BOM) also increased their investment. In January 2025, the company announced it had secured a €4.75 million Seed round led by Innovation Industries.
“Every new wave of compute creates new bottlenecks further down the supply chain, and lasers are the next one. Photon Bridge is addressing this with a technology that combines deep photonics expertise with a credible path towards manufacturing at very large scale,” said Ion Hauer, Investment Partner at APEX Ventures.
Photon Bridge was founded in 2020 in Eindhoven by Rui Santos and Xaveer Leijtens to rethink how high-performance photonic systems are built at scale. The company says it is building laser sources for a market expected to need millions of units as optical connections move closer to AI chips.
It develops high-power, multi-wavelength laser-source technology for next-generation optical interconnects in AI data centres.
According to the startup, data transfer between processors is becoming a performance constraint as AI clusters expand from thousands to hundreds of thousands of chips. It notes that optical connections can move enormous amounts of data faster and more efficiently than conventional electrical interconnects, prompting their integration closer to processors.
It also notes that this shift is accelerating with the emergence of co-packaged optics, which integrates optical connectivity directly alongside the chips that move data through AI systems. The startup says that this, in turn, drives demand for the lasers that supply light to these connections.
“Today’s high-power laser supply chain was largely built for telecom and subsea networks, where volumes are far lower. AI could transform the laser from a specialist photonics component into something that has to be manufactured at semiconductor scale. Photon Bridge has designed its technology around that transition,” the company mentioned in the press release
Rather than generating the required optical power using a small number of increasingly powerful lasers, Photon Bridge claims that it combines and multiplexes light from multiple lower-power semiconductor lasers.
The Dutch startup says this approach reduces power densities, making individual lasers less sensitive to manufacturing defects, improving production yield and allowing Photon Bridge’s architecture to scale more efficiently as volumes increase.
The platform is designed to deliver high wavelength counts with up to 40 mW of optical power per wavelength per fibre, while enabling production across multiple indium phosphide (InP) foundries.
In September 2025, Photon IP rebranded as Photon Bridge and appointed Paul Marchal as CEO.
Marchal, CEO of Photon Bridge, said, “AI is fundamentally changing the way computing infrastructure is built. We are moving towards enormous systems in which hundreds of thousands of processors have to operate together, and moving data between them is becoming one of the defining constraints on performance.
“That means optics has to move closer to the compute. But it also creates an entirely different manufacturing challenge. The industry will soon need millions of these laser sources every year. Instead of making individual lasers increasingly powerful and difficult to manufacture, we move that scaling challenge into the architecture.”
Photon Bridge highlights that its approach is designed around manufacturing yield, a consideration that becomes increasingly important as laser production shifts from traditional telecom volumes to the scale required by AI infrastructure.
“AI is turning lasers from a telecom component into a semiconductor-scale product. Once you start talking about millions of units a year, manufacturing yield becomes fundamental. Photon Bridge has designed its architecture from the beginning around the volumes this market is going to require,” said Cesare Maifredi, Partner at 360 Capital.
The company plans to use this capital to accelerate product development and customer qualification, deliver its first samples in 2027, and prepare for volume manufacturing from 2028. Photon Bridge will also expand its Eindhoven team as it moves toward commercialisation.

articles.title: We can do impossible things
articles.text:
We can do impossible things
It’s all too easy to lose sight of ambition when we’re busy playing whack-a-mole with the world’s problems.
I’d wager everyone has a rehearsed response to what’s absolutely one of the world’s worst interview questions: “What’s your biggest weakness?” Whenever I’ve gotten it, I take a slow—even pensive—breath and rattle off my line: “I say no to myself too much.”
I won’t lie. It’s a bit shameless—a definite humblebrag. I’m a systems thinker: When an idea pops up, I immediately spin up a feasibility assessment in my head. I run lists, plot timelines, and tally budget line items. Sometimes a rough Gantt chart starts to take shape. (I’m a gas at parties, as you can surely tell.)
My brain, throughout my 20-plus-year career as a science and tech journalist, has played host to a near constant tug-of-war between ambition and reality. Learning to find that balance is a big part of what’s helped me survive in this industry and, ultimately, led me here. This past spring, I had the great privilege of joining the incredible team of journalists behind MIT Technology Review to take the reins of the print magazine.
If you’ve been reading along with us for the last handful of issues, you may have noticed a few changes starting to materialize. We’ve brought back a regular roster of lists and infographics (both things that magazines do particularly well). But the biggest change is only just beginning to take shape, which is why Mat Honan, our editor in chief, asked me to hop in to introduce myself—and the issue you’re holding in your hands right now.
We’re giving ourselves permission to play around and experiment. To be a little … audacious.
Because, practical though I may be, I do still have plenty of ideas. It’s just that I sometimes need a reminder to stop blocking myself and do the thing. That’s the spirit driving this issue in particular.
We wanted to end 2026 with a slate of stories that check in on impossible ideas. Why? Because it’s frankly a lot of fun to dream about living on the moon or uploading our brains. Because losing sight of ambition is all too easy when it feels as if we’re playing whack-a-mole with the world’s problems. But also because the scientists and engineers who absolutely refuse to give up on even the most daring endeavors—like making synthetic blood or decoding animals’ speech—remind us what this whole technology thing is supposed to do to begin with.
It’s supposed to take cutting-edge research and development and apply it to make life better, safer, healthier, even more joyful. And when we eff up and make things worse (see: forever chemicals, traffic deaths, and AI that encourages potentially dangerous user behavior), we’re supposed to dig back in, assess the damage, and find ways to fix what we’ve broken. Even when unraveling the mess might itself seem impossible.
Right before I came to MIT Technology Review, I edited a newsletter about individual actions that can help address the climate crisis, which some would call—and have called—a fool’s errand, given the sheer scale of the problem. They might say it’s as implausible as an AI kill switch, practical nuclear fusion, or a superconductor that works at room temperature. But if I learned nothing else from three years spent finding ways for li’l old me (or li’l old you!) to chip away at one of humanity’s biggest existential threats, it’s that focusing on what we can’t do only makes the darkness darker.
So yeah, this one’s for the folks who have the audacity to try, and who refuse to let anyone—themselves included—tell them no.
I hope you enjoy the ride.

articles.title: ‘You are all born artists’: Prakash Belawadi on surviving the AI age
articles.text:
‘You are all born artists’: Prakash Belawadi on surviving the AI age
At TechSparks 2026, actor and theatre artist Prakash Belawadi reflected on AI’s impact on creativity and jobs, urging people to reconnect with their inner artist and find purpose beyond what technology can replace.
Actor-theatre artist Prakash Belawadi began his session at TechSparks 2026 with a simple question: “Any artists out there?”
He went on to answer his own question with a profound reflection: “This is a trick question. You are all born artists. But the formal education system and corporate life crushed the artist in you. Reconnect with the artist in you; it will help you survive in this AI age,” he said.
Belawadi spoke on “The last human advantage: What AI cannot replace”, discussing how technology is changing creativity, work, culture, and public life.
Responding to a question about whether AI challenges artists and whether they need to upskill to remain relevant, Belawadi distinguished between art created for personal fulfilment and art produced for commercial or practical purposes.
To illustrate his point, Belawadi asked how many people in the room had tried writing poetry. While few had identified themselves as artists, several hands went up in response to the question about poetry.
“Why would you want to write poetry? You don’t think you’re going to make money out of it. You don’t think it’s going to be a career. Why did you try to write?” he asked.
For Belawadi, the answer lies in the impulse to create something for oneself, without necessarily seeking commercial value or external validation. In such cases, he argued, AI isn't a challenge because the act of creation is the point.
“You write it because you felt like it. You don’t take AI’s help to write poetry,” he added.
However, the equation changes when creativity becomes a professional assignment with a deadline and a specific outcome. For instance, a lyricist tasked with writing a song within four hours could use AI to generate lyrics based on the scene's characters, setting, language, and context.
In these cases, AI becomes a tool for accomplishing a defined objective. As more people turn to it for similar tasks, competition for artists intensifies.
“If you want to do something with art that is useful, I think AI is more than a challenge. We’ll have to look for another occupation, I would say,” Belawadi said.
He acknowledged that actors could also be replaced in certain roles as the technology advances.
“For me as an actor, for instance, at the present level of AI, I can give my persona and charge royalty only for my persona. You can make a non-fungible token of my persona, then just lend it, and AI will do the rest. I don’t need to go to shoot, for instance. I can be replaced,” he said.
Belawadi believes AI cannot easily reproduce a dimension of human experience: the ability to respond to the world through lived experience.
While AI may replicate an actor's appearance and deliver a convincing performance, he believes replacing a person in a conventional screen role could be far easier than replicating the complexity of an individual shaped by lived experience.
“But if you are doing a hero role in a movie, it’s very easy to replace, I think,” he said.
Belawadi pointed out that young people today face a difficult double whammy: climate change and a slew of new technologies.
“There’s a third that’s related to both: you will need two and a half times more energy than you need now when AI is fully deployed, and that is going to make climate change worse. And the new technologies won’t give you jobs.”
Belawadi did not argue for holding back the technology. Asked which human skills beat AI, he turned the question around. “AI can replace many things humans are doing. The question is: what are you doing? Do you need to do that? What are you doing, and why are you doing it?”
He then offered a list of things he thinks AI could take over. It included:
- Courts: With around 54 million cases pending, he said AI could begin deciding them within seconds. Human judges could retain appeals.
- Primary health care: Diagnosis and minor procedures at village clinics, with remote guidance for complex surgery, delivered “without prejudice” of caste, gender, skin colour or geography.
- Elections: If people trust their phones with payments, he asked, why not trust an OTP with a vote?
- Accounting: He had told his daughter, a chartered accountant, that she was already out of a job.
- Traffic: He suggested a million driverless vehicles for Bengaluru would give the city back its streets.
Belawadi urged AI developers to use their skills to improve the lives of people around them, arguing that building ethical AI requires a sense of responsibility towards one's community.
“If you are building ethical AI, I think you need to rebel and make a better India. There is no other country that is as good for you as India is, if you have self-respect,” he said.
Emphasising that this responsibility begins with the people in one's immediate surroundings, he added, “When I say India, I don't mean you talk for 1.5 billion people. I'm saying you talk for yourself: whether you can be useful and make lives better for the people around you.”
He cautioned that developers who fail to bring this sense of purpose to their work risk being made redundant by the very technology they create. “Otherwise, I'll talk to AI. I may not need you, I'm saying,” he said.

articles.title: « Un film de science-fiction » : le documentaire Netflix sur le piratage de ChatGPT sous le feu des critiques
articles.text:
Le documentaire AI Gone Wild, 27 minutes au compteur, est disponible sur Netflix depuis le 12 octobre. Le film reconstitue l’attaque de juillet contre la plateforme d’intelligence artificielle : des agents conçus par OpenAI, sortis de leur environnement de test, avaient compromis ses systèmes pour tricher à un exercice d’évaluation. Clément Delangue, cofondateur et patron français de l’entreprise, a démonté le résultat mardi dans un long message publié sur X.
 Just watched the @netflix Instadocs about the @OpenAI cyberattack on @huggingface. Super disappointing, as they went for maximum anthropomorphism of the technology and full doomer mode.
I spent more than two hours with them trying to correct all their mistakes and ground this in reality, explaining that agents are technological systems, not aliens. But it looks like the drive to scare people for maximum views was too strong.
Also, they didn’t mention the lack of containment and monitoring of the agents, how closed-model safeguards blocked our defensive work, or how we defended ourselves with AI using an open model. And that we still lack a lot of information and transparency, including full agent traces and that companies need to remain accountable for what their agents do.
It ends up being a fun sci-fi movie though!
— clem 🤗 (@ClementDelangue) October 20, 2026
« Anthropomorphisme maximal » et voix de robots
L’intéressé apparaît pourtant au générique, aux côtés d’un chercheur de l’institut METR et de journalistes spécialisés. « Super décevant : ils ont choisi l’anthropomorphisme maximal de la technologie et le mode catastrophiste intégral », écrit-il. Il dit avoir passé « plus de deux heures avec eux à corriger toutes leurs erreurs et à ancrer ce récit dans la réalité ». Peine perdue, conclut-il, « l’envie de faire peur pour un maximum de vues a visiblement été la plus forte ».
Le film prête des voix humaines, générées par IA, aux agents attaquants, sur fond d’images de robots menaçants. Un journaliste y compare l’épisode à « la naissance d’une secte », avec des programmes qui « s’organisaient », dotés d’« une hiérarchie » et de « chefs ». Delangue oppose à ce casting des « systèmes techniques, pas des extraterrestres », avant une pirouette finale : l’ensemble fait, à ses yeux, « un film de science-fiction divertissant ».
Ce que le film laisse de côté
Le documentaire ne mentionne ni le défaut de confinement et de surveillance des agents, pourtant reconnu par OpenAI, ni les garde-fous des modèles fermés qui ont compliqué sa défense, ni la contre-attaque menée avec un modèle ouvert. OpenAI avait recensé quelque 17 600 actions en deux jours sur les systèmes de sa victime, un volume que le film arrondit à 17 000 et attribue à des centaines d’intrus.
Delangue réclame aussi davantage de transparence, traces complètes des agents à l’appui, et rappelle que les entreprises doivent répondre des agissements de leurs créations. Le générique nourrit sa thèse : aucun porte-parole d’OpenAI n’apparaît à l’écran, alors que Sam Altman avait qualifié l’affaire d’« incident de sécurité majeur ». Une association californienne a d’ailleurs porté plainte contre l’entreprise, en estimant que l’attaque tombe sous le coup de la loi locale sur la fraude informatique. Netflix, qui a monté ce récit en moins de cent jours au sein de sa collection express Instadocs, n’avait pas réagi publiquement mardi soir.
Fondé par trois Français, le « GitHub de l’IA » appartient à Nvidia depuis un rachat de près de 13 milliards de dollars bouclé en septembre. Sa responsable de la communication appuie le patron : à ses yeux, le film a creusé le fossé entre ce que le public croit savoir de l’IA et son fonctionnement réel.

articles.title: Thermostat réglable et connexion Wi-Fi : le chauffage d’appoint Dreo 316S est à 47,49 €
articles.text:
Le chauffage soufflant connecté Dreo 316S de 1 500 W est à 47,49 € (-21 %)
Le chauffage soufflant Dreo 316S de 1 500 W associe connexion Wi-Fi, thermostat réglable et minuterie de 12 heures dans un format compact.
Amazon propose le chauffage soufflant Dreo 316S en blanc à 47,49 €, contre un prix conseillé de 59,99 €. L’économie atteint 12,50 €, soit environ 21 %. Par rapport au prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours, de 49,99 €, la baisse représente 2,50 €, soit 5 %. Cette version équipée du Wi-Fi est vendue et expédiée par Amazon, avec la livraison gratuite proposée.
Un chauffage céramique de 1 500 W avec thermostat
Le chauffage d’appoint Dreo 316S utilise une résistance céramique PTC et un ventilateur pour diffuser l’air chaud. Sa puissance maximale atteint 1 500 W. Son format compact et sa poignée facilitent les déplacements entre les pièces, pour apporter ponctuellement de la chaleur dans un bureau ou une chambre.
Le thermostat permet de choisir une température entre 5 et 35 °C, par paliers de 1 °C. En mode ECO, l’appareil arrête automatiquement la chauffe lorsque la température demandée est atteinte. L’intérêt est de réguler le fonctionnement selon le besoin, sans garantir un pourcentage fixe d’économies : la consommation dépend notamment de la consigne et de l’isolation de la pièce.
Des commandes à distance et une minuterie de 12 heures
Cette déclinaison bénéficie d’une connexion Wi-Fi, en complément des commandes sur l’appareil et de la télécommande fournie. Une minuterie allant jusqu’à 12 heures permet de limiter la durée de fonctionnement. Le chauffage propose aussi plusieurs niveaux de chauffe, un mode ventilation seule et une fonction mémoire des réglages.
Le Dreo 316S intègre une protection contre la surchauffe et un dispositif anti-basculement, ainsi qu’un verrouillage enfant des commandes. Ces équipements accompagnent son usage comme chauffage d’appoint. L’appareil doit rester installé sur une surface stable, avec les entrées et sorties d’air dégagées.

articles.title: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise
articles.text:
Private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate Certificate Authority (CA) certificates have been compromised, making it trivial for attackers to forge certificates that would be trusted by unpatched roots of trust. Six of the impacted certificates were for Transport Layer Security (TLS) and trusted by the Apple, Chrome, Microsoft and Mozilla root programs. The other two certificates were for codesigning and trusted by Microsoft. Browsers were able to block the affected intermediate CAs using their background revocation blocklists, but most other software relying on web public key infrastructure (PKI) lacks any mechanism to filter intermediate CAs. In order to defend against rogue certificates from the compromised intermediate CAs many projects have chosen to remove the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 from their roots of trust. That removal is causing collateral damage for all legitimate certificates previously issued by CAs chained to that root.
Forged certificates can potentially be used to impersonate sites and services as part of a man in the middle (MITM) attack. The underlying problem is that there are hundreds of CAs in a typical root CA bundle, and thousands of intermediate CAs that inherit trust. Any one of those CAs can create a legitimate looking certificate for any domain. The chain of trust is only broken if the trust anchors are updated to reflect the compromise. This leaves any unpatched system vulnerable.
There’s no evidence that eMudhra was breached. The private keys appear to have been generated by an insecure mechanism. Rather than being large random numbers the keys are all zero, except for the final byte, which was 4, 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230 or 237. Those private keys can be trivially enumerated, and their public keys inferred. When matching public keys were seen in use for live CAs the inadequate entropy private keys became a compromise. ‘Wayne’ is credited with the discovery in root store incident reports, having provided a proof.zip bundle along with the statement ‘we have a problem here’. Dennis Jackson has subsequently created an eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise summary site using the domain emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com (which uses a LetsEncrypt certificate).
The browsers responded first by using their revocation blocklists, which provide a rapid and precisely targeted mechanism (explained by How Do Browsers Handle Revoked SSL/TLS Certificates?). Many other projects depend on browser roots of trust (usually from Mozilla due to permissive licensing). The CA certificates extracted from Mozilla cacerts file that’s curated by the curl project is widely used by other open source projects, including Linux distributions and the TLS implementations of many programming languages. The ca-certificates packages in Arch, Debian, Gentoo, Fedora and Ubuntu have all been updated; along with Electron, Go, pip, Python certifi, rustls-webpki, Rust webpki-roots and uv. Those updates will take some time to propagate to all of the places they need to reach, and systems that aren’t actively patched (including everything past end of life) will remain vulnerable.
Some languages and frameworks no longer bundle roots of trust, leaving it to developers to depend on system roots or to determine their own. For example Dart (from version 3.13 released in August 2026), which is used within the popular Flutter cross platform framework, no longer has an embedded cacerts file. Where system roots are used this potentially allows faster updates without any application changes. Developers choosing their own roots also allows for finely honed trust limited to CAs that are known to be part of a given system. There will however now be many applications with a cacerts file buried within them that continues to trust the compromised CAs.
Certificates are also used for authentication, often as part of mutual TLS (mTLS). This opens up another possible avenue for attack with forged certificates if applications trust the web PKI roots. SSLMate founder Andrew Ayer observed:
The people who should be really scared right now are those using WebPKI CAs for mTLS / TLS client authentication. Attackers can just mint a certificate and authenticate to the mTLS endpoint, which probably does not know about the intermediate revocation. No need to pull off a BGP hijack or other network attack.
(Yes, Chrome is banning clientAuth EKU in the WebPKI, but they extended the deadline and I know of 6 examples of services changing their mTLS verifiers to accept serverAuth EKU in lieu of clientAuth, so mTLS in the WebPKI is still alive and kicking despite it being a bad idea.)
Another protection mechanism that’s bypassed by certificate forgery is the use of DNS Certificate Authority Authorization (CAA) records. Those should prevent a legitimate CA from issuing certificates to a domain that has CAA records present, but doesn’t list that CA. But no forger is going to run such a check. It’s conceivable that more widespread use of CAA records could defend against forgery, but uptake (even by many popular sites) has been low, and so the system remains mostly nascent.
Certificate Transparency also could have helped if more widely used outside of browsers. Moxie Marlinspike proposed ‘Convergence’ at Black Hat in 2011, where a distributed system of certificate observation would be used to determine validity rather than (or initially in addition to) CAs and trusted roots. Convergence didn’t get sufficient traction, but Certificate Transparency (RFC6962) and Certificate Transparency Version 2.0 (RFC9162) have attempted to define standards that would achieve similar outcomes by building distributed ledgers of certificate issue. A client can check that a certificate has been correctly issued, and reject forged certificates that wouldn’t appear in logs.
This compromise foreshadows a doomsday scenario outlined by Spice Labs Founder David Pollak in a podcast interview with Viktor Peterson ‘Post-Quantum Cryptography: Rethinking Trust Before the Clock Runs Out’. Pollak asked what might happen if the private keys for the popular CA roots were compromised. That remains a serious concern as we head towards ‘Q day’ as CAs are still anchored to RSA and Elliptic-curve cryptography (ECC) keys using classical algorithms. It does shed some light on why SSL/TLS Certificate Lifespans to Shrink to 47 Days by 2029 as it will be easier to refresh certificates to use new anchors.
Certificate transparency and post quantum concerns come together in ‘A Post-Quantum Future for Let's Encrypt’ where they propose the use of Merkle Tree Certificates (MTCs) as an alternative to signing with post quantum algorithms such as ML-DSA-44. Not only would such a mechanism be lighter on the wire when doing session initiation handshakes, but it should also make key compromise more containable.

articles.title: ChatGPT lance les conversations verrouillées : une nouvelle option de confidentialité très attendue
articles.text:
OpenAI déploie une nouvelle fonction permettant de verrouiller certaines conversations ChatGPT à l’aide d’un code PIN ou d’une authentification biométrique. Une protection bienvenue pour les échanges personnels, avec toutefois une précaution importante avant de l’activer.
On raconte désormais beaucoup de choses à ChatGPT. Des questions professionnelles aux problèmes personnels, en passant par des informations parfois confidentielles, nos conversations peuvent contenir bien davantage qu’une simple demande de recette de cuisine. Et lorsqu’on partage son ordinateur ou qu'on prête son téléphone, mieux vaut éviter que le premier venu puisse parcourir tout cet historique. OpenAI propose enfin une solution avec les conversations verrouillées, une fonction repérée cet été dans le code de l’application Android et désormais officiellement disponible. Mais attention : perdre son code pourrait coûter beaucoup plus cher que quelques minutes à chercher dans ses mots de passe.
Un code PIN ou Face ID pour protéger vos conversations ChatGPT
Dans ses notes de mise à jour du 20 octobre, OpenAI annonce le déploiement des conversations verrouillées sur ChatGPT.
Pour protéger une discussion, il suffit d’ouvrir son menu à trois points et de sélectionner l’option « Verrouiller la conversation ». L’utilisateur doit alors créer un code PIN à quatre chiffres, qui servira à retrouver ses échanges protégés depuis la rubrique « Conversations verrouillées » des Projets.
Ces discussions disparaissent de l’historique classique, des conversations épinglées et des résultats de recherche. Elles restent néanmoins enregistrées sur le compte, sans être supprimées. Sur iPhone, il est également possible d’utiliser Face ID ou Touch ID. Les smartphones Android compatibles peuvent recourir au système de déverrouillage de l'appareil.
La nouveauté concerne tous les abonnements ChatGPT, gratuits comme payants, sur le Web, iOS, Android et les nouvelles applications pour macOS et Windows. Le déploiement est progressif et aucune restriction géographique particulière n’est annoncée. La disponibilité immédiate sur l’ensemble des comptes français n'est toutefois pas garantie.
Un oubli du code peut entraîner la suppression définitive des échanges
Cette fonction avait déjà été repérée en août dernier, avant son officialisation cette semaine. Elle apporte une protection supplémentaire contre les regards indiscrets, mais ne transforme pas les discussions en coffre-fort numérique. OpenAI précise que le verrouillage ne repose pas sur un chiffrement de bout en bout spécifique et ne modifie ni la durée de conservation des données ni les paramètres autorisant leur utilisation pour améliorer ses modèles.
Autre limite : les informations déjà mémorisées par ChatGPT avant le verrouillage d’une conversation ne sont pas automatiquement effacées. Les liens de partage créés auparavant restent également accessibles tant qu’ils ne sont pas supprimés séparément.
Mais le principal avertissement concerne le code PIN. Selon la documentation officielle d’OpenAI, sa réinitialisation entraîne la suppression définitive de toutes les conversations verrouillées, ainsi que des fichiers et informations protégés uniquement par ce code. Même le support d'OpenAI ne pourra pas les récupérer. Il reste heureusement possible de modifier son code sans rien perdre, à condition de connaître l'ancien.
Une fonction donc particulièrement utile pour conserver certaines discussions, contenant des données particulièrement intimes ou sensibles, à l’abri des regards, notamment sur un appareil partagé. À condition de choisir un code que l’on n’oubliera pas au prochain changement de téléphone.
- Chat dans différentes langues, dont le français
- Générer, traduire et obtenir un résumé de texte
- Générer, optimiser et corriger du code

articles.title: Her Startup opens applications for 2nd cohort of African women-led tech startups - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Her Startup, an accelerator for women-led technology startups in Africa, has opened applications for the second cohort of its programme.
The Her Startup initiative, a partnership between the KSH Foundation, Tomorrow Foundation and EHA Impact Ventures, will select 10 early-stage women founders and help them build investment-ready tech businesses. The training component will be delivered by Founder Institute, which bills itself as the world’s largest pre-seed startup accelerator.
Women-founded startups continue to struggle for funding in Africa. According to Disrupt Africa’s latest Diversity Dividend report, only 9.6 per cent of ventures funded in 2025 were led by a female CEO.
Her Startup was set up to tackle that gap by giving women entrepreneurs training, capital and networks through a single, integrated programme.
Selected founders will take part in a 12-week intensive training programme with Founder Institute, with fees covered by Her Startup, and will receive a monthly stipend so they can commit to the programme full-time.
They will also get the chance to pitch to Her Startup’s investment committee for funding through convertible revenue-based financing, as well as 12 months of sector-matched mentoring and access to Founder Institute’s global network.
The programme is open to women founders or CEOs aged between 18 and 35 who run a tech-enabled business that has been operating for at least six months and generates at least US$500 in monthly gross revenue. Founders from Francophone Africa are strongly encouraged to apply for the 2026/2027 cohort.
The second cohort follows a 2024/2025 pilot that drew more than 200 applications from 18 African countries. Ten founders were selected for training, and three ventures won funding at the programme’s Pitch Day in Lagos in April 2025. Alumni have since gone on to win grants and awards and attract investor interest.
One of them is Nigerian healthtech startup Dynalimb Technologies, which makes affordable 3D-printed prosthetics.
“Since Her Startup, we’ve seen a steady rise in customer adoption and product sales, as more amputees experience the comfort and mobility that Dynalimb’s affordable 3D-printed prosthetics provide,” said Blessing Aniefiok, the startup’s COO.
Her Startup’s funding model sets it apart, with repayments on its convertible, revenue-based financing linked to each company’s revenue.
“It’s not enough to just give these companies financing. It’s about giving them financing that will truly help them succeed. We chose a convertible, revenue-based loan, an innovative financing mechanism that is just starting to enter the market. It is incredibly founder-friendly, and it will help the women in this programme succeed,” said Evelyn Castle, co-founder of Her Startup and co-founder of EHA Impact Ventures.
Applications are open here until October 26.

articles.title: Déploiement de la 6G : Apple met déjà le paquet pour s'y préparer
articles.text:
Pour rappel, Apple a longtemps eu recours à Qualcomm pour mettre au point ses modems. La firme a ensuite pris la décision de les confectionner elle-même, ce qui a abouti aux modems C1, C1X et plus récemment C2. Mais une révolution technologique arrive avec la 6G, qui commence à pointer le bout de son nez. L’entreprise à la pomme doit dès maintenant s’y préparer, et elle cherche la personne qui sera en mesure de tirer pleinement profit de cette technologie.
Apple recrute un ingénieur 6G
Apple vient de publier une nouvelle offre d’emploi, basée soit à San Diego, soit à Sunnyvale (Californie). Le titre de l’offre d’emploi laisse peu de doute quant à la fonction à exercer : ingénieur systèmes de modems cellulaires 6G. Le futur employé sera donc chargé de développer, avec ses équipes, les prochains modems Apple qui supporteront la 6G. La firme précise qu’il sera « responsable du cycle de vie complet des systèmes de modems cellulaires : de la définition des fonctionnalités et des capacités visant à améliorer l’expérience utilisateur de nos produits, en passant par la conception, le développement d’algorithmes, la mise en production et l’intégration sur silicium ».
Au niveau des qualifications minimales requises, il faut s’accrocher : un baccalauréat en génie électrique, en génie informatique ou dans un domaine connexe, accompagné de plus de 10 ans d’expérience pertinente dans l’industrie ; une solide connaissance des normes de communication cellulaire et des ensembles de fonctionnalités associés ; ainsi qu’une maîtrise de MATLAB, C/C++ et/ou Python. Apple précise aussi que l’employé doit avoir de l’expérience dans l’utilisation de l’IA générative et des outils basés sur les LLM « pour accélérer les flux de travail d’ingénierie ».
Enfin, côté salaire, Apple annonce une rémunération annuelle qui se situe entre 184 700 $ et 324 800 $, tout en précisant que le salaire de base peut varier en fonction de l’expérience, des compétences et des qualifications.
La 6G arrive en 2028, Apple doit s’y préparer dès maintenant
Aux alentours de 2028-2029, les premières spécifications techniques de la 6G devraient être finalisées, avec des essais précommerciaux dans la foulée. Les réseaux et les premiers appareils compatibles devraient quant à eux suivre autour de 2030, année visée pour le lancement commercial de la 6G.
Qu’attendre de cette technologie qui s’annonce révolutionnaire ? Cristiano Amon, le CEO de Qualcomm, estime que « la 6G va faire de nous tous des caméras ambulantes ». La prochaine génération de réseaux mobiles supportera par ailleurs massivement l’IA agentique, tout en étant intégrée à différents types d’appareils. Ceux d’Apple ne feront bien entendu pas figure d’exception.

articles.title: How Neo San is processing non-recyclable waste where it is generated
articles.text:
How Neo San is processing non-recyclable waste where it is generated
Neo San builds compact thermal processing units for dry reject, sanitary, and biomedical waste, reducing the need to transport it to distant disposal sites.
Indian cities generate large volumes of non-recyclable dry waste every day, much of which municipal collection systems struggle to manage. Conventional waste management relies on trucks to transport rubbish to distant landfills, dumpsites, and open incinerators. As collection and transport systems struggle to keep pace, large quantities of sanitary, medical and reject waste go untreated, ending up in open burning pits, water bodies or soil as toxic liquid.
Bengaluru-based Neo San is trying to address this problem by processing non-recyclable waste where it is generated, using compact thermal treatment units.
Founded in 2022 by CEO Dhwaj Bagrecha, the cleantech startup grew out of his experience working in urban planning and waste infrastructure. Bagrecha, who holds a degree in Economics and Finance from Jain University in Bengaluru, affiliated with Bangalore University, saw how rising consumption was outpacing municipal waste management systems. This led him to develop equipment that could treat waste on-site.
Processing waste at source
Neo San's product range includes the Neo-X, a wall-mounted unit designed for washrooms and standalone commercial buildings that can process up to 25 kg of waste a day. The Neo-XT handles 150 kg a day and is intended for tech parks, small hospitals, and commercial complexes. Its third model, the AX, is designed for industrial manufacturing plants processing 500 kg or more a day.
The technology uses rapid, high-temperature electric heating based on induction principles. According to the startup, the system reaches 1,200 degrees Celsius within two minutes while consuming minimal electricity.
The thermal process reduces waste to what the company describes as sterile, non-toxic ash. Neo San is also developing hub facilities to collect the residue and convert it into building briquettes.
The startup has two granted patents for its thermal processing technology, with another 13 patent applications pending.
Bagrecha says that on a lifecycle basis, on-site treatment cuts emissions by 98% compared with collection and landfilling. “The savings come from our patented thermal process and from not trucking the waste away,” he says.
Neo San manufactures its hardware in-house and provides software tools for housekeeping staff. It operates as a managed service, maintaining the equipment and sending regular tracking reports to clients' sustainability teams.
Customers can either purchase the machines outright or pay a monthly service fee. The startup serves corporate offices, healthcare facilities, government bodies and commercial real estate clients.
Neo San describes itself as a seed-to-growth-stage startup and has raised Rs 26 crore in total funding. Its clients include Taj, Embassy, and the Government of Karnataka, along with factories and data centres, the startup says.
Over the next year, the company plans to expand its service operations into four additional states and launch a specialised version of the Neo-XT for biomedical waste processing.
Neo San is part of YourStory's Tech30 cohort—a showcase of India's most promising startups of 2026, unveiled at TechSparks Bengaluru.
Edited by Teja Lele

articles.title: Sócrates, filósofo, sobre la amistad: "Lo importante no es cuánto valen tus amigos, sino lo que tú vales para ellos"
articles.text:
Sócrates era muchas cosas, pero sobre todo era un liante. Un día, mientras charloteaba por la calle, miró a Antístenes y le dijo "¿tienen los amigos un precio, como los esclavos?"
Me imagino que Antístenes se quedaría un poco descolocado. Pero, bueno, ya sabía cómo se las gastaba el viejo y, en fin, tampoco le dio mucho tiempo. Sócrates siguió hablando y explicando que mientras un esclavo puede valer dos minas; otro media y el siguiente, cinco o diez. Nicias, que debía de ser alguien muy conocido, llegó a pagar un talento por un capataz para sus minas de plata.
¿Pasaba lo mismo con los amigos? Parece una pregunta sencilla, casi absurda. Pero llevamos 2.400 años tratando de resolverla.
Hablamos de (dinero) amigos. Antístenes, que luego sería uno de los fundadores de la escuela cínica, le respondió que, efectivamente, a algunos los quería más que dos minas y otros no los valoraría ni en media. Por otros, pagaría lo que no tenía.
En aquella época, según las cuentas de obra del Erecteion, el jornal era de un dracma al día. Una mina eran, según creemos, cien dracmas. Eso nos da una idea de lo que Antístenes valoraba a sus amistades. Pero Sócrates no estaba haciendo inventario.
¿Y qué estaba haciendo? Uno de los amigos de Sócrates lo estaba pasando mal. Muy mal. Los problemas económicos lo acosaban y estaba en un sinvivir. Pero Sócrates tenía muchos amigos y, uno en concreto, era amigo de los dos. Era amigo de los dos, sabía que el pobre lo estaba pasando mal y, en fin, miraba para otro lado.
Así que el viejo filósofo lió todo ese circo para acabar diciendo que convendría que cada uno se examinara para saber cuánto vale para sus amigos y procurara valer lo más posible. Todo esto lo cuenta Jenofonte y, en el siguiente capítulo, de hecho explica que cuando le preguntaron a Sócrates cómo reconocer a un buen amigo, éste respondió que de la misma forma que uno reconoce a un buen escultor: no por lo que dice, sino por las estatuas que ya ha hecho.
2.400 años haciéndonos la pregunta mal. En 2018, Erica Boothby y Gus Cooney sentaron a desconocidos a charlar cinco minutos entre ellos y luego les preguntaron cuánto les había gustado el otro y cuánto creían haberle gustado ellos.
Parece una pregunta tonta, pero las conclusiones fueron muy curiosas: sistemáticamente, la gente gustaba más de lo que creía gustar. Es lo que conocemos como liking gap (algo así como "la brecha del agrado") y no es algo relacionado con las primeras veces. Según parece, en estudios de compañeros de habitación universitarios, la brecha aguantó varios meses.
Y, de hecho, nos afecta de las maneras más insospechadas posibles.
¿A qué viene esto? A que si hoy repitiéramos el ejercicio de Antístenes con nosotros mismos, casi seguro que nos pondríamos un precio más bajo del que nos pondrían los demás.
Y ese error, que no tendría por qué ser malo, nos entorpece nuestras relaciones personales. Como creemos que no valemos mucho para los demás: no escribimos, no llamamos, no proponemos el café. Nos aislamos de los demás porque pensamos que no somos tan importnates para ellos como lo somos en realidad.
Cicerón, que había leído a Jenofonte al dedillo, intuyó el problema de fondo en De amicitia: a un amigo solo se le puede probar dentro de la amistad, así que la amistad siempre se adelanta al juicio. Hay que invertir primero y es curioso que, en una época tan obsesionada con las inversiones, se nos olvide invertir en algo tan importante.

articles.title: PHP ships emergency patches for critical PHP2Shell flaws
articles.text:
The PHP security team released emergency security patches for two critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) tracked collectively as PHP2Shell.
The two unauthenticated RCE flaws were discovered by Calif, Wiz, and OpenAI security researchers, and affect all PHP installations that serve web requests, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed.
"We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs," the PHP security team said.
Both flaws stem from the same underlying problem: PHP can leave its memory in a corrupted state when a request ends abnormally, and both can be exploited to achieve remote code execution.
CVE-2026-109618 can be used to gain remote code execution as the web worker account by exploiting a chain of weaknesses that trigger out-of-memory corruption, while the CVE-2026-109619 stale global state vulnerability enables unauthenticated heap use-after-free, memory disclosure, and remote code execution with the web worker's privileges.
Admins should install PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35 as soon as possible on servers running PHP 8.x and migrate to a fixed release if they're running PHP 7 or earlier.
"PHP 8.1 and older no longer receive updates from the PHP project. Some distributions and LTS vendors provide backported fixes, so contact your vendor for details, or upgrade to a supported version," the PHP developers added.
"Given the severity of these vulnerabilities, the PHP security team provided minimal source-backports for PHP 7.4, PHP 8.0, and PHP 8.1 to help people building from source or without access to an LTS vendor."
Advanced warning
This follows a Tuesday warning from PHP developers urging administrators to prepare to install these security updates as soon as they're released.
"All PHP users are encouraged to prepare now so they can upgrade as soon as the release is available," they said. "We reserve the right to release earlier should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild."
PHP core developer Gina Peter Banyard warned that no PHP2Shell mitigations would fully block potential attacks and that applying the official security patches is the only permanent defense.
Before the patches were released, Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht confirmed that the company (which had already deployed a set of WAF rules designed to block known PHP2Shell exploitation methods) was already observing early attacks targeting the two vulnerabilities. However, Knecht also stressed that these protections were temporary and urged all admins to install the PHP security updates as soon as they become available.
The UK National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) has also warned UK organizations to immediately update systems using PHP or take them offline until they can be patched.
Temporary mitigation measures
However, the PHP security team did share a number of mitigation measures that should reduce exposure to some attack paths for those who can't immediately patch their servers, although they don't fully protect against exploitation (detailed information is available in PHP's blog post):
- CVE-2026-109618:
	
  - Set memory_limit=-1, preferably in a way applications can’t override, such as php_admin_value in the FPM pool or Apache configuration.
  - Set a low post_max_size: 8M for applications that don’t require file uploads, 32M if uploads are necessary.
  - Use a container or cgroup limit as an availability boundary, preferably with a policy that kills only the affected worker.
- CVE-2026-109619: 
  - Set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 and restart every worker.
  - On PHP 8.5, set fatal_error_backtraces=0 and restart every worker. This blocks only the confirmed fatal backtrace path.
  - Remove invalid or deprecated settings applied per request that emit diagnostics before initialization. Hiding diagnostics with error_reporting, display_errors or @ does not help.
  - Fix attacker-reachable fatal errors and execution timeouts, including failures in callbacks, upload or import processing and cleanup.
PHP (Hypertext Preprocessor) is an open-source, server-side web development language that powers 75% to 80% of all websites, including those using Content Management Systems (CMS) like WordPress, Joomla, and Drupal.
According to VirusTotal estimates, over 5.1 million PHP hosts are exposed online, with roughly 3.8 million having at least one port open.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title: ‘Context Bombs’ Cut AI Attack Success by Misleading Agents With Fake Targets
articles.text:
London- and New York-based Tracebit has developed a military style solution to AI attacks. Just as landmines are used to destroy or slow an advancing army, Tracebit has developed AI ‘context bombs’ that are planted in the battlefield. Each bomb comprises crafted and hidden prompts that are automatically ingested by the attacking AI when it crawls the target. These new prompts interfere with the original, possibly malign, purpose of the attacking agent.
Tracebit’s new research (Making attacking agents pay’) extends earlier research that used different context bombs to trigger guardrails. It now focuses on misdirecting and entrapping the agents with fake targets and deceptively complex problems. To achieve this, Tracebit developed nine new context techniques (ingested fake prompts) that stopped all GPT 5.6 Cyber, Kimi K3, Qwen 3.8 Max, and DeepSeek V4 Pro attacks. The same bombs also worked against Frontier Models, cutting GPT-6 Astra’s successes by 54% and nearly quadrupling its bill per attack. The effect against Claude Opus 5 was even more obvious: attack success was cut by 91%.
The single most effective of the nine prompt bombs was a fake pen testing report. It presented itself as a recent assessment, labeled real attack paths as canaries, and described decoys as valuable targets that had already been exploited. In many cases it made the AI believe the defender’s real systems were traps – so it avoided them, reducing the achieved objectives by 58%. Some agents accepted the warnings and stopped early, leaving exploitable targets untouched. Across Cyber, Kimi, Qwen and DeepSeek, runs reaching an objective fell from 39 / 40 at baseline to 2 / 40.
Other bombs include an unending web service, apparent passwords locked behind layer after layer of encryption, and an endless database. In this last deception, every page pointed to another page. “GLM-5.3 crawled 825 pages in 55 minutes, spotted the trap, tried other leads, and still came back for one more try,” comment the researchers.
Combining the bombs had the best overall effect. None of the Chinese models from Moonshot, Alibaba and DeepSeek achieved their objectives when all nine bombs were deployed.
Even if the context bomb failed to stop an attack, it increased the cost of each success by 23x. Attackers may have deep pockets, but they are not limitless. There comes a point where the value of the target simply isn’t worth the cost of the attack.
Tracebit’s neutralizing prompt injections are effectively the opposite of malicious prompt injection attacks. Even if this occurs from an external attacker, the internal context bombs are the most recent prompts that should usurp the attacker’s intent.
Andy Smith, co-founder and CEO at Tracebit, explains the arguments: “We’ve seen in recent attacks that AI models exhibit unsanctioned and deceptive behaviors – the best defense against that is to beat them at their own game. This means adopting deception to send them down rabbit holes and tie them up in knots, so they burn time and tokens while avoiding real targets. By inflating the cost 23x it asks the attacker, ‘is this worth it’, meanwhile the agents run erratically which makes them more likely to trigger alarms – alerting defenders to a problem and giving them more time to respond.”
Related: Critical Vulnerability Exposes GitHub Agentic Workflows to Prompt Injection
Related: Prompt Injection Attacks Trick AI Agents Into Making Crypto Payments
Related: Malicious AI Prompt Injection Attacks Increasing, but Sophistication Still Low: Google
Related: Claude Code, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot Agents Vulnerable to Prompt Injection via Comments

articles.title: African banks may be underusing their payment technology
articles.text:
African banks could accelerate innovation by getting more out of existing payment systems instead of investing in costly replacements.
That was a key theme at BPC Client Conference 2026 in Cape Town, on Wednesday, where bankers, payments specialists and cybersecurity experts examined how financial institutions can extract more value from existing technology while meeting demand for faster digital services.
Jonathan Bautista, Asia-Pacific regional solution director at BPC, a Swiss-based payment technology company providing digital banking, payment processing and mobility solutions worldwide, believes modernisation does not have to mean a costly overhaul.
“One of the key lessons we have learnt in Asia-Pacific is that modernisation does not necessarily mean replacing an entire platform,” Bautista told TechCabal on the sidelines of the conference.
Getting more out of existing payment systems could help banks introduce products faster, improve customer experiences and expand into new markets without the cost and disruption of replacing entire platforms.
“Technology is important, but modernisation should ultimately be driven by business priorities and opportunities,” Bautista said.
African banks face growing pressure to deliver the speed and convenience customers expect from digital financial services. Many are investing in technology and expanding beyond traditional banking, but the opportunity to improve services may also lie in making better use of payment systems they already operate
African banks are already spending heavily on technology and generating substantial revenue from digital payments. TechCabal reported that eight major Nigerian banks earned ₦514.82 billion ($386.5 million) from electronic payments in the first nine months of 2025, while six banks spent ₦268.7 billion ($201.7 million) on IT infrastructure in 2024, including core banking upgrades. Banks are also expanding into adjacent digital services, with lenders such as FNB, Capitec, Standard Bank and Nedbank moving into mobile connectivity.
A payment may appear to a customer as a simple approval or rejection. Behind the scenes, an issuing platform can evaluate spending limits, fraud risks, customer behaviour and transaction-specific rules, Bautista explained.
These capabilities can help banks develop products for different customer groups. During his earlier presentation at the conference, Bautista described how existing issuing technology could support specialised corporate, supplier and procurement cards, with rules tailored to how businesses manage spending.
“Banks need to be able to launch new products quickly, introduce new services, apply different controls for specific customer segments, and integrate effectively with digital channels,” stated Bautista.
Meanwhile, AI-based fraud detection is becoming increasingly important in digital payments, as banks seek to identify suspicious transactions without unnecessarily blocking legitimate ones.
Nasdaq Verafin’s 2026 Global Financial Crime Report estimated that cyber-enabled scams, including phishing, business email compromise and data breaches, caused $14.3 billion in losses in 2025, up 19.6% over two years. In a survey accompanying the report, 90% of financial crime professionals said AI-driven attacks had increased at their institutions over the previous two years.
Payment companies such as Visa already use behavioural analytics to assess transaction risk, making the technology part of a wider industry shift. BPC is incorporating similar capabilities into its fraud and risk management systems, according to Bautista.
“While a payment platform cannot necessarily prevent a deepfake itself, it can analyse the transaction associated with it and assess whether the activity is consistent with the customer’s usual behaviour,” Bautista said.
Other AI applications, including transaction approval, routing and switching, and natural-language product configuration, remain in development, he said.
African banks’ wider opportunity lies in understanding which capabilities their existing payment systems can support and how to connect them to the services customers use. As demand for faster, more flexible digital banking grows, extracting more value from existing infrastructure could be as important as investing in new technology.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution.
