articles.title: DLSS 5 Just Got a Lot Faster, but Is It Worth Using?
articles.text:
Nvidia has released a new version of DLSS 5 neural rendering, claiming it runs twice as fast as the previous model. This October update reduces the number of parameters in the DLSS 5 model by 24%, halving execution time and reducing VRAM usage by 20%. All of this has been achieved while maintaining comparable image quality, according to Nvidia.
We thought it was worth revisiting DLSS 5 in everyone's favorite title, NBA 2K27, which is once again the first game to officially ship with the latest model. Does the new version really run twice as fast across all RTX 50 series GPUs without compromising image quality? Does it address some of the issues we raised in our initial DLSS 5 analysis? And does this performance improvement make DLSS 5 worth using now?
 – WolfOfDarkness® (@WolfOfDarknesss) October 19, 2026
 – Sim Racing Esport (@SimRacingEspor) October 14, 2026
One thing to clarify before getting into the benchmarks... when Nvidia says the new DLSS 5 model is twice as fast, that doesn't mean games with DLSS 5 enabled will run at twice the frame rate. The improvement refers specifically to the rendering cost of DLSS 5, not everything else the game needs to render.
As a result, actual frame rates won't double after this update. However, Nvidia does claim a 1.4x performance improvement in NBA 2K27, so we'll see whether that holds up.
How the New Model Performs
Let's kick things off with Nvidia's gaming flagship, the GeForce RTX 5080 (see what we did there?). Previously, DLSS 5 was quite taxing on this GPU at 4K, dropping NBA 2K27 from 185 FPS with DLSS 5 disabled to just 53 FPS with the feature enabled.
As we showed in our previous investigation, performance doesn't change much when adjusting settings or increasing the level of upscaling, because the official DLSS 5 implementation operates on the output frame at the output resolution, rather than before upscaling is applied.
The new model improves performance considerably at 4K, increasing frame rates from 53 to 78 FPS, a 47% gain in this title. This makes 4K playable on this GPU to some degree, though there's still a 58% reduction in FPS compared to running without DLSS 5. Previously, that reduction was 71%, so the gap has narrowed somewhat.
At 1440p, we saw a 42% increase in frame rate with the new version of DLSS 5 compared to the old model, reducing the overall performance loss from 54% to 34%. Enabling the feature still significantly reduces in-game performance, just not to the same degree as before.
Meanwhile, at 1080p, the RTX 5080 is quite capable of running DLSS 5, though with neural rendering disabled, we run into CPU and game engine bottlenecks that cap performance.
RTX 5070 Ti and RTX 5070: Big Gains at 1440p
The RTX 5070 Ti also benefits from the DLSS 5 model improvements. At 4K, the new model delivered 48% better performance, pushing NBA 2K27 above 60 FPS at this resolution for the first time. However, without DLSS 5 enabled, the game ran at 166 FPS, so the new model still comes with a massive 61% performance hit.
At 1440p, though, the situation is much better. The new model delivered 47% higher FPS than the previous version, cutting the performance loss from 62% to 44%. The game now runs above 120 FPS at this resolution with DLSS Quality upscaling enabled, which is very playable in this title. At 1080p, we saw a performance loss of 25% when enabling the new model, compared to 45% previously.
With the old DLSS 5 model, the RTX 5070 struggled at both 4K and 1440p. The new model provides a substantial boost in both scenarios. While this isn't enough to push 4K performance above 60 FPS, it does deliver 100 FPS at 1440p.
The overall performance loss compared to running without DLSS 5 is still pretty large, though. Frame rates were reduced by 60% at 4K and 54% at 1440p, although both are an improvement over the first model. At 1080p, the performance impact of enabling DLSS 5 on the RTX 5070 was around 39%.
RTX 5060 Ti and RTX 5060: More Playable, Still Costly
DLSS 5 was not usable on the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB at 4K with the old model, and that remains the case with the new version, despite a significant performance improvement.
Going from 24 to 35 FPS represents a 46% gain at 4K, but without DLSS 5, the game runs at 95 FPS. That's still a whopping 63% performance loss when enabling neural rendering.
At 1440p, the situation is better. The old model ran below 60 FPS at this resolution, while the new version pushes performance above 60 FPS, a welcome improvement for what used to be a mid-range GPU option. At 1440p, enabling DLSS 5 reduced performance by 55%, while at 1080p, we saw the frame rate cut in half.
On the RTX 5060, we're using Low settings to avoid VRAM issues. The new model delivers 57%, 54%, and 53% higher frame rates at 4K, 1440p, and 1080p, respectively. This makes 1440p gaming in particular a lot more pleasant, with the game now running at 71 FPS.
1080p also becomes more usable on the RTX 5060, with the new DLSS 5 model now capable of 112 FPS at this resolution. It technically exceeded our threshold for usability previously as well, but dropping from 240 to 73 FPS was a bit of a sting. The performance loss has now been reduced to 53% at this resolution.
RTX 5050: Playable at 1080p, with a Catch
Then we have the RTX 5050. This entry-level model was previously not fast enough to run DLSS 5 in our opinion, achieving just 33 FPS at 1440p and 53 FPS at 1080p with the old model.
The new version runs considerably faster on this GPU, delivering a 55% increase in FPS at both 1440p and 1080p. While this isn't enough to push performance above the 60 FPS threshold at 1440p, it does increase the frame rate to 82 FPS at 1080p. That's still a huge performance loss compared to running without DLSS 5, but at least it's playable.
One weird result we noticed with the RTX 5050 specifically, and not so much with the other graphics cards, is that 1% low performance didn't really improve with the new DLSS 5 model.
In some cases, it actually went backwards. It could simply be a testing quirk, but at 1080p, an 82 FPS average with 1% lows still in the 30s doesn't make for the smoothest experience.
RTX 5090: The Best Case for DLSS 5
Lastly, here's a look at Nvidia's RTX 5090. This was clearly the best GPU to use with DLSS 5, as even with the old model, it delivered playable frame rates at all resolutions.
The new model works quite well here. At 4K, frame rates increased by 45%, while the performance loss compared to running without DLSS 5 dropped from 60% to 43%.
At 1440p, the situation is even better, though performance without DLSS 5 enabled is again limited by other bottlenecks. The new model delivered a 35% higher frame rate, and the overall performance loss was relatively small at just 18%. So if you happen to be using an RTX 5090 to play NBA 2K27 at 1440p, you may as well enable DLSS 5 given the frame rates we're seeing here.
And of course, the RTX 5090 is also more than capable at 1080p, though we're not sure how many people are pairing a 5090 with a 1080p display.
Render Times: How Much Faster Is the New Model?
With this performance data in hand, we can calculate DLSS 5's render time across the entire RTX 50 series lineup and use those figures to estimate performance in various scenarios with neural rendering enabled.
For reference, let's revisit the results from our previous DLSS 5 performance analysis, using the original model. At 4K, many performance scenarios simply weren't possible. On the RTX 5070 Ti, for example, DLSS 5 had a render time of 17ms, meaning that no matter how fast the rest of the game ran, you'd never achieve a 60 FPS render rate on that GPU. The only way to achieve the visual smoothness of 60 FPS would be through heavy frame generation.
Measured DLSS 5 Render Times (previous model)
|  | RTX 5090 | RTX 5080 | RTX 5070 Ti | RTX 5070 | RTX 5060 Ti 16GB | RTX 5060 | RTX 5050 | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4K DLSS 5 Render Time (ms) | 7.9 | 13.7 | 17.0 | 22.1 | 31.1 | 37.8 | 53.1 | 
| DLSS 5 Estimated Frame Rate (120 FPS Game FPS) | 62 | 45 | 40 | 33 | 25 | 22 | 16 | 
| DLSS 5 Estimated Frame Rate (80 FPS Game FPS) | 49 | 38 | 34 | 29 | 23 | 20 | 15 | 
| Required Game FPS to Hit 60 FPS | 114 | 332 | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | 
| Required Game FPS to Hit 80 FPS | 217 | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | 
| 1440p DLSS 5 Render Time (ms) | 3.6 | 6.1 | 7.8 | 10.2 | 14.1 | 16.9 | 24.0 | 
| DLSS 5 Estimated Frame Rate (120 FPS Game FPS) | 84 | 69 | 62 | 54 | 45 | 40 | 31 | 
| DLSS 5 Estimated Frame Rate (80 FPS Game FPS) | 62 | 54 | 49 | 44 | 38 | 34 | 27 | 
| Required Game FPS to Hit 60 FPS | 77 | 95 | 113 | 156 | 387 | n/a | n/a | 
| Required Game FPS to Hit 80 FPS | 112 | 157 | 213 | 444 | n/a | n/a | n/a | 
At 1440p, more cards were capable of running DLSS 5 at acceptable frame rates, but there were still plenty of scenarios that we felt weren't particularly reasonable. The RTX 5070, for example, could achieve 60 FPS with DLSS 5 enabled, provided the game was already running at 156 FPS before switching the feature on. The RTX 5060 Ti and below weren't really capable of running DLSS 5 at this resolution.
The newer model is much faster, significantly reducing render times. On average, the model ran 83% faster at 4K in our testing and 94% faster at 1440p. These are averages across the RTX 50 lineup, so we're not quite at the doubling Nvidia claimed, but the improvement is substantial and close enough. An 83% increase in speed at 4K is massive.
Measured DLSS 5 Render Times (October model)
|  | RTX 5090 | RTX 5080 | RTX 5070 Ti | RTX 5070 | RTX 5060 Ti 16GB | RTX 5060 | RTX 5050 | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4K DLSS 5 Render Time | 3.8 | 7.4 | 9.3 | 12.0 | 17.9 | 21.5 | 30.6 | 
| DLSS 5 Estimated Frame Rate (120 FPS Game FPS) | 82 | 64 | 57 | 49 | 38 | 33 | 26 | 
| DLSS 5 Estimated Frame Rate (80 FPS Game FPS) | 61 | 50 | 46 | 41 | 33 | 29 | 23 | 
| Required Game FPS to Hit 60 FPS | 78 | 108 | 136 | 216 | n/a | n/a | n/a | 
| Required Game FPS to Hit 80 FPS | 116 | 196 | 312 | 2217 | n/a | n/a | n/a | 
| Required Game FPS to Hit 120 FPS | 223 | 1076 | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | 
| 1440p DLSS 5 Render Time | 1.6 | 3.1 | 4.1 | 5.4 | 7.5 | 9.2 | 13.1 | 
| DLSS 5 Estimated Frame Rate (120 FPS Game FPS) | 101 | 88 | 81 | 73 | 63 | 57 | 47 | 
| DLSS 5 Estimated Frame Rate (80 FPS Game FPS) | 71 | 64 | 60 | 56 | 50 | 46 | 39 | 
| Required Game FPS to Hit 60 FPS | 66 | 74 | 79 | 89 | 109 | 134 | 277 | 
| Required Game FPS to Hit 80 FPS | 92 | 106 | 119 | 141 | 201 | 305 | n/a | 
| Required Game FPS to Hit 120 FPS | 149 | 191 | 235 | 343 | 1231 | n/a | n/a | 
Interestingly, the speedup varies depending on the overall performance of the GPU. On the RTX 5090, for example, the new DLSS 5 model was slightly more than twice as fast at 4K. The RTX 5070 saw an 83% improvement, while the RTX 5060 was 76% faster. Even the RTX 5050 ran the new model 73% faster at 4K, which is an excellent outcome from a performance standpoint.
What Faster Render Times Mean for Gaming
These improvements make DLSS 5 a lot more usable across most of the GeForce RTX 50 series. Previously, the RTX 5080 took 13.7ms to render DLSS 5 at 4K, making it very difficult to hit 60 FPS unless the game was already running at a very high frame rate.
The new model takes just 7.4ms to render, meaning a game only needs to be running at 108 FPS before enabling DLSS 5 to still achieve 60 FPS afterward. For games previously running at 80 FPS, the new model now delivers 50 FPS, compared to 38 FPS with the old version.
There's also good news for the RTX 5070 Ti, which was largely unusable at 4K. The old model turned 120 FPS gaming into 40 FPS gaming. The new model is much more capable, with a starting frame rate of 136 FPS allowing the game to run above 60 FPS with neural rendering enabled. That's still a huge performance hit, but at least this configuration is realistic in games.
The news is even better at 1440p. With the old model, the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti were usable at this resolution, and both become considerably more practical with the update. On the RTX 5070 Ti, you previously needed a game to run at 113 FPS to achieve 60 FPS with DLSS 5 enabled. That requirement has dropped to just 79 FPS, meaning a game running at 79 FPS without DLSS 5 will only drop to 60 FPS with the feature enabled.
It's still a sizeable performance hit for a single visual feature, a 24% reduction in FPS in this example, but it's not that crazy. We're now within the realm of other performance-intensive graphics settings, rather than dealing with such a huge outlier.
The Performance Penalty Is Smaller, but Still Significant
With the new DLSS 5 model running ~80% to 90% faster than the original, the performance penalty has been reduced across the board. Take a game running at 120 FPS as an example.
Across the RTX 50 series lineup, enabling the old DLSS 5 model resulted in an average 71% performance loss at 4K. That's been reduced to 58% with the new model. At 1440p, the average performance loss has dropped from 54% to 39%.
In situations where you were enjoying a high frame-rate gaming experience, the performance loss remains substantial with neural rendering enabled. The RTX 5070 drops from 120 FPS to 73 FPS at 1440p. Essentially, you sacrifice those high frame-rates along with the latency benefits, to use DLSS 5 feature. But you don't have to sacrifice nearly as much as before.
For games running at 80 FPS, the impact of enabling DLSS 5 is smaller because its render time accounts for a lower proportion of the overall frame time. With the old model at 1440p, enabling DLSS 5 took games from 80 FPS to 44 FPS on average, a 45% performance loss. That penalty has been reduced to 31% with the new model.
Image Quality: Little Has Changed
Do these performance improvements come at the expense of visual quality? We're not going to do an exhaustive analysis here, but our general impression from using the new model in NBA 2K27, which features the official implementation, is that image quality is broadly the same, potentially slightly worse in some situations.
For a better representation of image quality comparisons, check out the HUB video below:
There are two ways to look at this. On the one hand, it's great that Nvidia has been able to improve performance while delivering largely similar visual output. That's a step in the right direction. On the other hand, DLSS 5's original model had quite a few visual issues, so stagnation or even a small step backward in image quality is not ideal. What we really need to see from DLSS 5 is performance and visual quality improving simultaneously.
The new DLSS 5 model still has noticeable issues with image stability, though it's difficult to say based on our testing whether these problems have gotten worse. Lighting flicker, where surfaces shift slightly in tone from frame to frame, is still very much present in the updated October model, and we noticed it in the same scenarios as in our original DLSS 5 analysis.
We also found with the original DLSS 5 model that neural rendering had a hard time keeping objects consistent at different distances from the camera.
This ugly effect also extends to skin tones. DLSS 5 is best equipped to enhance skin when a character is relatively close to the camera and occupies a large portion of the frame. As you zoom out or move farther away from a character, their skin typically becomes darker and shinier with neural rendering enabled, something that doesn't occur with the feature disabled. In our opinion, this can make human characters look a bit strange unless they're close to the camera.
Another major artifact we discovered was related to disocclusion. DLSS 5 had a tendency to create a halo-like effect around characters, and I think this has actually become slightly worse and more noticeable with the new model.
Has Nvidia Toned Down Neural Rendering?
Interestingly, while researching the new DLSS 5 model, we came across quite a few posts from people using modded versions who complained that the updated model appears toned down compared to the original. According to these reports, it produces a less intense effect and a smaller overall visual change, particularly with the sliders set to higher levels.
This is interesting because in NBA 2K27 (with the official DLSS 5 implementation), the effects of neural rendering look broadly similar to what they were before. Then again, NBA doesn't have an aggressive implementation. It mostly attempts modest visual improvements to avoid overcooking the image and generating an AI slop-like result.
DLSS 5 Got Faster, but It's Still a Work in Progress
The new DLSS 5 model is a step in the right direction toward making it a genuinely usable feature in games. The updated model runs much faster, while visual quality appears broadly similar. It's a decent level of optimization that makes neural rendering viable on more GPUs than it was at launch.
But doubling the processing speed is only one of many improvements this technology needs. Enabling neural rendering still comes with a high performance cost, even after this update. It's just that the penalty isn't nearly as massive as it used to be.
It's clear that performance was the focus of this DLSS 5 release and not visual quality. All of the artifacts and issues with the original release remain, and these need to be addressed. Otherwise, neural rendering will continue to produce worse image quality in some respects than traditional rendering. Whether Nvidia can improve both performance and image quality simultaneously remains to be seen.
I do find it bizarre that Nvidia didn't simply wait a few weeks and make this faster model the official release of DLSS 5. The tech has been integrated into a single game so far, and there has hardly been a rush of developers jumping on board (in contrast, modders appear to be all-in). How much optimization headroom remains is unclear, but it's an interesting jump in performance just weeks after launch.
Going forward, DLSS 5 titles will use the new model, so the original version is effectively going to be consigned to history. The upcoming Hogwarts Legacy update in November will use the new model, and we'll likely revisit DLSS 5 when that arrives.

articles.title: ¿Cuándo podrás usar el iPhone Duo con un Apple Pencil? La espera será más breve de lo que piensas
articles.text:
El iPhone Duo se prepara para su tan ansiado debut en el mercado. Este viernes 23 de octubre se pondrán en marcha las entregas del primer plegable de Apple, aunque es un hecho que solo unos pocos afortunados podrán disfrutarlo desde el primer día. Para la gran mayoría de los compradores, la espera se extenderá hasta noviembre o diciembre, o incluso hasta enero de 2027. La buena noticia para quienes sí tengan acceso al móvil desde su lanzamiento es que el soporte para Apple Pencil llegará en apenas cuestión de días.
Cuando los de Cupertino anunciaron el iPhone Duo, indicaron que el soporte para usarlo con el Apple Pencil se añadiría "más adelante" en el año. No obstante, como no brindaron mayores precisiones al respecto, todo hacía pensar que sería más cerca de finales de 2026. La buena noticia es que la opción de usar el stylus se incorporará con la próxima actualización de iOS.
Si bien Apple no ha realizado anuncios oficiales en tal sentido, es un hecho que el uso del Apple Pencil en el iPhone Duo se activará con iOS 27.2, que estará disponible la próxima semana. Esto fue confirmado por Max Weinbach, quien ya tuvo acceso al nuevo móvil plegable de la manzana.
El analista instaló la Release Candidate de iOS 27.2, que se puso a disposición el pasado lunes, y ya pudo comenzar a usar el Apple Pencil en el iPhone Duo. Tengamos en cuenta que el smartphone se lanzará con iOS 27.1 preinstalado, de modo que un simple update será suficiente para aprovechar esta característica.
El iPhone Duo estrenará el soporte para Apple Pencil en iOS 27.2
Respecto de cómo funcionará el Apple Pencil en el iPhone Duo, Weinbach ha ofrecido los primeros detalles. En una imagen que compartió en X (Twitter), se observa el uso del lápiz para escribir en la pantalla interna de 7,6 pulgadas. Sin embargo, la compatibilidad no se limitará a dicho panel.
En respuesta a una consulta al respecto, el susodicho indicó que el iPhone Duo permitirá el uso del Apple Pencil en sus dos pantallas. De modo que también se podrá usar con la de 5,4 pulgadas que se encuentra en el exterior del smartphone. Es lógico pensar que se sacará mayor provecho del accesorio en la pantalla interior, pero los de la manzana no han querido retacear su implementación.
Es importante recordar que no todos los Apple Pencil son compatibles con el iPhone Duo. Apple ha confirmado que el único modelo del lápiz que funciona con el plegable es el Apple Pencil con puerto USB-C. Así que si tienes los modelos de primera o segunda generación, o un Apple Pencil Pro, no podrás usarlos con el dispositivo. Y si debes salir a comprar el Pencil USB-C, vas a tener que desembolsar 89 euros adicionales a los 2.339 euros que como mínimo has pagado por el foldable.

articles.title: Netflix Bridges AWS IAM and Internal Identity with Workload Attestation
articles.text:
Netflix has developed a workload attestation mechanism that allows Apache Spark jobs running on Amazon EMR to exchange their AWS execution identity for a short-lived internal workload identity. The approach bridges AWS IAM with Netflix’s internal Metatron PKI, allowing managed compute workloads to authenticate to internal services without manually injecting credentials.
Dhruv Pratap, Big Data Platform Engineer at Netflix, described the design in a LinkedIn post as
On infrastructure you build yourself, you can bootstrap your own identity however you like.
Netflix operates two identity systems. AWS provides managed workloads with an IAM execution role, while internal services use Metatron, a private PKI that issues short-lived X.509 certificates for mutual TLS. Netflix also uses Data Projects as the ownership and identity boundary for data access. A Spark job running on EMR therefore needs to establish that its AWS identity corresponds to the internal identity associated with its Data Project.
The design maps each Data Project to a dedicated IAM role. Because Netflix expects Data Projects to reach the tens of thousands, these roles are deterministically distributed across a pool of dedicated AWS accounts rather than concentrated in one account.
Netflix workload attestation flow (Source: Netflix Blog Post)
When a job is submitted, Netflix’s control plane validates the request, resolves the Data Project’s IAM role, and creates a signed workload metadata payload identifying the intended workload. The control plane is the only service authorized to create these claims.
The Spark driver uses credentials associated with its execution role to create a pre-signed request to the AWS Security Token Service GetCallerIdentity endpoint. Netflix’s Identity service retrieves the request from AWS STS to determine which IAM role signed it, providing an independently verifiable statement of the workload’s AWS identity.
The Identity service then compares the AWS response with the signed metadata from the control plane. The AWS response proves possession of the expected IAM role, while the signed metadata identifies the intended workload. Their intersection allows the service to issue a Metatron certificate.
The architecture also addresses Spark’s executor fan-out. Rather than independently attesting thousands of executors, Netflix has the driver attest once and distribute credentials through authenticated and encrypted Spark RPC. This avoids attestation traffic proportional to executor count while making the driver an additional credential distribution trust boundary.
Netflix’s driver-based credential distribution for Spark executors (Source: Netflix Blog Post)
Credential renewal is handled separately from initial bootstrap. The driver periodically re attests before its short lived certificate expires, while executors do not independently renew credentials. Netflix notes that repeatable attestation is important for long-running workloads. The pattern separates internal workload identity from the managed compute provider while retaining the provider’s identity as cryptographic proof. Netflix says the approach can also apply to other managed environments where workloads receive a cloud identity but need to establish a separate organizational identity.

articles.title: Nuclear-powered spaceships
articles.text:
Nuclear-powered spaceships
A new era of spaceflight could save astronauts time and cut exposure to cosmic radiation as they rocket to Mars—and beyond.
Just before the Artemis II crew began its historic slingshot around the moon this past April, NASA announced plans to build Space Reactor-1 Freedom. SR-1, the first-ever nuclear-reactor-powered interplanetary spacecraft, is meant to fly an uncrewed mission to Mars by the end of 2028, arriving in 2029. A successful mission would herald a new era of more efficient, potentially faster spaceflight—saving astronauts time and cutting their exposure to harmful cosmic radiation as they travel to Mars and beyond. “You wake up to that announcement, and it puts a big smile on your face,” says Simon Middleburgh, co-director of the Nuclear Futures Institute at Bangor University in Wales.
The sticking points
Running a nuclear reactor in space may sound like lunacy, but it’s not. The Soviet Union sent dozens of reactors into orbit, often to power spy satellites. And experts say there aren’t any major technical obstacles to making nuclear space propulsion happen. “I think it’s a very doable technology,” says Philip Metzger, a spaceflight engineering researcher at the Florida Space Institute.“I’m happy to see them finally doing this.”
Still, developing space propulsion using reactors has been slow going. The US has started—and terminated—several programs looking into it over the past 75 years. The latest casualty was DRACO, a collaboration between NASA and the Department of Defense, which ended in 2025. The project was canceled because of high experimentation costs, an inability to compete with conventional rocket propulsion on price, and difficulty ensuring that ground tests could be performed safely and effectively. (You are creating an incredibly powerful nuclear reaction, after all.)
The progress
After much wavering, it now appears that nuclear-powered interplanetary travel is a $2 billion bet NASA is willing to make. The agency is pursuing an approach called nuclear electric propulsion, which uses the neutrons produced in a self-sustaining, uranium-atom-splitting reaction to create heat and ultimately electricity. The electricity is used to ionize a gas, which is blasted out of the spacecraft with the help of magnetic fields, generating thrust. The approach “is very low thrust, but very efficient,” says Sebastian Corbisiero, the US Department of Energy’s national technical director of space reactor programs. “So you can use it for a long period of time.”
What might such a rocket look like? A presentation by Steve Sinacore, program director of NASA’s SR-1 program, offers some clues. So far, the concept art makes the craft look like a colossal fletched arrow. The back will house the power-and-propulsion system, while the tip will hold a uranium-filled nuclear reactor with a capacity of at least 20 kilowatts. (For context, a typical nuclear plant on Earth is about 50,000 times more powerful.) The “fletches” on SR-1 are large fins that help cool the reactor by radiating heat into space.
Like many other pieces of space hardware, the reactor will need to be put through its paces on the ground before it’s cleared for the rough rocket trip to space. “Going through the launch safely is going to be a challenge,” says Middleburgh. “You are being shaken, rattled, and rolled.” For safety reasons, the reactor will be switched on around two days post-launch, when it’s comfortably far from Earth. Uranium isn’t tremendously dangerous by itself, but that can’t be said of the waste products that emerge when the reactor is running. If SR-1 works as planned, its journey to Mars will take about a year.
Will this novel form of space propulsion actually reach the Red Planet by 2029? It’s possible. NASA says the Idaho National Laboratory, which is building SR-1’s reactor, is making progress and is on target for a late-2028 launch. “Procurement of major components is underway, and integration work on the power and propulsion element is advancing steadily,” Sinacore told MIT Technology Review. The outlook will get even sunnier if the Artemis program, which aims to start laying the foundations for a base on the lunar south pole by the decade’s end, keeps to its own bold deadline.
“It’s an aggressive timeline,” says Lindsey Holmes, who is vice president of advanced projects at Analytical Mechanics Associates, an aerospace company in Virginia. She suspects the push is being driven partly by China’s and Russia’s own deep-space nuclear ambitions. The two countries have spoken about plans to place a reactor on the moon’s surface in the mid-2030s to power a jointly operated lunar base. Whether it flies or fails in space, SR-1’s development should help NASA put its own reactor on the moon; the technology involved in the two projects is broadly similar, given that the lunar surface, like space itself, is a vacuum. If an interplanetary nuclear-powered spacecraft works, a nuclear reactor on the moon should too.
Progress meter . . . . . . . . . . . . 6
Most of the technology for SR-1 already exists; it’s going to come down to piecing it all together and then seeing how it performs in space.

articles.title: Spotify: Teilen des Familienabos wird schwieriger
articles.text:
Der Streamingdienst Spotify geht mit einer QR-Code-Verifizierung gegen geteilte Familien- sowie auch Duo-Abos vor. Mitglieder einer Gruppe sollen damit beweisen, dass sie tatsächlich im selben Haushalt leben wie die Person, die das Abo verwaltet. Das Teilen über den eigenen Haushalt hinaus ist bei beiden Tarifen eigentlich ohnehin untersagt – alle Nutzer:innen sollen dieselbe Anschrift haben. Doch daran halten sich viele User:innen nicht.
Bisher reichte eine Adresse
Das bisherige Verfahren war simpel: Wer dem Premium-Familienabo (22 Euro) beitrat, das sich bis zu sechs Personen teilen können, oder dem Duo-Tarif für zwei (18 Euro), musste lediglich die vollständige Adresse angeben und bestätigen, mit dem Hauptnutzer zusammenzuwohnen. Spotify erklärt dazu, man verfolge den Standort nicht, sondern prüfe die Adresse nur zur Verifizierung. Praktisch konnte so auch jemand am anderen Ende der Welt Teil des Abos sein.
Laut Spotifys Support-Seite müssen Mitglieder eines Familien- oder Duo-Abos künftig „unter Umständen“ einen QR-Code scannen. Der Code erscheint auf dem Smartphone der Person, die das Abo verwaltet. Das Mitglied scannt ihn mit der Handykamera – beide müssen sich dafür am selben Ort befinden. Zu finden ist der Code in der Mitgliederverwaltung der App: erst auf das Profilbild tippen, dann auf „Dein Abo“ und anschließend auf „Verwalten“. Verpflichtend ist das Verfahren offenbar derzeit nicht, das könnte aber kommen.
Kein Scan, zwölf Monate Sperre
Wer die Aufforderung erhält, hat sieben Tage Zeit, den Code zu scannen. Verstreicht die Frist, kann die Person zwölf Monate lang keinem anderen Family- oder Duo-Abo beitreten – bleibt also nur ein eigenes Abo oder die kostenlose Version.
Damit niemand einfach einen Screenshot weiterschickt, erneuert sich der QR-Code nach Angaben von Spotify alle paar Sekunden. Ganz dicht ist das System trotzdem nicht: Ein Nutzer berichtet auf Reddit, er habe die Prüfung per Bildschirmfreigabe in Microsoft Teams bestanden. Spotify könnte letztlich auch verlangen, dass die Mitglieder der Familiengruppe die gleiche Geoposition haben, wenn der QR-Code gescannt wird. Dazu müsste man der Firma aber erlauben, diese sensiblen Informationen auszulesen.

articles.title: ONU cobra Meta por possíveis restrições políticas nas eleições brasileiras
articles.text:
Especialistas independentes da ONU pediram, nesta quarta-feira (21), que a Meta investigue se seus sistemas de moderação, recomendação e inteligência artificial restringiram de forma desproporcional conteúdos de um dos lados da disputa eleitoral brasileira.
Os peritos querem explicações sobre os critérios usados pela empresa, as restrições relatadas e os mecanismos de contestação disponíveis. A preocupação é que decisões das plataformas prejudiquem a liberdade de expressão e o equilíbrio entre as campanhas.
Relatos apontam diferenças no funcionamento das plataformas
Os problemas relatados envolvem Instagram, WhatsApp e Facebook. Segundo os especialistas, informações de monitoramento e relatos atribuídos a funcionários da própria Meta sugerem que contas ligadas a um dos lados da corrida presidencial foram afetadas de maneira desproporcional.
Entre os episódios mencionados estão interrupções temporárias no perfil de campanha de um candidato, diferenças na contagem de visualizações e restrições a publicações no Instagram. Os observadores também apontaram possíveis disparidades na geração de imagens por inteligência artificial, nos resultados de busca por canais do WhatsApp e na distribuição de Stories.
“Informações, inclusive de funcionários da Meta, sugerem que contas vinculadas a um dos lados da disputa presidencial foram afetadas de forma desproporcional”, afirmam os peritos.
O comunicado também cita uma decisão do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) que determinou que a Meta aplique as mesmas regras às duas campanhas até o segundo turno, sem tratamento desigual nas buscas, recomendações ou no alcance das publicações.
O que a ONU quer esclarecer
A cobrança vai além de bloqueios individuais. Os especialistas querem que a Meta verifique se seus sistemas automatizados estão tratando conteúdos políticos de maneira desigual e explique como essas decisões são tomadas.
Entre as questões que precisam ser esclarecidas estão:
- Moderação: quais critérios justificam bloqueios, suspensões ou restrições a publicações políticas?
- Recomendação: como os algoritmos determinam o alcance de conteúdos de diferentes campanhas nos feeds dos usuários?
- Inteligência artificial: os recursos de geração de imagens apresentam diferenças no tratamento de solicitações relacionadas aos concorrentes?
- Buscas e distribuição: por que canais do WhatsApp e Stories de candidatos podem ter resultados ou alcance diferentes?
- Contestação: como usuários e campanhas podem questionar decisões e obter respostas em tempo hábil durante a eleição?
Os especialistas defendem que a empresa reavalie seus sistemas de moderação, recomendação e inteligência artificial, explique os motivos das restrições e corrija eventuais desigualdades. As perguntas não significam que o favorecimento de uma campanha esteja comprovado, mas indicam a necessidade de investigar os problemas relatados.
“Perder alcance pode significar perder voz no debate público e a capacidade de mobilizar comunidades. Algoritmos, sistemas de IA e decisões de moderação de conteúdo não devem se tornar árbitros invisíveis da discussão política”, afirmam os especialistas.
Transparência e respostas rápidas durante a eleição
Os peritos reconhecem a importância de combater a desinformação, mas ressaltam que esse objetivo não deve justificar restrições indevidas a manifestações políticas legítimas. Também defendem mecanismos eficazes para contestar decisões, com respostas rápidas o suficiente para que eventuais correções ainda tenham efeito durante a campanha.
A manifestação foi assinada por relatores especiais da ONU que atuam em áreas como liberdade de expressão, independência judicial, liberdade de reunião e associação e direitos humanos, além de integrantes do Grupo de Trabalho sobre Empresas e Direitos Humanos.
A Meta precisa esclarecer quais critérios orientam a moderação e a recomendação de conteúdo político, como seus sistemas identificam possíveis diferenças de tratamento e quais medidas podem corrigir eventuais problemas. As respostas também devem explicar como a empresa permite que campanhas e usuários contestem restrições. A questão central é verificar se as regras são aplicadas de forma consistente durante o processo eleitoral, sem presumir que as suspeitas relatadas já tenham sido comprovadas.
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

articles.title: Xbox Cloud Gaming’s pay-as-you-go option starts at $3.99 for 10 hours
articles.text:
Microsoft announced last month that it will let anyone access Xbox Cloud Gaming in November, without the need to subscribe to Xbox Game Pass. The new pay-as-you-go model will require players to purchase bundles of cloud hours, and now Microsoft is revealing today that bundles will start at $3.99 for 10 hours of cloud playtime.
Xbox Cloud Gaming’s pay-as-you-go option starts at $3.99 for 10 hours
Microsoft is opening up Xbox Cloud Gaming to anyone in November.
Xbox Insiders who don’t have a Game Pass subscription will be able to start purchasing cloud playtime today, ahead of a broader rollout next month. Insiders can access “introductory” launch pricing bundles:
- 10 hours for $3.99
- 25 hours for $7.99
- 50 hours for $11.99
All of these cloud hours will include ad-free cloud gaming, shorter wait times, and higher-quality streaming. These aren’t monthly bundles of hours either, so once you purchased a pack it remains available until the hours are used.
The pay-as-you-go Xbox Cloud Gaming option arrives just in time for Grand Theft Auto VI. I reported earlier this month that Microsoft has secured Grand Theft Auto VI streaming rights, but it’s not yet clear if this will be limited to just Xbox consoles. Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball revealed on X that Microsoft won’t be streaming Grand Theft Auto VI to PCs, suggesting that the web browsers and apps that can usually access Xbox Cloud Gaming will not be able to stream Grand Theft Auto VI.
Microsoft also continues to test free, ad-supported cloud gaming for Xbox Insiders, offering up another way to stream games without Game Pass. The free streaming sessions are limited to games you already own, and sessions are capped at one hour.

articles.title: Apple explique en détail comment Safari protège le pistage intersite par email
articles.text:
Apple détaille dans un billet publié sur le blog de WebKit la parade intégrée à Safari contre l'"identity resolution", une technique de pistage qui s'appuie sur votre adresse email plutôt que sur les cookies. La protection est déployée avec iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 et visionOS 27.
Safari bloque les cookies intersites depuis six ans, et la publicité en ligne a trouvé un autre moyen de reconnaître les internautes. Apple coupe maintenant l'accès à l'infrastructure qui rend ce suivi possible.
Quand l'adresse email remplace le cookie : ce que Safari bloque
Comme toutes les technique de pistage publicitaire, le mécanisme est particulièrement surnois. Lorsqu'un internaute saisit son adresse mail pour se connecter à un site ou s'abonner à une newsletter, un tiers invisible la récupère et l'envoie à ses serveurs. Ceux-ci l'associent à un identifiant opaque, un code sans lien visible avec vous, et le renvoient au site, qui le stocke. Cet identifiant sert ensuite à vous reconnaître, comme le ferait un cookie, et à vous suivre d'un site à l'autre. Se déconnecter ou se désabonner n'y change rien, puisque l'adresse et l'identifiant restent chez le tiers. Au fil des connexions et des formulaires remplis, celui-ci complète votre profil, ce que le secteur appelle un "identity graph".
A l'instar d'un numéro de téléphone, une adresse email est presque toujours une donnée personnelle identifiante. On la garde souvent pendant des années, voire des décennies. Mais du côté des annonceurs, elle permet donc de suivre une même personne d'un site à l'autre, mais aussi d'un appareil à l'autre. Apple précise que lorsque le site où vous vous connectez utilise votre adresse pour personnaliser son propre service, ce n’est pas du pistage. Cela reste le site auquel vous avez confié vos informations. Le problème vient du tiers qui s’intercale entre les sites. Présent en coulisses sur un grand nombre de pages, il reçoit votre adresse depuis chacune d’elles et peut ainsi rapprocher vos visites, d’un site à l’autre et d’un appareil à l’autre, puis servir de point de passage pour cibler des publicités. Aucun site, pris seul, n’a cette vue d’ensemble.
Dans les versions 27 de ses systèmes, Safari et WebKit bloquent donc l'accès réseau à ces services. Ils ne visent ni les fournisseurs de connexion ni les services de newsletter, mais les acteurs dont le seul rôle est de vous pister. L'adresse ne part plus vers leurs serveurs, aucun identifiant n'est généré et le profil ne se construit pas. Le filtrage se fait au niveau du nom de domaine. Changer la forme de la requête ne permet donc pas de le contourner. Nous rapportions en septembre 2017 que Safari allait intégrer l'Intelligent Tracking Prevention, qui limitait notamment à 24 heures l'usage de certaines données de navigation par les annonceurs. Le blocage porte cette fois sur l'adresse email, et non plus sur les cookies.
Au-delà du spam, il vaut donc mieux faire usage d'un service de messagerie capable de générer des alias afin d'avoir une adresse différente pour chacun des services utilisé. Une telle option est notamment disponible chez Simple Login (Proton), Addy.io, Firefox Relay ou DuckDuckGo Email Protection. Les abonnés à iCloud+ disposent aussi de Hide My Email.
Ces outils génèrent une adresse unique et aléatoire pour chaque site, tout en continuant à transférer les messages vers votre boîte. Comme aucune adresse n'est partagée entre deux sites, il n'y a donc rien à recouper.
Source : WebKit

articles.title: Britain’s Skyfly raises €8.91 million to bring its two-seat Axe eVTOL to market and develop Longbow for defence | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Skyfly Technologies, a British developer of electric and hybrid-electric vertical take-off aircraft, has closed an €8.91 million ($10 million) Seed round.
The round was led by HICO Investment Group, a specialist growth equity investor, with participation from Archangel, a €50 million early-stage fund and Europe’s only dedicated next-generation defence technology venture fund.
“What Skyfly’s team has achieved with so little is remarkable: a new aircraft, designed and built from scratch, flying and now leading the way through a brand-new certification pathway. We’re excited to back a team with a big vision and relentless drive to execute,” said Chris Hartnoll, Managing Director, HICO Investment Group.
Founded in 2019 and based in Thorpe Mandeville, Oxfordshire, Skyfly develops manned and unmanned aircraft and systems for civilian and defence markets. Its flagship product, the Axe, is a two-seat, fully electric, vertically-capable aircraft with a range of more than 100 miles and a cruise speed of 100mph, requiring no runway for take-off or landing. The Longbow is its hybrid-electric unmanned derivative for defence and government customers.
The Axe is developed under the leadership of CTO Dr. William Brooks, who has spent over three decades in light aircraft development and has certified more than 2,000 aircraft currently in service. Axe takes off like a helicopter using eight fixed-angle electric motors, transitions to forward flight where its wings generate aerodynamic lift and can operate from conventional runways.
Since there are no tilting motors or rotary wings, Axe is designed to eliminate the mechanical complexity and potential points of failure that characterise many eVTOL concepts. In an emergency power loss scenario, the winged design allows the aircraft to glide rather than fall.
The Axe offers a range of over 100 miles, a flight time of 60 to 90 minutes, a cruising speed of 100mph and a 200kg payload capacity. Skyfly projects an operating cost of around €83.57 (£70) per flight, which gives it a favourable standing against the likes of legacy two-seater aircrafts such as Robinson R22 or Cessna 152.
Longbow, Skyfly’s second aircraft, is a hybrid-electric unmanned aircraft with a range exceeding 400 miles and the same 200kg payload. It is designed for cargo resupply, intelligence and surveillance, medevac, and ship-to-shore logistics missions. The company says both the aircraft will be manufactured at Skyfly’s 10,000 sq.ft. facility in Thorpe Mandeville, Oxfordshire.
“Longbow addresses a clear requirement for unmanned systems that can move meaningful payloads over significant distances without relying on a runway. Archangel invests exclusively in defence-first companies, and our backing of Skyfly reflects the potential we see in its technology to deliver mission necessary capability for the modern battlespace,” said Nicholas Nelson, General Partner at Archangel Ventures.
Skyfly says its Axe prototype has completed more than 100 piloted flights, including Europe’s first airfield-to-airfield eVTOL flight. It holds experimental flight permits in both the UK and the US, and sixty-one private customers globally have already placed orders.
The fundraise comes amid a regulatory shift, with the FAA’s MOSAIC reforms taking effect in July 2026. The MOSAIC reforms rewrote the rules governing Light Sport Aircraft to admit electric propulsion, multi-motor architectures and vertical take-off aircraft into a category that has been historically restricted to private owners rather than commercial operators. Skyfly says its Axe, a two-seat electric Vertically Capable Aircraft (eVCA) classified as Light Sport-class, was designed precisely for this rulebook.
Michael Thompson, founder and CEO of Skyfly, said, “This investment gives us the resources to take the Axe from a flying prototype to a certified aircraft in customers’ hands. The FAA’s MOSAIC rules have opened a route to market that simply did not exist for electric aircraft before, and the Axe was designed for exactly this category. HICO and Archangel understood that timing, and their backing lets us move at the pace the opportunity demands: completing certification and standing up series production.”
The fresh capital will be deployed across three areas: completing FAA Light Sport Aircraft certification for the Axe under the MOSAIC rules, scaling manufacturing capacity on both sides of the Atlantic, and accelerating development of the Longbow.

articles.title: Une recharge en 5 minutes pour 10 000 € : BYD dévoile sa nouvelle Seagull en Chine
articles.text:
BYD a lancé ce mardi 20 octobre en Chine la deuxième génération de la Seagull, sa voiture électrique la moins chère. La présentation s’est tenue sur le circuit de Zhengzhou, dans la province du Henan. Comme cela était attendu depuis cet été, la nouvelle génération grandit. Elle mesure 4,21 m de long, soit 42,5 cm de plus qu’avant, ce qui la rapproche de la Dolphin, la compacte de la marque. Elle passe de quatre à cinq places, gagne un coffre avant de 94 litres et devient une propulsion. Enfin, sa puissance grimpe à 115 ou 129 ch selon les versions, contre 75 ch auparavant.
Pour mémoire, la Seagull pèse lourd chez BYD, avec environ 1,55 million d’exemplaires vendus depuis avril 2023. Ses ventes s’essoufflent pourtant. D’après les chiffres compilés par CnEVPost, elles ont reculé de 33 % sur les neuf premiers mois de 2026, à 265 901 unités. Sur toute l’année 2025, BYD en avait écoulé 529 537.
Des prix hallucinants en Chine pour la BYD Seagull
Le prix d’appel est en baisse comparé à la génération précédente : 65 900 yuans, soit environ 8 800 €, contre 69 900 yuans, environ 9 300 €. Surtout, la nouveauté phare de la citadine est l’arrivée de la technologie Flash Charging, qui promet de passer de 10 à 70 % de batterie en seulement cinq minutes. Pour l’avoir, il faut toutefois viser les versions à partir de 75 900 yuans, l’équivalent de 10 100 €.
| Caractéristique | Vitality | Freedom | Comfort | Flying | Smart | 
| Puissance | 116 ch | 116 ch | 129 ch | 129 ch | 129 ch | 
| Batterie | 30,1 kWh | 30,1 kWh | 39,2 kWh | 39,2 kWh | 39,2 kWh | 
| Autonomie (CLTC) | 320 km | 320 km | 420 km | 420 km | 420 km | 
| Recharge Flash | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | 
| Prix* | 8 800 € | 9 700 € | 10 100 € | 11 100 € | 13 300 € | 
*Prix en yuans converti à l’euro actuel
Quand les deux premières versions se contentent de 30,1 kWh et n’ont pas droit à la recharge Flash, les trois modèles les plus huppés adoptent un accumulateur de 39,2 kWh cette fois compatible avec la recharge ultra-rapide.
Attention aussi aux autonomies, mesurées selon le cycle chinois CLTC, plus généreux que la norme européenne WLTP. En convertissant, on se retrouverait avec des autonomies respectives d’environ 262 km et 344 km. Des valeurs comparables à la Renault Twingo E-Tech ou une Citroën ë-C3… pour un prix près de 10 000 € moins cher.
La recharge en cinq minutes a ses conditions
Zhang Zhuo, directeur commercial du réseau BYD, a indiqué que la marque comptait 12 165 stations Flash le jour du lancement, et en vise 20 000 d’ici à la fin de l’année. Début octobre, ces bornes ont d’ailleurs fait parler d’elles quand des enfants ont été filmés en train de se balancer à leurs câbles à Nanning. Pour convaincre, BYD offre un an de recharge Flash gratuite aux particuliers qui achètent l’une des trois versions compatibles.
Dans le cas de la nouvelle Seagull, pour passer de 10 à 70 % sur la batterie de 39,2 kWh, il faut y faire entrer environ 23,5 kWh en cinq minutes, soit une puissance moyenne d’environ 280 kW. Du jamais vu sur une citadine.
Pas chère et bien équipée, la BYD Seagull
D’après le dossier d’homologation déposé auprès du ministère chinois de l’Industrie (MIIT), la batterie LFP vient de FinDreams, la filiale batteries de BYD. Cette chimie lithium-fer-phosphate coûte moins cher, car elle se passe de nickel et de cobalt. Le moteur, lui, sort de l’usine BYD de Zhengzhou.
En revanche, la marque n’a pas rogné sur l’équipement. On trouve un écran central de 15,6 pouces avec l’IA chinoise DeepSeek, des sièges avant chauffants et ventilés, et un massage pour le conducteur. Les versions hautes peuvent recevoir un lidar, un capteur laser posé sur le toit qui cartographie les alentours, pour une aide à la conduite en ville et sur autoroute.
Les commandes sont ouvertes sur le site chinois de BYD. La marque n’a pas dit si cette deuxième génération arrivera en Europe, où la première est vendue sous le nom de Dolphin Surf. En France, le modèle vient justement de gagner une cinquième place et les services Google.

articles.title: El Oppo Find X10 Pro Max ya está disponible en España: el matagigantes con una de las cámaras más locas del mercado
articles.text:
Oppo acaba de lanzar en España su nueva serie Find X10, que se compone del modelo homónimo y de la variante Pro Max. Hablamos de dos móviles que destacan tanto por su diseño como por sus prestaciones técnicas, y que mantienen la calidad a la que la marca china ya nos tiene acostumbrados. Y este año el fabricante redobla la apuesta con una de las configuraciones de cámaras más locas del mercado.
El Oppo Find X10 Pro Max llega equipado con tres sensores de 200 megapíxeles cada uno, en tanto que el X10 estándar tiene "apenas" dos cámaras de 200 MP. La compañía asiática ha trabajado una vez más en estrecha colaboración con Hasselblad para ofrecer una experiencia fotográfica en otro nivel.
Si nos enfocamos en la opción tope de gama, nos encontramos que el Oppo Find X10 Pro Max equipa una cámara principal Ultra HDR con sensor ISOCELL HPC de 200 MP (1/1,28 pulgadas). Este componente se desarrolló junto a Samsung y ofrece hasta 17 pasos de rango dinámico.
Por su parte, la cámara ultra gran angular de 200 MP utiliza un sensor de 1/1,56 pulgadas que, según Oppo, captura el doble de luz que la versión previa. Por último, el teleobjetivo de 200 MP permite capturar imágenes nítidas en condiciones desfavorables gracias a su apertura ultrarrápida f/2,1 y su distancia de enfoque mínima de 10 centímetros.
Nuevo Oppo Find X10 Pro Max: una bestia para la fotografía y el vídeo
Entre los puntos atractivos de la nueva serie Find X10, es que ambos modelos incorporan la tecnología LUMO True Image Engine de Oppo. La misma permite capturar colores, tonos y texturas mucha más realistas al momento de tomar fotos. Esto no solo permite que la imagen sea lo más parecida posible a la escena real, sino que también evita (o reduce considerablemente) la necesidad de editarla posteriormente.
En lo que respecta a vídeos, el Oppo Find X10 Pro Max permite la captura en hasta 8K a 30 cuadros por segundo en sus tres cámaras. Asimismo, los sensores soportan la grabación en 4K a 60 o 120 FPS. Pero la historia no termina allí, pues tanto la versión tope de gama como el X10 estándar son compatibles con O-Log2, Dolby Vision y Open Gate Capture.
Vale mencionar que Open Gate es un modo de vídeo que no recorta el vídeo a un formato panorámico específico, sino que utiliza toda la superficie y resolución nativa del sensor durante la grabación. Es la primera vez que Oppo integra esta tecnología en sus smartphones, lo cual apunta a ser de gran ayuda para creadores de contenido y editores profesionales. Al utilizar toda la superficie del sensor, es más fácil cambiar el encuadre, el formato (vertical u horizontal) y el zoom sin perder la calidad original y utilizando un único archivo como fuente.
Oppo también está lanzando accesorios para profesionales y entusiastas que quieran exprimir al máximo las capacidades de los Find X10 y X10 Pro Max. Por un lado, se encuentra el kit teleconvertidor Oppo Hasselblad para el teleobjetivo de 200 MP. Por el otro, el Tilta Khronos Creator Kit, que incluye un adaptador para el teleconvertidor, un acople con agarradera, un ventilador para refrigeración activa y un adaptador para filtros de 67 milímetros.
Matagigantes con todas las letras
El Oppo Find X10 Pro Max también destaca en los apartados no vinculados con la fotografía y el vídeo, y lo mismo su hermano menor. Los nuevos móviles de la marca son los primeros en llegar al mercado con pantallas BT.2020. Esto significa que cubren un 40 % más de la gama cromática en comparación con el estándar DCI-P3.
El panel del modelo Pro Max es de 6,78 pulgadas, con tasa de refresco adaptativa de hasta 144 Hz y brillo máximo de 3.600 nits. En el caso del Oppo Find X10 estándar, la pantalla es de 6,59 pulgadas y brinda las mismas prestaciones que las del modelo más avanzado.
Bajo el capó, el Oppo Find X10 Pro Max tampoco decepciona. El teléfono llega equipado con un chip MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro de 2 nanómetros, 12 GB de memoria RAM y 512 GB de almacenamiento interno. La batería es de silicio carbono y tiene una capacidad de 7.150 mAh. Soporta carga rápida cableada de hasta 80 vatios e inalámbrica de hasta 50 vatios. Según el fabricante, puede ofrecer hasta 2 días completos de autonomía en uso típico.
El Finx X10 base tiene la misma batería, pero incorpora un chip ligeramente menos avanzado: el MediaTek Dimensity 9600M, de 3 nanómetros. De todos modos, es más que suficiente para ofrecer un desempeño de primer nivel. Además, llega con 12 GB de RAM y 256 o 512 GB de almacenamiento.
Precios de los nuevos Oppo Find X10 y X10 Pro Max
El Oppo Find X10 Pro Max ya se puede comprar en España. Tiene un precio de 1.799 euros para su única opción de 12 GB de RAM y 512 GB de almacenamiento interno. Por su parte, el Oppo Find X10 se consigue a cambio de 1.399 euros (12 + 256 GB) y 1.499 euros (12 + 512 GB).
Oppo está ofreciendo algunos descuentos y beneficios especiales por tiempo limitado. En el caso del Find X10 Pro Max, puedes obtener un regalo valorado en hasta 549 euros si compras antes del 8 de noviembre. Entre las opciones disponibles para elegir están el teleconvertidor, la tablet Oppo Pad Neo y el reloj Oppo Watch X3.
En cuando al Find X10 estándar, Oppo ofrece un descuento directo de 100 euros para el modelo de 512 GB. Esto significa que se puede conseguir por tiempo limitado a cambio de 1.399 euros; es decir, pagando el precio de la versión de 256 GB.

articles.title: Du hast Angst vor einer Beförderung? Dann liegst du voll im „Ladderdodging“-Trend
articles.text:
Nach Quiet Quitting kommt Ladderdodging: Warum Fachkräfte Titel und Führungspositionen meiden
Lange galt die Beförderung für Arbeitnehmer:innen als ultimatives Karriereziel. Das hat sich inzwischen geändert: Immer mehr Menschen lehnen den beruflichen Aufstieg heute bewusst ab. Die Gründe dafür sind vielfältig, oft steht dahinter aber der Wunsch, zusätzlichen Stress zu vermeiden. Für diesen Trend hat Rohit Bhargava, Gründer der Non-Obvious Company, jetzt einen neuen Begriff geschaffen: „Ladderdodging“. Diese Wortneuschöpfung beschreibt Menschen, die das Erklimmen der Karriereleiter lieber meiden.
„Ladderdodging“ als neuer Karrieretrend
In seinem neuen Buch 100 Future Words, das er gemeinsam mit Henry Coutinho-Mason geschrieben hat, definiert Bhargava diesen Trend als „das Ablehnen oder das bewusste Nicht-Anstreben einer Beförderung oder einer Führungsposition, um den zusätzlichen Druck, das Risiko und die Einsamkeit zu vermeiden, die oft mit Führungspositionen einhergehen“. Nicht jeder sei bereit, neben der Arbeit auch die zwischenmenschliche Dynamik der Mitarbeiter:innen zu managen, so Bhargava gegenüber Fast Company.
Für ihr Buch haben er und sein Co-Autor neben „Ladderdodging“ noch 99 weitere Wörter definiert, die in Zukunft eine noch wichtigere Rolle spielen könnten. Laut Bhargava hätten sie diese auf Basis neuer Forschungsergebnisse und Erfahrungsberichte aus der Zusammenarbeit mit Führungskräften aus der Wirtschaft erarbeitet. Das Ziel des neuen Buches sei es, Diskussionen anzuregen. Gleichzeitig wollen die beiden Autoren eine neue Sprache anbieten, um bestehende oder sich abzeichnende Trends zu beschreiben.
Beförderungen verlieren an Attraktivität
Auch in Deutschland ist der „Ladderdodging“-Trend zu beobachten. Laut der Talent-Trends-Studie 2026 der Personalberatung Michael Page nennen nur 18 Prozent der Beschäftigten in Deutschland eine Beförderung als ihr wichtigstes Karriereziel – deutlich weniger als im europäischen Vergleich. Anders sieht es in Südeuropa aus: So nennen zum Beispiel in Portugal 48 Prozent der Befragten eine Beförderung als ihr größtes Ziel. Paradoxerweise geben auch in Deutschland viele an, sich beruflich weiterentwickeln zu wollen. 49 Prozent möchten neue Fähigkeiten erwerben, 44 Prozent wollen sich weiterbilden oder zusätzliche Qualifikationen erlangen. Und 36 Prozent wünschen sich, ihre Expertise im aktuellen Tätigkeitsbereich zu vertiefen.
Warum ist also gerade der berufliche Aufstieg dabei nicht mehr so wichtig? Für viele geht die Rechnung schlichtweg nicht auf: Laut Michael Page würden 65 Prozent der Beschäftigten in Deutschland eine Beförderung samt Gehaltserhöhung ablehnen, wenn ihr Wohlbefinden darunter leidet. Der Titel ist ihnen der zusätzliche Stress also offenbar nicht wert. Michael Baier, Geschäftsführer von Michael Page, sieht deshalb auch die Unternehmen in der Pflicht: „Fachkräfte investieren gezielt in ihre Expertise, nicht in Titel. Dieser Trend prägt den Arbeitsmarkt, und Arbeitgeber:innen müssen ihn ernst nehmen, wenn sie Talente gewinnen und halten wollen. [Sie] sollten ihre Aus- und Weiterbildungsangebote klar sichtbar machen.”
Unternehmen müssen hinter den Trend blicken
Früher war es für viele undenkbar, eine Beförderung abzulehnen. Aktuelle Studien deuten allerdings darauf hin, dass genau das heute zur Norm geworden ist – besonders bei jüngeren Arbeitnehmer:innen. Dem Gefühl, das manche bei einem beängstigenden oder unerwünschten Beförderungsangebot empfinden, einen Namen zu geben, könne sich aber auch auf ihr Verhalten auswirken, so Bhargava. Ähnlich wie beim Quiet Quitting könnten Menschen den Begriff als Vorwand nutzen, um sich dem Trend anzuschließen. Trotzdem sieht auch er die Verantwortung bei den Arbeitgeber:innen. „Kluge Unternehmen sind diejenigen, die ein solches Wort als Hinweis auf einen Trend betrachten”, sagte er gegenüber Fast Company. Sie sollten seiner Meinung nach hinter die Fassade blicken und sich fragen, warum Mitarbeiter:innen einer Beförderung wirklich aus dem Weg gehen.

articles.title: How curiosity took Victoria Abiodun from anatomy to crypto
articles.text:
Growing up in a household steeped in healthcare, Victoria Abiodun’s path seemed predetermined: finish her anatomy degree at the University of Ilorin, Kwara State, northcentral Nigeria, head abroad for medical school, and never look back. As for cryptocurrency? She wanted nothing to do with it, convinced it belonged firmly in the realm of internet scams. But when an ASUU strike collided with the 2020 lockdowns, a persistent anatomy coursemate challenged her prejudice. To make sense of the dense, jargon-laden whitepapers, she began writing her own explanations from scratch. That curiosity set off an unexpected chain reaction: from ghost-writing technical primers as an undergraduate to co-founding a gaming startup, spearheading marketing for a European decentralised identity protocol, and bootstrapping a 100-strong Solana developer chapter in Ilorin. Today, while reading for an MBA at USC and researching high-density energy demand, she is writing the open-access, plain-English blockchain book she wishes she had read on day one. In this week’s My Life in Tech, JOHN ADOYI sits down with Abiodun to trace her accidental journey from anatomy labs to Web3 education.
Victoria Abiodun, a Web3 educator, is writing a book that explains distributed technology in plain language. Only a few years ago, she wanted nothing to do with it.
As an undergraduate at the University of Ilorin in north-central Nigeria, she viewed cryptocurrency as indistinguishable from fraud; the people who evangelised it seemed either to be perpetrating scams or falling victim to them.
One person challenged that conviction: a trusted friend from her anatomy class who spoke incessantly about blockchain. She struggled to reconcile his enthusiasm with the prejudice she held.
“In all honesty, the first thing that piqued my curiosity was the money he was making,” she says. “I was like, ‘What? This is crazy.’”
Yet financial curiosity was merely the entry point. Coming from a pure science background, she struggled to grasp the underlying technical concepts, prompting her to write about them to break them down.
“The goal was simply to teach myself the core concepts,” she says.
That curiosity soon propelled Abiodun beyond writing. She went on to advise blockchain companies, co-found a gaming startup, and establish Superteam Ilorin—a regional community supporting developers and founders deploying on the Solana network. Through those stints, she zeroed in on a question that transcended technical mechanics: how could builders harness the technology to solve acute, real-world problems?
Her forthcoming book is one prong of that mission. Across grassroots community building, technical writing, and her podcast, Abiodun is demystifying an ecosystem she once dismissed.
A medical household
Before encountering Web3, Abiodun had envisioned a healthcare career. Her mother was a nurse, and her elder sister pursued medicine. As a child, she briefly flirted with law because an uncle was an attorney and she thought it looked “pretty cool”, but in a home steeped in clinical practice, medicine exerted the stronger pull.
“I assumed I wanted to be a doctor as well,” she says, “and I simply followed that momentum.”
She enrolled at the University of Ilorin to read anatomy, intending to travel abroad after graduation for medical school or postgraduate training in public health. Technology did not feature in the plan.
“I never imagined I would go into tech,” she says, “nor did I think I was particularly interested in it.”
Yet an entrepreneurial streak was already evident. From her first year on campus, she launched small ventures across different sectors. Some gained traction, others collapsed, but the collective experience sharpened her commercial instincts.
Then the COVID-19 pandemic struck in 2020. With lockdowns compounded by a prolonged academic staff strike that shuttered Nigerian universities, her studies ground to a halt.
Rather than idling, she published an e-book on physical wellness, formed an online fitness community, and explored digital side projects.
Cryptocurrency was still off her radar. Her anatomy classmate, however, continued to evangelise the sector. Because he was already active in technology, regular conversations with him steadily dismantled her scepticism.
“During the lockdown, I immersed myself in reading and research,” she says, “and that was the turning point.”
A family ordeal crystallised the technology’s utility: her elder sister was studying medicine in Ukraine when conflict erupted in 2014, leaving their parents in Nigeria unable to wire tuition or living expenses through severed international banking corridors.
When Abiodun recounted the ordeal, her friend explained how peer-to-peer blockchain settlement could have bypassed legacy banking infrastructure to move capital instantly.
“Seeing the real-world gap this technology bridges made it instantly compelling,” she says.
She began writing essays to synthesise her research. When her classmate reviewed her work, he asked whether she realised that companies paid writers to produce technical blockchain content.
She did not.
Pitching agencies and niche publications, she landed an early commission to author a Q&A-style primer breaking down basic distributed ledger concepts. Between 2020 and 2021, while completing her degree, Abiodun freelanced as a content strategist across Web3 startups, corporate blogs, and trade outlets.
The gaming venture
Blockchain gaming was one of the first things that hooked Abiodun. The logic was simple when her friend explained it: players already spent real money on in-game assets, so why shouldn’t they be able to withdraw their earnings?
In 2021, she got the chance to build in that space. She met a co-founder who wanted to develop a blockchain game, and the idea grew into Sportrex, a gaming ecosystem built around play-to-earn.
The ambition extended beyond a single game. Sportrex was designed to let players track their winnings and rankings through a gaming wallet, while allowing other developers to bring their games onto the platform. The wider vision also included a competitive league system, virtual reality experiences, and a token for the gaming ecosystem.
But Abiodun believed that earning money alone would not keep players interested.
“Play-to-earn is nice, but if the game is not fun for people to play, nobody would want to play the game,” she says.
Blockchain gaming was among the first sub-sectors to capture her attention. The economic rationale was intuitive: if players were already spending hard currency on digital assets, they ought to own them outright and retain the ability to liquidate their earnings.
In 2021, she stepped into an operational role, partnering with a founder to establish Sportrex—a platform designed around play-to-earn dynamics.
The scope soon outgrew a standalone title. Sportrex was architected as an aggregator: players could monitor rewards and global leaderboards via a proprietary wallet, while independent developers could integrate their own games. The roadmap included esports tournaments, virtual reality modules, and a native utility token.
Yet Abiodun remained clear-eyed about the limitations of financial incentives alone.
“Play-to-earn is attractive, but if the gameplay lacks substance, retention plummets,” she says. “Nobody wants to play a game that isn’t enjoyable.”
As marketing lead, she drafted the company’s whitepapers, drove brand strategy, managed community acquisition, and negotiated strategic partnerships. She also spearheaded their presence at the Dubai Blockchain Summit, leading discussions with prospective institutional backers.
The venture crystallised her view that early-stage tech ventures must prioritise speed over flawless execution.
“I believe in putting products out early, letting them break, and iterating in public,” she says. “The industry does not wait for you.”
She stepped down from Sportrex in December 2022, carrying that bias toward rapid deployment into her next engagement.
Building a growth strategy from scratch
After leaving Sportrex, Abiodun joined Matchain, an early-stage project preparing to take its AI-driven decentralised digital identity platform to market.
“When I joined, there was no marketing team; there were just engineers and the founder in Lisbon, Portugal,” she says. “So it was just me, the COO and the founder.”
She helped define Matchain’s market position, customer acquisition strategy, and partnership plans. She also developed onboarding strategies for Match Hub, which brought other companies into the ecosystem, and wrote the company’s website content.
The role drew on skills she had developed as an entrepreneur.
“Most of the core skills that you apply to building your own businesses are skills that people employ others for,” she says.
She also had to understand how differently blockchain companies approach growth. In her experience, blockchain startups often need to build a community before a product is ready to launch.
“If you do not build a community around your product before the product is ready, you probably would not have a community that would adopt the product,” she says.
Abiodun worked with Matchain until 2023. Although she had planned to relocate to Lisbon, Portugal, visa interview availability for Nigerians prevented the move.
She says the company also wanted a team that could work more closely together; she eventually moved on.
Finding community outside Lagos
Her trajectory subsequently pivoted from corporate marketing toward grassroots capacity building. Having helped funded platforms scale, she wanted to mentor the engineers building baseline software.
In 2023, as the global Solana developer network Superteam expanded its international reach, Abiodun saw an opening to anchor a chapter in Ilorin, where she maintained a residence.
She volunteered to establish the regional presence. Though she had intended to take a sabbatical to travel and take up golf, she instead convened Ilorin’s inaugural Superteam meetup in February 2024—despite not considering herself an insider in local engineering circles.
“I was stunned by the initial turnout,” she says. “From that first session, attendance scaled into hundreds every month.”
Her execution led to her formal appointment as lead for Superteam’s Southwest Nigeria operations. Yet sheer attendance was secondary to her core objective: pushing local talent beyond tutorial exercises into shipping functional software.
“Nigeria has an exceptional concentration of technical talent,” she says. “Developers spend thousands of hours mastering complex frameworks, yet we rarely see that skill translated into solutions for local structural bottlenecks.”
Bootstrapping the community required tactical agility. When a venue billing dispute severed ties with the private coding hub hosting their initial sessions, Abiodun restructured operations—securing alternative halls, engaging campus hostels directly, and tapping alumni networks.
She also made pastoral engagement central to her leadership, tracking individual project milestones and providing personal mentorship.
“When people feel genuinely supported, enthusiasm compounds,” she notes. “Engineers kept returning with their peers because they wanted them to experience that collaborative culture.”
Though the compensation was a fraction of her previous commercial contracts, she considers it her most meaningful tenure. “It remains one of the most impactful assignments I have undertaken,” she says. “It was deeply fulfilling.”
Demystifying tech
That educational focus now centres on an introductory book aimed at non-technical founders, students, and corporate professionals.
“When I entered the space, the available literature was dense, forbidding, and cluttered with jargon,” she explains. “I wanted to write something conversational—matching the cadence of how I explain these concepts across a table.”
The manuscript covers core operational mechanics—distributed ledgers, network layering, consensus architecture, and cryptography—while exploring non-financial primitives including supply chain verification and verifiable identity credentials. She intends to publish it as an open-access resource.
Her outreach also includes Convergence, a podcast examining distributed systems, enterprise workflows, and tokenised assets. The series originated from informal discussions with professionals outside the crypto sphere looking to understand how decentralised protocols intersect with their native industries.
Abiodun’s horizons have since expanded toward core infrastructure. Currently reading for a Master of Business Administration (MBA) at the University of Southern California’s Marshall School of Business, she also serves as a graduate research assistant with the school’s Zage Business of Energy Initiative. Her focus on energy was prompted by the steep electrical baseload demands imposed by artificial intelligence clusters and high-density data centres.
The business curriculum has supplemented her operational background with formal training in corporate valuation, asset pricing, and financial modelling.
“Energy systems are not something I would have prioritised had I stayed solely within startup marketing,” she reflects. “Maximising the chance to interrogate these structural challenges has been an exceptional privilege.”
Whether evaluating distributed ledgers or energy transition models, Abiodun remains clear that technology is a mechanism rather than an end in itself.
“Directing my career toward solving problems that tangibly improve other people’s circumstances is what matters most,” she says. “Accolades and bull runs are fleeting; the real reward is knowing you helped clear a pathway for someone else.”
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. articles.title: Panne Orange : le réseau mobile perturbé ce mercredi, de nombreux abonnés privés d’appels et de données
articles.text:
[Mise à jour le 21 octobre à 19h34 : alors que la panne se poursuit en soirée chez certains abonnés, et Orange dit à BFMTV n’avoir à cette heure « aucune visibilité » sur un retour à la normale. Auprès de l’AFP, l’opérateur évoque une panne nationale liée à « un incident », sans plus de précisions. Sur X, Orange invite ses abonnés à se connecter à un réseau Wi-Fi « disponible et sécurisé » pour continuer à accéder à Internet et à communiquer via les applications de messagerie. De notre côté, le réseau 5G vient tout juste de faire son retour.
 Vous rencontrez actuellement des difficultés avec notre réseau mobile.
Dans l’attente du rétablissement du service, nous vous invitons à vous connecter à un réseau Wi-Fi disponible et sécurisé pour continuer à accéder à Internet et à communiquer via vos applications de messagerie et de visioconférence.
Nos équipes techniques restent pleinement mobilisées pour rétablir le service dans les meilleurs délais.
Nous vous présentons nos excuses pour la gêne occasionnée.
— Orange France (@Orange_France) October 21, 2026
Si l’origine de la panne n’est toujours pas officiellement connue, Clément Domingo, alias SaxX, a évoqué dans l’après midi un problème lié à la migration de lignes vers un nouveau cœur de réseau 5G.
 Infos exclusives panne géante Orange en France… “Ce n’est pas un hack”
Il ne s’agit pas d’un piratage on me dit en interne !
Orange introduit un nouveau coeur de reseau mobile (5G). Les lignes qui sont migrées dessus sont a priori Hs.
Pour rappel, depuis 11h ce matin plus de signal sur les mobiles. Des centaines de milliers de personnes et d’entreprises sont impactées…
— SaxX ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ (@_SaxX_) October 21, 2026
Cette hypothèse n’a pas été confirmée par Orange à ce stade.]
[Mise à jour le 21 octobre à 18h04 : la panne se poursuit chez de nombreux abonnés. Une astuce permet toutefois de retrouver appels et SMS sur certains smartphones : nous l’avons testée, voici comment faire.]
[Mise à jour le 21 octobre à 14h15 : après une brève amélioration, la panne a repris de notre côté. Le réseau mobile d’Orange est de nouveau totalement indisponible. Et chez vous, le réseau est-il revenu ? N’hésitez pas à nous le dire en commentaire.]
[Mise à jour le 21 octobre à 13h26 : la panne semble en cours de résolution, et le réseau est de nouveau disponible chez certains abonnés, dont nous à la rédaction.]
Article orignal
Vous êtes un abonné Orange ou Sosh et votre smartphone affiche « Aucun service » ou refuse de se connecter à Internet ? Vous n’êtes a priori pas seul. Depuis 11h30 environ, le réseau mobile d’Orange connaît des perturbations dans plusieurs régions de France. Sur Downdetector, les signalements se sont multipliés pour atteindre près de 11 500 à 11h50, et de nombreux abonnés font part de leurs difficultés sur les réseaux sociaux.
Nous avons nous-mêmes pu constater la panne à la rédaction avec une absence complète de réseau mobile. Il est impossible d’effectuer un appel ou d’utiliser les données mobiles. Orange vient de confirmer l’incident sur X : « Vous pouvez rencontrer actuellement des perturbations sur le réseau mobile Orange. Nos équipes sont pleinement mobilisées pour rétablir le réseau dans les meilleurs délais. Veuillez nous excuser pour la gêne occasionnée ». Pour l’heure, l’opérateur ne précise pas l’origine de la panne ni le délai de rétablissement. Nous mettrons cet article à jour dès que nous en saurons plus.
 Bonjour, vous pouvez rencontrer actuellement des perturbations sur le réseau mobile Orange.
Nos équipes sont pleinement mobilisées pour rétablir le réseau dans les meilleurs délais.
Veuillez nous excuser pour la gêne occasionnée.
— Orange France (@Orange_France) October 21, 2026
Ce n’est pas la première fois que le réseau d’Orange flanche cette année. Le 29 juin dernier, une panne nationale avait déjà privé des milliers d’abonnés Orange et Sosh d’appels et d’Internet mobile dès l’aube, avant un retour à la normale vers 11 heures. Deux jours plus tard, le 1er juillet, une nouvelle vague de perturbations avait touché cette fois les réseaux fixe et mobile.
En attendant, si votre box le permet, les appels Wi-Fi peuvent servir de solution de secours pour téléphoner, à condition que l’option soit activée sur votre smartphone. Pour les appels d’urgence, le 112 reste joignable via le réseau d’un autre opérateur, même sans réseau Orange.
