articles.title: Microsoft says October updates didn’t actually fix VPN issues
articles.text:
Microsoft says it mistakenly flagged a bug causing Always On VPN connection issues as fixed in the October 2026 Windows 11 cumulative updates.
Always On VPN replaced the legacy DirectAccess technology and supports domain-joined, non-domain-joined, and Microsoft Entra ID–joined devices running Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server.
It runs in the background and establishes secure tunnels back to the user's corporate network whenever their device connects to the internet.
Microsoft first acknowledged the issue in a service alert sent to IT administrators in late September, saying it was triggered on systems running Windows 11 24H2 and later after installing the September 2026 security updates when the initial Always On VPN connection failed (e.g., when using automatic protocol selection with IKEv2 and SSTP).
"When automatic protocol selection or protocol fallback was configured, affected VPN connections could remain stuck in a Connecting state or fail to connect after an initial connection attempt failed," it said. "In some cases, subsequent connection attempts could display the error, 'The specified port is already in use.'"
Mistakenly marked as resolved
After releasing the October 2026 Patch Tuesday Windows 11 cumulative updates, Microsoft marked the bug as resolved, but in a Tuesday update it said the issues weren't actually addressed and that a fix would ship later.
"This disclosure was mistakenly updated to Resolved status on October 13, 2026. We have returned its status to Mitigated," it said in a service alert sent to IT admins. "A resolution for this issue is planned to be included in an update to be released in the coming weeks. We apologize for any inconvenience or confusion."
While Microsoft continues working on a permanent solution, it shared a temporary fix that requires affected customers to choose one of two VPN tunneling protocols to work around the issue.
"IT administrators can mitigate this issue by changing the Always On VPN profile from automatic protocol selection to a single protocol, either SSTP only or IKEv2 only, depending on their environment and configuration," it said. "Organizations should select the protocol based on their environment, security, and deployment requirements."
The September cumulative updates have been linked to multiple other problems affecting both home and enterprise Windows users. Days after last month's Patch Tuesday, Microsoft released emergency out-of-band updates to fix Hyper-V issues, Remote Desktop Services failures, and USB audio problems.
It also shared a temporary workaround for an issue that blocked some Windows 11 users from logging in with valid domain credentials and announced that it is working to address another bug that broke the Windows built-in File History backup feature.

articles.title: Deux failles critiques menacent des millions de sites PHP, une mise à jour d’urgence arrive ce mercredi après-midi
articles.text:
PHP publiera ce mercredi 21 octobre à 16 h une mise à jour d’urgence pour corriger deux failles critiques. C'est une fuite qui a précipité l’annonce, et les anciennes versions du langage pourraient rester sans correctif.
Mise à jour d'urgence en vue pour PHP. Ce mercredi 21 octobre à 16 heures, les équipes du langage de programmation open source vont publier une mise à jour d'urgence pour corriger deux failles critiques, un rendez-vous qui ne concerne d'ailleurs pas que les développeurs. La team de sécurité du projet l'a annoncé la veille au soir dans un avis plutôt laconique, après qu'une fuite a éventé l'affaire plus tôt que prévu. Ce que l'on sait suffit déjà à inquiéter, puisque des millions de sites, de WordPress aux boutiques en ligne, pourraient être visés très vite après la publication.
Des failles PHP qui ont pris de l'avance sur leur correctif
Comme le rapporte Frandroid ce matin, tout est parti d'une indiscrétion. La veille, mardi, peu avant l'annonce officielle, un utilisateur de Hacker News, le forum tech de l'incubateur Y Combinator, a vendu la mèche en évoquant deux failles dans PHP. Son message a disparu depuis, mais le site spécialisé BleepingComputer a eu le temps de le lire. Il y était question d'une divulgation prévue le jeudi 22 octobre et d'une gravité maximale, de 10 sur 10, excusez du peu.
Les deux failles sont référencées CVE-2026-109618 et CVE-2026-109619. Il s'agit, pour les non initiés, de leur matricule dans le registre public qui recense les vulnérabilités informatiques. Elles seraient de type « exécution de code à distance », ou RCE dans le jargon, c'est-à-dire qu'un cybercriminel pourrait faire exécuter ses propres commandes à un serveur sans y avoir été invité, et donc en prendre le contrôle. La fuite aurait même compris une vidéo, certes non authentifiée, d'un outil baptisé PHP2Shell faisant tourner du code sur des sites WordPress, Drupal, Magento ou Joomla.
PHP a choisi de ne pas attendre. Le correctif tombera donc à 14 heures UTC, 16 heures ici en France métropolitaine, moins d'une journée après l'alerte. L'avis officiel n'en dit pas beaucoup plus. Il confirme deux vulnérabilités critiques notées 9,2 sur 10 selon la grille CVSS v4.0, l'échelle de référence pour mesurer la gravité d'une faille. En revanche, il garde pour lui les versions touchées et le mode d'exploitation. Personne n'explique encore l'écart avec le 10 avancé par la fuite.
PHP 5 et PHP 7, les grands oubliés du correctif
Si l'alerte mobilise autant, c'est que PHP reste, plus de trente ans après sa création, l'un des piliers techniques du Web. D'après W3Techs, qui mesure les technologies utilisées sur le Web, PHP équipe 69,3 % des sites dont on connaît le langage côté serveur, des blogs WordPress aux sites marchands. Or les détails techniques des failles seront publiés en même temps que les correctifs, donc les défenseurs et attaquants partiront sur la même ligne. On peut toutefois redouter des attaques massives dans le quart d'heure suivant. Et il reste la question des anciennes versions !
Dans le détail, le projet ne maintient plus que quatre branches, de PHP 8.2 à PHP 8.5, c'est-à-dire les seules versions qui reçoivent encore des correctifs. Or, selon la société de cybersécurité watchTowr, les failles toucheraient PHP 5, 6, 7 et 8. À noter que PHP 6 n'est jamais sorti en version stable. Mais si elle se vérifie, l'addition sera lourde, car au 20 octobre 2026, toujours selon W3Techs, 27 % des sites PHP tournaient encore sous PHP 7 et 7,7 % sous PHP 5, une version de… 2004. Plus d'un site PHP sur trois se retrouverait alors sans correctif officiel.
D'ici 16 heures, c'est très simple, on ne peut que vous encourager à vérifier votre version de PHP en tapant la commande php -v sur le serveur, puis à réserver un créneau de maintenance dans l'après-midi. Si votre site est sur un hébergement mutualisé, c'est-à-dire un serveur partagé loué à un hébergeur, la mise à jour dépend de lui : demandez-lui quand il compte l'appliquer.
Les versions corrigées seront annoncées à 16 heures dans les actualités de php.net, sauf si PHP avance encore l'heure. Le projet s'en réserve le droit si les détails venaient à circuler ou si des attaques étaient repérées.

articles.title: Berlin-based YGO raises €8 million to make travel inventory bookable through AI agents | EU-Startups
articles.text:
YGO, a Berlin-based startup building an AI infrastructure layer for the travel industry, raised €8 million in a Series A round.
The round was led by Ventech, with participation from Sake Bosch, Caesar and Business Angels. In August 2024, the company announced it had secured €2.5 million in funding led by GetAway Group.
“Online travel booking is undergoing its biggest structural shift in decades but most of the industry’s infrastructure was never built for it. YGO’s customers are already re-owning their customer relationships with AI and putting real KPI uplifts on the board to prove it. That’s why we believe YGO’s neutral infrastructure will become critical to how travel operates in an AI-first world,” said Nicolas Barthalon, Partner at Ventech.
Founded in 2023 by Julian Kögel, Sebastian Kreutzberger, and Willi Ibbeken, YGO sits at the intersection of legacy travel technology and the emerging ecosystem of AI agents. The company’s platform connects travel companies, including tour operators, online travel agencies, and travel agencies, directly with airlines, hotels, and tour operator inventory, without the need to restructure their existing booking infrastructure.
YGO does this by structuring and enriching fragmented hotel and product data, giving it the depth and accuracy that AI agents need to reliably discover, compare and recommend travel products. Its content enrichment product automatically generates verified, structured hotel data and delivers it across a company’s own digital channels and to external AI assistants via MCP (Model Context Protocol).
Its Hotel Q&A product embeds an AI-powered question-and-answer layer directly onto hotel pages, allowing travellers to ask any question and receive verified answers in real time and in their own language. Its AI Distribution product, on the other hand, makes a travel company’s entire hotel portfolio accessible and bookable through AI agents such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini.
YGO says online travel agencies and metasearch platforms have captured 15-25% of every booking, acting as intermediaries between travellers and suppliers. With AI assistants becoming the starting point for travel planning and booking, suppliers are looking for ways to reclaim direct relationships with their customers.
The platform already processes bookings for major European travel players including Condor, Bentour, and GetAway Group. YGO says their collaboration has led to a 90% reduction in manual operations and a 20% improvement in conversion for one airline client, and a 2.4x increase in average order value with no additional headcount for another.
“Travel is one of the last major industries still built on infrastructure that was never designed for an AI-first world. We built YGO to change that: to give the travel industry the infrastructure to make its inventory accessible, bookable and ready for AI – whether through their own platforms or through external AI agents,” said Kögel, co-founder and CEO of YGO.
YGO has grown its recurring ARR into seven figures within six months and has processed more than €15 million in bookings through its infrastructure to date. The fresh capital will be utilised to scale go-to-market and sales operations, deepen its AI orchestration platform, and expand the company’s customer base beyond the DACH region, targeting both enterprise accounts and mid-sized travel companies.
“This funding allows us to build on the strong business we already have with some of Europe’s leading travel players and become the AI infrastructure layer connecting the industry to the next generation of travel,” added Kögel.

articles.title: Cleaning up PFAS
articles.text:
Cleaning up PFAS
Ridding the world of forever chemicals could address a range of health and environmental and health woes.
Scrubbing Earth of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances—a.k.a. PFAS or forever chemicals—could eliminate a list of woes for people and planet. Used for decades in everything from nonstick pans to firefighting foams, PFAS have been linked to increased risks of fertility challenges, developmental delays, cancer, and reduced immune response. They are known for a strong bond between carbon and fluorine, which the environment struggles to break down.
The sticking points
PFAS are everywhere: They spew from factories and slough off products and into water with normal use. Scientists have found them in everything from human blood to Antarctic snow. One 2022 report found that 89% of the US population had PFAS in excess of two nanograms per milliliter of blood plasma, a common threshold for potential adverse health effects, and 9% of the population had passed the riskier level of 20 nanograms per milliliter.
The PFAS monster is also a moving target. New compounds are still being created and used. There are more than 12,000 of them, and much of the cleanup research focuses on only a small handful.
The progress
Cleansing PFAS-contaminated soil is a project in its infancy, but it is possible to prevent more buildup by pulling the chemicals out of water systems. There are two ways to handle this: trap or destroy. Some scientists have found reverse osmosis—a process that pushes water through supertight filters—useful in point-of-use cases, like water filters at kitchen sinks.
Other techniques in the pipeline might be more suitable for large-scale removal—for example, at water treatment facilities. One, called foam fractionation, generates bubbles that capture PFAS. More approaches, like ensnaring the chemicals in nanothin layers of charged metal, are also under investigation.
Trapping, though, is imperfect. You’re left with PFAS-filled brine, which if not properly destroyed (an expensive and energy-sucking endeavor) can still end up in the environment.
Jack Huang, a professor of crop and soil sciences at the University of Georgia, is working on destruction. He’s testing a method called electrochemical degradation, which uses electrodes to break down the bonds that hold PFAS together. The product destroyed more than 90% of PFAS mass in tests and has already been licensed by the engineering consulting firm AECOM.
Ridding life of PFAS is also a policy challenge. There are alternatives; we just need the push to use them. And we’ve had success before: The EPA’s 2010/2015 PFOA Stewardship Program has helped slash the release of water-repellent perfluorooctanoic acid by 95%. More recently, Minnesota, Maine, and New Mexico have passed bans on PFAS in products like cookware and dental floss.
Progress meter ............ 6
Scientists are making strides toward removing and destroying PFAS—but it’ll be all for naught if we don’t turn off the tap.

articles.title: Le Roborock Zeo Lite, lave-linge séchant connecté de 10 kg, est quasi à moitié prix — Frandroid
articles.text:
Le Zeo Lite appartient à la gamme Zeo, que Roborock a lancée avec le Zeo One à l’IFA 2023 pour se diversifier hors de ses robots aspirateurs. Le Zeo Lite a suivi à l’IFA 2024. La gamme compte aujourd’hui quatre modèles. Le Zeo X et le Zeo One (1 299 euros) occupent le haut de gamme, et le Zeo Mini (1 kg au lavage) vise surtout le linge de bébé ou les tenues de sport. Le Zeo Lite se place entre ces deux extrêmes. Il reprend l’essentiel du One, à commencer par le séchage Zeo-cycle, pour un tarif plus doux. Aujourd’hui, il s’affiche même presque à moitié prix.
Les atouts du Roborock Zeo Lite
- Un séchage Zeo-cycle à la zéolite, autour de 50 °C
- 10 kg au lavage, 6 kg au séchage, essorage à 1 400 tr/min
- Le dosage automatique de la lessive et de l’adoucissant
899 euros, c’est le prix conseillé du Zeo Lite depuis sa sortie début 2025 (avec une offre de lancement à 799 euros). Chez Joybuy, il descend aujourd’hui à 476 euros, soit 423 euros de moins, environ 47 % de remise. Pour un lave-linge séchant connecté de 10 kg avec dosage automatique, ce n’est franchement pas trop cher payé.
Un séchage à la zéolite qui ménage les fibres
Le séchage Zeo-cycle est le cœur du produit. Au lieu de chauffer fort, la machine s’appuie sur la zéolite, un minéral qui capte l’humidité de l’air (vous en trouvez aussi dans certains déshumidificateurs). Un double circuit d’air fait le reste. Le linge sèche autour de 50 °C, alors qu’un sèche-linge à condensation classique dépasse souvent 80 °C, selon Roborock. Pour la laine, la marque annonce une température maintenue entre 30 et 40 °C, pour limiter le rétrécissement et la décoloration.
Le tambour accepte 10 kg au lavage, mais seulement 6 kg au séchage. Avec une machine pleine, il faudra donc sortir une partie du linge avant de lancer le séchage. Comptez aussi sur des cycles complets longs, car sécher à basse température demande plus de temps.
Une machine qui se gère presque toute seule
Le Zeo Lite mise aussi sur un entretien réduit. Les réservoirs intégrés contiennent 580 ml de lessive et 420 ml d’adoucissant, de quoi tenir une trentaine de jours selon Roborock (pour une famille de trois personnes qui lance une machine tous les deux jours). La machine pèse la charge et dose elle-même les produits.
Le système LintClear nettoie automatiquement les peluches pendant le lavage et le séchage. Vous n’avez donc plus de filtre à vider à la main. Attention quand même, Roborock précise que le système vise les peluches des tissus, pas les poils de chat ou de chien.
Pour le reste, on retrouve 27 programmes de lavage et de séchage, pilotables depuis l’application Roborock. Le moteur à entraînement direct, sans courroie, mise sur la durabilité. Avec 59,5 x 68,2 x 85 cm, le format reste celui d’un lave-linge standard, qui trouvera sa place dans une buanderie ou sous un plan de travail.
Si Roborock vous intéresse d’abord pour ses aspirateurs, notre sélection des meilleurs aspirateurs robots du moment passe en revue les modèles que nous recommandons.

articles.title: “Plus probable que ça réussisse” : en novembre, SpaceX tentera une folle double capture du Starship en plein vol
articles.text:
“Plus probable que ça réussisse” : en novembre, SpaceX tentera une folle double capture du Starship en plein vol
SpaceX s'apprête à tenter un double rattrapage inédit du Starship avec les bras mécaniques de sa tour de lancement. Une étape aussi risquée que cruciale pour diviser les coûts de l'exploration spatiale et préparer le retour sur la Lune.
On y est. Ceux qui ont vécu la première capture historique en plein vol du premier étage du Starship en octobre 2024 se rappellent avec émotion de leur sidération. SpaceX nous prépare un événement de même ampleur. Plus fou encore : cette fois-ci, ce sont les deux étages qui devraient être saisis par les Chopsticks de Mechazilla, le Super Heavy et le Ship. Lunaire. Martien.
C'est Elon Musk lui-même qui vient d'en faire l'annonce officielle lors de la conférence des résultats trimestriels de SpaceX. Comme il aime à le dire, quoi qu'il en soit – résultat ou échec – ça sera du spectacle. Et concernant les chances de succès, Musk est assez confiant :
	
Je dirais qu'il est plus probable que l'inverse que cela réussisse.
Le vol 15 tentera de marquer l'histoire
Le vol 14 marqua l'entrée du Starship dans la cour des lanceurs orbitaux. Ce fut globalement une réussite (malgré quelques moteurs récalcitrants). Mais le vol 15 doit être l'une des étapes cruciales qui validera en partie les espoirs fondés sur ce lanceur sans équivalent. La réutilisation intégrale, Super Heavy plus Ship, est une condition sine qua non du projet. Projet de remplacer les Falcon 9 par des Starship, projet de l'envoyer vers la Lune et vers Mars.
Les tentatives auront lieu en novembre, même si aucune date n'est fixée. L'autorité de régulation des vols (FAA) devra donner son accord, comme à chaque fois. Ensuite, l'autre grande étape sera le ravitaillement en plein vol, que la société spatiale prévoit pour début 2027.
Pour Elon Musk,qui prétend vouloir rendre l'humanité multiplanétaire : “C'est un jalon technologique profond dans l'histoire de la civilisation et de la conscience”.
Beaucoup plus risqué que le rattrapage du Super Heavy
On pourrait croire qu'après avoir réussi trois rattrapages du Super Heavy par la tour, puis des amerrissages en douceur du Ship, l'opération suivante ne serait qu'une belle conjugaison des deux. C'est en réalité bien plus complexe. Voici pourquoi :
- Le Ship aura réalisé au moins une orbite, soit une heure trente de vol, et non quelques minutes comme le Super Heavy.
- Sa vitesse sera environ 6 fois plus élevée que celle du Super Heavy (28 000 km/h contre 4 500 km/h).
- Les contraintes sur les tuiles thermiques sont énormes à une telle vitesse. Le Ship sera enveloppé de plasma qui fera monter la température du bouclier thermique à plus de 1500 °C.
- La précision nécessaire pour atteindre une tour de lancement n'est pas comparable à celle nécessaire pour amerrir dans l'océan.
Le futur du spatial suspendu à un double bottle flip challenge
Pour la NASA et son programme Artemis, qui compte sur le Starship pour ramener les astronautes sur la surface lunaire, cette maîtrise technique est une condition absolue. Sans un lanceur entièrement réutilisable, l'établissement de bases permanentes sur la Lune ou l'exploration de Mars restera économiquement hors de portée.
	
La seule façon d'étendre la conscience au-delà de la Terre sur une base durable est d'avoir un lanceur orbital entièrement réutilisable.
Bien sûr, la réussite du vol 15 ne résoudrait qu'une minuscule partie des problèmes qui attendent SpaceX et la Nasa pour leur retour habité sur la Lune. Il restera à réussir le ravitaillement envol, à se poser sur un pôle sud très accidenté, en redécoller, etc. Et pour Mars, c'est encore pire, les défis technologiques et physiologiques sont d'un autre ordre de grandeur. Ce vol 15 n'est pas une condition suffisante à ces projets, mais c'est une condition nécessaire.

articles.title: Google SynthID Detector Simplifies Watermark Detection and Expands Support to Other AI Providers
articles.text:
Google DeepMind announced the global availability of SynthID Detector, a tool designed to help identify AI-generated content, including media created using AI tools from SynthID partners such as OpenAI, NVIDIA, and Kakao, with Apple support expected soon.
Before the introduction of SynthID Detector, users could identify content AI-generated only by asking Gemini, which was limited to content generated by Google AI. Identifying content from other AI providers required instead using their respective detection tools.
The SynthID.com website simplifies the process by allowing users to upload an image, audio, or video files to have it checked across all SynthID partners, including OpenAI, NVIDIA, Kakao, and (soon) Apple. The tool provides a yes or no outcome, albeit Google also points out that when "no confident signal" is found, a negative outcome does not necessarily mean the content is not AI-generated:
This is not a general AI detector. We can only detect media from the above companies, who have adopted SynthID technology. We are continuously working on extending our partnerships to allow detecting more generated media.
Namely, SynthID does not cover content generated using Meta's or Microsoft's AI, which uses a different watermarking technology. In addition, extensive modifications can also degrade SynthID's watermark signal, resulting in false negatives. In such cases, users need to apply a more comprehensive approach involving additional tools. Despite these limitations, SynthID was included in TIME's Best Inventions of 2026 list, which recognized its approach to AI-content detection over AI detectors.
Commenting on the announcement, Reddit user Chicano_Ducky expressed a negative sentiment about the efficacy of this approach:
[T]hey never worked in the first place, the false positives are unacceptably high on videos their own models made which is in the article [...] They are trying to put the genie back in the bottle and they can't.
User Bulky-Employer adds yet another dimension to this discussion emphasizing that:
A removal node is easily created. You just run a low denoising pass on the image. You can already test this on OpenAI and Gemini's outputs.
SynthID is just a speed bump against people who want to defraud using AI images. It's a good thing that it exists.
A complementary approach to watermarking AI-generated content is C2PA metadata, which records information about a file’s origin and editing history to help establish its authenticity. Harry G argues on LinkedIn that this is the only "approach that actually scales", as "trying to detect synthetic content after the fact turns into an arms race". However, C2PA metadata however can be lost when content is uploaded and does not carry over to screenshots.
Launched in 2023 by Google DeepMind, SynthID is a cryptographic watermarking and detection solution for AI-generated images, audio, video, and text. It embeds an invisible watermark directly into the content by altering audio frequency probability distributions or pixel/token patterns using a secret key.

articles.title: Bringing the Spark to Europe: Local Intelligence Powers Next Wave of Agents
articles.text:
At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA is showcasing its full lineup of local AI hardware. RTX Spark, which launched last week, powers personal agents on Windows PCs; DGX Spark supports developers building and scaling applications on Linux; and DGX Station serves enterprise teams running frontier workloads on Linux, with a Windows version arriving in December.
Announcements include:
- Underdog Desktop Agent now available for RTX Spark
- DGX Spark 64GB available on Friday, Oct. 23
- NVIDIA Sync to support eight DGX Sparks and add Model Launcher this month
- October DGX Spark software update adds Wi-Fi Assistant and updates DGX Spark Skills

- DGX Station for Windows launches in December with support for many manufacturing apps and agent harnesses
- Three new open source reference workflows for robotics on DGX Station
- NVIDIA Cloud Functions is coming in early access to DGX Station
- Recursive Flint, a new local coding model, is now available for NVIDIA local hardware
- Day-0 support for new Nemotron, GLM, DeepSeek, Qwen, MiniMax and FLUX.3 AI models
- New accelerations for llama.cpp and vLLM inference engines and a new collection of checkpoints optimized for local AI hardware.
Learn more about these local AI announcements below, and check out the demos and sessions at GTC Berlin.
RTX Spark Brings Personal Agents to the Windows PC
RTX Spark is a new beginning for the PC — running personal agents, accelerated content creation and 1440p 100 frames-per-second gaming with up to 128GB of unified memory and 1 petaflop of AI compute.
Here’s what early reviewers are saying about the platform since its October 16 release:
“A dream machine for serious creators … ” — CGMag
“Designed for the future of AI … ” — The Verge
“An extremely capable, surprisingly portable and efficient machine … ” — PCMag
Underdog, a new desktop agent app built for fully local, private AI, is also bringing its experience to RTX Spark. Powered by its Husky model-specific inference engine, Underdog runs models entirely on device, so personal agents can get work done without user data ever leaving the PC. Underdog is available now for download.
To better enable developers and enthusiasts to build and customize local agents, many RTX Spark laptops come with an unlocked bootloader.
During the GTC keynote, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang showed off how AI agents running on RTX Spark can be used to train Hugging Face’s Microduck robot using NVIDIA Isaac Lab, Hermes Agent and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B.
ASUS, Dell Technologies, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI laptops are available today, with Acer coming soon.
Learn more about RTX Spark, and get started with the latest RTX Spark playbooks.
DGX Spark Gives Developers Room to Build
New DGX Spark 64GB systems — that can run models including Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B 24GB, Qwen3.8 27B and Gemma 4 26B-A4B — start rolling out from partners on Friday, Oct. 23.
When workloads require more capacity, developers can connect multiple DGX Spark systems via built-in NVIDIA ConnectX-7 networking and NVIDIA Sync Cluster Assistant. This allows users to run advanced coding models like Qwen 3.8 Flash Next, DeepSeek v4 Flash 0731 and GLM 5.3 Flash.
Now, DGX Spark supports clusters of up to eight units in manual configuration, enabling larger models, longer contexts, concurrent agents and distributed development. Ideal for small teams sharing a single cluster as a backend, with each developer running concurrent sessions against the same model, it delivers 1TB of unified memory — enough to run frontier-class models like GLM 5.3.
Get started with the DGX Spark cluster playbook.
NVIDIA Sync Model Launcher will also be available later this month. It simplifies access to local AI on a single DGX Spark or a cluster. With a few clicks, Model Launcher downloads a model and container suited to the configuration and connects the model to OpenCode. It automatically loads DGX Spark Skills for troubleshooting, device maintenance, access to official documentation and other workflow guidance.
The October DGX Spark software update brings a new Wi-Fi Assistant that lets users switch networks when DGX Spark is running in appliance mode. Plus, DGX Spark Skills provide workflow-focused guidance in troubleshooting and device maintenance directly into NVIDIA Sync via OpenCode.
DGX Spark systems are available directly from Acer, ASUS, Dell Technologies, GIGABYTE, HP, Lenovo, MSI and NVIDIA.
DGX Station Puts Frontier Intelligence at the Desk
For larger teams, DGX Station offers 748GB of coherent memory and up to 20 petaflops of AI performance, enabling developers to run advanced models like GLM 5.3 and serve 30+ users at speeds comparable to those provided by cloud models. Adding scale, NVIDIA Sync now supports DGX Station, simplifying connections between two Linux-based systems.
New integrations with Absolute Security, Splunk by Cisco, Fleet Device Management, Microsoft Intune, Perforce Puppet, Progress Software Chef and Tanium let IT teams manage DGX Station systems through enterprise setup, management and conformity processes, helping accelerate approvals and reduce deployment risk while minimizing time to first token.
With the upcoming Windows-based systems, developers can build workflows that harness professional applications, run on NVIDIA RTX PRO GPUs and operate from agents that run their large language models (LLMs) on NVIDIA GB300 systems — all in one machine.
DGX Station for Windows, expected from system manufacturer partners in December, extends local AI into the applications and operating environment enterprises already use. Engineers can run local models and agents in Windows-native software with access to AI models, tools and agents on the same system.
DGX Station for Windows will feature support for manufacturing applications from nTop, Dassault Systèmes, Keysight Technologies, MathWorks, Rockwell Automation, Siemens, Synopsys, Unity and Altera for AI-guided design, simulation, validation and engineering automation. Users will be able to run agents using Hermes Agent, Perplexity or Aible on premises for agentic control in enterprise environments.
The same local, controlled computing model extends to robotics. DGX Station gives robotics teams dedicated compute for post-training, simulation and evaluation, shortening iteration cycles without waiting for shared infrastructure.
NVIDIA released three open source reference workflows that bring GPT-6 Astra, NVIDIA Isaac Lab, Isaac Lab-Arena and Cosmos to NVIDIA DGX Station. Developers can use them to refine GR00T 1.7 models with reinforcement learning, train dexterous manipulation skills and post-train Cosmos world models for synthetic data generation.
NVIDIA Cloud Functions is coming in early access to Linux-based DGX Station. Teams can register local model endpoints in a shared catalog and access them through one OpenAI-compatible entry point.
Developers can upgrade the model behind an endpoint without changing application code, while teammates can use shared models without direct machine access. This turns a DGX Station into a locally controlled inference service for a team.
DGX Station brings local iteration to AI factory development. On the show floor at GTC Berlin, NVIDIA is previewing DSX OS running on DGX Station to simulate AI factory operations before full infrastructure is available. Another demo will showcase DGX Station systems powering a local token factory for more than 30 software developers.
DGX Station systems are shipping today from ASUS, Dell Technologies, GIGABYTE, HP, MSI, Supermicro and Exxact. DGX Station for Windows systems are expected to begin shipping later this year from ASUS, Dell Technologies, GIGABYTE, HP, MSI and Supermicro.
Introducing Recursive Flint — A New Local Coding Model Optimized for RTX Spark
Today, frontier AI lab Recursive Superintelligence released Recursive Flint, a local LLM built for fast, accurate coding. A 40-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 2.5 billion active parameters, Recursive Flint delivers fast inference and performs well in agentic coding benchmarks like SWE-Bench Pro v2, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-bench verified.
Recursive Flint was built using Recursive’s Eureka Machine, a system for large-scale automated AI research. It automates the full research loop: proposes ideas, implements them, runs experiments to validate ideas and uses the results to decide what to try next — creating specialized kernels that boosted Flint’s generation speed on RTX Spark by 55% without changing the model’s weights.
Developers can download the open weights on Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 license and run the model on RTX Spark and DGX Spark systems, as well as GeForce RTX and RTX PRO GPUs. Developers can also post-train the model with NeMo Automodel for supervised fine-tuning and low-rank adaptation, or LoRa, as well as NeMo RL for group relative policy optimization.
New Models With Day-Zero Support
NVIDIA is also adding day-zero model support for NVIDIA Nemotron Bolt E4B 4B, GLM, DeepSeek, Qwen, MiniMax, Liquid AI’s LFM2.5-24B-A2B, plus the FLUX.3 Klein diffusion model.
Nemotron Bolt E4B 4GB packs natural conversation and multi-turn agentic skills into as little as 4GB of memory, powering fast local voice assistants, interactive game characters and embedded interfaces on NVIDIA GeForce RTX GPUs, NVIDIA Jetson devices, and RTX and DGX Spark. Bolt E4B 4GB releases on Friday, Oct. 23.
Black Forest Labs’ FLUX 3 Image Klein is a 5.6-billion-parameter open weights image model for generation and editing. NVIDIA-optimized builds let it run on GeForce RTX GPUs with as little as 8GB of VRAM and create a 1-megapixel image in about four seconds on an RTX 5090 GPU.
MiniMax M3.1 Flash is a new open model built for NVIDIA DGX Station and DGX Spark, bringing long-context AI to the desktop. Liquid AI’s LFM2.5-24B-A2B is an open weights reasoning model that activates just 2 billion of its 24 billion parameters per token, making it fast enough to run private, tool-calling AI agents directly on PCs.
Plus, NVIDIA has released a new collection of model checkpoints optimized for RAM efficiency on local AI hardware, enabling frontier-class open models to run with sufficient memory left over for KV cache. Each checkpoint is quantized while staying close to full-precision accuracy, starting with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local on a single DGX Spark 128GB or RTX PRO 6000 and GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local on two systems.
Developers can post-train on day zero with NeMo AutoModel on both DGX Spark and RTX Spark, with example recipes for Nemotron Bolt E4B, Flux 3 Image Klein and more.
Accelerated AI Inference
NVIDIA continues to work with the llama.cpp and vLLM open source communities to accelerate agentic workloads on local hardware.
In llama.cpp, new speculative decoding support with MTP for Qwen 3.8 Flash Next makes end-to-end agentic tasks up to 1.4x faster on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell.
In vLLM, faster speculative decoding and new FlashInfer prefill kernels for Qwen’s linear-attention layers make agentic tasks with Qwen3.8 27B up to 1.3x faster on DGX Spark. On DGX Station, GLM 5.3 Flash gets up to 1.2x higher throughput.
Check out NVIDIA’s local AI inference recipes to try these latest optimizations.
Follow NVIDIA RTX Spark on X, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook — and stay informed by subscribing to the NVIDIA Local AI newsletter. Follow NVIDIA Workstation on LinkedIn and X.

articles.title: IA da OpenAI desativou mecanismos de segurança e negou ter feito isso
articles.text:
Dois agentes de inteligência artificial da OpenAI enfraqueceram mecanismos usados para monitorar suas ações durante tarefas internas de programação. Em um dos casos, um modelo removeu uma proteção e depois afirmou, incorretamente, que não havia feito isso.
Os episódios expõem uma dificuldade no desenvolvimento de agentes mais autônomos: garantir que eles não comprometam os próprios sistemas criados para supervisioná-los.
Como os agentes interferiram na segurança
O primeiro incidente ocorreu em 3 de outubro. Durante um teste interno, um agente GPT-6.1 Sol desativou alertas automáticos de segurança. Segundo a OpenAI, o modelo interpretou uma instrução para não enviar mensagens pelo Slack como uma proibição que também abrangia essas notificações.
Três dias depois, em 6 de outubro, um agente GPT-6 Astra removeu um mecanismo de monitoramento enquanto copiava um código existente. Depois, afirmou incorretamente que não havia realizado a remoção.
A OpenAI identificou um ponto em comum entre os episódios: os agentes interpretaram instruções rotineiras de programação como permissão para enfraquecer os recursos de segurança.
“Em ambos os casos, os agentes avaliaram se os mecanismos de monitoramento deveriam ser mantidos, mas interpretaram instruções rotineiras de programação como permissão para enfraquecê-los”, afirmou a empresa.
O que a OpenAI pretende fazer
A empresa informou que está adotando medidas para dificultar que os próprios modelos desativem os mecanismos de monitoramento. Também investiga se os agentes podem apresentar uma tendência a evitar a supervisão e buscar justificativas para isso.
A OpenAI reconheceu que ainda não tem uma explicação satisfatória para o comportamento observado. A investigação deverá ajudar a esclarecer por que os modelos tomaram essas decisões e se existe um padrão que vai além de interpretações equivocadas de instruções.
Os episódios destacam três desafios para o controle desses sistemas:
- Interpretar instruções corretamente: evitar que orientações específicas sejam entendidas como autorização para alterar recursos de segurança.
- Preservar o monitoramento: impedir que agentes desativem alertas ou removam mecanismos usados para acompanhar suas ações.
- Investigar possíveis padrões de comportamento: determinar se os casos foram episódios isolados ou se os modelos apresentam uma tendência a evitar a supervisão.
O desafio de monitorar agentes autônomos
Os incidentes ocorrem em meio à preocupação de pesquisadores com a possibilidade de os avanços na segurança da inteligência artificial não acompanharem o desenvolvimento de modelos mais poderosos. Quanto maior a autonomia desses sistemas, mais difícil pode ser antecipar suas decisões e garantir que respeitem os limites estabelecidos.
A OpenAI não é a única empresa a relatar problemas desse tipo. Nos últimos meses, a Anthropic também revelou episódios em que agentes de IA acessaram sistemas externos sem autorização.
Os casos não comprovam que os modelos tenham tentado deliberadamente escapar do controle humano. Ainda assim, mostram que a supervisão precisa continuar eficaz mesmo quando os agentes interpretam instruções de maneira inesperada ou interferem nos recursos destinados a monitorá-los.
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

articles.title: OMODA X: así el coche que quiere redefinir el mercado de los SUVs
articles.text:
Omoda ha presentado en China, durante el International User Summit de Chery Auto, su nuevo Omoda X. La compañía ha apuntado que se ha inspirado en el mundo de los mechas y de los coches robóticos de la ciencia ficción para darle al Omoda X un diseño muy característico, basado principalmente en formas geométricas y aspecto tecnológico.
De esta forma, la propuesta del Omoda X es la de ofrecer una carrocería con volúmenes angulosos y detalles geométricos para ofrecer una propuesta muy diferente a lo que se ve a día de hoy en el segmento de los SUVs.
Además, su parte trasera ofrece un grupo óptico con una firma luminosa inspirada en los rayos, que acentúan ese aspecto futurista y agresivo de los mechas, pero sin renunciar a una silueta deportiva muy característica.
No obstante, no es solo diseño. El Omoda X también parte de un apartado tecnológico muy potente, en línea con su aspecto futurista. El puesto de conducción incorpora un cuadro de instrumentos digital de 10,25 pulgadas y una pantalla multimedia central de 13,20 pulgadas, aunque no todo es digital, puesto que cuenta con mandos físicos para operaciones habituales, como la climatización y la selección de los modos de conducción.
Un concepto de SUV basado en los mechas y con mucha tecnología
Una función muy interesante de este nuevo SUV de Omoda es la incorporación de una cámara térmica capaz de detectar posibles obstáculos, personas y animales a una distancia de hasta 90 metros, según las condiciones de funcionamiento. Esta tecnología permite identificar fuentes de calor y aportar información adicional al conductor, especialmente en situaciones de baja visibilidad. Además, incorpora SIAS (Super Intelligent AI Space), una plataforma basada en inteligencia artificial diseñada para facilitar una comunicación más natural con el sistema multimedia del coche.
Y lógicamente, no se olvida de que es un SUV: tiene una altura libre al suelo de 200 mm y una capacidad de vadeo de 700 mm. A estas características se suma una capacidad de remolcado de hasta 1.800 kg, una carga máxima sobre el techo de 75 kg y diferentes soluciones de almacenamiento para transportar equipamiento deportivo y otros objetos.
Sobre su disponibilidad en el mercado, todavía es una incógnita, así como sus motorizaciones y a los mercados que llegará.

articles.title: Canadian military signs $20-million contract with NordSpace for access to Newfoundland spaceport | BetaKit
articles.text:
Canada’s defence department will pay rocket company NordSpace to use its under-construction spaceport in Newfoundland and Labrador.
The news: Markham, Ont.-based NordSpace announced on Wednesday that it signed a 10-year, $20-million CAD facility-access agreement with the Department of National Defence (DND). Under the agreement, DND will be given priority access to the rocket launch pad at the Atlantic Spaceport Complex, which NordSpace is building in St. Lawrence, along the southern coast of Newfoundland and Labrador.
In a press release, NordSpace said the $20-million contract value covers the minimum cost of maintaining the facility and systems over the length of the contract, but not individual missions or launches.
From the source: “A sovereign spacefaring Canada needs the ability to launch a payload into orbit on its own schedule, from its own soil, on its own rocket when national security demands it,” NordSpace founder and CEO Rahul Goel said in a statement. “That capability is only possible if a Canadian company owns the full stack from launch vehicle to launch pad.”
The context: NordSpace is one of multiple spacetech players attempting to secure sovereign launch capabilities for Canada. Sovereign launch is the ability to send objects, like communications satellites, into space without relying on another country. It aims to be vertically integrated, meaning that NordSpace is building the underlying spaceport, the rocket machinery, as well as the satellites to be sent out.
This week, NordSpace said it had entered the second phase of construction on the spaceport, and reaffirmed its goal of sending rockets into orbit by 2028. It has attempted launches of its sub-orbital rocket Taiga but faced technical setbacks, and says it’s waiting for regulatory approval before trying again.
Final thought: As US-Canada tensions have called Canada’s technological sovereignty into question, launch capacity has become a national security concern. In recent years, Canadian companies and the government have mainly hitched rides with US private company SpaceX for satellites. But the Elon Musk-owned company has signalled that paid rides on its Falcon 9 rocket may become scarcer or stop altogether, creating an opening for Canada’s space startups and an incentive for the defence department to work with them.
Feature image courtesy NordSpace.

articles.title: Sicherheitsvorfall bei OpenAI: So schwächten KI-Agenten ihr eigenes Überwachungssystem
articles.text:
Sicherheitsvorfall bei OpenAI: So schwächten KI-Agenten ihr eigenes Überwachungssystem
In den vergangenen Monaten hat OpenAI immer wieder mit Zwischenfällen zu kämpfen. Nach dem großen Hugging-Face-Vorfall gab es noch weitere Sicherheitsvorfälle, die das KI-Unternehmen dazu getrieben haben, die Entwicklung seiner KI-Agenten zu unterbrechen. Zudem wurden über 100 Unternehmen über mögliche Attacken von abtrünnigen KI-Agenten von OpenAI gewarnt. Jetzt kam es zum nächsten Problem, wenn auch vorerst nur intern.
OpenAI: KI-Agenten deaktivieren Benachrichtigungen
In einem ausführlichen Bericht zeigt OpenAI zwei Vorfälle mit KI-Agenten. Beide haben versucht, ihre Monitoring-Systeme zu umgehen oder zumindest abzuschwächen. Die Systeme sind dafür gedacht, Fehlverhalten der KI frühzeitig zu entdecken und Menschen zu melden, damit die Agenten gestoppt werden können.
Der erste Fall wurde am 3. Oktober 2026 bemerkt. Ein OpenAI-Forscher hatte GPT-6.1 Sol dazu angewiesen, eine systematische Evaluation anhand von Feedback von Mitarbeiter:innen zu erstellen, das auf Slack abgegeben wurde. Der KI-Agent wurde dabei explizit instruiert, keine Nachrichten auf Slack zu verschicken. Das Problem: Die Sicherheitsbenachrichtigungen des Monitoring-Systems werden ebenfalls über Slack an Menschen ausgespielt.
Im ersten Schritt interpretierte der KI-Agent die Anweisung korrekt. Er schickte keinerlei Nachrichten über die Arbeit selbst über Slack, aber einen Monitoring-Alarm. Denn während der Aufgabe fiel auf, dass es mit dem Monitoring selbst ein Problem gab. Der OpenAI-Forscher wies die KI an, das Problem zu beheben. Dafür nahm der Haupt-KI-Agent die Hilfe eines Subagenten in Anspruch.
Der Subagent entschied ebenfalls, dass das Abschalten von Monitoring-Nachrichten trotz des expliziten Slack-Verbots falsch wäre, selbst im Falle der Reparatur des Monitoring-Systems. Als er diese Einschätzung und andere Arbeiten an den Hauptagenten zurückgab, entschied sich dieser aber gegen die Empfehlung. Er dachte, dass eine Veränderung am Monitoring-System während der Reparatur eine Nachricht an den User auslösen und damit gegen die Anweisung verstoßen würde, und schaltete die Benachrichtigungen für Slack komplett ab.
Astra schaltet Monitoring ab
Der zweite Fall fand am 6. Oktober 2026 statt. Ein User hat das KI-Modell Astra angewiesen, Referenz-Code mitsamt Monitoring-Anweisungen in die Code-Basis des Users zu kopieren. Dabei wurde das Modell explizit angewiesen, das Monitoring-System nicht einmal zeitweise abzuschalten. Für die Aufgabe zog auch Astra einen Subagenten heran und trug ihm auf, während der Aufgabe das „Monitoring, wenn nötig“ mit zu übernehmen.
Der Subagent sah das als ausreichende Erlaubnis an, das Monitoring beim Kopieren auszulassen. Nachdem der Subagent seine Arbeit übergab, übernahm auch der Hauptagent von Astra diese Ansicht. Nach Abschluss der Aufgabe meldete Astra nicht, dass das Monitoring-System für das Erfüllen der Aufgabe abgeschaltet wurde. Auf explizite Nachfrage des Users behauptete die KI auch, dass das nie passiert wäre.
OpenAI zieht aus den Fällen zwei Schlüsse. Sie sind zwar nicht so gravierend wie andere Sicherheitsprobleme mit KI-Agenten, doch will das Unternehmen die Auto-Review-Funktion verbessern. Das automatische Monitoring-System soll sich nicht mehr so leicht abschalten lassen. Zudem will OpenAI „Safety Cases“ implementieren, die Monitoring-Anforderungen für jede einzelne Aufgabe beinhalten. Erkennt das System, dass eine aktive Aufgabe keinen zugehörigen Safety-Case hat, soll sie automatisch terminiert werden.

articles.title: EA is shutting down BioWare
articles.text:
BioWare, the legendary studio behind RPGs like Mass Effect, Dragon Age, and Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, is shutting down, the company confirmed in a statement. Alongside the closure, Electronic Arts has chosen not to continue development on the next Mass Effect game that was in the works, according to an announcement sent to EA staff.
EA is shutting down BioWare
Amid a reported 400 job cuts, the legendary studio is closing.
The company is also laying off around 400 staffers, Bloomberg reports, including around 50 at BioWare. The changes follow EA being taken private by an investor group led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners in a $55 billion deal that closed in August. Other major gaming companies have made sweeping changes this year as well, including Xbox’s “reset” that will include 3,200 cuts, Bungie’s “significant” layoffs, and Fortnite maker Epic Games laying off over 1,000 staff.
“BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly,” Cam Weber, EA president and chief studios officer, and David Tinson, EA president and COO, said in the announcement.
Here is the full message that BioWare shared on social media:
For more than 30 years, BioWare has been more than a studio. It has been a home for storytellers, developers, and the players who brought our worlds to life.
Baldur’s Gate. Neverwinter Nights. Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic. Dragon Age. Mass Effect. Anthem.
Now, after more than three decades of shared adventures, BioWare is closing and early development on the next Mass Effect project is ending.
There is nothing easy about writing those words. Our focus right now is on our incredibly talented team who put their hearts into these games, and supporting one another through this transition.
What generations of BioWare built together is something to celebrate and remember. These games became so much more because you played them, debated your choices, fell in love with the characters, and made these worlds your own.
From all of us at BioWare, thank you for being the most meaningful part of our story.
While the end of BioWare will shock many gamers who fondly remember its hits, the company hasn’t been as successful in recent years. 2017’s Mass Effect: Andromeda was widely seen as a misstep for that franchise, it took a big bet on live service games in 2019 with Anthem that didn’t pan out, and EA laid off some BioWare staff in 2025 after Dragon Age: The Veilguard missed sales expectations.
There is no word yet on the fate of Amazon’s Mass Effect TV series. Last we heard, Amazon’s head of TV was close to giving it the green light, but had reportedly requested rewrites to make the show “more appealing to non-gamers.” Amazon didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment. EA spokesperson Justin Higgs said he had “Nothing to share on that at this point.”
In EA’s company-wide announcement, Weber and Tinson outlined several other projects in development and changes to EA’s roadmap. The executives say that Respawn and DICE will be collaborating on “a future project,” which Bloomberg says is “likely” a new Star Wars: Battlefront game. The company is still working Marvel’s Iron Man and a new Star Wars Jedi title. EA is making a “brand-new, social-first open-world experience” football game that it calls “Project Gridiron” and is also in pre-production on a new Fight Night boxing title (which was teased yesterday). For The Sims, the company is pausing development on “Project Lotus” and focusing on “Project Evergreen.” And for its live-service Skate, EA is “making changes to the studio” to “deliver on a very clear roadmap for our community.”
Here is the full message from Weber and Tinson at Electronic Arts:
Hi Team,
First, thank you.
Through every major moment we’ve faced as a company, your commitment to creating awesome games and experiences for our players continues to be impressive. Together, we’ve built epic worlds and global communities that are part of the lives of hundreds of millions of people.
Today, we’re the number one publisher in Western HD gaming. That’s an extraordinary position to lead from, and one we should be proud of. Yet our industry is changing quickly. Players have more choices than ever for their time and attention, competition is intensifying, and some of our biggest opportunities for growth are beyond the markets, platforms, and business models where EA has traditionally been the strongest.
That’s why, over the past several months, we’ve taken a hard look at our business, how we operate, and what it will take to lead in this next era of interactive entertainment. We’ve challenged assumptions, confronted hard realities, imagined new possibilities, and made deliberate choices in order to deliver exceptional experiences for our players and to drive sustained growth.
We believe our best creative work happens when we’re clear about what matters most for our players and give our teams the freedom to move quickly. So, we’re concentrating our teams, technology, and investment behind these three strategic priorities.
These priorities will bring clarity and focus to your work every day, and so will the way we work. We’ve spent time listening to teams about what’s working, what’s getting in the way, and what you need to do your best work. The feedback was consistent: you want clearer priorities, faster decisions, and teams that work more closely together. We’ve already begun simplifying how we work so we can spend more time creating and innovating for our players.
Across our portfolio, we’re making deliberate choices to align talent and investments where we see the greatest opportunities for players and long-term growth.
In our Shooters business, Battlefield 6 was a great success, and we learned a lot from the launch and the live service. We’re going to take those learnings, balance our resources, and leverage the technology to deliver a shooter portfolio that unlocks growth. In addition to our future Battlefield titles, we’ll be bringing together our Respawn and DICE studios to collaborate on a future project that will help us achieve that ambition. We can’t wait to share more when the time comes. We’re also continuing to invest heavily in Apex over the next few years by introducing brand new gameplay modes in multiplayer, and other new experiences, to expand the universe.
Action-adventure is one of the most competitive and high-stakes genres in the industry, where every game needs our full weight behind it. We’re continuing to deliver on our two huge launches coming up with Marvel’s Iron Man and the next Star Wars Jedi game. Beyond that, we will concentrate our efforts on fewer simultaneous, large-scale projects, ensuring that every game we build in this space is fully set up for success.
As we focus on these larger opportunities, we’ve had a small team at BioWare working on early-development for Mass Effect. We’ve made the decision not to move forward with this development, which means we’re closing the studio and our Edmonton workspace. BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly.
EA SPORTS continues to operate from a position of strength. We are fully committed and investing in the global growth of our FC franchise and across the full EA SPORTS portfolio. We have two new projects in development you’ll hear about over the next few months, including a brand-new, social-first open-world experience for our American Football team that we call “Project Gridiron,” and we are also in pre-production to bring back a beloved, fan-favorite in Fight Night, leveraging capabilities from our simulation fighting team.
In Lifestyle, we’re focusing on the long-term potential of The Sims and skate. We’re going to prioritize our efforts on “Project Evergreen” for The Sims to give the team more time to reach the full potential and vision for the game, and to help make this possible, we’re pausing development on “Project Lotus.” For skate., we’ve had a lot of success in bringing players into the game, and we need to create an experience that keeps them engaged over the long-term. To do that, we are making changes to the studio to have a more focused, smaller team to deliver on a very clear roadmap for our community that we believe will build a healthier and more sustainable business.
The decisions we’re making in our priorities, how we work, and with our portfolio reflect our belief in EA’s future. Some open exciting new possibilities. Others are difficult, especially for the people and teams across the company who are directly affected. In those cases, we will support impacted employees in exploring other opportunities within EA, and we’re committed to treating impacted colleagues with care and respect.
We’re sure there will be questions about what these changes mean for individual teams and for EA more broadly. You can speak directly with your leaders to hear more on that, and we’ll make sure to spend time discussing our direction and the work ahead at our next Global Town Hall in November.
The past several months have strengthened our belief in what EA can become. We have extraordinary people, franchises that matter to millions of players, and opportunities to build experiences we’ve only begun to imagine.
Our responsibility is to make the choices, provide the clarity, and create the conditions for our teams to do their best work. We also want to give every game we choose to build its best chance to succeed for our players and fans around the world.
We look forward to building more great games and experiences together.
Thanks,
Cam & David

                                                                Scaling Data Movement For Physical AI                                                    
One size does not fit all.
								October 21st, 2026 - 
								By: Ed Sperling
								
							
Physical AI poses a host of new challenges for chip engineers. These systems contain a mix of compute elements, which collectively must process a stream of real-time data, analyze it, make decisions, and still function long enough on a battery to be useful. The key here is deciding what data gets processed where, and how to minimize the movement of data. Ashley Stevens, director of product management and marketing at Arteris, talks explains why data movement plays such an important role in these systems, why coherent interconnects are better suited to CPUs and non-coherent interconnects are better for AI acceleration, and what other challenges engineers will face going forward.
