articles.title: Getting old is hard. This age-tech housing aims to make it easier. | BetaKit
articles.text:
My grandmother was a commanding woman. In her 92 years, she raised three children and a grandchild, mostly by herself. She helped manage a series of successful restaurants and nightclubs; in her little spare time, she hiked and skied. She was decidedly capable.
But when I unexpectedly knocked on her door one autumn when I was 19, something was different: she asked me the same questions, different only in sentence structure, again and again.
What brought me to town?
Where was I going to school?
What was I doing in town?
What college was I enrolled in?
Over the years, she lost more of her faculties. Eventually, she left the stovetop on for so long that a steel pot melted into molten coagulant. That was the boiling point: a week later she moved in with my parents.
My grandmother’s experience was not abnormal. Like many seniors, she was caught between her desire to remain independent and the limitations of her advancing age; she didn’t want to leave her home, but could also no longer live safely on her own. With little money to afford in-home care, those years put untold pressure on my parents and left my grandmother in a sort of purgatory: she wasn’t independent, but she also didn’t have round-the-clock care.
If Calgary’s Garden Loft had been around back then, might things have been different?
“The world’s first full-stack house”
The small, loft-styled suites Garden Loft builds look like the type of in-fills you might see in a trendy Calgary neighbourhood: angular, with glassy entranceways and teak-wood finish. But inside, they’re full of cutting-edge tech masquerading as modern decor.
Garden Loft was founded in 2022 by University of Calgary dean of architecture John Brown, his wife and fellow co-founder Carina van Olm Brown, and third co-founder, Matthew North. The company builds modular, prefabricated housing for older people and others with differing abilities. Its tech is imbued with “gerontechnology,” more commonly called age-tech. Age-tech is digital technology used to improve or manage the health, well-being, and independence of seniors.
“This is more than a smart home. It’s a new model of care.”
Garden Loft evolved out of the trio’s previous business, a boutique design and construction firm called Housebrand. In its capacity as a custom builder, Housebrand had been receiving customer commissions asking for housing that could adapt to their needs as they aged.
“The costs of [renovating] all of that makes sense for a person that needs it, but it doesn’t make sense for the larger housing market,” Brown told me last July when I visited the industrial Calgary workshop where he and his partners are building Garden Loft’s homes. “We started to think about a separate solution: What if we had a house that already had everything in it?” he said.
That notion led to a research partnership in 2014 between Brown, in his capacity as dean of the U of C’s School of Architecture, Planning, and Landscape, and the Cumming School of Medicine. Its purpose was to explore the potential of integrating medical technology into backyard suite housing that could be leased, installed, and removed as a person’s health needs change.
Fast forward a decade and Garden Loft now describes itself as the Tesla of housing: a full-stack alternative to expensive in-home care and assisted living facilities that are often underfunded.
“Tesla, notwithstanding Elon Musk being crazy, was the first full-stack car. Deeply integrated technology on all kinds of levels,” Brown said, claiming that Garden Lofts is the “world’s first full-stack house.”
A mix of built-in tech and digital infrastructure, Garden Loft attempts to set itself apart from its peers in the seniors-housing space by the breadth of the technology it integrates into its products. Think injury-resistant flooring that Brown says can dampen fall impacts by as much as 43 percent, digital sensor technology to monitor activity levels, and a digital community platform with curated service delivery for users.
For its efforts, the company was awarded the City of Calgary’s 2023 accessibility award.
But where Garden Loft really makes its stand is in its use of software. Building on a proprietary digital platform, a Garden Loft suite can continuously measure 37 different data streams, looking for deviations in metrics like sleep quality, hydration, stability, gait speed, toilet use, activity levels, and more. That data runs through an algorithm that identifies potential early warning signals of declining health and compiles them along a gradient: green for good, yellow when three or four indicators emerge, and so on. All of this can be accessed by residents via Garden Loft’s digital platform.
If all of that data collection sounds a little Big Brother, Brown maintains that Garden Loft’s clients, most of whom are in their mid-80s or older, retain agency over how their data is used and shared.
RELATED: Canada’s housing supply is in crisis. Can robots help?
“You have control over your data. You can cede it; give access to your family or your healthcare provider,” Brown told me, adding that residents must choose what data, if any, they want to share with healthcare providers or supports like friends or family.
While Brown was clear that the data measured by Garden Loft’s systems is technically behavioural, not medical, information he recognized that it would still be sensitive. He said the company is working on ways to protect that data, though he didn’t explain exactly what those protections would look like.
“We generate the data, and we have control over it, and we’re just working right now around data privacy,” he said last August.
After our initial conversation, I reached out to Brown to follow up on the issue of data privacy. He told me that Garden Loft would house the data it generates on private, domestically located servers and that user data “will not be sold or otherwise shared.”
It takes a village
Garden Loft has spent the last few years incubating with the support of Calgary funding catalyst and growth studio Thin Air Labs (James Lochrie, a Thin Air managing partner, now sits on the company’s board). In that time, the company has deployed several prototype properties: three in Calgary, three in Edmonton, one in Airdrie, Alta., and one in Ottawa.
Currently, Garden Loft is working on several projects to build 10-to-30-unit “village” style housing that Brown thinks has the potential to upend the assisted-living model in Canada.
“You get 80 percent of what’s delivered in a supported living environment or long-term care facility at 50 percent of the cost, and you stay in the housing market rather than entering the care industry,” Brown claimed.
A 10-unit prototype village is under construction in Bassano, Alta., with four additional village projects in development, including in an as-of-yet-undisclosed Northern Alberta Indigenous community. The village design concept can include a different care model than the standalone homes the company currently has in the market. In the village scenario, Garden Loft is leaning into a telehealth model of care, integrating clinical and pharmaceutical support services that residents can contact on an as-needed basis. Those resident healthcare providers can in turn access residents’ real-time biometrics if they choose to make that data available.
The Bassano village project, which Brown says will open next year, is partnering with the Dr. Barrie Strafford Centre for Learning, Innovation, and Quality (CLIQ) on an Alberta Innovates-funded research project that will evaluate health outcomes over two years to fine-tune the company’s wellness monitoring platform.
A new kind of care
Much like Garden Loft’s village project aims to change what congregated supportive living looks like, age-tech is changing what supportive care looks like broadly at a moment when healthcare for older people in Canada is buckling.
Laura Tamblyn Watts is the CEO of CanAge, Canada’s national seniors’ advocacy organization. She’s also a board member of AgeWell, a national centre of excellence that studies aging and technology. Tamblyn Watts said that in the current senior-care environment, technology is playing a growing role in expanding the continuum of what care looks like as people get older.
“When you read statistics that say things like 90 percent of people want to remain in their own home—well, of course they do because the questions being asked are: ‘Do you want to move into long-term care or do you want to live in your home as long as you want?’ Those aren’t very good questions. They set up this false dichotomy [between long-term care and living alone].
“You get 80 percent of what’s delivered in a supported living environment or long-term care facility at 50 percent of the cost, and you stay in the housing market rather than entering the care industry.”
“There’s a continuum in between,” Tamblyn Watts said. “That idea of integrated age technology is so critically important; it’s part of a broader trend to look at prefabricated housing supports where they are both integrated, as well as accessible, affordable, and inclusive.”
That matters because regardless of where a person lives on that continuum of care, prices are steep. Retirement home costs average just over $3,000 per month, and can spike into the tens of thousands. In-home care isn’t much better, according to Tamblyn Watts, who said hiring a caregiver with only six weeks of formal education—far less than a registered nurse requires—can cost in the hundreds of thousands per year.
Put the soaring prices aside for a moment, and there is another chokepoint: capacity. According to the Canadian Institute for Health Information (CIHI), Canada has just shy of 200,000 long-term care beds. Meanwhile, Canadians 85 and older are among the country’s fastest-growing demographics, with researchers projecting that capacity in long-term care will need to double in the next decade to meet demand.
As I walked through Garden Loft’s warehouse last summer, its dual bays littered with halfway finished homes, my mind kept returning to my grandmother and the ways that as her cognition declined, the space she inhabited, and the life she had built for herself, diminished, too. Could such futuristic housing have slowed the pace at which her world shrunk? Might it have eased the burden of care as she transitioned from capable to dependent?
RELATED: AlayaCare raises $51 million CAD to scale homecare provider platform
Against that backdrop, Brown believes new caregiving models like the one he and his partners are building now will come to serve as a necessary release valve for the long-term care industry, the governments funding it, and the people whose health and dignity rely on these systems of care.
“Governments in North America realize they can’t provide the level of healthcare [needed], that we can’t keep everyone in a facility or hospital. There has to be home care,” Brown said, adding that what Garden Loft is building constitutes a new kind of supportive living.
“This is more than a smart home. It’s a new model of care,” he said. “We have to try to age people in place, and what we’re doing is providing a technical, digital, and physical framework to enable that to happen to a higher degree.”

articles.title: NVIDIA Cloud Partners Scale Across Europe — Sovereign, Open and Built for Safe AI Agents
articles.text:
Demand from AI-natives is pulling the European AI cloud ecosystem forward faster than ever. Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design.
NVIDIA Cloud Partners across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do.
Together, they’re turning Europe’s energy, data, research and industrial expertise into productive intelligence — supporting new models, applications, organizations and jobs while giving people more control over where and how they develop and deploy AI.
Sovereign: AI Clouds Building European AI Infrastructure
Europe is home to world-class research, engineering talent, industrial expertise, data, the next generation of models and applications that requires large-scale computing close to where that knowledge resides. Regional AI clouds provide the infrastructure foundation on which model builders, enterprises and entire industries can grow.
As AI factories scale, power becomes a constraint which makes it critical for every watt to produce more intelligence. Nscale is using the NVIDIA DSX Platform to coordinate power allocation with workload requirements. In tests using NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems, Nscale demonstrated that NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS enabled 37% more GPUs and nearly 50% higher aggregate inference throughput within the same provisioned power budget.
Nscale also plans to deploy NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure for frontier-model training and production workloads to support leading model and application builders using its full-stack, vertically integrated platform with expansion across five European markets.
Crusoe is developing Spark, its liquid-cooled modular AI factories designed for the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, to bring Crusoe Cloud capacity closer to users for low-latency AI inference. Crusoe Cloud serves leading model and application builders across EMEA, including Base44, Gradium, LTX and Wonderful.
Aleria, Cassava Technologies, Firebird, G42, Radiant, SWI Compute and Vultr are also developing and expanding NVIDIA-powered AI infrastructure across Europe, the Nordics, Africa and Central Asia.
Regional capacity from AI clouds combines the full-stack NVIDIA DSX AI Factory platform, including NVIDIA Vera Rubin, NVIDIA BlueField and NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet networking, giving customers greater choice and control over where workloads and data reside while advancing sovereign computing services and economic growth.
Open: Models and Libraries, From Training to Inference
Across the ecosystem, AI clouds are expanding NVIDIA-powered infrastructure and services for developers to build applications with open models and libraries. This new capacity supports model training, fine-tuning for specialized tasks and inference at scale, including applications deployed at the edge.
For production inference, Nebius has adopted NVIDIA Groq 3 LPX, using Spectrum-X Ethernet networking to integrate it with Vera Rubin NVL72 on Nebius Token Factory. The combination will bring faster token generation to latency-sensitive applications and agentic systems through the platform’s managed serverless and dedicated endpoints and familiar application programming interfaces.
For robotics and physical AI, Nebius offers a purpose-built AI cloud solution that includes its full-stack Physical AI Workbench. Robotics companies including Rhoda AI, RoboForce and Sereact are building on the platform. The company also launched three NVIDIA retail agent blueprints — covering inventory, store operations, and fine-tuning —- into early access on Nebius infrastructure.
Nebius is expanding its cloud services widely across the continent with its Physical AI Living Lab, and in Germany as a computer supplier for the Next Frontier Challenge of SPRIND, the Federal Agency for Breakthrough Innovation.
Baseten has developed a specialized model for code-review routing with Nemotron 3.5 Lightning used by CodeRabbit. Through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, CodeRabbit improved routing agreement from 75.8% to 80.7% while reducing estimated inference costs by 50% for the evaluated workload. The results demonstrate how AI developers can customize NVIDIA open models for specialized tasks while improving accuracy and inference efficiency.
Fireworks and Era4 are partnering to bring open models to enterprises across the U.K. and Europe. The collaboration combines Fireworks’ model training and inference platform with direct liquid-cooled capacity powered by NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs at Era4’s Chesterfield facility, supporting plans for enterprise AI solutions in financial services, insurance and life sciences.
Mistral is expanding its NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure to support model training, customization and inference. The expansion includes NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure planned for delivery in 2027. Trained on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral-operated European data centers, Mistral Large 4 is the company’s latest frontier multimodal model, advancing capabilities across coding, agentic workflows and multimodal understanding.
Verda plans to deploy NVIDIA Vera Rubin, continuing to promote open weight models with NVIDIA Nemotron and NVIDIA Cosmos already in production, and using the NVIDIA Dynamo open source framework for inference optimization.
Safe: Secure Boundaries for AI Agents, From Silicon to Software
As developers connect models to tools and business systems, they also need controls over what agents can access and do.
Announced at GTC Berlin, the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture with support from AI cloud ecosystem partners. Built on the foundation of NVIDIA OpenShell secure runtime software, the architecture is designed to give organizations full-stack control to deploy AI agents with clear boundaries around what agents can access and do.
NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 for model inference, NVIDIA Vera CPUs with OpenShell for agent harnesses and tool use, and NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs running NVIDIA Sentry for in-silicon enforcement. Each play a distinct role in delivering that control, working together so agents can achieve what they’re meant to do without moving beyond the boundaries people set for them.
Partners including Aleria, Baseten, Cassava, CoreWeave, Crusoe, DigitalOcean, Firebird, Fireworks, Firmus, G42, GMI Cloud, IREN, Lambda, Lightning AI, Nebius, Nscale, Radiant Verda and Vultr are supporting the OpenShell Reference Architecture to enable secure agentic deployments for their customers.
Together, European AI clouds are connecting regional infrastructure investment with the work of building and deploying AI. Expanded capacity gives builders more places to run workloads. Model and inference services help them put that capacity to use. Agent controls address what applications are allowed to do as they move into production.
Explore NVIDIA Cloud Partners for infrastructure and services, and the OpenShell Reference Architecture for agent deployment controls.

articles.title: Four workers killed after fall at TSMC’s 2nm fab construction site — accident marks at least nine construction deaths since 2024, broken bolt on a steel connection plate suspected as cause behind tragic accident (updated)
articles.text:
Four workers killed after fall at TSMC’s 2nm fab construction site — accident marks at least nine construction deaths since 2024, broken bolt on a steel connection plate suspected as cause behind tragic accident (updated)
Four contract workers fell with steel parts during Phase 4 hoisting work, which is now halted.
Update - October 21, 11:20 am ET: In an update, local media reports that all four TSMC workers involved in an accident at its 2nm Fab 22 site in Kaohsiung have died. Reports indicate the accident was caused by a broken connecting plate bolt. TSMC has suspended all steel structure work at the site and all of its new plants in Taiwan while it investigates the cause of the accident. The rest of the story remains below as first published.
Three contract workers died, and one more is in intensive care after an accident at the construction site for TSMC’s 2nm Fab 22 in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, reports Taiwan’s Central News Agency. The Southern Taiwan Science Park (STSP) Bureau suspects the cause was a broken bolt on a steel connection plate that sent the workers and steel components tumbling. Steel hoisting on the project has been halted, and the STSP has sent labor inspectors to investigate. The accident is not the first of its kind but rather follows at least a half dozen others since September 2024 at TSMC construction sites in Taiwan, according to local reports. Each of those earlier accidents killed one worker.
Local police said that the men were welding a steel beam on an upper floor and fell with it, while the STSP said the workers were performing steel-structure hoisting and installation when a third-floor connection-plate bolt apparently broke.
10 emergency vehicles were sent to the site with 22 personnel, and all four men involved in the incident were taken to the hospital. On-site medical staff gave first aid, but three of the workers died despite resuscitation efforts, and the fourth was moved to intensive care. The workers were employed by a contractor working on the fourth phase of the complex’s construction, and TSMC said the area was within that contractor’s scope of work.
According to the report, TSMC stopped the related construction work on its own and is working with authorities and supervising the subcontractor’s follow-up.
The Fab 22 complex, located in Kaohsiung’s Nanzi District, is part of the science park and is being built to accelerate 2nm manufacturing. TSMC entered high-volume 2nm, or N2, manufacturing in the fourth quarter of 2025, including at Fab 22. The complex has five phases planned, with a total investment TSMC puts at more than NT$1.5 trillion, or about $46 billion. The accident happened on the construction side, not in a producing fab. Kaohsiung’s deputy mayor said construction on Phase 4 began in August 2025, with operations expected in the fourth quarter of 2027.
Business Today reports that TSMC fab construction has increased, from four fabs a year in 2017–2024 to nine a year in 2025 and 2026. The deaths come as the company plans for 13 new leading-edge and advanced-packaging fabs in Taiwan, with company-wide capex of $60 billion to $64 billion this year.
The faster pace has encouraged the addition of a contractor’s safety record as a weight in selection and a plan for a Taiwan Semiconductor Construction Engineering Safety Association with construction partners. TSMC Chairman C.C. Wei said at last year’s shareholders meeting that safety cannot be compromised, and the company’s 2025 annual report said it will keep investing in fabs across several locations in Taiwan “with a strong emphasis on construction site safety.”
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Cliff Hou, TSMC senior vice president and deputy co-COO, told Business Today that increased worker count and overlapping construction have raised the risk, requiring careful supervision, and that TSMC’s contractor lost-time injury rate had fallen about 42% from last year’s high as of late May, when the publication toured the Nanzi site to see the overhaul. It’s too early to call the program a failure, with the cause as yet unknown.
The accident comes less than a week after an explosion killed two people at Intel’s chip plant in Israel, though that was an operating fab rather than a construction site. Both accidents come as chipmakers race to meet demand, with global chip sales passing $1 trillion through August, according to the Semiconductor Industry Association.
The STSP’s findings will determine what penalties, if any, will fall under Taiwan’s Occupational Safety and Health Act, while it assists the victims’ families. No date has been given at this time for that or for the Phase 4 steel hoisting restart. Nor has TSMC commented on any schedule impact.

articles.title: Supernatural’s comeback starts today, with more music and VR workouts coming soon
articles.text:
Despite Meta saying it would stop creating new content for Supernatural, the beloved fitness VR game is back after spinning off to go its own way and is relaunching with an Early Access preview in the Meta Horizon Store. Thousands of “remastered” workouts and some new ones are available in the new app starting today, but more are on the way. As previously announced, the newly independent app also costs more, going from $9.99 per month to $20 per month or $200 per year.
Supernatural’s comeback starts today, with more music and VR workouts coming soon
Supernatural is relaunching in early access, but it comes with a higher subscription price.
Starting next week, Supernatural will get new workouts every week. The game’s developers also write, “More back-catalog favorites will return in the weeks and months ahead, with new music, higher-definition destinations and new features on the way.”
Other new features coming later include the return of Supernatural Together, which has been “rebuilt from the ground up.” Supernatural is also getting a mobile companion app it says members can use to “Track progress and heart rate and stay connected beyond the headset.”
Supernatural says people who played the original version of the game “can transfer their points, start date, streaks, favorites and badges” to the new version through December 3rd. It’s also offering rewards for “founding members,” starting with a custom bat, with more coming throughout early access.

articles.title: Snapchat se paye Iron Man pour faire la promotion de ses lunettes connectées à 2 295 euros
articles.text:
Snap a officialisé le 20 octobre l’arrivée de Robert Downey Jr. chez Specs, sa filiale consacrée aux lunettes de réalité augmentée. L’interprète d’Iron Man y devient « directeur honoraire de l’expérience client », un intitulé créé pour l’occasion. Sa feuille de route couvre les contenus originaux, les Lenses, ces applications en réalité augmentée maison, et des collaborations sur le matériel comme sur des événements physiques.
Quarante secondes pour conquérir Iron Man
L’acteur assure avoir cédé vite : « Après avoir testé à peu près toutes les technologies portables sorties ces vingt dernières années, sans être vraiment impressionné, les Specs m’ont totalement conquis en quarante secondes ». Il file lui-même la référence à sa filmographie, en décrivant des lunettes qui « tiennent la promesse faite par un certain super-héros techno-optimiste » qu’il a incarné. Evan Spiegel, le patron de Snap, salue de son côté un partenaire qui « imagine ce que cette technologie pourrait devenir depuis près de vingt ans ». Le communiqué assigne à l’acteur une mission moins poétique : « guider les clients pour comprendre et imaginer ce qui est possible » avec l’objet.
Le recrutement s’accompagne d’une série d’épisodes publiés sur YouTube et le site de Specs : aménager son espace de travail, progresser au golf, suivre une série au lit ou apprendre à peindre, lunettes sur le nez. Un premier spot a été diffusé le soir même, pendant le match d’ouverture de la saison NBA entre les Knicks et les Sixers. Un épisode inédit accompagnera ensuite le premier match des World Series, le 23 octobre. Des expériences signées HBO et NBA figurent déjà au catalogue des Lenses.
2 295 euros chez Orange et 3,5 milliards déjà engloutis
Les Specs se précommandent aux États-Unis à 2 195 dollars en Wi-Fi, 2 395 dollars avec la 5G de Verizon, pour des livraisons attendues dans le courant de l’automne. La France suivra au même étage tarifaire : 2 295 euros, ou 2 495 euros en version 5G, avec Orange dans le rôle du distributeur. L’objet se veut autonome, sans téléphone ni boîtier externe : le calcul loge dans les branches, derrière deux verres à réalité augmentée. Les lunettes connectées de Meta, bien moins chères, jouent dans une autre catégorie, celle de l’accessoire arrimé au smartphone.
Présentées en juin à la conférence AWE, les lunettes ont d’abord récolté des moqueries pour leur gabarit, et l’action Snap a reculé d’environ 4 % le jour de la présentation. L’investisseur activiste Irenic Capital chiffre à plus de 3,5 milliards de dollars la facture du projet et réclame un examen de toutes les options, cession comprise. Evan Spiegel défend un « pari à long terme » et a filialisé l’activité, une structure qui ouvre la porte à des capitaux extérieurs. Le montant du contrat reste secret, mais une enveloppe d’environ 100 millions de dollars en actions circulait dès le mois de juin, sans jamais être confirmée par les deux camps.

articles.title: La máquina arcade en miniatura de Pac-Man cae (mucho) de precio: ideal para exponerla en casa o jugar donde quieras
articles.text:
Muchas marcas se sirven de la nostalgia para comercializar sus productos y en el terreno de las máquinas arcade podemos encontrar numerosos modelos en miniatura de algunos de los videojuegos más clásicos. Si siempre te ha encantado el juego del Comecocos, mucho ojo porque Amazon ahora mismo tiene de oferta la máquina My Arcade Micro de Pac-Man por un precio de 29,99 euros.
My Arcade Micro Pac-Man
Una máquina arcade pequeña, portátil y con el Pac-Man

Lo llamativo es que se trata de una máquina arcade totalmente funcional que cuenta con un diseño inspirado en Pac-Man presentando un acabado en color amarillo con algunos dibujos del personaje. Además, incluye todo lo necesario para echar unas partidas al Comecocos.
Esta mini máquina arcade incorpora una pantalla de 2,75 pulgadas y viene con algunas funciones para regular el brillo. Funciona con pilas AA o con cable USB-C, cuenta con licencia oficial y viene con el videojuego de Pac-Man incluido, además de un joystick para que podamos jugar.

articles.title: Amazon hikes Prime membership by up to 30% in Australia ahead of Black Friday and holiday sales
articles.text:
Amazon hikes Prime membership by up to 30% in Australia ahead of Black Friday and holiday sales
Effective immediately for new members, while the price hike comes into effect from November 25 for existing subscribers
- Amazon Prime subscriptions will increase to AU$12.99 per month or AU$99 per year, up from AU$9.99 and AU$79, respectively
- These prices are effective immediately for new subscribers, while existing members will be charged starting from November 25
- Inclusions and perks like Prime Video, Music Prime and sale events remain unchanged
Amazon Australia has revealed its monthly Prime membership fee has increased from AU$9.99 to AU$12.99, effective immediately for new subscribers — a significant 30% hike from the previous cost. The annual membership price also increases from AU$79 to AU$99, a 25% rise.
In emails sent to Prime members, Amazon said the new pricing reflects the growing range of products and benefits available through the service, although the inclusions remain the same, including free and expedited delivery, Prime Video, Prime Music, Prime Reading, video games with Amazon Luna, and member-only events such as Prime Day and Prime Big Deal Days.
Existing customers will continue to pay the usual AU$9.99 per month and the price increase will apply from their first membership renewal date on or after November 25, 2026.
In a statement, an Amazon spokesperson told TechRadar that this price change is specific to Australia and attributes it largely to the expanded delivery footprint, new Prime Video content and access to Alexa+.
"We are committed to growing the value of Prime for members, and in just the last six months we have brought Prime Free overnight delivery before 8am on hundreds of thousands of products to four cities, expanded Prime Free Same-Day Delivery available now in nine regions across Australia, added new TV series and movies to Prime Video plus live sport, given free access to Alexa+, provided exclusive deals through events like Prime Day, and more," the spokesperson said.
"With the continued expansion of Prime member benefits, and so we can continue growing the offering, we will change the price of Prime to $12.99 per month or $99 per year. Prime has never offered as much value for members as it does today."
This price hike comes just in time before Amazon’s own Black Friday sale in Australia, which we expect to start a few days before the actual Black Friday date of November 27, and will run until Cyber Monday on November 30.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
While the US has seen multiple price increases recently, this is Amazon’s second round of hikes in Australia since launching in 2018. Initially just AU$6.99 per month or AU$59 per year at launch, Amazon later bumped that up to AU$9.99 per month (43%) or AU$79 per year (34%) in May 2023 as more inclusions were added. As mentioned, the price doesn’t reflect better inclusions, which is surely going to factor into household costs for many regular Amazon shoppers.
Earlier this month, Amazon opened its third Sydney fulfilment centre located in western suburb of Horsley Park which is “a 12-hour drive of 80% of Australia”, meaning even more shoppers will benefit from same-day delivery. Perhaps this goes some way in justifying a price increase, along with the fact that Amazon typically offers the best prices on thousands of items even outside of major sales. However, with an additional AU$2 monthly payment to get rid of ads on Prime Video, this news is sure to sting some customers.
While the Amazon Black Friday sale in Australia isn’t a Prime-exclusive event, the best prices will be for subscribers, so it does still pay to have a subscription. Thankfully, Amazon also makes it easy to cancel your subscription any time, although you won’t be eligible for the usual 30-day free trial if you’re a returning customer.

Nico is an experienced writer and journalist, having previously written for business titles across Australia. He mainly focuses on evergreen content like buying guides and reviews, as well as finding deals and coupon codes at TechRadar Australia. Outside of work, Nico is a keen cyclist and occasionally goes on runs and hikes.

articles.title: Seigneur des anneaux : fin des rumeurs, Peter Jackson parle enfin de Shadow of the Past
articles.text:
Début octobre 2026, le site Knight Edge Media affirmait que Skydance, le groupe né du rachat de Warner Bros. Discovery par Paramount, avait mis le film « en pause ». Warner Bros. avait ensuite assuré que le projet n’était pas annulé.
Entre deux détails sur le tournage de The Hunt for Gollum (attendu dans les salles françaises le 15 décembre 2027), le cinéaste néo-zélandais, qui produit les deux films sans les réaliser, a confirmé à ScreenRant ce 20 octobre que le scénario de cette suite de la trilogie originale était toujours en chantier. Il n’a donné ni date de tournage ni date de sortie.
Une suite 14 ans après Le Retour du Roi pour Shadow of the Past
Warner Bros. a posé le cadre de ce nouveau long-métrage dès son annonce, le 25 mars. Intitulé Le Seigneur des Anneaux : Shadow of the Past (un titre provisoire), le film se déroulera 14 ans après le départ de Frodon, qui clôt Le Retour du Roi.
Selon le synopsis officiel, Sam, Merry et Pippin partent sur les traces des premiers pas de leur aventure en Terre du Milieu. En parallèle, Elanor, la fille de Sam, découvre un secret longtemps enfoui et cherche à comprendre pourquoi la guerre de l’Anneau a failli être perdue avant même d’avoir commencé. Le scénario est signé par la fidèle Philippa Boyens, coscénariste de la trilogie originale, et par deux renforts inattendus : l’ancien animateur du Late Show Stephen Colbert, grand connaisseur de Tolkien, et son fils, le scénariste Peter McGee. Stephen Colbert a expliqué que l’histoire puiserait dans les premiers chapitres de La Communauté de l’Anneau absents du film de 2001, dont la rencontre avec Tom Bombadil et la traversée des Hauts des Galgals.
The Hunt for Gollum presque tourné, Tintin 2 sur les rails
Si Shadow of the Past n’est encore qu’au stade du scénario, les autres projets de Peter Jackson sont plus avancés :
Réalisé par Andy Serkis (qui reprend son rôle aux côtés d’Ian McKellen en Gandalf et d’Elijah Wood en Frodon), The Hunt for Gollum touche à sa fin : il restait environ deux semaines de tournage en Nouvelle-Zélande, selon Jackson. Le réalisateur avait déjà comparé l’approche du film à celle du Joker de Joaquin Phoenix, une histoire racontée de l’intérieur, centrée sur la psychologie et l’addiction de Gollum.
Aussi, la suite de Tintin est enfin sur les rails : le scénario de cette suite des Aventures de Tintin, coécrit avec Fran Walsh, est entièrement rédigé et le film sera officiellement le tout prochain projet qu’il réalisera personnellement.

articles.title: Chez Xbox, on recrute un « Games Supply Strategist » pour gérer… les jeux en version physique
articles.text:
Alors que Sony prévoit toujours d’arrêter la production de disques pour les nouveaux jeux PlayStation en janvier 2028, Microsoft entretient encore le flou sur l’avenir des boîtes chez Xbox. Récemment, une offre d’emploi officielle vient de remettre le sujet sur la table…
Voilà quelques années maintenant que le jeu vidéo dématérialisé progresse à pas de géant, et Xbox n’a pas attendu 2026 pour prendre le virage. Game Pass, téléchargements, sorties multiplateformes… Chez Microsoft, le jeu se consomme de plus en plus sans passer par un magasin (et même sans passer par une Xbox). Pourtant, le fabricant recrute sur son site officiel un « Games Supply Strategist », un poste qui touche à la stratégie d’approvisionnement de son activité gaming.
Xbox cherche toujours à gérer ses jeux physiques
L’intitulé du poste est intrigant, mais c’est surtout la mission qui retient l’attention, puisque Microsoft évoque explicitement « le lancement de jeux physiques Xbox sur différentes plateformes », ainsi que la gestion des approvisionnements et de la distribution.
Autrement dit, le constructeur veut optimiser la manière dont ses jeux en boîte arrivent dans les rayons et répondent à la demande. Alors non, ce recrutement ne signifie pas pour autant que Xbox prépare un retour en force du physique. Il montre néanmoins que cette activité reste un sujet suffisamment concret aujourd’hui encore, pour justifier un poste dédié.
Et à l’heure où l’on s’interroge (plus que jamais) sur l’avenir des supports physiques, Microsoft ne semble pas avoir complètement tourné la page. Mais cette stratégie concerne-t-elle une offre limitée, les jeux Xbox distribués sur d’autres consoles ou des projets plus larges ? Difficile de savoir…
Des jeux Xbox de plus en plus rares en boutique
Sur le terrain, la tendance est pourtant difficile à ignorer. Les jeux Xbox occupent une place de plus en plus réduite dans les rayons de nombreuses enseignes, avec des stocks parfois très (très) limités. Ces dernières années, il n’était pas rare également de voir certains titres disponibles en boîte sur PlayStation et Nintendo Switch, sans équivalent physique sur Xbox donc.
Cette situation reflète la stratégie récente de Microsoft, qui a très largement misé sur le numérique, sans oublier les sorties de ses jeux sur les consoles concurrentes. Pour les collectionneurs et les joueurs attachés à leurs bibliothèques de boîtes, le constat est amer, et trouver certains jeux Xbox en magasin relève parfois du parcours du combattant.
Récemment, le géant américain a déployé une mise à jour visant à permettre aux joueurs de réclamer une licence numérique de leurs jeux physiques. Pour certains, c’est une manière de continuer à faire vivre le physique, pour d’autres, une manière de préparer l’avenir « tout numérique » que pourrait constituer l’écosystème Xbox Helix à venir.
Le disque va-t-il survivre chez Xbox ?
Contrairement à PlayStation, chez Xbox, et malgré des signaux qui témoignent d’un net recul, aucune annonce officielle ne permet aujourd’hui de conclure à un abandon du physique. Les jeux en boîte restent donc une réalité chez Microsoft (on l’imagine au moins jusqu’en 2028, comme son rival direct), et leur distribution nécessite toujours d’être organisée.
Dans ce contexte, le recrutement d'un « Games Supply Strategist » n’a rien d’illogique, puisqu’il s’agit de gérer une activité encore bien réelle, même si elle occupe une place de plus en plus réduite.
Faut-il y voir un signe encourageant pour les amateurs de boîtes ? Pas nécessairement. Cette annonce ne garantit en rien la présence de jeux physiques sur les futures consoles Xbox, ni même le maintien de l’offre actuelle au-delà des prochaines années. Elle rappelle simplement que Microsoft n’a pas encore tiré un trait sur le format. Mais pour combien de temps…
- La rétrocompatibilité au top
- Le Quick Resume, difficile de revenir en arrière
- Taillée pour l'avenir (HDMI 2.1, dolby vision/atmos, VRR)
- Niveau de finition exemplaire
- Grip généralisé sur les poignées
- Gâchettes et palettes plus abouties
- Finitions et ergonomie impeccables
- Très nets progrès de l'interface Xbox
- Puissance du Ryzen AI Z2 Extreme

articles.title: Design Proteins with RFD4-Proteina Using Reward-Guided Inference-Time Search | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
Protein design is a search problem. Choose amino acids for an eight-residue protein sequence and more than 25 billion combinations are possible. Choose amino acids for a 100-residue protein sequence and the number of possibilities exceeds the number of atoms in the observable universe. Somewhere in that space is a protein that opens a path to a new therapy. There are too many combinations to search exhaustively, so finding it depends on knowing where to look.
RFD4-Proteina, an NVIDIA BioNeMo open model co-developed with the Institute for Protein Design at the University of Washington’s School of Medicine, navigates that space using patterns learned from nature. It co-designs protein sequences and all-atom structures, and uses reward-guided inference-time search to focus compute on the most promising candidates.
This tutorial shows computational biologists, ML engineers and drug discovery researchers how to design protein binder candidates against PD-L1, an oncology target, using reward-guided inference-time search and introduces experimental validation results across design tasks.
You can access RFD4-Proteina in two ways:
- Choose the open model for training, inference, method development, and direct control over sampling code or
- Choose the NIM microservice for rapid inference deployment with an HTTP interface
Building on Proteina-Complexa’s partially latent approach, RFD4-Proteina combines explicit backbone coordinates with latent representation, learned sequence and atomistic variables. Its autoencoder decoder produces the sequence and all-atom structure together, removing the separate inverse-folding handoff to a model such as ProteinMPNN.
Prerequisites
- Open model
  - Supported Linux GPU host and Python 3.12; follow the repository setup guide and use a supported NVIDIA GPU.
  - Model cache: Setup downloads the Hugging Face bundle automatically; set HF_HOME only if you want a different cache directory.
- NIM
  - Self-host: x86_64 or arm64 Linux meeting the NIM prerequisites, Docker, NVIDIA Driver, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, and an NGC API key.
  - NIM API endpoint (not recommended for production runs): HTTP access through NVIDIA build.nvidia.com via Shell and Python scripts, no local GPU or model installation required.
About RFD4-Proteina
The search loop shown in Figure 1, above, is where RFD4-Proteina focuses its compute.
During inference-time reasoning search, the model denoises generation trajectories to obtain structures, scores these designs, retains and branches promising partial states, and continues until the generation criteria are reached.
Rewards can measure geometry, interactions, or independent prediction confidence. This kind of extra search optimizes designs against a specified objective to yield higher-scoring designs. Later in this tutorial, you will see how a user can enable this functionality through the open model and the NIM.
RFD4-Proteina is faster and uses less memory than RFD3 for several reasons:
- It works on a residue-level latent representation instead of atom-level, which avoids memory blow-up.
- Engineering of the diffusion process cuts sampling from about 400 steps in Proteina-Complexa to 60, and computation is concentrated on the parts of the process that matter most thanks to reasoning capabilities in the model.
- Inference-time search is also faster, since the oracles (OF3 and physics methods like tmol) are CUDA-accelerated.
- The model and kernels were co-designed with the cuEquivariance and BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BIR) teams for speed and scalability.
From a molecular design idea to candidate designs
The workflow in Figure 3, above, demonstrates how to use RFD4-Proteina to go from a scientific objective to candidates for experimental testing. An agent can coordinate these tools and track results, while scientists define the objectives and use experimental evidence to guide the next round.
Preparing the molecular inputs and environment
Begin by defining the criteria and requirements for generation. For example, RFD4-Proteina expects users to define what may change, what must remain fixed, and computational and experimental success criteria.
Use AtomWorks to generate /manipulate the input data. AtomWorks is the molecular data layer used to prepare structures and design annotations for RFD4-Proteina. Its Python and PyMOL workflows prepare fixed atoms, designable residues, hotspots, and molecular context. Preserve the supplied ligand or motif chemistry when designing surrounding protein.
Both the open model and NIM accept annotated CIFs or a condition specification plus its source structure. The specification below fixes the target and defines the new binder.
The repository’s cropped PD-L1 structure from PDB 5O45 serves as the target. Fix the target’s sequence and backbone coordinates, allow its side chains to repack, and direct binder generation toward hotspot atoms on Tyr56, Met115, and Tyr123. The new binder has 100–150 residues, with free sequence and coordinates.
Clone the repository, then run the examples from its root. This writes pdl1.json; both paths use the same target CIF and conditions.
git clone https://github.com/RosettaCommons/RFD4-Proteina.git
cd RFD4-Proteina
cat > pdl1.json <<'JSON'
{
  "pdl1_binder": {
    "input": "docs/examples/inputs/5o45_cropped.cif",
    "contig": "100-150, /0, A17-131",
    "conditions": {
      "C_CRD": {"true": [{"select": "sel('A') and is_protein_backbone"}]},
      "C_SEQ": {"true": [{"select": "sel('A')"}]},
      "C_HOT": {"true": [
        {"select": "sel('A/*/56/[CG,OH]')"},
        {"select": "sel('A/*/115/[CG,SD]')"},
        {"select": "sel('A/*/123/[CD2,OH]')"}
      ]}
    }
  }
}
JSON
Open model setup
On a supported Linux/CUDA system, install the repository environment with a current uv release (validated with 0.12.24). If uv is already installed, update it first so it recognizes CUDA 13.2. Setup caches the Hugging Face model bundle, including the paired autoencoder. While the model repository is private, authenticate with hf auth login using an account with access.
bash setup.sh --native
source .venv/bin/activate
NIM environment setup
To host the NIM, run this block in Bash on a supported GPU host with Docker and NVIDIA Container Toolkit installed.
read -rsp 'NGC API key: ' NGC_API_KEY; echo
export NGC_API_KEY
printf '%s' "$NGC_API_KEY" | docker login nvcr.io \
  -u '$oauthtoken' --password-stdin
image=nvcr.io/nim/ipd/rfd4-proteina:latest
docker pull "$image"
export RFD4_NIM_IMAGE="$(docker image inspect \
  --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' "$image")"
printf '%s\n' "$RFD4_NIM_IMAGE" > nim-image.txt
export LOCAL_NIM_CACHE="$HOME/.cache/nim"
mkdir -p "$LOCAL_NIM_CACHE"
docker run -d --rm --name rfd4-proteina \
  --runtime=nvidia --gpus 'device=0' -p 8000:8000 \
  -e NGC_API_KEY -v "$LOCAL_NIM_CACHE":/opt/nim/.cache \
  --shm-size=16g "$RFD4_NIM_IMAGE"
Generate sequences and structures
Open-model generation
Save the following as design.py in the repository root. The same script supports generation and search. Proteina.from_pretrained("nvidia/RFD4-Proteina") loads the current Hugging Face model and paired autoencoder checkpoints.
import hydra
from rfd4_proteina import Proteina
from rfproteina.generate import run_generation
@hydra.main(config_path="configs", config_name="inference", version_base="1.3")
def main(cfg):
    model = Proteina.from_pretrained("nvidia/RFD4-Proteina")
    run_generation(cfg, model=model)
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
Generate one candidate from the repository root:
python design.py inputs=pdl1.json out_dir=runs/pdl1-open seed=42 compile_lengths=null
Outputs are saved under runs/pdl1-open/inference_samples/. Add num_replicates=10 for ten candidates and choose a new out_dir for each run. Hugging Face caches downloads; add revision=”<commit>” to from_pretrained to reproduce a particular model version.
NIM generation
Save this as nim_client.py. It sends the PD-L1 condition spec and target CIF to the NIM, then saves generated structures and response metrics.
import json
from pathlib import Path
import requests
spec = json.loads(Path("pdl1.json").read_text())["pdl1_binder"]
target = Path(spec["input"])
spec["input"] = target.name
payload = {
    "task": "motif_scaffolding",
    "input": {"format": "condition_spec", "example_id": "pdl1_binder",
              "spec": spec, "files": [{"filename": target.name, "content": target.read_text()}]},
    "sampling": {"num_replicates": 1, "seed": 42},
    "metrics": {"tags": ["design", "hotspot_conditioning"]},
}
def submit(payload, out):
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    response = requests.post("http://localhost:8000/biology/ipd/rfd4-proteina/generative",
                             json=payload, timeout=1800)
    response.raise_for_status()
    result = response.json()
    (out / "response.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    for i, design in enumerate(result["designs"]):
        dest = out / f"design-{i}.cif"
        dest.write_text(design["structure"]["content"])
        print(design["design_id"], dest)
if __name__ == "__main__":
    submit(payload, Path("runs/pdl1-nim"))
Install requests and run the client from the repository root. Keep pdl1.json beside the target CIF.
python -m pip install requests
python nim_client.py
Performance optimizations across open model and NIM
For faster design iteration, the BioIR backend accelerates RFD4-Proteina by 1.37–1.73× over the default compiled backend across six tested Hopper GPU configurations (see Figure 4, below). On H100 PCIe, total suite time drops from 161 to 111 seconds, about 31% less runtime. The benchmark uses batch size 1 and sums warm end-to-end timings across 15 sequence lengths (128–1,024 tokens).
Inference-time search with external oracles
Open-model search with OpenFold3
Install the optional OpenFold3 runtime and weights with ./scripts/download_example_data.sh ./data_path. Set OF3_IMAGE, OF3_MODEL_DIR, and OF3_JAX_CACHE_DIR to the paths it prints, then run mkdir -p "$OF3_JAX_CACHE_DIR". Apptainer must be available on the GPU host.
This example uses the AlphaFold3 codebase, which is released under the open-source Apache 2.0 license, and the OpenFold3 model weights, which are also released under the Apache 2.0 license.
Reuse design.py with the search preset:
python design.py inference_experiment=inference_beam_example \
  metrics/refolding_oracles=of3 inputs=pdl1.json subset_to_examples=null \
  num_replicates=1 out_dir=runs/pdl1-open-search seed=42 compile_lengths=null
The preset uses two branches, a beam width of three, and scoring at steps 20, 40, 50 and 60. It rewards the designed chain’s OpenFold3 pLDDT (oracle.plddt_coi), with a floor of 50, and saves qualifying rollouts at reward 80. This measures confidence in the binder, not evidence of binding; inspect interface and refolding metrics separately. Outputs are under runs/pdl1-open-search/.
NIM search with OpenFold3
Save this as nim_search_request.py. It reuses the PD-L1 input and submits a reward-guided OpenFold3 search.
from pathlib import Path
from nim_client import payload, submit
key = "oracle_of3_nvcf.overall_plddt"
payload["sampling"]["num_steps"] = 60
payload["search"] = {
    "step_checkpoints": [0, 20, 40, 50, 60],
    "n_branch": 2, "beam_width": 3,
    "reward_metrics_tags": ["unconditional_refolding"],
    "weights": {key: 1.0}, "clip_values": {key: {"min": 50.0}},
    "intermediate_save_min_reward": 80.0,
}
payload["metrics"] = {"tags": ["design", "unconditional_refolding"]}
submit(payload, Path("runs/pdl1-nim-search"))
Enable the NIM oracle
Mount the OpenFold3 reward.py callback as described in the oracle guide. It reports oracle_of3_nvcf.overall_plddt for the whole complex; evaluate the binder interface separately.
Save the OpenFold3 NVCF callback from the oracle guide as reward.py and export OF3_NIM_API_KEY with an NVCF invoke credential. Relaunch the service with this callback:
docker stop rfd4-proteina
docker run -d --rm --name rfd4-proteina \
  --gpus 'device=0' -p 8000:8000 --shm-size=16g \
  -e NGC_API_KEY -v "$LOCAL_NIM_CACHE:/opt/nim/.cache" \
  -v "$PWD/reward.py:/opt/nim/reward.py:ro" \
  -e NIM_ALLOW_ORACLE_PLUGIN=true -e OF3_NIM_API_KEY \
  "$RFD4_NIM_IMAGE"
Run the search script. It saves designs and response metrics under runs/pdl1-nim-search/.
python nim_search_request.py
This request uses two branches, checkpoints [0, 20, 40, 50, 60], and a beam width of three. It sets a reward floor of 50 and saves intermediate designs with scores of at least 80. These are example thresholds for OpenFold3 overall pLDDT, a prediction-confidence metric for the whole complex. Search-time reward tags and final reporting tags are separate.
Search output counts vary. Inspect the generated CIFs and retained metrics before selecting candidates. Include refolding and scoring in compute comparisons.
Filter and rank candidates
Check constraints, motif preservation, clashes, interfaces, refolding consistency, and structural diversity metrics. OpenFold3, and RoseTTAFold3 provide prediction options; TMol provides Rosetta-inspired all-atom scoring and optimization.
Common metrics include ipTM (interface Predicted Template Modeling), ipSAE (interaction prediction Score from Aligned Errors), and RMSD (Root Mean Square Deviation) scores from protein structure prediction models like OpenFold 3, along with interaction energies from physics-based models like TMol.
Test experimentally and refine
Table 1, above, highlights RFD4-Proteina’s broad range of capabilities across molecular tasks. It not only supports this variety of tasks, in the accompanying manuscript it is demonstrated that the model is also the state-of-the-art model across this breadth of molecular tasks, both in terms of output quality and throughput.
Turn that throughput into scientific progress by selecting diverse candidates for synthesis, expression, and task-specific assays. Feed experimental outcomes back into the objective, constraints, and ranking criteria for the next round.
Run a campaign with an AI agent
Use the rfd4-proteina-campaign skill to coordinate generation, search and evaluation with a record of inputs, model versions and compute use. The rfd4-proteina-package skill produces a results archive with structures, metrics and a filtering report.
Use rfd4-proteina-campaign to design 100–150-residue PD-L1 binders from pdl1.json, preserving its target and hotspot constraints. Use the Hugging Face model via from_pretrained and OpenFold3. Agree on criteria and a compute budget, then compare generation with reward-guided search and run a campaign via rfd4-proteina-campaign. Return up to ten diverse candidates with scores and compute usage; package the results with rfd4-proteina-package.
Apply the workflow to your design problem
RFD4-Proteina combines fast generation, smart search, and agent programmability in one workflow. Joint sequence and all-atom structure generation streamlines candidate creation, while reward-guided search focuses compute on task-specific objectives. Shared condition specifications connect both form factors to common evaluation tools, and NIM’s HTTP API lets agents submit requests and inspect results.
Use the open model for method development and NIM for application integration with optional BioIR acceleration, bringing computational exploration and experimental feedback into an iterative design campaign.
Get started with the RFD4-Proteina NIM microservice, explore the open model on GitHub, or point your agent at BioNeMo Agent Toolkit skills.

articles.title: Yaiza Canosa, exitosa empresaria española: “Conozco más fontaneros bajándose de un Land Rover que a desarrolladores”
articles.text:
Yaiza Canosa, en una entrevista en Actitud Constante, compara a los fontaneros con los programadores informáticos, afirmando: “Conozco a más fontaneros bajándose de un Land Rover que a desarrolladores de IT”.
Canosa cuestiona el menor reconocimiento que reciben los oficios frente a las empresas de tecnología y las startups, al plantear esta comparación sobre las personas que conoce.
Los oficios que apenas aparecen en las redes
Con la atención que se ha prestado a las startups, sostiene que se ha restado valor al trabajo manual y que, en las redes sociales, los profesionales de los talleres y las instalaciones no tienen visibilidad, al tiempo que afirma que en esos sectores “se puede crecer” y constituir empresas.
Canosa, al centrar la conversación en las actividades cotidianas con la inteligencia artificial, sostiene que su uso en los procesos ayudará a optimizar los resultados, pero que hay oficios que no pueden automatizarse. La declaración que hace de estas profesiones sugiere que la IA no las dejará sin trabajo, aunque esa opinión no demuestra plena inmunidad contra ese riesgo. Canosa da a entender que podría valer la pena emprender un negocio de talleres en lugar de desarrollar software.
La falta de profesionales también aparece en los datos
En España, según el informe del SEPE de 2026, hay dificultades persistentes para encontrar fontaneros y electricistas que cubran las vacantes. El Servicio Público de Empleo Estatal relaciona la falta de candidatos, de competencias técnicas y de experiencia profesional con la dificultad para cubrir las vacantes.
La dificultad a la que se enfrentan los empleadores para contratar indica cierta oportunidad para quienes adquieran las cualificaciones necesarias.
Qué hay detrás de la promesa de aprender un oficio en tres meses
En el texto de una publicación de Expertia Formaciones, en la plataforma de TikTok, se dice que una persona puede formarse en ciertos oficios en tres meses, sin contar con estudios previos.
La electricidad y la fontanería se mencionan como alternativas a la universidad, con la posibilidad, según el centro, de un salario mejor que el de algunos puestos universitarios.
TodoFP da información para determinar la formación que lleva a un título oficial. Fabricación y Montaje, con un total de 2.000 horas de estudios, figura como un título básico, entre cuyas salidas profesionales está la fontanería.
Lo que hay que tener claro es que el hecho de que existan programas más cortos no significa que puedan considerarse equivalentes a este título oficial.
Menos candidatos por cada oferta de fontanero
En el análisis de InfoJobs sobre oficios técnicos, la información publicada el 29 de abril de 2026, basada en datos de 2025, muestra 19 candidatos por vacante para la profesión de fontanero, en comparación con 56 en el conjunto de la plataforma. Con estos datos se puede ver que hay menos competencia por las ofertas de fontanero que la media general, pero no garantizan que una vacante esté disponible para un candidato ni que quienes se inscriben cumplan los requisitos del puesto.
De acuerdo con el informe de InfoJobs y Esade de 2025, que clasifica las categorías por niveles salariales, informática y telecomunicaciones ocupa el segundo lugar con un salario medio bruto anual ofertado de 35.031 euros. Por su parte, el salario medio ofertado en todas las vacantes de la plataforma asciende a 27.336 euros. La diferencia salarial mencionada está sujeta a las condiciones de las ofertas publicadas y describe promedios, no un salario específico para cada puesto.
Al comparar los ingresos brutos de un fontanero con la remuneración de un trabajador de TI, se deben tener en cuenta las diferencias entre un salario mensual neto y una factura.
La cantidad de ingresos brutos que una empresa o un profesional obtiene por un trabajo puede incluir importes destinados a materiales y otros gastos de la actividad, que deben descontarse para calcular sus ingresos netos. Al buscar trabajo asalariado, es importante preguntarse si la remuneración se expresa en bruto o en neto y si hay varias pagas al año.
Qué puede cambiar la IA en estos trabajos
La Organización Internacional del Trabajo (OIT) observa, en su informe sobre exposición a la IA de 2025, que uno de cada cuatro trabajadores en el mundo está en una ocupación expuesta, al menos en parte, a la inteligencia artificial generativa.
La OIT considera más probable que la IA transforme las tareas laborales que la sustitución completa de los trabajadores, ya que la mayoría de las ocupaciones conserva tareas que requieren intervención humana. La exposición a la IA no implica necesariamente la sustitución, aunque tampoco permite descartar pérdidas de empleo.
El estudio explicado por las economistas de la OIT, Isaure Delaporte y Veronica Escudero, en una publicación del 29 de septiembre de 2026, examinó la importancia de las habilidades presentes en la demanda local de empleo ante las tecnologías digitales.
Sus conclusiones, que abarcan más de mil áreas geográficas en sesenta y nueve países, entran en cuestiones sobre la relación entre las habilidades y las nuevas tecnologías. La investigación analizó cuarenta tecnologías emergentes, un campo más amplio que la inteligencia artificial generativa.
Las dos economistas creen que, aunque la creciente disponibilidad de tecnologías digitales puede transformar muchas ocupaciones, no existen habilidades específicas que sean universales y protejan a todos los trabajadores contra los cambios.
Entre las habilidades asociadas a una mejor respuesta del empleo se encuentran la alfabetización digital, como los conocimientos informáticos básicos, y capacidades como la gestión de proyectos y de personas. Los consejos para un trabajador digital que busque un cambio de carrera hacia los oficios implican la necesidad de adquirir las competencias pertinentes para el puesto y el sector. La elección de la profesión no sustituye el estudio de sus aspectos técnicos.

articles.title: Browsers Block eMudhra Intermediate CAs Over Recoverable Private Keys
articles.text:
The private keys associated with eight intermediate certificates issued by Indian certificate authority (CA) eMudhra have been compromised, and root programs and trust stores have started blocking them.
The certificates were issued in April 2025, and some of the compromised keys could allow attackers to generate fraudulent certificates and impersonate any website.
On October 17, Mozilla and Google blocked the certificates in Firefox and Chrome. Apple and Microsoft blocked them on October 19 and October 20, respectively. Sectigo took revocation steps too, and Cloudflare patched its services.
eMudhra revoked the compromised certificates, and the issue was communicated to downstream trust stores.
“The private keys for these certificates were generated with insufficient randomness (i.e., weak cryptographic entropy), enabling anyone to forge trusted HTTPS certificates to impersonate any website against clients that have not yet removed trust in those CAs,” Google explains.
Although the certificates have been blocked and revoked, some clients may require software updates to ensure that the compromised intermediates are no longer trusted.
Mozilla’s Dennis Jackson has published a tool to check whether clients still trust the compromised certificates. He also explains that the private keys were incorrectly generated and could be retrieved from the certificates.
In fact, Jackson warned that several individuals have independently retrieved the keys, as the process is fairly easy and fast.
“The private keys are effectively all-zeroes apart from the last byte. They can be recovered near instantly via the baby-step giant-step discrete log algorithm,” Jackson said.
There appears to be no evidence in Certificate Transparency (CT) logs that the keys were used maliciously before revocation, but not all clients enforce CT, and threat actors may have used them to impersonate those clients.
According to eMudhra, a flaw in the script used during the key generation ceremony created a second, weaker key pair, which was mistakenly used to create the certificate signing requests because its labels were similar to those of the original keys.
“Some additional context – these issuers created were meant for export to our US and European data centers to solve data sovereignty issues for some of our customers (but never ended up operationally in production except for one),” the CA said.
“There were human errors in multiple steps of the process that resulted in significant flaws in the key lifecycle integrity process for this KGC. We are now digging deeper for code flaws, process gaps, and maker/checker controls specific to this issue. Over the next week, we will reverify every key ceremony we have done,” eMudhra added.

articles.title: Cilium 1.20 Expands Gateway API and Opens eBPF Datapath for Kubernetes
articles.text:
Cilium 1.20 has been released with broader Kubernetes Gateway API support, an extensible eBPF datapath and further work on sidecarless mutual TLS. The release also makes the newer netkit network device easier to introduce across Kubernetes fleets that run different Linux kernel versions.
In the release announcement, Cilium engineers Nico Vibert and Donia Chaiehloudj describe Gateway API as a "much broader traffic management layer" in version 1.20. Cilium moves from Gateway API 1.4 to 1.6, adding ExternalAuth, ListenerSets, CORS filtering, TCPRoute and UDPRoute. These additions bring HTTP authentication and non-HTTP services such as databases and DNS under the same Kubernetes API used for web and gRPC traffic.
According to Vibert and Chaiehloudj, ExternalAuth allows an HTTPRoute to consult an external authorisation service before sending a request to an application. Depending on the response, the gateway can forward the request, redirect a user to a login page, or reject it. The authoriser can also pass identity headers to the application. TCPRoute and UDPRoute remove the need to fall back to LoadBalancer or NodePort Services for plain Layer 4 traffic.
ListenerSets address a separate ownership problem. Application teams can add listeners from their own namespaces while a platform team retains control of the shared Gateway and decides which namespaces may extend it. Platform engineer Mohamed Salem BEN ATAIA wrote on LinkedIn that ListenerSets close the gap between teams owning Routes and needing a central change for a new hostname or port. In his assessment, "It removes a platform bottleneck."
"Gateway API becomes a much broader traffic management layer."
Nico Vibert and Donia Chaiehloudj
The direction is consistent with work elsewhere in Kubernetes networking. InfoQ previously reported that the Kubernetes community recommends Gateway API as organisations move away from the retired Ingress NGINX controller. AWS also reached general availability with Gateway API support in its Load Balancer Controller, covering HTTP and gRPC through Application Load Balancer and TCP and UDP through Network Load Balancer. Cilium's implementation differs in that the same project can provide the CNI, service networking and gateway functions.
A second change opens Cilium's eBPF datapath to third-party plugins. Previously, cloud providers that needed custom instrumentation or networking behaviour had to contribute the change upstream or maintain a fork. A plugin now runs as a separate process and can be built, versioned and upgraded independently. Cilium communicates with it through a small custom resource and a gRPC interface.
"Datapath plugins, developed by Google, make Cilium less like a sealed networking appliance and more like a network operating system."
Nico Vibert and Donia Chaiehloudj
The plugin mechanism is beta and is not presented as a general extension system for ordinary cluster users. Cilium's documentation says it is intended for operators with detailed knowledge of Cilium's internals. It also warns that a plugin can break Cilium or weaken security, and that maintainers may need to update their code as Cilium's internal architecture changes.
Cilium 1.20 also introduces automatic selection of the pod datapath. Setting bpf.datapathMode=auto makes each agent test its host at start-up, use netkit where the kernel supports it, and fall back to a traditional veth pair elsewhere. Netkit requires Linux 6.8 or later. The default remains veth, so existing installations do not change unless an operator opts in. Vibert and Chaiehloudj say this avoids dividing mixed fleets into separate node pools solely to select a datapath mode.
The fourth main area is ztunnel, the per-node proxy introduced in Cilium 1.19 for sidecarless mutual TLS. Version 1.20 adds a choice between an internal certificate authority and SPIRE-issued workload identities, together with Prometheus metrics for enrolment and connection health. Ztunnel holds a new connection while it establishes TLS 1.3 over an HBONE tunnel, avoiding the first-packet loss possible with Cilium's older mutual-authentication design and encrypting supported TCP traffic between pods on the same node.
This has parallels with Istio's ambient mode, and the Cilium implementation builds on the ztunnel project originally created for Istio. Cilium's ztunnel remains beta, while its older Mutual Authentication feature is now deprecated. Operators considering an upgrade should also consult the 1.20 release notes, which identify possible action for users of legacy Mutual Authentication, Kafka-aware policies, Envoy Go extensions, custom CNI configuration and several deprecated APIs.

articles.title: Q&A: Why CoLab is in the “sweet spot” of engineering software | BetaKit
articles.text:
The small but mighty St. John’s, Nfld. tech scene has garnered attention in recent months for being an “unlikely” hub for startups, and rapidly scaling companies such as CoLab Software have helped build that reputation.
“That’s a huge Newfoundland advantage… the connections are so rich between people that people want to be here and they want to come back.”
CoLab makes an AI-powered engineering design platform that helps engineers plan out complex products before they are manufactured. The scaleup was founded in 2017 by two Memorial University graduates who did co-ops in Silicon Valley and later went through Y Combinator before returning to build in Newfoundland. Since then, it has raised more than $100 million USD ($140 million CAD) from local and US investors, grown its team to roughly 250 people, and was reportedly last valued at around $500 million USD. It has also landed big-name clients like Bombardier and Ford.
As CoLab’s chief strategy officer, Taylor Young works side by side with co-founders Adam Keating and Jeremy Andrews to guide the company’s direction, orchestrate partnerships, and lead corporate development. BetaKit sat down with Young to learn more about CoLab’s business journey and the advantage of running the business from Newfoundland.
The following conversation has been compiled from BetaKit’s interview with Young, as well as her on-stage remarks at the techNL conference on Tuesday. It has been edited for clarity and length.
CoLab has been around for nine years now and has a mature product. What’s the landscape like for engineering software and AI?
The engineering software landscape has gotten almost no attention over the past 30 years. When you compare it to almost any other B2B (business-to-business) realm, from life-saving medical devices to airplanes to rocket ships, they are still using 30-year-old technology.
You have the incumbents—the computer-aided design and product life-cycle management companies—then you have thousands, lately, of very small technology startups that were not around when CoLab started, and then you have a small group of us that have been doing this for 10 years or so.
For our customers who are desperately trying to understand how they transform in the age of AI, and who face increasing pressure to do everything faster, who do they bet on? There’s no one right answer, but we are getting chosen a lot as that partner, I think, because we’re in a real sweet spot of maturity.
In a fast-growing startup, how do you prioritize what to work on and what to put aside?
Sometimes, some things feel good to solve because they’re easy or actionable, but that doesn’t mean they’re the things you should work on. In the early days of getting a company off the ground, you have to train yourself to say no to most things.
We needed to pick a market that was small enough that we could win, but referenceable enough to other markets that it could help us tap into that growth. For us, it was industrial equipment and HVAC—not the most exciting technology in the world. We had to do that for a long time and focus on a small subset of use cases until we earned the right to do more.
How do you follow where the market’s heading versus leveraging feedback from customers?
Customers show you the problems and, generally, we show them potential solutions. I think that was simpler before AI-driven product development. We used to be able to identify problems and build solutions specific to a use case, and it was very clear for a customer to wrap their heads around if they wanted it or not. Now we can build things a lot faster that are a lot broader.
We’ve gotten into a mentality of trying more and putting more in front of the user. We work with very large companies—that means the person who is buying the tool, and the people who will use it, could be several layers removed, with hundreds of people between them. So you have to put stuff in front of them and wait and see.
What would you say is the biggest benefit of building a company in St. John’s?
I think we are subject to a lot less noise than your average Silicon Valley startup. What that forces us to do is focus on our customers, use that as the most important source of information for what we’re going to do, and to pay a little bit less attention to what everybody else is doing.
“I think we are subject to a lot less noise than your average Silicon Valley startup.”
Obviously we need to understand what’s changing, but our customers are often fairly removed from that, and there’s an enormous amount of noise and distraction if you spend too much time concerning yourself with the startup ecosystem.
We have an amazing team based here that intends to be a part of CoLab the whole way. They have an emotional connection to CoLab and they want to see it through. From what I understand, that’s unusual in other parts of the world where people are focused on growing a career more than they’re focused on growing a company.
I was going to ask about challenges with talent retention, but it sounds like you have a loyal core.
That’s a huge Newfoundland advantage. I’m sure it’s not specific to this province, but it’s an advantage that we’ve found. I think the connections are so rich between people that people want to be here and they want to come back. Obviously, some people are dying to get to Toronto or New York or Montréal, but by and large, we see that going away is a short-term decision. They’re going to go work in the Bay Area, and then they’re going to figure out how to get back.
Feature image courtesy techNL. Image by Ritche Perez.

articles.title: Eliminating traffic deaths
articles.text:
Eliminating traffic deaths
Deploying simple, proven methods for making our roads safer could save more than 1 million lives worldwide each year.
Every year, traffic crashes kill more than one million people, and they’re the leading cause of death for children and young adults. In the US, 100 people a day lose their lives this way, in many cases not on highways but on rural and local streets. “Traffic deaths are a leading cause of preventable death, yet we treat it like it’s inevitable,” says Leah Shahum, founder and director of the Vision Zero Network, a nonprofit focused on making streets less deadly.
The sticking points
The causes of a crash can be muddy. Drivers make mistakes like speeding or getting distracted, but infrastructure fails them too: Perhaps they were on a road built for speed and not safety, in a screen-filled vehicle, or at an intersection where pedestrians, cyclists, and other cars aren’t visible.
Cheap and proven traffic-calming opportunities abound—from using planters to tighten intersections to lowering speed limits—but government logjams and red tape can be speed bumps. “There’s so many moving parts,” says Laura Sandt of the University of North Carolina Highway Safety Research Center. “On the flip side, it shows that we have so many opportunities for injury prevention.”
The progress
The total number of traffic deaths has increased over the last century. And though the US rate has dipped from a peak of 30.8 deaths per 100,000 people in the 1930s, the past decade has seen a concerning jump in deadly pedestrian incidents. At the same time, communities are waking up to the essential role of traffic safety policy, Shahum says.
One success story is Hoboken, New Jersey, which hasn’t had a traffic fatality since 2017. This is due to a combination of efforts like boosting investment in public transit, promoting walkability by extending curbs, and using cameras to identify crash-prone intersections in need of a redesign. But even there, obstacles remain. If an intersection hasn’t been proved to be deadly, for example, it can be an uphill battle to argue for removing parking spaces to widen curbs. “You’re kind of selling insurance through these improvements, and that’s not always easy,” says Greg Francese, the city’s acting director of transportation and parking.
There’s also no silver bullet that will work everywhere. Situated directly across the river from New York City, Hoboken is a highly transit-oriented city of less than 60,000 people. Success there might not translate to traffic-death hot spots like Memphis or Dallas. But it’s not impossible. Take Edmonton, Alberta, a sprawling, car-centric Canadian city of around one million people: Between 2015 and 2020, it cut traffic fatalities by 63% and serious injuries by 40% by adjusting speed limits and improving signals at crosswalks.
Progress meter ............ 6
We know how to tweak intersections and adjust traffic signals. Getting the funding and will to roll out those changes is the big red light.
