articles.title: tvOS 27.2 : votre Apple TV 4K va gagner trois nouvelles fonctionnalités
articles.text:
Apple prépare une mise à jour qui devrait rendre l’Apple TV 4K plus agréable à utiliser au quotidien. Au programme, des économiseurs d’écran plus variés, un choix plus précis des photos affichées et de nouvelles options d’accessibilité dans l’application Apple TV.
Prévue pour la semaine prochaine, tvOS 27.2 apportera trois nouveautés aux utilisateurs de l’Apple TV 4K. Apple s’attaque notamment aux économiseurs d’écran, avec davantage de liberté pour choisir ce qui s’affiche sur le téléviseur lorsque celui-ci n’est pas utilisé. L’application Apple TV évolue elle aussi, avec une option destinée à faciliter l’accès à certains films et séries.
Des économiseurs d’écran plus variés et personnalisables
Jusqu’ici, il fallait obligatoirement choisir parmi les catégories d’économiseurs d’écran de tvOS : les paysages aériens, les souvenirs et diaporamas, les portraits ou encore Snoopy. Avec la nouvelle option « Aléatoire », l’Apple TV 4K pourra dorénavant alterner entre toutes ces catégories au fil de la journée. Cela permettra notamment aux utilisateurs de varier les images affichées sur leur téléviseur sans devoir modifier manuellement leurs préférences.
La mise à jour donne aussi davantage de contrôle sur les photos personnelles. Dans les catégories « Souvenirs et diaporamas » et « Portraits », il sera maintenant possible de sélectionner directement les clichés à afficher depuis un iPhone ou un iPad. Jusqu’à présent, l’utilisation de sa photothèque comme économiseur d’écran impliquait de laisser l’Apple TV accéder à l’ensemble des photos.
La langue des signes arrive dans l’application Apple TV
La troisième nouveauté concerne les personnes sourdes ou malentendantes qui utilisent la langue des signes. Sur certains films et épisodes de séries compatibles, l’application Apple TV permettra d’activer cette option directement depuis les commandes du lecteur vidéo. Deux langues sont pour l’instant prises en charge : l’ASL (langue des signes américaine) et la BSL (langue des signes britannique).
D’autres évolutions sont prévues, mais elles ne font pas partie de tvOS 27.2. L’Apple TV 4K de quatrième génération, dont la sortie est annoncée pour le 13 novembre prochain, doit notamment prendre en charge Siri avec des fonctions d’intelligence artificielle, qui ne sont pas encore disponibles en France, ainsi qu’une configuration de son surround reposant sur quatre HomePod.
Source : 9to5Mac

articles.title: How NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture Secures and Governs AI Agent Workloads at Scale | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
Autonomous agents can work for hours on complex tasks, accessing files, tools, the internet, and spawning other agents to collaborate with. Executing complex tasks over long time horizons leads to compounding risk: the agents may download code, build new tools, request additional privileges, and touch more of the underlying infrastructure.
The agents’ action paths are determined as they work and reason through the steps needed to complete their goals. As they interact with the tools and systems around them, they adapt their reasoning and behavior to achieve their task.
The adaptability of agents is what makes them so powerful, but they are goal-oriented and may not prioritize safety in pursuit of their objectives. In order for agents to work both autonomously and safely, we need to build environments that provide control and visibility in what the agent is doing.
An agent cannot govern itself. Security and governance belong in the infrastructure the agent operates in.
OpenShell provides deterministic governance outside of the agent’s reach
NVIDIA OpenShell is an open-source runtime to build the security and governance needed for agentic systems into the computing infrastructure. OpenShell defines and enforces which systems and data an agent can access, from files and internet services to systems that interact with physical devices.
It is the foundation of the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture for building safe AI agents. OpenShell treats agent workloads as untrusted throughout execution. An agent is given access to what it needs, when it needs it.
OpenShell has four key components:
- Gateway: The control plane that manages sandbox lifecycles and policies
- Supervisor: Checks outbound requests against policy and mediates access to credentials. This runs completely separate to the sandbox
- Sandbox: Isolates the agent workload and restricts filesystem and process access
- Policy prover: Adds formal verification, checking whether a policy’s permissions stay within an organization-defined ceiling.
As the agents evolve, these components provide the infrastructure controls that allow them to work safely.
Extending and integrating OpenShell
Extensibility is a core principle of OpenShell’s design. Supervisor middleware lets you inspect, block, or change the content that an agent sends and receives over the network as an additional enforcement layer. Gateway interceptors let operators add deployment-specific governance to OpenShell control-plane operations without modifying the gateway.
Organizations also need to establish who an agent acts for, what authority it holds, and whether an action fits the task. Identity, authorization, data protection, and auditing each address part of that problem. OpenShell provides enforcement points where those systems can be integrated.
In the reference architecture, OpenShell runs on NVIDIA Vera CPUs.
NVIDIA Vera, the compute layer beneath the controls
OpenShell defines what agents can do. Vera determines how fast they can do it. Agents operate through loops of dependent steps where each step must complete before the next begins: reasoning, calling tools, executing code, querying data.
AI factories run thousands of these loops concurrently, placing new demands on CPU architecture across five dimensions:
- They need massive core counts to run many concurrent workflows, and fast individual cores to shorten each sequential step.
- They need high-bandwidth fabric and memory to keep those cores fed with the live data agents depend on.
- They need massive I/O to move data at speed between CPUs, GPUs, storage, and network.
- They need hardware-enforced security, because agents increasingly operate on sensitive enterprise data and must be isolated from each other and the host.
- They need to deliver all of this within the power envelope of a modern data center (more agent work per watt, not just more raw performance).
NVIDIA calls this combination the max single-threaded CPU at scale, and NVIDIA Vera is built for it: massive Olympus cores, a second-generation Scalable Coherency Fabric, LPDDR5X memory, Gen 6 I/O, confidential computing, and an energy-efficient design purpose-built for power-limited data centers.
Three architectural properties make Vera fast for agent workloads
- First, 88 NVIDIA-designed Olympus cores with a 10-wide front end, neural branch predictor, and deep out-of-order execution deliver up to 2x performance on critical agentic workloads versus x86, shortening each tool call, code execution, and evaluation.
- Second, Vera’s second-generation Scalable Coherency Fabric provides up to 3x core-to-core bandwidth and up to 50% lower core-to-core latency than x86 alternatives, keeping data moving predictably under load. Vera also integrates 96 lanes of PCIe Gen 6, delivering the I/O bandwidth to connect GPUs, high-speed storage, and network at the throughput agentic infrastructure demands.
- Third, up to 1.2 TB/s of LPDDR5X memory bandwidth, with up to 40% lower loaded memory latency than chiplet-based designs, keeps agents supplied with the live context they need without stalling on memory access. LPDDR5X also makes Vera dramatically more efficient: Vera delivers 2x more performance per watt than x86 CPUs, while the LPDDR5X memory subsystem itself draws an order of magnitude less power than competing DDR5-based memory configurations, enabling more agent work within the same power envelope.
Agent workloads depend on sandboxes: isolated execution environments where agents run code, invoke tools, and complete tasks without interfering with each other or the host system. The denser and faster those sandboxes spin up, the more agent work a given infrastructure footprint can sustain.
CoreWeave, the AI cloud platform purpose-built for training and serving models at scale, found sandbox startup to be more than 3x faster on Vera than on x86, with a single rack supporting more than 11,000 concurrent agent environments.
Running Terminal Bench, which measures CPU performance across real agentic loop tasks, CoreWeave found Vera delivered 1.8x faster performance versus x86, across agentic tasks ranging from scripting to database recovery. That density and performance under load is what agent infrastructure actually requires.
NVIDIA BlueField and NVIDIA Sentry for hardware-enforced protection
OpenShell places authority outside the agent. For deployments that require additional protection, that separation can also extend into purpose-built silicon.
NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs provide a hardware-isolated trust domain outside the agent’s reach. In the OpenShell reference architecture, BlueField-4 sits in the I/O path between agents running on Vera and the models they access. NVIDIA Sentry, a security software framework built on NVIDIA DOCA, runs in this independent domain to continuously monitor agent behavior and enforce runtime policy.
NVIDIA Sentry observes requests and responses, networking and file activities, verifies identity and delegated authority, and analyzes selected host memory to detect deviations from authorized behavior without relying on agent self-reporting.
When it detects a threat or policy violation, BlueField-4 enforces policy in silicon, allowing NVIDIA Sentry to quarantine the agent within milliseconds. Together, they add an optional hardware safeguard alongside OpenShell’s software boundaries. Learn more about NVIDIA Sentry in this technical deep-dive.
Bringing secure agent runtimes to scale
Running agents in production requires infrastructure that can keep thousands of workflows moving while governing every action they take. Vera provides the compute, memory bandwidth, and I/O to sustain those workflows. OpenShell supplies the runtime boundaries that determine which actions execute and which resources agents can reach.
Together, Vera and OpenShell make secure agent execution a foundation for scale. Agents can run longer, use tools, and work with enterprise data within policies enforced outside their control. For deployments that require additional protection, NVIDIA Sentry on BlueField-4 adds independent monitoring and in-silicon enforcement.
The NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, where LLMs run, together with OpenShell and NVIDIA Sentry on BlueField-4, are the pillars of the OpenShell reference architecture. They form the complete stack for safe AI agents: a complete, hardware-rooted foundation that gives organizations the performance to make agents productive and the controls to keep their work within authorized boundaries.
Get started
To implement secure agent governance in your organization, begin with NVIDIA OpenShell, follow the documentation, and explore how NVIDIA Vera CPUs accelerate agent workloads.

articles.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
articles.text:
AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
- Summary:
- A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.
- Share:
Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.
How Scientists Tested Perceptions of AI Consciousness
Published in the journal Cognition, the study was led by Dr. Louis Longin of LMU's Chair of Philosophy of Mind, working alongside Dr. Bahador Bahrami, Professor Ophelia Deroy, and other researchers.
"Whereas previous studies have typically asked general questions about whether AI actually has mental states, our study is the first to directly compare how people attribute the same mental states to AI and humans behaving in exactly the same way, under identical circumstances," says Longin.
"We may be using mental terms to refer to AI, but this may only be because we lack better words," says Ophelia Deroy, philosopher and a senior author of the study. "After all, AI is trained to act and speak like a human, so these descriptions seem natural."
To investigate how people judge consciousness, the researchers conducted experiments involving nearly 1,100 participants. One group read brief descriptions of artificial agents that showed different levels of responsiveness to their environments. For example, some agents reacted to sounds or recognized the emotional states of others.
Another group encountered the same situations, except the characters were described as humans rather than AI systems. Participants then evaluated how conscious or aware each character seemed to be of its surroundings.
A Surprising Gap Between Human and AI Consciousness
The experiments revealed that responsiveness influenced how participants judged both humans and artificial intelligence. Characters that reacted more actively to their surroundings were generally considered more conscious and more aware.
However, a striking difference emerged when participants evaluated consciousness specifically. Even the most responsive AI was rated as less conscious than the least responsive human. In other words, identical behavior did not lead people to assign the same level of consciousness to humans and machines.
The results changed considerably when participants were asked about awareness instead. For this characteristic, judgments of humans and AI followed largely similar patterns, suggesting that people interpret awareness and consciousness in fundamentally different ways.
"There is a growing worry in public discussion that people will see AI behaving in a human-like way and start treating these systems as if they had human-like mental states," says Longin, lead author of the study. "We found something much more nuanced: People are quite willing to say that an AI notices things and is aware of its surroundings. But they clearly draw a line when it comes to the term 'consciousness'. People consistently attribute less consciousness to AI than humans -- even when their behavior is identical."
Although people sometimes describe AI as conscious when discussing its actions, the findings indicate that they still distinguish between artificial systems and human minds.
Why One Word Changes How We Perceive AI
The researchers believe the difference between consciousness and awareness offers an important insight into how people understand artificial intelligence.
Awareness is a relatively neutral term that can describe an agent's ability to detect and respond to information in its environment. Consciousness, however, carries deeper implications about subjective experience and what it means to have an inner mental life.
Because awareness focuses more directly on observable behavior, people appear comfortable applying it to both humans and AI. Consciousness carries a different meaning, leading people to judge the two much less similarly.
The findings also highlight why the language used to discuss artificial intelligence matters, particularly as AI systems become increasingly capable of producing convincing human behavior.
"Our study teaches us lessons for how we communicate about AI," says Bahador Bahrami, who is also a senior author of the study and an expert in social neuroscience. "Companies and journalists often reach for hyped descriptions of AI models, and credit them with intentions, plans, or even moral conscience and hesitation. What our study shows is that everyday judgments are much more discriminating: People do not simply put AI and humans on the same mental scale. But the boundary also depends on which terms we use. For more neutral descriptors such as 'awareness', the distinction can largely disappear. That makes our choice of language important."
Story Source:
Materials provided by Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Louis Longin, Jurgis Karpus, Nadine Meertens, Bahador Bahrami, Ophelia Deroy. AI is not as conscious as humans: Essentialism in mental state attributions to artificial systems. Cognition, 2027; 278: 106733 DOI: 10.1016/j.cognition.2026.106733

articles.title: Panne nationale Orange et Sosh depuis 6 heures : ce que l'on sait — Frandroid
articles.text:
Mise à jour à 17H00 : la panne Orange est toujours en cours. L’opérateur ne communique toujours pas sur l’incident depuis son tweet de 12h12.
La préfecture de la Drôme alerte sur la panne et rappel que les numéros d’urgences restent opérationnels.
La panne pourrait avoir été causée par une migration de la part d’Orange sur son coeur de réseau 5G, ce qui explique pourquoi le réseau Internet fixe ne semble pas touché par le problème.
Mise à jour à 14H00 : le réseau Orange est en panne depuis 2 heures et 40 minutes. L’opérateur a indiqué travailler à la résolution du problème, mais n’a toujours pas indiqué d’explications. Une panne de cette longueur est assez rare.
En quelques minutes, ils étaient plusieurs milliers à signaler une panne complète de réseau chez Orange et Sosh. L’origine des signalements est datée de mercredi 21 octobre autour de 11h20. On ne connaît pas l’origine de la panne pour le moment.
Sur Downdetector, on relève déjà plus de 6000 signalements. Nous avons également pu constater à la rédaction que nous n’avons plus de réseau Orange Mobile, quel que soit le lieu, que ça soit à Paris ou en Bretagne. Par contre, nos connexions fibre optique sont fonctionnelles.
On retrouve également de nombreux signalements d’abonnés sur les réseaux sociaux et notamment sur X : « Suis-je la seule à ne plus avoir de réseau sosh ? Il se passe quoi ? Je voulais sortir faire des courses mais je n’ai aucun moyen d’être joignable si je m’enlève de la wifi ? » écrit Georgia Sarah.
Orange vient de poster un message sur son compte X où il confirme qu’il y a bien un problème technique. L’opérateur évoque des perturbations sur le réseau mobile.
Ironie de la situation, le site de suivi des incidents d’Orange n’est lui-même plus accessible. On peut imaginer qu’il subit une surcharge de trafic.

articles.title: FOSSA Systems e IENAI Space han puesto en órbita el primer satélite español con propulsión eléctrica
articles.text:
Este 20 de octubre de 2026 se ha lanzado un satélite 6U desde Cabo Cañaveral, Florida, a bordo de un cohete Falcon 9, de SpaceX. El lanzamiento, que forma parte de la misión compartida Bandwagon-5, ha sido todo un hito español, ya que es el primer satélite de propulsión eléctrica de fabricación española.
Más español que la paella. El satélite ha sido fabricado por la compañía española Fossa Systems. Es el número 27 que se lanza desde 2020; por lo que, según comunicados recogidos por Actualidad Aeroespacial, sería ya la empresa de España que más objetos ha puesto en órbita. En cuanto a sus sistema de propulsión eléctrica, llamado ATHENA NANO, es obra de la compañía madrileña IENAI Space. Pleno a la tecnología española.
Bandwagon-5. Una misión compartida es esa en la que varias empresas o instituciones contratan un mismo cohete de una sola empresa para lanzar sus dispositivos de forma simultánea. En este caso, junto al satélite de FOSSA han viajado otras 31 cargas útiles, incluyendo la cápsula de reentrada Starfall de SpaceX.
Electropulverización. Así se llama el método de propulsión que emplea este satélite. A grandes rasgos, consiste en un depósito de sal líquida al que un campo eléctrico le arranca iones que salen disparados a velocidades enormes. Esto, provoca la propulsión del vehículo por acción-reacción.
En realidad, el sistema ATHENA NANO había volado ya al espacio, pues ya había volado a bordo de un satélite lanzado en el Spectrum 2 de la alemana Isar Aerospace . Ahora, por lo tanto, es la primera vez que trabaja con otra empresa española.
Una constelación con dos utilidades. La constelación de FOSSA se encarga de garantizar comunicaciones seguras y detectar y analizar emisiones electromagnéticas desde el espacio. Esto puede tener aplicaciones tanto civiles como militares.
¿Y ahora qué? El lanzamiento, que tuvo lugar a las 13:04 (hora peninsular española) del 20 de octubre, fue todo un éxito. Ahora, habrá que esperar unos días para que el satélite lleve a cabo los primeros encendidos. Después, se simularán maniobras típicas de constelaciones, como ir a la órbita operacional, mantener la posición respecto al resto de satélites y evitar colisiones con otros satélites o basura espacial. Si todo esto funciona correctamente, podrá unirse al resto de satélites de FOSSA para llevar a cabo su misión.
Nueva sede. Todo esto ocurre pocos días después de que FOSSA presentara su nueva sede en Las Rozas (Madrid). Se trata de unas instalaciones de 3.000 metros cuadrados en las que se llevan a cabo tanto las actividades de fabricación, como integración y operación de satélites. Se ha construido con el objetivo de aumentar tanto la producción como la complejidad de los satélites que fabrican. De momento, el satélite que acaba de partir al espacio ya es dos veces más grande que los anteriores. Puede ser el principio de una nueva era para FOSSA Systems.

articles.title: Americana en Dinamarca: Lo que aprendí sobre el equilibrio entre el trabajo y la vida
articles.text:
Brooke Black pensaba que permanecer trabajando mientras sus colegas se iban de vacaciones demostraría su compromiso. Su elección resultó ser inadecuada en Dinamarca, donde las personas con las que necesitaba hablar estaban ausentes y prácticamente no podía avanzar. La culpa por la productividad que ella consideraba poco satisfactoria la llevó entonces a comentar esa sensación con su marido danés y sus compañeros de trabajo, quienes no compartían su perspectiva.
Esta ciudadana estadounidense cuenta su historia y explica que se mudó con su familia a Dinamarca en 2020, convencida de que las condiciones laborales le permitirían tener una excelente relación entre trabajo y vida personal. Seis años después, describe las dificultades para aprovechar la experiencia danesa.
Trabajaba en la industria musical de Nueva York y Los Ángeles y tenía más de 40 horas de trabajo a la semana, además de estar disponible muchas noches y fines de semana. Recuerda un Día de Acción de Gracias en el que seguía trabajando cuando su familia estaba comiendo en otra habitación. Black ahora planifica estrategias de comunicación para empresas emergentes y grandes corporaciones del sector del entretenimiento y la tecnología.
Trabajar constantemente tampoco encajaba bien con las normas de la oficina. Black solía trabajar durante la hora de comer, mientras que sus colegas se juntaban a comer a las 11:30 cada día. Las cabinas para llamadas de la empresa solían estar ocupadas, pero atender el teléfono desde su escritorio tampoco resultaba viable. La flexibilidad del horario para ir a recoger a sus hijos y el “fredagsbar” semanal (encuentro el viernes por la tarde con bebidas y aperitivos) le resultaban atractivos, aunque seguía intentando demostrar su dedicación trabajando más.
Las vacaciones eran una parte del calendario que le costaba gestionar. Black primero acumuló días que, según ella, perdió al no pasarlos al siguiente periodo. Luego reservó sus días de descanso para el último trimestre del año, pero acabó trabajando durante ellos. Según Black, el parón estival y las vacaciones coincidentes de padres con hijos en edad escolar concentraban el trabajo a finales de año. Decidió quedarse trabajando durante el parón de verano porque pensaba que eso la convertiría en “una especie de heroína”.
Black empezó a irse de vacaciones durante el verano hacia 2023, pero tomarlas no eliminó su actividad constante. No dejaba de trabajar y dedicaba tiempo a algunas actividades complementarias (festivales, talleres de marca y conferencias) además de su tarea principal y solo tenía una semana para pasar tiempo con su familia.
El marido de Black le recordaba a menudo que muchas familias de su entorno podían pasar tres o cuatro semanas seguidas de vacaciones juntas. Sin embargo, a ella le preocupaba que descansar se interpretara como falta de ambición: “Si me tomaba tiempo para relajarme, eso indicaría que no era seria ni ambiciosa”.
También le costaba disfrutar del hygge, que describe como bajar el ritmo y apreciar las pequeñas cosas. Había reunido velas, material para tejer, libros e ingredientes de repostería sin conseguir aquietar su mente. El cambio llegó al pasar una semana en la casa de verano de su suegra. Black mencionó haberse sentido más descansada y creativa después de regresar, aunque su equilibrio personal aún no estaba resuelto. Había concluido: “No necesitas ganarte el descanso”.
¿Qué significan las 37 horas y las cinco semanas?
La situación de Black tiene una explicación estructural. Según el sitio web Workindenmark, la jornada laboral habitual es de 37 horas y suele distribuirse entre lunes y viernes. Esta guía sobre la cultura laboral danesa, que ha sido actualizada en enero de 2026, describe la autonomía para organizar las tareas y cumplir los plazos.
En algunos centros incluye la posibilidad de gestionar el horario. Muchas condiciones de trabajo se fijan mediante convenios colectivos entre sindicatos y asociaciones empresariales. Eso sí, Workindenmark advierte que no todos los empleos están cubiertos por ellos. En esos casos, las condiciones se negocian directamente entre el trabajador y la empresa. Conviene informarse al revisar la oferta de condiciones laborales antes de aceptar el empleo.
Además de las condiciones individuales sobre el uso del tiempo, la gestión del calendario gira en gran medida en torno a la organización. Las instrucciones de Workindenmark mencionan que los empleados deben proporcionar resultados en el plazo establecido e informar cuando no tienen acceso a los recursos necesarios para lograrlos. A su vez, los empleados deberían ofrecer su ayuda y asumir tareas relacionadas con la cooperación.
Asimismo, merece atención la distinción entre el derecho al tiempo libre y su remuneración. Los empleados tienen derecho a 25 días de vacaciones, cinco semanas, aunque no hayan generado el derecho a cobrarlos todos. Por ejemplo, se generan 2,08 días de vacaciones pagadas por mes de trabajo. En consecuencia, uno debe comprobar cuántos días pagados ha acumulado antes de contar con cinco semanas íntegramente remuneradas.
La Agencia Danesa de Mercado Laboral explica las reglas generales para las vacaciones de los empleados, incluido el derecho a disfrutar de tres semanas seguidas entre el 1 de mayo y el 30 de septiembre.
El traslado de días que confundía a Black tiene límites legales. El sitio web oficial Life in Denmark, sobre vacaciones, actualizado el 1 de octubre de 2026, menciona que el periodo ordinario para disfrutarlas abarca 16 meses, desde septiembre hasta diciembre del año siguiente. El trabajador y el empleador pueden acordar por escrito trasladar al siguiente periodo los días acumulados que excedan de cuatro semanas, sujeto a posibles reglas del convenio. Hay excepciones por impedimentos como enfermedad o permisos de maternidad, paternidad o adopción; una gran carga de trabajo no es un impedimento válido.
Desconectar también depende de la organización de la semana laboral
Las horas adicionales también se tienen en cuenta al calcular las horas realmente trabajadas. Aquí ya hablamos sobre cuánto se trabaja en distintos países a partir de datos de la Organización para la Cooperación y el Desarrollo Económicos (OCDE). Su descripción menciona que las horas efectivamente trabajadas incluyen las horas extraordinarias y las de empleos adicionales, pero excluyen el tiempo de vacaciones sin trabajar.
El trabajo adicional de Black incluía proyectos secundarios, además de su empleo principal. La oportunidad de distinguir entre el horario pactado y las horas de trabajo reales, incluidas las dedicadas a proyectos adicionales, sigue siendo relevante.
Una investigación de 2025 analiza la relación entre vacaciones y bienestar. Ryan Grant, Beth Buchanan y Kristen Shockley publicaron un metaanálisis de 32 estudios de nueve países en el Journal of Applied Psychology. La Universidad de Georgia explicó que los beneficios para el bienestar duraban más de lo estimado anteriormente.
La desconexión mental del trabajo se relacionaba con mayores mejoras, y la actividad física también se asociaba con una mejor recuperación. Las vacaciones más largas podían aportar mayores beneficios, aunque también podían ir seguidas de una caída más pronunciada del bienestar al regresar al trabajo.
Malissa Clark, profesora y jefa del departamento de Psicología de la Universidad de Georgia, aconsejó desactivar las notificaciones de correo electrónico laboral o de Slack.
Clark aconsejó a los gerentes que programaran el envío de correos electrónicos dentro del horario laboral. Explicó que añadir una frase al final diciendo que no se espera una respuesta inmediata puede seguir generando presión para contestar por la relación de autoridad.
Se sugirió programar estos envíos para que el empleado no tenga que decidir durante su descanso si su responsable espera una respuesta inmediata.

articles.title: Mit Videos und Beratung: Experten sollen bald direkt auf Linkedin Geld verdienen können
articles.text:
Mit Videos und Beratung: Experten sollen bald direkt auf Linkedin Geld verdienen können
Immer mehr Menschen nutzen Linkedin nicht nur für ihre berufliche Karriere, sondern auch für eigene Projekte und zusätzliche Einnahmequellen. Laut dem Business-Netzwerk ist die Zahl der Gründer:innen auf Linkedin um 70 Prozent gestiegen. In welchem Zeitraum, ist aber unklar. Im Vergleich zu 2019 hat zudem der Anteil der Nutzer:innen, die mehr als eine berufliche Position angeben, um 26 Prozent zugenommen. Auch mehr als 80 Prozent der Creator veröffentlichen ihre Inhalte neben einer weiteren beruflichen Tätigkeit. Für die Gründer:innenzahl nennt Linkedin allerdings keinen konkreten Vergleichszeitraum.
Mit den jetzt angekündigten Funktionen will Linkedin diesen Entwicklungen Rechnung tragen und Nutzer:innen neue Möglichkeiten bieten, ihre beruflichen Kontakte zu pflegen und mit ihren Inhalten sowie ihrem Fachwissen Geld zu verdienen. Geplant sind unter anderem kostenpflichtige Beratungsgespräche über das eigene Profil, Werbeeinnahmen für Video-Creator und ein neues Creator-Dashboard. Außerdem testet das Business-Netzwerk einen eigenen Network-Feed und führt digitale Visitenkarten sowie persönliche Notizen für Kontakte ein.
Advice-Sessions: Beratungen über das Linkedin-Profil verkaufen
Mit dem neuen Feature Advice-Sessions können Expert:innen kostenpflichtige Einzelberatungen über ihr LinkedIn-Profil anbieten. Interessierte können dort Termine buchen, bezahlen und die Beratung per Video wahrnehmen. Linkedin übernimmt damit auch die Abwicklung von Beratungsleistungen, für die Berater:innen und andere Selbstständige bisher auf externe Buchungs- und Zahlungsdienste angewiesen waren.
Vorerst steht das Feature allerdings nur Business-Premium-Abonnent:innen in den USA zur Verfügung. Weitere Länder sollen folgen. Wann Advice-Sessions in Deutschland starten und welche Gebühren anfallen, hat Linkedin noch nicht mitgeteilt.
Mit In-Stream-Ads auf Linkedin Geld verdienen
Creator wiederum können mit ihren Videos auf Linkedin Geld verdienen. Über das In-Stream-Ads-Programm erhalten ausgewählte Nutzer:innen Werbeeinnahmen, wenn vor ihren Videos sogenannte Pre-Roll-Ads ausgespielt werden. Die Teilnahme am Programm soll künftig über das neue Creator-Dashboard möglich sein.
Mit der Monetarisierung von Videoinhalten beschäftigt sich Linkedin bereits seit einiger Zeit. So führte das Unternehmen 2025 mit BrandLink neue Werbeformate für Videos ein. Nun sollen weitere Creator von den Werbeeinnahmen profitieren können. Vorerst testet Linkedin das In-Stream-Ads-Programm allerdings nur mit ausgewählten Creatorn und Advertisern in den USA. Eine Ausweitung ist geplant.
Das neue Creator-Dashboard soll außerdem die Verwaltung von Inhalten erleichtern und einen Überblick über die Content-Performance sowie verfügbare Einnahmemöglichkeiten bieten. Linkedin will es in den kommenden Wochen weltweit einführen. In der mobilen App ist es dann über das Profilbild oben links erreichbar. Welche Monetarisierungsfunktionen dort angezeigt werden, hängt allerdings von der jeweiligen Verfügbarkeit ab. So bleibt das In-Stream-Ads-Programm zunächst auf ausgewählte Teilnehmer:innen in den USA beschränkt.
Linkedin testet neuen Network-Feed und führt digitale Visitenkarten ein
Neben den Einnahmemöglichkeiten gibt es auch Neuerungen beim Networking. Linkedin testet einen eigenen Network-Feed, in dem Beiträge von Kontakten und abonnierten Profilen zusammengeführt werden. Nutzer:innen sollen so leichter verfolgen können, was Menschen aus ihrem beruflichen Umfeld veröffentlichen, statt sich ausschließlich auf die Auswahl des bisherigen Feeds verlassen zu müssen. Der Test startet zunächst in den USA, Indien, Großbritannien und Australien. Wann die neue Ansicht in Deutschland verfügbar sein wird, ist noch offen.
Außerdem führt Linkedin personalisierbare digitale Visitenkarten ein, die sich im Smartphone-Wallet speichern und bei persönlichen Treffen teilen lassen. Die Funktion soll in den kommenden Monaten weltweit verfügbar werden. Premiumabonnent:innen können bereits jetzt private Notizen zu anderen Profilen hinterlegen und beispielsweise festhalten, wo sie jemanden kennengelernt haben, worüber gesprochen wurde oder wann ein erneuter Austausch ansteht.
Autor:innen können zudem Kommentare künftig anpinnen und damit etwa besonders hilfreiche Ergänzungen oder Antworten hervorheben. Linkedin reagiert mit den neuen Networking-Funktionen nach eigenen Angaben auch auf Unsicherheiten beim Aufbau beruflicher Beziehungen. Laut einer Untersuchung des Unternehmens weiß mehr als die Hälfte der befragten Angehörigen der Generation Z nicht genau, wie sie nach dem ersten Vernetzen eine berufliche Beziehung weiterentwickeln soll.
Linkedin will mehr Geschäft über das eigene Netzwerk abwickeln
Linkedin arbeitet schon länger daran, aus beruflicher Reichweite neue Einnahmemöglichkeiten zu schaffen. Im Juni 2026 führte das Unternehmen einen eigenen Creator-Marketplace für Kooperationen zwischen Marken und B2B‑Influencern ein. Hinzu kommen Funktionen wie die Collaborative-Posts, mit denen sich Inhalte gemeinsam veröffentlichen lassen. Mit Advice-Sessions nimmt Linkedin nun auch den Verkauf von Beratungsleistungen in den Blick und will neben der Kund:innengewinnung künftig deren Buchung, Bezahlung und Durchführung ermöglichen.
Für Selbstständige liegt der Vorteil vor allem darin, dass sie ihre Beratungsleistungen dort anbieten können, wo sie bereits Kontakte pflegen, Reichweite aufbauen und potenzielle Kund:innen erreichen. Linkedin könnte damit einen Teil jener Geschäftsprozesse übernehmen, die bisher über externe Anbieter:innen abgewickelt werden. Das spart möglicherweise Aufwand, macht Selbstständige aber auch stärker von dem Business-Netzwerk abhängig, das nicht nur die Sichtbarkeit ihrer Angebote beeinflusst, sondern künftig auch Buchungen und Zahlungen verarbeitet.
Wie attraktiv die neuen Einnahmemöglichkeiten wirtschaftlich sind, lässt sich noch nicht beurteilen. Linkedin hat weder mögliche Gebühren für Advice-Sessions noch konkrete Verdienstmöglichkeiten durch In-Stream-Ads genannt. Für Nutzer:innen in Deutschland bleibt die Frage vorerst ohnehin theoretisch, denn während das Creator-Dashboard und die digitalen Visitenkarten weltweit eingeführt werden sollen, sind die beiden Monetarisierungsangebote zunächst auf die USA beschränkt.
Der Artikel stammt von Larissa Ceccio aus der OnlineMarketing.de-Redaktion und wird im Rahmen einer Content-Kooperation auf t3n veröffentlicht.

articles.title: Conversational Gemini navigation comes to Apple CarPlay
articles.text:
After introducing its Gemini AI assistant to Android Auto last year, Google is now bringing it to Apple CarPlay users. The conversational Gemini in navigation is available today for US drivers, with “rollout happening globally too,” according to Google (we’ve asked for specific regional availability details).
Conversational Gemini navigation comes to Apple CarPlay
CarPlay users in the US can now use Gemini to chat with Google Maps.
It’s taken almost 12 months for Google to bring this to CarPlay users, but now they can talk to the voice assistant in Google Maps to get some hands-free help while driving. That includes asking it multi-step questions, such as recommendations on places to visit and then prompting it to direct you there while avoiding toll roads. Users can activate the feature by tapping the Gemini icon in Google Maps on their Car’s infotainment display.
Google describes this CarPlay support update as a conversational way to report traffic disruptions and find information about stops and places on-the-go. There’s no mention of any of the Personal Intelligence features that were announced yesterday for Gemini in Android Auto and cars with Google built-in, however, which enable the voice assistant to access user information from Google apps, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, YouTube, and Search. We’ve asked Google if CarPlay users will also receive the personalization update and will update if we hear back.

articles.title: China Defends DeepSeek After US Ban of Its AI From Government Systems
articles.text:
China hit back Tuesday at a U.S. ban on the use of Chinese artificial intelligence startup DeepSeek’s products by federal civilian agencies and warned of retaliatory measures as the two AI powers race to develop the technology.
The Department of Homeland Security said the agencies should remove DeepSeek products as well as third-party products and services developed using DeepSeek from their IT systems, according to a notice made public on Monday.
The latest warnings reflect “the depth of strategic distrust between Beijing and Washington” even as U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping work hard to keep their personal relationship “warm and constructive,” said George Chen, partner and chair of digital practice at Washington-based The Asia Group consultancy.
The Homeland Security order, dating back to late July, also blocks civilian agencies from procuring DeepSeek products and services.
DeepSeek’s open-source models are widely available in countries including the United States, and are mostly free to use.
The notice in the Federal Register alleges that DeepSeek’s models “present multiple threat vectors.” Concerns include that DeepSeek’s servers are located in China and that Chinese authorities could potentially access private company infrastructure and sensitive U.S. data, the order says.
Asked in Beijing about the U.S. ban, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said China “will resolutely safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies.”
“China consistently opposes the overstretching of the concept of national security,” she told reporters.
China’s Ministry of Commerce also expressed “strong dissatisfaction and firm opposition” against the U.S.’s move, saying late Tuesday that the U.S. side disregarded the consensus reached between Xi and Trump and ignored the broader landscape of China-U.S. economic and trade relations.
Through discriminatory restrictions under “the guise of national security,” the U.S. is trying to suppress and contain China, the commerce ministry statement said. “China will closely monitor the situation and take all necessary measures to firmly defend its legitimate rights and interests.”
DeepSeek did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
China and the U.S. have recently made progress in some collaboration on AI governance, including a U.S. proposal for setting up a notification system on national security-related incidents, but they remain at odds on many issues.
AI is expected to be on the agenda when Trump and Xi meet again in mid-November on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China. The two leaders last met in September as Xi made a state visit to Washington.
U.S.-led restrictions still ban China from accessing some of the world’s most advanced AI chips and the machines that make them.
The U.S. also has said Chinese AI startups including DeepSeek had engaged in large-scale “distillation,” or extraction of capabilities, from frontier American AI models, claims that Beijing has dismissed.
And last week, Beijing rolled out its own proposals to restrict exports of certain advanced AI models.

articles.title: NVIDIA Confidential Computing Expands, Enabling Frontier Model Builders to Securely Scale Across Global Infrastructure
articles.text:
NVIDIA builds tools to enable safe agents across the stack. The NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture, announced today, is part of NVIDIA’s growing portfolio of technologies that enables organizations to safely deploy agents at scale. NVIDIA Confidential Computing is the infrastructure layer that protects the models and data those agents depend on while running.
Today, NVIDIA is expanding that layer with Confidential Bare Metal, a new deployment option with NVIDIA Confidential Computing that enables frontier model builders to run sensitive workloads on dedicated third-party infrastructure while retaining control of their models and data.
NVIDIA is introducing new platform security controls that protect data in transit, measure platform integrity and enforce hardware-level access restrictions. These new controls let frontier model builders use bare-metal instances to own and operate their bespoke software stack, including host and platform infrastructure software, when operating on NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure across third-party cloud, neocloud and enterprise infrastructure.
NVIDIA Confidential Computing now offers a converged security architecture with three deployment options:
- Confidential Bare Metal for bare-metal infrastructure
- Confidential Containers for Kubernetes environments
- Confidential Virtual Machines for virtualized environments
Organizations can match the right model to their trust boundaries and operating requirements.
NVIDIA Confidential Computing is also expanding across NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Rubin systems and will integrate with NVIDIA DSX OS as a reference architecture for cloud providers building AI factories.
Model Builders Tap Global Capacity
Confidential Bare Metal gives supported providers a path to serve high-value workloads that require strong model and data privacy protections. For model builders, the expanding ecosystem offers more geographic, sovereign and operational options for scaling training and inference worldwide.
Cohere plans to integrate Confidential Bare Metal into Cohere Model Vault, using NVIDIA Confidential Computing trusted execution environments to extend hardware-rooted security directly to the GPU — protecting models and data in memory and across interconnects during execution.
“Enterprises trust Cohere to provide a secure and confidential platform for inference,” said Phil Blunsom, chief technology officer at Cohere. “With NVIDIA Confidential Computing in Cohere Model Vault, we’re extending hardware-rooted security directly to the GPU, protecting customer data in memory and across interconnects during execution.”
Google Cloud is extending support for  Confidential Bare Metal to A4X Max instances powered by NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems. These will combine non-virtualized NVIDIA accelerated computing with cryptographic protection for training data and model intellectual property.
“Google Cloud introduces Confidential Bare Metal to provide AI labs with hardware-isolated, non-virtualized compute environments and end-to-end cryptographic protection. Our A4X instances, built using NVIDIA Confidential Computing, preserve the privacy of user data, protect model IP, provide top-line serving performance,” said Andrés Lagar-Cavilla, distinguished engineer and AI infrastructure security lead at Google Cloud.
Confidential Computing Expands Across the NVIDIA Platform
NVIDIA Confidential Computing uses hardware-rooted isolation and cryptographic attestation to help protect models and data during execution.
Support now extends to NVIDIA Grace Blackwell NVL72 — bringing Confidential Computing to NVL72 rack-scale systems — as well as x86-based NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 and NVIDIA DGX Rubin NVL8 systems.
CoreWeave, Firmus, GMI Cloud, Google Cloud, IREN, Lambda, Microsoft Azure Infrastructure, Nebius, Nscale and Vultr support NVIDIA Confidential Computing deployments. Global systems partners including Cisco, Dell Technologies, HPE, Lenovo, Supermicro and Bull will support these capabilities with NVIDIA-Certified Systems.
NVIDIA DSX OS will support all NVIDIA Confidential Computing modes, giving cloud providers a software foundation for building and operating AI factories that support confidential workloads.
Learn more about NVIDIA Confidential Computing.

articles.title: Dunkle Energie: So könnten schwache Radiowellen ihr Geheimnis lüften
articles.text:
70 Prozent des Universums unerklärt: Wie schwache Radiosignale das Rätsel der Dunklen Energie lösen sollen
Was steckt hinter Dunkler Energie? Dies ist eines der großen Rätsel der Kosmologie. Die unsichtbare, hypothetische Form der Energie gilt als verantwortlich für die Ausdehnung des Universums, nachdem der erste Schub durch den Big Bang abgeklungen war.
Neuer Weg zum Verständnis von Dunkler Energie?
Direkt nachgewiesen werden konnte die Dunkle Energie, die fast 70 Prozent der Energiedichte des Universums ausmachen soll, noch nicht. Ein Forschungsteam könnte aber nun einen Weg gefunden haben, Dunkle Energie künftig besser zu verstehen.
Die Resultate ihrer Forschung haben die Wissenschaftler:innen in gleich zwei Papern vorgestellt, die beide in der Fachzeitschrift The Astrophysical Journal erschienen sind.
Analyse von neutralem Wasserstoff
Die Forschenden haben mit dem Radioteleskop Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME) nach Spuren von kosmischem Wasserstoff gesucht. Genauer gesagt nach neutralem atomaren Wasserstoff, der nicht ionisiert und also elektrisch ungeladen ist.
Neutraler Wasserstoff sendet eine Radiostrahlung mit einer Wellenlänge von etwa 21 Zentimetern aus. Durch die Expansion des Universums wird die Strahlung auf dem Weg zur Erde zu niedrigeren Frequenzen verschoben.
Je stärker die Verzerrung im Vergleich zur ursprünglichen Wellenlänge ist, desto länger waren die Strahlen unterwegs. Daraus kann man ablesen, aus welcher Zeit die Signale stammen. Die Strahlung des neutralen Wasserstoffs, die CHIME auffing, wurde vor acht bis neun Milliarden Jahren ausgesendet. Sie stammt also aus dem relativ jungen Universum.
CHIME beobachtete erstmals direkt neutralen Wasserstoff
Bei der Analyse von neutralem Wasserstoff gibt es eine Schwierigkeit. Sein Signal ist so schwach, dass es von anderen Radioquellen überlagert wird.
Bisher konnten Forschende mit CHIME Wasserstoff nur indirekt wahrnehmen. Sie mussten die empfangenen Signale mit bereits kartierten Galaxien abgleichen.
Mit Hilfe neuer Algorithmen ist es den Wissenschaftler:innen nun gelungen, mit CHIME die Wellenlängen des Wasserstoffs unmittelbar zu erkennen. Das Radioteleskop konnte eigenständig Störsignale erkennen und ausblenden. So soll die Detektion von neutralem Wasserstoff künftig einfacher werden.
Verteilung von Wasserstoff gibt Aufschluss über Ausdehnung des Universums
Was hat dies alles nun mit Dunkler Energie zu tun? Um diese mysteriöse Kraft zu verstehen, ist es wichtig, die Verteilung von Materie im Universum zu unterschiedlichen Zeiten zu kennen.
Nur daraus kann man ablesen, wie schnell sich das Weltall ausgedehnt hat und welche Rolle die Dunkle Energie dabei gespielt hat. Und da Wasserstoff das häufigste Element im Universum ist, ist es der beste Marker, um die Verteilung von Materie und ihre Veränderung zu analysieren.

articles.title: TornadoVM 7 Enables GPU-Native Workloads From Java Applications
articles.text:
TornadoVM, an open-source heterogeneous GPU programming framework for Java has reached version 7.3, a major milestone for the project.
InfoQ previously covered the project in December 2025 and in 2022.
TornadoVM automatically accelerates Java programs on multi-core CPUs and GPUs. Rather than replacing existing JVMs, it works alongside them and provides a rich GPU programming ecosystem in Java that you can use with any mainstream JDK distribution such as OpenJDK, Graalvm, Temurin, or Zulu.
It offloads Java code to hardware backends, manages memory between the Java heap and accelerators, and runs the resulting compute kernels. This makes it a useful building block for modern cloud and machine learning workloads.
During development, TornadoVM compiles the source Java code to OpenCL and Apple Metal backends. The idea is that you can develop locally on your laptop and use the hardware available locally, and then deploy into a server that has Nvidia GPUs, and achieve major performance improvements - a form of "Write Once, Run Anywhere" for modern ML workloads.
Version 7 brings several architectural changes. The backends now use the Foreign Function & Memory (FFM) API in place of the Java Native Interface (JNI). The experimental JVM Compiler Interface (JVMCI) dependency has also been removed. According to the team, TornadoVM now sources "all compiler metadata through a reflection + ASM + Unsafe layer" which is the single, uniform path on every supported JDK (21, 25, 26 and 27).
The release also deepens integration with the Nvidia ecosystem through an optimized CUDA backend. This includes support for the cuTile programming model (via a new TileContext) and the ability to call CUDA libraries such as cuBLAS and CUTLASS directly from within TornadoVM TaskGraphs. Developers can swap JIT-generated kernels for CUDA library calls, or chain the two together, depending on their performance and portability needs. Similarly, TornadoVM adds the same functionality for Apple's MXL library again via the hybrid API. Finally, support for multi-GPU execution has been added.
Not every Java computation benefits from offloading. The best candidates are data-parallel workloads, such as loops with no dependencies between iterations, because their iterations can run in parallel on the accelerator.
One of the goals of recent TornadoVM versions is to produce an idiomatic JVM environment for accessing the libraries that Nvidia have been tuning for different hardware platforms. The aim is for Java developers to tap into things like Linear Algebra, Fast Fourier Transforms (for Signal Analysis), Deep Neural Networks and hand-optimized matrix multiplication for sparse matrices. TornadoVM has library integrations with Quarkus, Lang4j, Flink, Spring AI and others and is also available through SDKMan.
For example, consider the integration of Apache Flink with TornadoVM - the main idea is that the developer writes a standard query as they normally would with the Table API. A configuration flag is used to indicate that this query should potentially be accelerated on a GPU.
Then, when the computation reaches the task manager, the framework checks if there is a GPU available in the node it is executing on and, if so, it connects to a library provider - which analyzes the intermediate representation (IR) of the query to see if the computation is actually suitable for GPU execution.
In total, TornadoVM offers four ways to program Nvidia GPUs as a Java programmer - Firstly, the parallel API which is really just an annotation that annotates a loop, and provides a hint for the compiler that this loop can be potentially paralyzed. This simple API did not prove to be sufficient in the long-term to get the desired performance for production applications, so additional APIs were added - such as the kernel context API and the already-mentioned TileContext.
Alongside the 7.3 release, the TornadoVM team introduced jitLLM v2.0, its next-generation Java AI inference engine built on TornadoVM. The team positions jitLLM as a direct competitor to llama.cpp and Ollama in performance, and it ships as a single JAR file.
Both TornadoVM and jitLLM are being commercialized through Beestream.ai, a spin-off founded by the TornadoVM team.
Further details can be found on the TornadoVM site, and also in recent videos from Devoxx Belgium, including: "Tap into the NVIDIA Ecosystem from Java with TornadoVM's Hybrid API".

articles.title: Developing an AI Factory Digital Twin with an Agent-Assisted Workflow | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
Building an AI factory digital twin requires developers to bring site plans, equipment assets, and engineering requirements into a consistent model that teams can inspect, revise, and prepare for simulation. Connecting these inputs into an editable workflow helps teams explore design alternatives and incorporate engineering feedback as the design evolves.
The NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint, part of NVIDIA DSX Sim, provides reference digital twin assets, sample scripts, and workflows for developing AI factory digital twins. Built on OpenUSD and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries, the blueprint gives developers a foundation for assembling facility and equipment models with SimReady assets, and connecting them with engineering simulation tools.
Frontier AI models can help developers work with this foundation through agents and connected applications and tools, as explained in Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations with Frontier AI Agents. Developers guide agents to bring together design inputs, assemble and revise OpenUSD scenes, and inspect the results. The blueprint supplies reusable assets and workflows, and the agents help developers apply and adapt them to specific design requirements (Figure 1).
This post demonstrates an agent-assisted workflow for turning reference assets, site data, and design requirements into an editable OpenUSD campus model. Developers can use this approach to explore layouts, revise equipment placement, and prepare designs for engineering review and downstream simulation. Developers connect tools and guide changes, while engineers review results to inform the next iteration.
Providing agents with a design foundation for AI factory modeling
Consider a practical question: How should an AI factory hall be configured when the available power is fixed? Changing the compute configuration can impact equipment quantity, placement, electrical distribution, and cooling. Evaluating the alternatives requires those disciplines to work from consistent requirements and design data.
An agent needs context before it can make a useful design proposal. Given only photos or renderings, it can produce a model that looks plausible but may have incorrect dimensions and proportions. Reference assets and project documents help ground the proposal, but the resulting model still requires dimensional checks and engineering review.
A grounded workflow starts with the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint and reference design, then incorporates the project’s requirements, drawings, equipment information, and site constraints. Each source has a different role: existing geometry supplies reusable buildings and equipment while architectural references inform appearance; aerial imagery and elevation data provide geographic context; project drawings and equipment information establish dimensions and placement; requirements define the conditions the design must satisfy.
For example, the team used the NVIDIA Santa Clara Headquarters building, Voyager, as design inspiration for an AI factory campus site based on the DSX reference design. The inputs included:
- DSX 3D models: Data hall, central utility buildings, substations, generators, cooling equipment, vehicles, and vegetation.
- Architectural references: Images of Voyager from various aerial and on-the-ground views to inform the roof, facade, solar canopies, and landscaping.
- Site plans (DSX Reference Design): PDFs describing the campus arrangement and a more detailed first phase, including buildings, roads, utility areas, and access areas.
- Requirements documents: An indexed collection of architectural drawings, form-factor studies, Basis of Design documents, room layouts, and other records.
- Geographic data: USGS aerial imagery and elevation data of the selected site used to place the campus in the surrounding terrain.
Together, these sources provide a starting point for an agent-assisted workflow and basis for reviewing its output. They help teams trace design choices to their sources—for example, building placement to a site plan and facade styling to an architectural reference. That traceability supports review; dimensional accuracy still depends on checking the model against the applicable drawings, specifications, and site constraints.
Building an OpenUSD campus site model using an AI agent
To implement this workflow, a frontier AI model runs in an agent harness: software that manages context, instructions, and tool calls. Skills encode repeatable tasks and AI factory domain knowledge. Developers connect modeling and analysis operations through tool interfaces, including the Model Context Protocol (MCP), where supported, and define which changes the agent may propose or apply.
In the campus model example, existing DSX reference designed buildings from the DSX Blueprint and equipment supplied the starting geometry, while the site plans guided placement and first-phase details. The team supplied photographs and the architectural references from the NVIDIA Voyager campus to guide the architectural additions.
For the solar canopy, the frontier AI agent used USD Content Agents to help generate its geometry and materials, then refined the design using the Voyager references. This gave the team an editable architectural element to review alongside the existing buildings and equipment. The canopy remained a conceptual design where an engineering team could check for dimensions, structural properties, and suitability for simulation.
The team then combined the reused assets and new architectural geometry in additive USD layers, keeping changes separate from the source assets. In the Omniverse RTX viewport, the team could inspect the canopy in the context of the campus, review its appearance and placement, and revise the model as design decisions change. USGS aerial data was used for the landscape and elevation plan.
Extending the campus model to evaluate a fixed power budget
The campus model could support a subsequent capacity planning study: How should an AI factory hall be configured within a fixed power budget? The proposed extension would connect the modeled layout with compute, electrical, and cooling requirements to evaluate alternative configurations.
One starting point is an illustrative NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 inference comparison. It contrasts a baseline using MaxP—the highest static GPU-level power setting—with DSX MaxLPS, an AI factory design and operating framework that coordinates facility design, dynamic power allocation, and performance-per-watt optimization. Applying this comparison to a hall would require evaluating the support power, cooling, and networking infrastructure.
Normalized to a 1 MW power basis, assuming a power usage effectiveness (PUE) of 1.1, the illustrative scenario shows a DSX MaxLPS capacity of 400 GPUs and aggregate token throughput of 1.35x the MaxP baseline (Figure 4). These figures are reference assumptions for the proposed study, not results generated by the campus model.
In the proposed workflow, developers would connect the agent to project data and engineering tools so it could help identify equipment and design assumptions requiring review. The reference comparison would inform capacity targets. Engineers would evaluate feasible configurations using complete racks, including their placement, electrical distribution, cooling connections, and network resources.
Using Systems Modeling Language (SysML), teams can represent requirements and link them to system elements. A project team could use these relationships to organize requirements drawn from source documents. If the modeling tool exposes those relationships through an API, MCP, or other supported interface, the agent could query them to flag potentially affected dependencies affected by the proposed change. Drawings and CAD would provide dimensions and placement references, while equipment catalogs would supply the parameters for engineering analysis.
The handoff would be a proposed design revision, accompanied by the requirements, equipment, and follow-up engineering studies. After engineering reviews, the agent could help update the OpenUSD scene to reflect the selected rack configuration and layout. Preparing the scene for a specific simulation would require additional checks and configuration, including geometry, equipment properties, system connections, and boundary conditions.
Assembling the digital twin with OpenUSD and SimReady
After the team reviews a proposed configuration and its affected requirements, the next step is to prepare the design for analysis. This requires more than geometry: engineers need equipment properties and connection data to evaluate power and cooling. OpenUSD brings building geometry, equipment assets, and associated data into a shared scene. USD attributes and custom schemas can preserve links to engineering records and requirements, keeping changes traceable across applications.
The DSX system architecture connects asset preparation, data storage, simulation services, and the digital twin application. For the fixed-power scenario, this provides a framework for bringing the revised layout together with the equipment information needed to evaluate its power and cooling implications.
SimReady Foundation describes the asset data needed for particular simulation uses. While OpenUSD provides the shared scene, SimReady specifications help teams assess whether its assets contain the required data needed for the intended analysis, select the requirements and supported validators appropriate to the equipment and analysis, then check the geometry, properties, and connection data they cover. The agent can help surface missing information and associate it with the affected equipment for the team to review.
Developers can also source equipment assets from the SimReady Central Library on Hugging Face, a free, ungated library of more than 2,000 simulation-ready OpenUSD assets. For AI factory digital twins, teams can discover and reuse OEM-provided racks, power and cooling equipment, reducing asset preparation.
The AI factory pipeline samples provide examples for CAD conversion, optimization, metadata, and validation. Through connected tools, an agent can help invoke these preparation steps and collect their reports.
The resulting handoff is an assembled scene tied to the proposed design revision, with its supporting data, completed checks, and remaining gaps visible. This gives the simulation team the context needed to prepare the study and evaluate how the configuration behaves within the fixed power budget.
Evaluating power and cooling simulations to guide design revisions
With the revised scene assembled and the data gaps identified, prepare the studies needed to evaluate the configuration. In the fixed-power scenario, electrical loading and cooling analysis help determine how the proposed equipment arrangement behaves under the specified operating conditions. The application uses the geometry, equipment properties, and system connections, with additional solver preparation where required.
Where developers have implemented supported solver connections, an agent can submit studies, retrieve results, and associate findings with the affected equipment and requirements. Engineers review the assumptions and results to determine whether the design supports the proposed configurations or needs further revision. Each finding should identify the tested design revision and distinguish calculated results from stored results or AI approximations.
The capacity question now becomes a basis for making design decisions: which equipment configuration to pursue, what supporting infrastructure it requires, and where further analysis is needed. Those decisions feed back into the editable design, enabling the team to refine the proposal and repeat the affected studies.
Selecting compute for agent development, visualization, and simulation
For a workflow like the campus example, select hardware around the task: developing the agent tool connections, editing the scene, or running the engineering studies.
- NVIDIA DGX Spark for personal agent development: Prototype agents, test compatible local AI models, and connect engineering tools. Pair with an RTX system for DSX visualization and simulation.
- NVIDIA RTX PRO Blackwell Workstation Edition GPU for interactive design and simulation: Prepare OpenUSD assets, review digital twins, and run supported engineering simulations.
- NVIDIA DGX Station for larger local AI workloads: Develop and run larger AI models and agents locally. Add an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition GPU for visualization and supported simulation applications.
- NVIDIA RTX PRO Server for shared development and simulation: Follow the NVIDIA RTX PRO AI Factory reference architecture, which specifies eight RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs per server and groups four servers into a scalable unit. Size the deployment for inference, visualization, and supported simulation workloads based on scene complexity, solver requirements, and concurrent users.
Connecting applications to the engineering decision
Extending the campus model into an engineering study requires applications that manage requirements, supply equipment data, and calculate physical behavior. Application providers are addressing these scenarios across the workflow:
- Dassault Systèmes addresses the challenge of keeping system requirements and design decisions consistent with CATIA Magic. Its SysML tools let engineers model system elements and interfaces, check model consistency, and evaluate designs against the architecture. Within an agent-assisted workflow, simulation findings can inform proposed updates to the SysML model configuration, subject to engineering review, keeping requirements and the systems model connected throughout design iterations. Dassault Systèmes also supports the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol for agent-to-agent integration, complementing MCP-based access to tools and data.
- PTC is working to keep digital twin studies connected to the product data they represent through Windchill and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries. Windchill manages version-controlled Creo and other CAD data; the announced integration is intended to bring that data into a shared 3D environment for engineering review and simulation. This addresses the handoff from the managed equipment design to the AI factory digital twin.
- Cadence Reality Digital Twin Platform answers the fixed-power question: how many GPUs can run, and can they be cooled? It couples equipment and power models with computational fluid dynamics to simulate MaxP, MaxQ, and DSX MaxLPS. Stakeholders see the impact on power, cooling, and token throughput before a single rack is installed and continues through the life of the AI factory. Built on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries, SimReady assets, and OpenUSD, the Cadence Reality Digital Twin allows collaborative and agentic optimization of AI factory performance.
- Siemens supports detailed evaluation of fluid flow and heat transfer with Simcenter STAR-CCM+, where engineers calculate how a proposed design behaves under specified conditions. For AI factory infrastructure, Siemens has also developed DSX-aligned reference architectures that combine power distribution, automation, and simulation-ready assets. These address the need to represent supporting infrastructure alongside compute equipment in the factory design.
Get started with the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint
Choose one engineering question, connect the required data and tools, assemble the digital twin with OpenUSD, and use SimReady requirements to prepare assets for the intended analysis. Review the result before expanding.
Ready to get started?
- Build with the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint
- Assemble your digital twin with OpenUSD
- Prepare and validate your assets with DSX asset guidance and SimReady Foundation
- Prepare content for your workflow with AI factory pipeline samples
- Explore related simulation examples in Putting Astra to Work in Simulation With NVIDIA Omniverse Libraries
Stay up to date by subscribing to NVIDIA news and following NVIDIA Omniverse on Discord and YouTube.

Geschlossen gegen offen: Die Debatte tobt in der KI-Szene so heftig wie noch nie. Doch die Diskussion ist komplexer, als es auf den ersten Blick scheint.
Open-Weight-Modelle: Gefährlich oder richtig? (KI-generiertes Bild: Nano Banana 2 / MIT Technology Review)

articles.text:
Home >
                                                                    Manufacturing, Packaging & Materials >
                                                                Accelerating Manufacturing-Aware Simulations For Photonic Integrated Circuits...                                                    
Manufacturing, Packaging & Materials
                        WHITEPAPERS
		
Fab workflow connects GDS layout import, 3D process simulation, GPU-accelerated FDTD, design of experiments, with AI-based surrogate modeling.
								October 21st, 2026 - 
								By: Silvaco
								
							
Photonic integrated circuit (PIC) performance is increasingly bounded by fabrication realities such as sidewall angle, critical-dimension bias, thickness variation, and line-edge roughness, which idealized, as-drawn FDTD simulations fail to capture. Here, we show a Fab Technology Co-Optimization (FTCO) workflow that connects GDS layout import, three-dimensional process simulation, GPU-accelerated FDTD, design of experiments (DOE), with AI-based surrogate modeling. We show that when manufacturing variations are included in the modeling that the simulation results align well with experimentally reported results. A directional-coupler DOE with 25 unique combinations of 4 different process variations requiring a 65-million-cell 3D FDTD model and completes in under 10 hours on a single NVIDIA A100-equipped workstation is showcased. The generated digital twin provides intuitive and real-time access to the process-to-performance relationship for non-simulation experts: A game-changer in the industry.
